articles.title: A Molybdoenzyme Mediates Carbon–Sulfur Bond Making and Breaking in Ergothioneine Biosynthesis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The molybdopterin-dependent ergothioneine synthase (MES) from Caldithrix abyssi is the first molybdoenzyme known to catalyze the formation of carbon–sulfur bonds. To complete its catalytic cycle, this bifunctional enzyme desulfurates l-cysteine at a pyridoxal 5′-phosphate binding site and transfers the harvested sulfur atom (S0) to the molybdenum center of a bis-molybdopterin guanine dinucleotide cofactor more than 50 Å away. Subsequently, the sulfurated Mo-center transfers the labile sulfur atom onto the imidazole ring of Nα-trimethyl histidine (TMH). Combining experimental observations from cryo-electron microscopy, X-ray crystallography, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, sequence-activity correlation, and substrate-specificity studies, we delineate the structural basis for long-distance sulfur transfer via a persulfide relay, the identity of the imidazole sulfurating species, and key sequence motifs that are indispensable for activity. Furthermore, the reversibility of MES-mediated sulfurization of TMH under physiological conditions suggests that ergothioneine may serve as a soluble reservoir of oxidizing equivalents, supporting anaerobic metabolism in deep-branching bacteria such as C. abyssi.

articles.title: Wireless battery-free deep brain stimulators with extendable microelectrode probes
Exciton Transport in Disordered Perovskite Nanocrystal Solids
articles.abstract: Solution-processed thin films of colloidal lead halide perovskite (LHP) nanocrystals (NCs) show great potential for next-generation optoelectronic devices. However, these NC solids exhibit non-negligible size and shape polydispersity, which introduces both structural and energetic disorder. Here we resolve the exciton dynamics in space, time, and energy to elucidate the impact of disorder on exciton transport. We show that the disorder depends sensitively on the alkylamine ligand used in the synthesis. While shorter alkyl chain lengths lead to high polydispersity, longer alkyl chains lead to a narrower size distribution and smaller particles where quantum confinement becomes more pronounced, consequently leading to increased energetic disorder. Strikingly, we find that exciton transport is less efficient in NC solids with long alkyl chains, despite the fact that they have significantly more narrowly size-distributed ensembles. This demonstrates that energetic disorder rather than structural disorder is the dominant factor for predicting exciton transport within these disordered systems.

articles.title: A Fungal Hyaluronate Lyase with a Distinct Catalytic Machinery Expands the Polysaccharide Lyase Landscape
articles.abstract: Hyaluronic acid (HA) is a major glycosaminoglycan of the vertebrate extracellular matrix whose biological functions depend strongly on its molecular weight. Controlled depolymerization of HA into defined oligosaccharides is therefore of considerable biomedical and biotechnological interest. Although bacterial HA lyases have been extensively characterized, fungal HA-degrading enzymes remain poorly understood, and none has been structurally assigned to a defined CAZy family. Here, we identify and characterize PlLya44, an HA lyase secreted by the filamentous fungus Purpureocillium lilacinum. The enzyme was detected in the fungal secretome, produced in Pichia pastoris, and shown to efficiently depolymerize high molecular weight HA, generating mainly unsaturated oligosaccharides with both even- and odd-numbered products. Product analysis supports a predominantly processive endolytic mode of action distinct from the classical exo-processive mechanism of bacterial HA lyases. The crystal structure of PlLya44 uncovers an α-helical α6/α6 barrel fold characteristic of the (α/α)n toroid superfamily, harboring an elongated polarity-partitioned catalytic cleft. Structural comparisons and sequence similarity network analyses demonstrate that PlLya44 does not cluster with any currently defined polysaccharide lyase (PL) family, supporting its classification as the founding member of a distinct PL family. Ligand-bound structures, mutagenesis, ensemble refinement, and molecular dynamics reveal a reorganized catalytic architecture, reversing substrate orientation relative to previously characterized HA lyases. Together, these findings provide structural insight into a fungal HA lyase, uncover a previously unrecognized catalytic strategy for HA depolymerization, and establish PlLya44 as the founding member of a hitherto undescribed PL family, expanding the enzymatic landscape of glycosaminoglycan-active enzymes.

articles.title: Durability Assessment of α-MnO2 Nanorods for Alkaline ORR under Application-Relevant Conditions
articles.abstract: This study investigates the durability of α-MnO2, one of the most cost-effective catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in alkaline media. A comprehensive set of various characterization techniques, including identical location transmission electron microscopy (IL-TEM), differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), rotating ring-disk electrode (RRDE), and online inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) coupled to both flow cell and gas diffusion electrode (GDE) half-cell, was employed. In addition, accelerated stress test (AST) measurements in the GDE half-cell followed by post mortem X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and TEM analysis were performed. Three electrolyte and temperature combinations ranging from standard lab conditions to application-relevant conditions were systematically investigated. The results reveal that Mn dissolution occurs under oxygen-free conditions due to oxidation-state transitions of the catalyst, whereas under oxygen, it is further accelerated by degradation processes associated with peroxide formation as a byproduct of the ORR, particularly at higher ORR overpotentials. Both increasing KOH concentration and temperature significantly enhance Mn dissolution due to accelerated Mn reduction and dissolution kinetics. Despite the increased dissolution, the condition of 4.0 M KOH at 25 °C exhibits the highest ORR activity after 5000 AST cycles. This apparent discrepancy is attributed to surface roughening of the catalyst, leading to an increased electrochemically active surface area. Overall, the results demonstrate that α-MnO2 exhibits promising initial ORR activity but undergoes substantial Mn dissolution under operating conditions. These findings provide mitigation strategies to limit catalyst degradation and improve operational durability.

articles.title: Halogen Fluorine Unlocks Ru Activity for Olefins Production from Syngas
articles.abstract: Olefins production from syngas via Fischer–Tropsch synthesis requires catalysts that favor olefins formation, maintain intrinsic activity, and suppress CO2 and CH4 formation. Sodium-promoted ruthenium nanoparticles shift the product distribution toward α-olefins but suppress Ru activity by more than 90%, necessitating higher Ru loadings. We show that incorporating inorganic fluorine into Na-promoted Ru catalysts increases activity 2.5-fold while maintaining 72.1% α-olefins selectivity and ∼5.0% combined selectivity to CO2 and CH4. At a Ru loading of 1.26 wt %, the catalyst achieves a Ru time yield of 1.14 molCO·gRu–1·h–1 and olefins space-time yield of 1516.1 g·molRu–1·h–1, outperforming most reported Ru-based catalysts. Fluorine also restores activity in Fe- and Co-based systems. Mechanistic studies indicate that surface Na–F cation–anion pairs modulate the electronic structure, weaken Ru-CO binding, and generate hydrogen species that accelerate CO activation and suppress olefins hydrogenation. This work established a halogen-mediated strategy to address the activity–selectivity trade-off in sodium-promoted syngas conversion.

articles.title: Interactive Learning with Low‑Performance Data for Accurate CO2 Reduction Catalyst Prediction
articles.abstract: Emerging machine learning (ML) approaches offer transformative strategies to accelerate discovery for challenging objectives, such as developing practical catalysts through rational design. We propose an iterative learning framework and strategy that effectively enhances the predictive capability of the ML model, thereby accelerating catalyst development. By leveraging low-performance catalytic results, we have proven a practical, scalable framework for data-efficient catalyst development and for the broader application of ML methods in heterogeneous catalysis. The ML approach effectively captures the intrinsic relationship between metal type/content and catalytic performance, thereby enhancing prediction accuracy through iterative optimization. The case example regards the development of metal-supported catalysts for CO2 reduction. The results show that incorporating low-performance catalytic results into the iterative learning process markedly improves the predictive accuracy of the random forest (RF) model (R2 increased from 0.80 to 0.86, and mean square error (RMSE) decreased from 1.20% to 0.89%). The deviations between the experimental and predicted values for the CO2 reduction performance of the four catalysts identified through this approach were all less than 2%, demonstrating the model's reliability and predictive capability. Among them, the 1.5Pt2Fe/TiO2-R catalyst exhibited high CO2 reduction activity and long-term stability (>200 h), highlighting the practical potential of ML-guided catalyst design. The use of low-performance catalytic data outperforms high-performance ones in improving predictive accuracy when coupled with a suitable iterative learning framework, providing mechanistic insight into how they help the model define the boundaries of the feasible performance region.

articles.title: MoO x as an Oxidized Incorporation Modulates Nickel Sites for Efficient H2O2 Electrosynthesis at 200 mA cm–2
articles.abstract: Electrochemical H2O2 synthesis via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e– ORR) enables on-site production, yet its practical application is hindered by the scarcity of catalysts that can simultaneously deliver high selectivity, activity, and stability at industrial current densities. Here, we report molybdenum incorporation into nickel oxide, where Mo is predominantly present as atomically dispersed, oxygen-coordinated Mo species (denoted as MoOx). The resulting MoOx–NiO catalyst features a hybrid crystalline–amorphous structure. Spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations reveal that MoOx induces a localized electron redistribution, generating electron-rich Ni sites with a formal valence below + 2 (Ni2–x) adjacent to MoOx as key active sites. These Ni2–x sites tune the adsorption free energy of the critical OOH intermediate and favor the 2e– pathway over the competing 4e– pathway. The MoOx–NiO achieves >95% H2O2 selectivity over a potential range of 0.25–0.70 V vs RHE and a high production rate of 34.8 ± 0.8 mol gcat–1 h–1 at an industrial current density of 200 mA cm–2 in a flow cell, together with high Faradic efficiency and long-term operational stability. These findings show that engineering the chemical state and oxygen coordination of a dopant can modulate the local electronic structures of host metal sites and thereby influence catalytic pathways, providing a strategy for the design of advanced oxide electrocatalysts.

articles.title: Non-Thermal Plasma-Assisted CH4–CO2 Co-Conversion: A Reservoir of Surface Species is the Key to Selective Liquid Product Formation
articles.abstract: Non-thermal plasma (NTP) catalysis enables the direct co-conversion of CH4 and CO2 into thermodynamically limited liquid products under mild conditions. However, achieving high selectivity toward liquid products and clarifying the role of the catalyst in steering product distribution remain significant challenges. Here we uncover a previously unrecognized mechanism governing selectivity in plasma catalysis: the formation of a reservoir of strongly adsorbed surface species that evolves during reaction and dynamically controls liquid-product formation. We investigated the catalytic performance, catalyst structure, plasma properties, and surface species during time-dependent liquid methanol production—in addition to valuable syngas and C2 hydrocarbons in the gas stream—over an α-Fe2O3 catalyst. Stable catalyst structure and plasma conditions were unable to explain the transient product selectivity towards methanol. Instead, in situ plasma–IR studies revealed that strongly bound C═O and C–H species progressively accumulated with time-on-stream (TOS) and correlated with the observed increase in methanol yield. The strongly bound C═O and C–H species are proposed to enhance methanol selectivity by modifying the surface Brønsted and Lewis acidity, promoting methoxy hydrogenation, and weakening methanol adsorption. Studying the plasma interaction of select reaction species (CH4, CO2, CO, methanol, acetaldehyde, and acetic acid) with the catalyst surface showed that the main liquid product, methanol, was responsible for populating the surface with hydrogenated carbonyl species that boosted its own production. A methanol-plasma pretreatment was envisioned and implemented to preload a reservoir of the C═O and C–H species on the surface of α-Fe2O3, resulting in a significant improvement in catalyst performance for selective methanol production. After 8 h TOS, the treated catalyst exhibited a 30% relative increase in selectivity and a threefold increase in methanol yield compared to the untreated catalyst, offering a promising route toward highly selective liquid product formation. Additionally, the methanol–plasma pretreatment to boost methanol production was extended to other metal oxide catalysts, highlighting the broad versatility and potential of this strategy across a wide range of plasma catalyst systems.

articles.title: Oxygen Vacancy Distribution as a Structural Switch for Oxygen Cycling: A Local Oxygen Chemical Potential Descriptor for Methane Oxidative Coupling on SrTiO3
articles.abstract: Oxygen species evolution is central to the catalytic performance of oxidative coupling of methane (OCM), yet understanding and controlling this evolution remains a major challenge. SrTiO3 is a promising OCM catalyst due to its high C2 selectivity and stability but suffers from low activity. Here, DFT calculations combined with kMC simulations were employed to investigate facet-dependent oxygen species cycling on SrTiO3. Our findings reveal that SrTiO3(100)-Ti is the most favorable facet, sustaining a regenerable oxygen cycle (“O2− → OV → O22− → Ti-OH → O2−”). The local oxygen chemical potential (μO) is further identified as a thermodynamic descriptor linking oxygen stability with CH4* activation ability, following the order OV > O22− > Ti-OH > O2−. Furthermore, the spatial distribution of OV acts as a structural switch, directing two competing Mars–van Krevelen (MvK) cycles. kMC simulations reveal that the peroxide-mediated pathway dominates under operando conditions, whereas the overall activity is limited by the low activity of O2− and the accumulation of inert OlatH that further poisons active sites. Notably, B-site La doping effectively overcomes this bottleneck by activating OlatH and increasing the μO of O2− from –9.12 eV to –6.57 eV, which enhances the CH4(g) turnover frequency from 4.79 × 10−1 to 2.40 s−1 at 1073.15 K. These results establish μO and oxygen vacancy distribution as general design principles for perovskite oxide catalysts, offering a promising strategy to enhance OCM activity.

articles.title: Relating Cu Phase Transitions to Selectivity Recovery During Pulsed CO2 Reduction on Gas Diffusion Electrodes
articles.abstract: Pulsed electrochemical CO2 reduction on Cu catalysts represents a promising strategy to mitigate catalyst degradation and sustain high selectivity toward multicarbon (C2+) products. However, developing a detailed mechanistic understanding of the oxidative pulses remains challenging due to the inability to resolve the Cu oxidation state and the local electrolyte pH in the vicinity of the catalyst, especially inside a porous gas diffusion electrode. In this study, we investigate the impact of different potential pulse profiles on the recovery of CO and C2+ product selectivity, the latter representing C–C coupling. The potential-pH trajectories of the pulses are mapped onto calculated potential-pH Cu phase diagrams for CO2-saturated aqueous KCl and KHCO3 electrolytes to identify the thermodynamically accessible Cu phases during pulses. We show that abrupt pulses at a local alkaline pH lead to simultaneous C2+ and CO recovery. In contrast, quasi-adiabatic pulses, where the local pH remains equilibrated with the bulk pH, recover CO selectivity independently of C2+ products. Furthermore, in acidic KCl electrolytes, where no Cu oxide is thermodynamically accessible during a quasi-adiabatic pulse, the recovery of C2+ is attributed to Cu dissolution and redeposition. Importantly, this finding demonstrates that the formation of a Cu oxide phase, even temporarily during the pulse, is not required for C–C coupling. In contrast, in KHCO3 electrolyte, the formation of a Cu oxide phase remains thermodynamically accessible during pulses. Moreover, we show that the oxidative charge of the pulse recovering CO selectivity scales with prior reduction time, hypothesized to be a removal of surface poisoning species. Our findings enable rational design of pulse protocols based on electrolyte-, potential-, and pH-resolved Cu phase diagrams and provide a framework that can be extended to other catalysts and electrolytes.

articles.title: Rhδ+ Anchored on Rh–Fe Bimetallic Nano-islands Ensures Highly Efficient CO Hydrogenation to Ethanol
articles.abstract: The direct synthesis of ethanol from syngas faces a key challenge: achieving high selectivity at high CO conversion while elucidating the catalytic reaction mechanism. Here, we develop a catalyst comprising highly dispersed Rh–Fe bimetallic nano-islands supported on mixed-phase TiO2, which overcomes the trade-off between catalytic activity and ethanol selectivity, achieving an ethanol selectivity of 62.5% among all carbon-containing products at a CO conversion of 55.8%. Meanwhile, CO2 selectivity is greatly reduced to 8.1%. Mechanistic studies reveal that the breakthrough stems from the enhanced density of interfacial active sites, that the Fe species modulate the local electronic environment to optimize the Rhδ+/Rh0 ratio, and Rhδ+ species in contact with the TiO2 support are stably anchored via the formation of FeOx–Rhδ+–Ov–Ti3+ interfacial sites. The in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS), chemical transient kinetics (CTK), and density functional theory (DFT) characterizations reveal that the surface Rh0 sites facilitate CO dissociation and hydrogenation, whereas the FeOx–Rhδ+–Ov–Ti3+ interfacial sites promote the coupling of CHx with CHxO while suppressing the CO* + O → CO2 pathway. This work provides a route for suppressing CO2 formation and enhancing ethanol production in syngas conversion.

articles.title: Cucurbit[ n ]uril-Programmed Chlorogenic Acid Release for Collagen Mineralization and Pulp–Dentin Repair in Near-Pulp Bonding
articles.abstract: Long-term failure of resin–dentin bonding arises from persistent hydration and enzymatic degradation of exposed collagen in the deep hybrid layer, whereas diffusion of bioactive components through dentinal tubules toward the pulp may cause pulpal irritation. An ideal pretreatment should therefore promote collagen remineralization and interfacial stabilization while reducing pulp-adjacent cellular irritation and supporting pulp–dentin repair. Herein, supramolecular complexes of chlorogenic acid (CGA) and cucurbit[n]uril (Q[n], n = 6, 7, and 8), denoted CGA@Q[n], were constructed to regulate CGA loading, release, and interfacial exposure. CGA@Q[6] showed limited loading, release, and mineralization capacity. CGA@Q[7] exhibited faster early release and achieved complete collagen mineralization within 24 h, whereas CGA@Q[8] showed the highest encapsulation efficiency, sustained CGA supply, complete mineralization at 36 h, and a continuous, dense, integrated intrafibrillar mineral phase. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated that CGA released from Q[8] reanchored to collagen and recruited Ca2+, promoting mineral formation within confined intrafibrillar spaces. These advantages extended to three-dimensional collagen networks and demineralized dentin, yielding higher HAp content, enhanced mineral–collagen integration, tubule occlusion, mechanical recovery, and MMP-9 inhibition. As a bonding pretreatment, CGA@Q[8] reduced nanoleakage, endogenous gelatinolytic activity, and aging-induced bond-strength loss. It also improved cytocompatibility relative to free CGA and promoted mineralization and odontogenic differentiation of human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs). In vivo, CGA@Q[8] promoted dentin remineralization, maintained near-pulp interfacial stability, alleviated pulpal irritation, and enhanced odontogenic repair. Together, these findings identify CGA@Q[8] as the most effective formulation and show that homologue selection can tune CGA exposure kinetics for coordinated dentin interface repair.

articles.title: Deciphering Charge Delocalization across Mercaptobenzonitrile Ligand Terminals and Inner Hydrides in Atomically Precise Cu14H10 Nanoclusters for Electrocatalytic CO2 Reduction
articles.abstract: Cu hydride nanoclusters with atomic precision in composition and structure offer exciting catalytic activities and opportunities for rigorous structure–function correlations. Determination of their atomic structures, especially the hydride locations, hinges on the availability of high-quality single crystals and neutron beams, while their relatively weak UV–visible absorption and electrochemical instability challenge the analysis of their electronic properties. Herein, we synthesize a Cu14H10 nanocluster coordinated by three 4-mercaptobenzonitrile (MBN) and eight triphenylphosphine ligands. Two-dimensional NMR analyses combined with single crystal X-ray diffraction reveal unequivocally the locations of the ten hydrides in four groups (stoichiometry ratio of 1:3:3:3) with drastically different environments (chemical shifts 11–3 ppm): one H at the inversion center and three triangular layers along the C3 axial bridging together the Cu core. MBN serves two additional purposes besides stabilizing ligands: its electron-withdrawing nature and a highly sensitive vibrational reporter of its local charge density. The first property gives rise to a low-lying Cu-core-to-MBN metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) excited state, and the second property enables direct spectroscopic probing of both the charge transfer nature and dynamics of the MLCT excited state through the dynamic spectral shift of the MBN CN stretching mode. Through combined transient IR absorption spectroscopy and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations, we obtained the complete atomic and electronic structure, revealing core-to-ligand charge transfers in these nanoclusters. Computed under identical conditions using an iso-structure with a mildly electron-donating ligand, the Cu14H10 featuring charge delocalization toward the electron-withdrawing MBN has a smaller HOMO–LUMO gap, which is deemed favorable for electrocatalytic CO2 reduction. The preferential formation of complex multielectron-hydrogenation products (8–12 e–, C1 hydrocarbons, and C2+ products) over two-electron pathways such as CO formation or the competing hydrogen evolution reaction highlights their promise as atomically precise catalysts for deep CO2 reduction.

articles.title: Decoupling Conductivity and Interfacial State in Pristine-Like Carbon Nanotube Coatings Reveals Their Distinct Contributions to Neuronal Function
articles.abstract: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) combine high electrical conductivity, mechanical robustness, and nanoscale architecture, making them promising materials for neural interfaces. However, the strong coupling between CNT morphology, electrical transport, and surface chemistry has limited identification of the material properties that directly regulate neuronal function. Here, we establish an experimental strategy to disentangle morphology-dependent network transport from interfacial wettability using pristine-like CNT coatings. Multiwalled CNTs with comparable diameters but distinct lengths were reversibly functionalized, spray-coated, and thermally defunctionalized to produce homogeneous conductive networks while recovering pristine-like electrical transport and surface chemistry. Subsequent conditioning in phosphate-buffered saline substantially reduced surface hydrophobicity without detectable alteration of the graphitic CNT framework, generating coatings with comparable interfacial wettability but distinct network morphologies. Primary spinal cord neuron-glia cultures grown on these substrates were characterized by immunocytochemistry, electrophysiology, and calcium imaging. All CNT coatings supported comparable neuroglial density and network formation, whereas PBS-conditioned coatings, characterized by a more wettable interface, consistently exhibited enhanced spontaneous bursting and calcium activity compared with their untreated coatings. Across all conditions, neuronal network activity was more consistently associated with the initial interfacial state of CNT coatings, as experimentally reflected by their wetting behavior, than with CNT length or morphology-dependent electrical transport. These findings identify the initial CNT interfacial state, with wettability serving as an experimentally accessible descriptor, as a key design parameter for CNT-based neural interfaces. Furthermore, they suggest that the initial interfacial state may influence the subsequent evolution of the biomolecular layer at the cell-facing interface, thereby contributing to the modulation of neuronal function.

articles.title: Defect-Tolerant Frenkel Exciton Delocalization in Supramolecular Nanotubes
articles.abstract: Preserving exciton delocalization in the presence of structural and environmental disorder is a central challenge for nanoscale photonic and optoelectronic materials. Here we show that Frenkel excitons in two-dimensional supramolecular nanostructures retain extensive delocalization even in the presence of intentionally incorporated deep-energy traps. Fluorescent trap molecules introduced during the self-assembly of double-walled molecular nanotubes provide a controlled model system in which strong local energetic perturbations are created without significant distortion of the host structure. Increasing the trap concentration shortens the host-exciton PL lifetime from ∼190 ps to ∼15 ps, while polarization-resolved microscopy of individual nanotubes shows that the collective excitonic polarization remains essentially unchanged. Frenkel-exciton calculations based on experimentally established molecular structures reproduce this robustness and reveal that delocalization decreases only weakly because the excitonic wave functions redistribute around the trap sites while remaining extended over large molecular domains. These results demonstrate an intrinsic defect tolerance of delocalized Frenkel excitons in a two-dimensional supramolecular architecture and identify dimensionality as an important design principle for preserving collective excitonic states in structurally imperfect nanomaterials.

articles.title: Engineered Peptide Nanoparticle Targeting Both Bacterial Load Reduction and Bone Repair for the Treatment of Bone Infections
articles.abstract: Bone infection is a common and serious complication in orthopedic surgery. Conventional antibiotic strategies frequently induce antibiotic resistance, leading to the persistence of bone infections. In this study, an engineered peptide nanoparticle named C8-IK21 was designed based on the coiled-coil motif. Specifically, C8-IK21 effectively targeted bacterial cell membranes, further exacerbating bacterial death through lipid peroxidation. At safe doses, local administration of C8-IK21 demonstrated high efficacy in treating S. aureus-infected cortical bone defects in mice. No detectable resistance emerged under the tested experimental conditions. Additionally, C8-IK21 exhibited anti-inflammatory activity. Furthermore, C8-IK21 could enter cells by binding to ADAM9, activating the ERK signaling pathway to regulate osteoblast differentiation. Meanwhile, C8-IK21 reduced the expression of ITGB1 via ADAM9, thereby inhibiting osteoclast differentiation and function. Moreover, the pro-osteogenic effect of C8-IK21 was validated in organoids. In conclusion, C8-IK21 represents a promising therapeutic approach for the treatment of refractory bacterial infections and bone homeostasis disorders.

articles.title: Ferroelectric-Empowered van der Waals Spectrometer with Record-High Sensitivity and Ultralow Noise
articles.abstract: Miniaturized spectrometers are essential for portable and consumer-oriented applications, yet their reduced physical footprint inherently limits the detector’s active area, leading to compromised sensitivity. Conventional strategies to enhance sensitivity, such as cryogenic cooling or photomultiplier tubes, are incompatible with miniaturization due to their bulk, cost, and power demands. Here, we present a miniaturized spectrometer based on a van der Waals heterojunction integrated on a ferroelectric thin film. Spectral discrimination is enabled by engineering both interlayer and intralayer photoresponses within the heterojunction, which can be dynamically tuned solely via the source-drain bias, eliminating the need for a gate electrode and enabling a two-terminal architecture. This design is inherently compatible with simple two-pad readout integrated circuits, facilitating scalable array integration for compact spectroscopic systems. Critically, the built-in electric field generated by the ferroelectric polarization promotes efficient dissociation of interlayer excitons, yielding an ultralow noise floor of below 5 × 10–16 A Hz–1/2, more than 2 orders of magnitude lower than existing miniaturized spectrometers and surpassing the performance of most benchtop instruments. This work in sensitivity without sacrificing size or complexity present a strategy for deploying high-performance spectroscopy in real-world applications.

articles.title: Full-Length Protein Classification through Sequence Reading by Solid-State Subnanopores
articles.abstract: Nanopore sequencing for full-length proteins is daunting due to inaccuracy of fingerprinting amino acids with ionic current and lack of theoretical models. Here, we demonstrate that nanopores drilled in 5 nm-thick membranes with constriction diameter <1 nm, i.e., subnanopores, can site-specifically read the primary structure of amyloid-β (Aβ) isoforms after 50-fold coverage. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that charged side chains near the constriction swing and modulate the volume exclusion of neighboring residues, resulting in a sequence context-dependent signal altered between translocation orientations. Orientation of individual label-free molecules is inferred by clustering, which yields high-fidelity empirical consensus that strongly correlates with computational trajectories (PCC = 0.78 ± 0.03). A homemade self-supervised learning method categorizes Aβ42 and Aβ40 at the single-molecule level (AUC = 0.88 ± 0.02) and predicts the mole fraction in agreement with actual ratios. Solid-state subnanopores offer a straightforward strategy for proteoform single-molecule classification and sequence extraction in mixtures.

articles.title: Janus Biofuel Cells for Electrosynergistic Enhancement of Microenvironment-Adaptive Cascade Catalysis in Infected Diabetic Wound Healing
articles.abstract: The treatment of infectious diabetic wound is greatly hampered by hyperglycemia, inflammation, and microcirculatory dysfunction. Bioelectric stimulation and nanozyme catalysis provide a potential strategy for chronic wound repair but suffer from limitations including external electric power, low activity, and competitive multienzyme reactions. Given this, we developed microenvironment-responsive Janus GOx-Au@PCH–Pt nanoparticles (NPs) as biofuel cells, integrating cascade enzymatic catalysis and self-powered electrical stimulation. The biofuel cell features hydroxylated polyaniline (PCH) NPs as conductive bridges, Pt nanoclusters as the cathode, and glucose oxidase (GOx)-grafted Au (GOx-Au) as the anode. Under infection (acidic pH), conductive PCH shuttles electrons to generate microcurrent that accelerates enzyme catalysis on both the Au anode (GOx) and Pt cathode (peroxidase, POD). The enhanced GOx-POD cascade strengthens ·OH generation, and the self-powered electric field enhances ·OH diffusion across phospholipid bilayers, achieving significant bacterial killing and biofilm dispersion. During tissue repair, neutral/alkaline conditions switch Pt nanozyme from POD to catalase (CAT) and transform PCH into a benzoquinone structure as the electron acceptor. Reversed electron flow boosts the GOx-CAT cascade catalysis on the electrodes, accelerating glucose consumption, suppressing advanced glycation end product formation, and alleviating oxidative stress, while electrical stimulation reduces hypoxia-inducible factor-1α expressions. This synergistic effect promotes collagen deposition and orderly arrangement and normalizes microenvironment with oxygen-generating, hypoglycemic, anti-inflammatory, and macrophage phenotype-shifted features, thereby accelerating wound healing. This designed nanoscale biofuel cells realize adaptive microcurrent modulation and spatiotemporal cascade catalysis, offering a minimally invasive paradigm for infected diabetic wound therapy.

articles.title: MXene-PS-Based Soft Actuator with Deformation Reversal Capability through Time-Sequence Difference of Asymmetric Water Absorption Kinetics
articles.abstract: Many soft actuators have been developed to achieve bending deformation under external stimuli through asymmetric structures or nonuniform material distributions. However, most existing actuators can only produce bending in a single direction, and developing soft actuators with deformation reversal capability remains a challenge. To address this issue, this study proposes an MXene-PS/MXene bilayer soft actuator, which is fabricated by sequential vacuum-assisted filtration, resulting in a loose MXene-PS top layer and a dense MXene bottom layer. The MXene-PS layer features a high water absorption/desorption rate but low capacity, while the MXene layer exhibits a low rate but high capacity. This complementary kinetic-capacity coupling mechanism, termed the time-sequence difference of asymmetric water absorption kinetics, enables the actuator to achieve reversible deformation reversal under NIR light and humidity stimuli. Furthermore, simply by changing the placement orientation of the actuator, two distinct self-sustained oscillation behaviors can be obtained in a humidity gradient environment, namely, periodic motion toward or away from the water surface. Leveraging this deformation reversal capability, we demonstrate two proof-of-concept applications: a biomimetic flower and a self-sustained motion sailboat. This work introduces a deformation mode and actuation principle for MXene-based soft actuators and further broadens their application prospects in biomimetic devices and soft robotics.

articles.title: Nontrivial Edge Superconductivity in Dirac Superconductor PdTe2
articles.abstract: Superconducting topological materials with coexisted superconductivities and topological boundary states are promising platforms for realizing intrinsic topological superconductivity. In this work, the superconducting type-II Dirac semimetal PdTe2 is shown to exhibit clear periodic critical current oscillations in perpendicular magnetic fields due to the fluxoid quantization, indicating the existence of edge superconductivity in PdTe2. Furthermore, a comparative study of the different superconducting properties of the bulk and edge of PdTe2 provides direct evidence for this edge superconductivity. More importantly, by a careful analysis of the flux penetration area, the nontrivial character of the edge superconductivity is revealed, i.e., the edge superconductivity appears not only at the physical boundary of the flake, but also at the interior interface between superconducting and normal regions of PdTe2. The emergence of nontrivial edge superconductivity, indicative of the putative bulk topological superconductivity, not only reveals the great potential of PdTe2 but also provides an experimental avenue for exploring intrinsic topological superconductivity by leveraging bulk-boundary correspondence.

articles.title: Receptor-Modular Nanocaptors for Programmable Cytokine Sequestration
articles.abstract: Pathological cytokine networks underlie inflammatory injury and tumor-associated immunosuppression, yet most cytokine-targeted therapies rely on molecularly fixed, pathway-specific antagonists. We present a receptor-modular nanomaterial strategy for constructing modular cytokine nanocaptors (MCNs) whose sequestration profiles can be reconfigured by exchanging receptor modules. Cytokine receptor ectodomains are engineered as independently producible serum albumin fusion proteins and coassembled with poly(L-lactic acid) (PLLA) into compositionally defined nanoparticles. This architecture decouples cytokine-binding specificity from nanoparticle structure, enabling high-density codisplay of multiple receptor modules on single particles. Representative MCNs simultaneously sequester IL-6, TNF-α, and IFN-γ and suppress cytokine-driven inflammatory signaling more effectively than matched soluble receptor mixtures. By altering module composition while preserving the same assembly framework, MCNs can be redirected from sequestering pro-inflammatory cytokines in sepsis, acute lung injury, and fulminant hepatitis to depleting immunosuppressive mediators in tumors. These results establish receptor-modular nanocaptors as programmable materials for disease-tailored cytokine sequestration and immune-microenvironment reconfiguration.

articles.title: Tunable Gaussian Random Number Generator from a Nanoscopic Domain-Wall-Based Spintronic Device
articles.abstract: Existing hardware implementations of Gaussian random number generators (RNGs) rely on large arrays of binary devices, resulting in substantial hardware footprints or sampling-time overheads. Here, we present a racetrack memory-based random number generator (RTM-RNG) that directly generates analog Gaussian random number streams from a single domain-wall-based nanoscale racetrack. A geometrically engineered racetrack tip creates a localized current-density gradient, enabling field-free stochastic domain-wall nucleation driven by nanosecond current pulses. The domain-wall nucleation probability is continuously tunable via an electrically generated Oersted field or an external magnetic field, providing direct control over the mean of the output distribution. We demonstrate more than 256 distinguishable states from a single nanoscopic RTM-RNG device, thus making a Gaussian RNG with more than 8-bit resolution possible. Compared with conventional binary random bitstreams, the RTM-RNG achieves high-quality Gaussian distributions up to 83 times faster.

articles.title: ZnO–Te Anti-Ambipolar Switch Integration with Complementary Field-Effect Transistors Enabling a Pull-Middle Architecture for Standard Ternary Inverters
articles.abstract: We demonstrate a pull-middle architecture for standard ternary inverters (STIs) operating at 77 K, enabled by the cointegration of a ZnO–Te antiambipolar switch (AAS) and vertically stacked ZnO/Te complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs) using a BEOL-compatible low-temperature process (≤150 °C). Operation at 77 K not only isolates the intrinsic pull-middle switching mechanism by suppressing thermally activated off-currents but also establishes the architecture’s immediate viability for extreme-environment computing, such as radiation-hardened space data centers and cryogenic aerospace systems. In this architecture, the ZnO–Te AAS acts as an independent pull-middle device connected to an explicit Vdd/2 node, while the ZnO and Te FETs in the CFET serve as the pull-down and pull-up devices, respectively. Unlike conventional ternary logic schemes governed by precise pull-up/pull-down current matching, by explicitly clamping the intermediate state, this architecture structurally prevents variation-induced voltage shifts and suppresses static power dissipation. Consequently, the proposed STI exhibits a narrow middle-state voltage distribution across 25 cells and achieves an I/O swing ratio of 1, with cascaded operation without level-restoring circuitry supported by measurement-calibrated circuit simulations. Ultimately, this vertically integrated ZnO/Te STI offers a compact and variation-tolerant platform for cryogenic logic, while presenting a material-optimization pathway toward room-temperature multivalued systems.

Harnessing Contact Electrification and Static Charge for Chemical Reactions: Fundamentals and Applications of Contact Electrocatalysis
articles.abstract: The chemical industry is the largest industrial energy consumer and the third-largest emitter of CO2 globally. Despite efforts to enhance energy efficiency, many chemical reactions still require significant external energy due to fundamental thermodynamic barriers. Thus, transitioning to a sustainable chemical industry requires new renewable energy or catalytic technologies that reduce energy demand. In catalytic systems, flowing liquids, moving parts, and gas separation mean local static charge is often generated on the nanoscale. This review explores the static charge formation at solid–solid, solid–liquid, and solid–gas interfaces, such as those that occur in catalytic reactions, and then extends this discussion to a deeper focus on how these generated static charges can be used for catalysis, including electrostatic catalysis, static charge electrochemistry, and contact electrocatalysis (CEC). CEC, where motion-induced charge separation leads to local static charge formation, is then specifically examined, exploring why and how it has emerged as an exciting tool to enable these green chemical transformations. The focus is to highlight the most recent developments in CEC, with mechanistic interpretation, factors that affect CEC performance, and emerging applications, and to provide outlook and guidance for the field─specifically highlighting the need to build structure–property relationships for CEC performance and static charge formation for target chemical reactions.

articles.title: Lithium–Oxygen Batteries: Fundamental and Practical Considerations
articles.abstract: Lithium–oxygen batteries (LOBs) have emerged as a compelling next-generation energy storage technology for aviation due to their high theoretical energy densities and the use of abundant oxygen as a cathode reactant. Unlike conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), which are limited by the mass of intercalation materials and one-electron redox processes, LOBs leverage multielectron oxygen redox chemistry to achieve gravimetric energy density exceeding 3,500 Wh kgLi2O2–1 based on lithium peroxide and up to 5,200 Wh kgLi2O–1 for lithium oxide. However, practical implementation of LOBs remains constrained by significant challenges including low round-trip efficiency and low system-level energy density, the latter arising from the need for oxygen management in both open and closed architectures. The electrolyte viscosity, oxygen solubility, volatility, and chemical stability toward reactive oxygen species can profoundly influence discharge capacity, rate capability, reversibility, and long-term stability. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of recent progress in LOBs, focusing on electrolyte designs, electrode engineering, and strategies for mitigating parasitic reactions as well as the interplay between material-level properties and system-level constraints, offering a critical perspective on the path toward realizing high-energy, practical LOB systems.

articles.title: Named Reactions under Mechanochemical Conditions: A Critical Survey
articles.abstract: Mechanochemistry has progressed from a niche interest to a core method for solvent-free synthesis, providing sustainable and mechanistically unique alternatives to traditional solution-based chemistry. When controlled impact, shear, or vibrational energy is applied under solvent-free or solvent-lean conditions, reactions are promoted within dynamically renewed interfacial regions, revealing new patterns of selectivity, energy efficiency, and process design. This review surveys the historical development, fundamental principles, and analytical frameworks of mechanochemistry, together with an extensive compilation of named organic reactions conducted under mechanochemical conditions. By comparing mechanochemical reactions with their solution-phase counterparts, this review clarifies how stress-induced activation, microsolvation (η control), and auxiliary-mediated interfaces influence reaction kinetics, selectivity, and scalability. Emerging platforms, such as twin-screw extrusion (TSE), resonant acoustic mixing (RAM), and bead mills, extend these advantages toward scale-up and, in the case of TSE, continuous manufacturing, bridging laboratory-scale discoveries and industrial applications. Mechanochemistry functions both as a practical enabling platform and as a conceptual framework for Green Chemistry, embracing atom economy, solvent reduction, and operational safety within a unified solid-state synthetic framework.

articles.title: Exciton Dynamics and Charge Diffusion in Supramolecular Porphyrin Polymers
articles.abstract: Controlling chromophore aggregation across nano- to mesoscale dimensions provides a powerful strategy for tailoring the properties of π-conjugated materials and accelerating advances in organic optoelectronic technologies. Because exciton generation, migration, and dissociation in organic assemblies are governed by molecular packing, precise control over nanoscale order is critical for defining structure−function relationships in organic semiconductors. In this context, one-dimensional supramolecular polymers offer compelling design platforms, where assembly pathways and packing geometries can be leveraged to modulate excitonic coupling, promote delocalization, and direct transport. Although porphyrin superstructures with J-type excitonic coupling have been widely studied as models for efficient energy migration, the excited-state processes of H-type porphyrin assemblies remain comparatively underexplored, despite the structural robustness of these constructs and their potential to promote directional exciton and charge diffusion. Here, we address this gap using a novel zinc porphyrin derivative PZn-OTEG-OH, which undergoes cooperative supramolecular polymerization to form one-dimensional aggregates with H-like photophysics. Ultrafast pump−probe transient absorption measurements in solution reveal that the supramolecular polymer exhibits a nanosecond excited-state lifetime together with diffusive exciton migration over nanometer length scales. In the solid state, the preorganized aggregate translates into an interconnected fibrillar network, in contrast to the comparatively featureless films obtained from monomeric solution. Solid-state electrochemical measurements reveal only modest shifts in redox inflection potentials between monomer- and aggregate-derived films, whereas chronoamperometry indicates faster charging dynamics and an increased apparent diffusion coefficient for the aggregate-derived films. Together, these results demonstrate that cooperative H-like porphyrin assemblies can integrate efficient exciton migration in solution with enhanced charge accumulation in the solid state, establishing a molecular design strategy for light-harvesting organic semiconducting materials.

articles.title: Phase- and Thickness-Controlled Chemical Vapor Deposition of SnSe and SnSe2 Films: Thermodynamic and Kinetic Insights into Phase Selection
articles.abstract: Phase selection among competing stoichiometric compounds during nonequilibrium vapor-phase growth remains a fundamental challenge because experimentally accessible growth parameters ultimately influence phase formation through both thermodynamic driving forces and atomic-scale kinetic processes. Here, we investigate phase selection between SnSe and SnSe2 during low-pressure chemical vapor deposition (CVD) by integrating systematic growth experiments, first-principles thermodynamic calculations, and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. Systematic regulation of the relative Sn/Se chemical environment and growth temperature establishes distinct SnSe- and SnSe2-dominant growth regimes. Thermodynamic calculations show that SnSe is preferentially stabilized under Sn-rich conditions with low Se chemical potential, whereas increasing the Se chemical potential shifts the thermodynamic preference toward SnSe2. Complementary atomistic simulations reveal that increasing Se availability progressively promotes SnSe2-like local coordination, while elevated temperature enhances Sn−Se interdiffusion and redistributes Se toward more spatially dispersed, locally Se-deficient configurations. Building on the established phase-selective growth conditions, we further demonstrate independent thickness tunability through growth-time control, with SnSe and SnSe2 film thicknesses spanning 15−123 and 13.5−120 nm, respectively. Together, these results show that stoichiometry-dependent phase competition under nonequilibrium growth conditions reflects the combined effects of thermodynamic stability and atomic kinetics, while film thickness can be adjusted through growth-time control. These results provide insight into the relationship between growth conditions, phase selection, and film thickness in compositionally related layered chalcogenides.

articles.title: Abstract P1060A: CPR Training Perception and Willingness to Act: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Pre-Medical Students
articles.abstract: Introduction/Background: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is critical step for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest survival. Pre-medical students represent an unstudied and high-potential bystander population, yet predictors of post-training CPR willingness remain poorly characterized. Hypothesis: Pre-medical students from a public university in Argentina perceiving CPR training as highly important would demonstrate greater willingness to perform CPR after course completion. Methods: Prospective, cross-sectional study post mandated CPR-course survey of all pre-medical students (full cohort 2026) at Universidad Nacional de La Matanza, Argentina. The educational program comprised a 3-hour, theoretical-practical course led by university instructors in accordance with the 2025 AHA guidelines. Variables included demographics, prior CPR exposure (awareness, prior formal course, real-life CPR performance), perceived training importance (Likert 1-5), post-course CPR willingness (Likert 1-5; high=4-5). Real-life CPR performance was operationally defined as the delivery of chest compressions with or without the use of an automated external defibrillator (AED). Bivariate analyses used chi-square and crude odds ratios (OR, 95%CI). Two multivariable logistic regression models identified independent factors associated to: Model 1: high post-course CPR willingness and model 2: prior real-life CPR performance. Results: 448 students responded (mean age 21.9±5.5 years; 70.8% female). Prior awareness of CPR was high (94.9%); 32.1% had completed a prior formal CPR course; only 6.5% had performed CPR in a real-life emergency. Perceived importance was: 96.2% rated 5/5. High post-course CPR willingness was reported by 67.2%. In bivariate analysis, maximum importance perception was associated with high willingness to render CPR in real life (OR=3.07, 95%CI:1.14-8.23, p=0.020), as was prior formal CPR course (OR=1.82, 95%CI:1.16-2.84, p=0.008). In multivariable analysis (Model 1), maximum importance perception independently predicted high willingness (adjusted OR=2.96, 95%CI:1.07-8.22, p=0.037). For real-life CPR performance (Model 2), prior formal CPR course (adjusted OR=5.24, 95%CI:2.06-13.36, p<0.001) and older age (adjusted OR=2.18 per SD, 95%CI:1.63-2.92, p<0.001) were the sole independent predictors. Gender was not associated with either outcome. Conclusions: Perceiving CPR training as maximally important independently predicted greater willingness to perform CPR post-course. Prior formal CPR training was the strongest predictor of real-life CPR performance. These findings support early, repeated CPR training in medical curricula and emphasize framing instruction within clinical relevance to enhance motivation and real-world application. These cross-sectional associations warrant confirmation in longitudinal studies.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Health Promotion for US Veterans: Current State, Gaps, and Strategies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
articles.abstract: US veterans represent a large and diverse population with distinctive demographic characteristics, comorbidity profiles, and social determinants of health shaped by military service. These factors contribute to a high burden of cardiovascular risk and low attainment of ideal cardiovascular health. At the same time, the Department of Veterans Affairs, which operates the nation’s largest integrated healthcare system, provides a unique infrastructure for delivering population-level cardiovascular disease prevention for veterans. Understanding its successes and ongoing challenges can inform broader strategies across all health systems for promoting health among veterans. This scientific statement applies the American Heart Association’s Life’s Essential 8 framework, expanded to include mental health and substance use, to evaluate veteran cardiovascular health. For each domain, we review guideline recommendations, barriers to achieving optimal health, and major Veterans Affairs programs such as Patient Aligned Care Teams, the MOVE! Weight Management Program for Veterans, Whole Health, telehealth-based interventions, and integrated mental health and substance use disorder services. Across domains, veterans receiving Veterans Affairs care often achieve outcomes that are equal to or better than those of their non–Veterans Affairs counterparts, reflecting the strengths of the system in coordinated, team-based care and research-driven implementation. Despite substantial progress, opportunities remain to improve veteran lifestyle behaviors, metabolic health, lipid and blood pressure control, engagement in mental health and substance use care, and detection and management of sleep disorders. Addressing these challenges at the Veterans Affairs will require continuing to expand care access, enhancing digital data integration, tailoring interventions to high-risk subgroups, and strengthening implementation strategies to improve uptake and engagement across Veterans Affairs services.

articles.title: Diversity and composition of benthic marine communities under contrasting management and temperature regimes
articles.abstract: The sustainable management of small-scale fisheries is key for the well-being of coastal communities. Environmental conditions are known to influence the ecology of the coastal zone, yet their interactions with fisheries management regimes remains poorly understood. We examined spatial changes in the structure of benthic communities under distinct management regimes (TURF or Territorial Use Rights for Fisheries, and OA or open access areas) located in areas with different temperature patterns (warm and cold). Using underwater visual censuses, we assessed benthic community patterns across four locations in northern-central Chile and examined how species diversity and composition varied between management and environmental regimes. Our results showed that communities differed significantly between management and temperature regimes. In general, sessile community richness was 65% higher under cold regimes compared to warm regimes. For mobile invertebrates, richness and diversity were 42% and 41% greater in TURF areas than in OA areas, while both attributes were 4% and 5% higher under cold than warm temperature regimes. In the case of fish communities, species composition varied as a function of the interaction between management and temperature regimes. In cold sites, benthic communities within TURF areas were characterized by the kelp Lessonia trabeculata, the whelk Concholepas concholepas, and keyhole limpets (Fissurella spp.), whereas OA areas were dominated by kelp, the sea urchin Arbacia nigra, and the starfish Meyenaster gelatinosus. Benthic communities of TURF areas in warm sites were associated with anemones, sea urchins and kelps, whereas OA areas were dominated mainly by anemones and sea urchins. Overall, our results support the notion that the structure of benthic communities can be influenced by an interaction between management regime and environmental conditions. The two temperature regimes stem from the differential exposure to coastal upwelling between sites, which suggests that other environmental processes, such as productivity or wave exposure, are implicated. Overall, the marked ecological differences between TURF and OA areas under contrasting temperature patterns suggest that environmental conditions should be incorporated into the design of novel fishery policies to promote the sustainable management of small-scale coastal fisheries.

articles.title: Late Triassic Dipnoi from south Gondwana, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
articles.abstract: Mesozoic lungfishes are often represented in the fossil record by isolated tooth plates, which impose limitations on their taxonomic identification and on the interpretation of their diversity. In the Triassic of South America, these organisms remain poorly documented. The present study describes eight isolated tooth plates from the Candelária Sequence of the Santa Maria Supersequence (Carnian, Late Triassic), southern Brazil, being attributed to three taxa: Ptychoceratodus phillipsi, P. eliseui sp. nov., and Ferganoceratodus cabreirai sp. nov. The description was made using morphological and morphometric approaches and the tooth plates. The results highlight the strong morphological similarity between Ptychoceratodus and Ferganoceratodus, as well as the overlap of diagnostic characters, which reinforces the difficulties in distinguishing between these genera when only isolated tooth plates are available. The association with other ichthyofauna and the presence of deposits indicative of varying depositional energies suggest a seasonal environment, with alternation between wet and dry periods. From a paleobiogeographic perspective, the record of Ferganoceratodus represents the first occurrence of the genus in the Triassic of South America, extending its previously known distribution. The occurrence of P. phillipsi, in turn, reinforces the wide dispersal of lungfishes throughout Pangaea during the Mesozoic. In this context, the materials described herein represent a relevant contribution to the Gondwanan record of Mesozoic lungfishes and reinforce the importance of the Candelária Sequence as a key unit for Triassic dipnoan paleobiogeography and biostratigraphy. The occurrence of these genera in Brazilian continental deposits is consistent with the distribution pattern observed for Mesozoic lungfishes and suggests faunal affinities with assemblages from other portions of Gondwana.
