articles.title: All-Visible Wavelength-Gated Multistate Photochromic AIEgen: High-Efficiency Photocyclizations in a Single Luminogenic System
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Synthetic photochromic molecules that enable noninvasive orthogonal control using distinct wavelengths of light are still in their infancy, yet ensuring the independence of photoreaction pathways and multiple addressable states in a single luminogenic system remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report an aggregation-induced emission (AIE) luminogen capable of undergoing wavelength-selective photocyclizations under visible-light irradiation, exhibiting a photorearrangement at 410 nm purple light and an oxidative photocyclization at 465 nm blue light to yield two stable yet distinct photochromic states. Experimental and theoretical results provide insight into the wavelength-dependent reaction pathways, as well as the corresponding synergistic mechanism of aromaticity, steric strain, and inductive effect in its photocyclizations. Eventually, a model information encryption system was developed to showcase its practical potential for all-visible-light-controlled multistate operations. This work thus offers both a viable strategy and a versatile structural motif for developing visible-light-controlled multistate luminogens and advanced multifunctional systems.

articles.title: An Experimental MOF-Polymer Latent Space for Composite Design
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have tremendous promise for filtration, catalysis, and sequestration, but they are limited by the polymer matrices in which they must be embedded to form functional composites. Here, we find an experimental approach in which composite performance can be predicted using a single MOF particle. In particular, we attach single MOF particles to atomic force microscope (AFM) probes and find that the forces between the MOF-tipped probe and polymer films can be transformed into an instructive low-dimensional descriptor of MOF-polymer interactions. This two-dimensional latent space provides direct measures of chemical compatibility as well as the work of adhesion and can be used to understand interfacial phenomena in MOF-polymer composites. For example, polymer intercalation is observed via X-ray scattering for MOF-polymer combinations with high chemical-compatibility latent-space variables. Bulk composite performance can also be predicted using the latent space values for cases where the MOF is held constant. For example, a simple linear model was trained to predict CO2 absorption into composites of UiO-66-NH2 based solely on the latent space variables. In addition to providing a rapid way to screen polymer matrices to complement a MOF chosen for its bulk properties, these results suggest that composite performance may be a separable function of bulk properties and the interfacial latent space. In this way, this transfer-learning approach can vastly accelerate the design and understanding of functional composites.

articles.title: Decyanation, Dioxygenation, and Oxidative Ring Contraction Catalyzed by the DUF4243 Oxidase OzmD Rely on Ferric Oxygen Activation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Domain of unknown function 4243 (DUF4243) family proteins are an emerging class of nonheme mononuclear iron enzymes characterized by a distinctive iron-binding motif comprised of four histidine (His) and one Nε-carboxylysine (Kcx) residue. Although predominantly found in fungi, OzmD is the only characterized bacterial member. OzmD catalyzes oxidative rearrangement of an aminopyridone ring into a 1,3-oxazine moiety with concomitant cyanide elimination in the final step of oxazinomycin biosynthesis. Herein, the X-ray crystal structure of OzmD is solved, demonstrating the presence of a conserved 4-His-1-Kcx iron-binding motif similar to other DUF4243 family proteins. Biochemical characterization using a substrate analog carrying a hydroxypyridone ring reveals that OzmD also exhibits intrinsic dioxygenase activity, catalyzing a transformation analogous to those of fungal DUF4243 dioxygenases. Electron paramagnetic resonance and Mössbauer spectroscopic characterization of MinCC, a functionally equivalent homologue of OzmD, reveals that the as-isolated protein predominantly contains ferric iron, which can be reduced to the ferrous state upon binding with either the native substrate or the hydroxy analog under anaerobic conditions. These findings support a unified mechanism in which catalysis begins with single-electron transfer from the substrate to ferric iron, enabling molecular oxygen activation and formation of an alkylperoxide intermediate. Overall reaction mechanisms for substrates bearing aminopyridone and hydroxypyridone rings are proposed based on chemical precedents and computational analyses. These findings reveal that OzmD employs a distinctive FeIII-dependent path for oxygen activation in contrast to the classical FeII-dependent route used by most oxygenases and establish a functional connection between bacterial and fungal DUF4243 enzymes.

articles.title: Dynamic Nonlinear Effects in the Asymmetric Kinetic Resolution Polymerization of Racemic Diazoacetates to One-Handed Helical Polycarbenes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The asymmetric kinetic resolution polymerization (AKRP) of racemic diazoacetates mediated by a [Rh(cod)Cl]2/chiral amine dual catalyst system exhibits dynamic nonlinear effects (DNLEs) in the relative rate constant (Krel). The overall Krel increases nonlinearly with the monomer conversion during polymer chain propagation and reaches a plateau at a medium conversion. These DNLEs originate from synergistic chirality amplification between the catalytic chain end and the evolving helical conformation of the growing polymer chain. Under optimized conditions, Krel increases from 15 at 3% monomer conversion to ∼ 138 at 33% conversion, and then reaches a plateau. The steric bulk of both the pendant groups of monomers and the chiral amine ligand critically regulates the magnitude and evolution of DNLEs, and reducing this bulk leads to a pronounced decrease in Krel. Chain extension experiments using the preformed helical macroinitiators exhibited a constant Krel, confirming that a well-formed helical conformation maintains stable enantioselectivity for AKRP. Computational studies further revealed that, during chain propagation, decameric species with well-developed helical conformations exhibit more pronounced energy differences between the R- and S-enantiomers than the corresponding initial monomer-inserted species. These results suggest that the one-handed helical conformation is associated with the enhanced enantiomer recognition at the catalytic center. This study reveals DNLEs in AKRP in which enantioselectivity evolves nonlinearly during polymer chain propagation, highlighting a dynamic chiral amplification mechanism that can surpass the intrinsic selectivity of a static catalyst through the cooperative action of chiral chain ends and helical conformation.

articles.title: Effect of Water on Elementary Reactions in Solid-Acid Catalyzed Reactions: Thermodynamics of Acid–Base Interactions in H-ZSM-5
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The influence of water on acid–base interactions in zeolites was quantified by measuring the enthalpy of pyridine adsorption on H-ZSM-5 with three Si/Al ratios (11.5, 40, and 140) in water using isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC). This calorimetric study reconciles the liquid- and gas-phase energetics of acid–base interactions in a solvated, pore-filled zeolite through a Born–Haber cycle analysis. In water, the apparent adsorption enthalpy is about 150 kJ/mol less exothermic than the gas-phase value and becomes more exothermic as the Si/Al ratio increases, whereas the gas-phase enthalpy is near −200 kJ/mol and independent of the Si/Al ratio. Since the intrinsic acid strength of the framework does not vary with Si/Al ratio, this increasing apparent adsorption energy trend with increasing Si/Al ratio reflects the influence of solvation rather than acidity. Water stabilizes both the acidic proton and the pyridinium ion, and a fraction of this stabilization is lost when adsorbed pyridine displaces water from the acid site. By combining ITC data with vapor-phase water adsorption isotherms and differential scanning calorimetry to construct a Born–Haber cycle for each zeolite, the aqueous-phase enthalpies are quantitatively reconciled with their gas-phase counterparts, and their dependence on Si/Al ratio is traced to the different extents to which the initial and final states are solvated.

articles.title: Electronic Dynamics in Long Linear and Cyclic Polyynes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Carbyne─the one-dimensional sp-hybridized allotrope of carbon─has long been predicted to exhibit unique properties, yet its synthesis remains elusive. To probe its behavior, finite sp-carbon chains such as cumulenes and polyynes have been studied. While much has been established about the ground-state properties of cumulenes and polyynes, our understanding of their photophysical dynamics, which gives critical insight into how electronic relaxation, structural reorganization, and spin formation evolve, has focused almost exclusively on short, linear systems, with little consideration of topology. Here, we investigate long 48-carbon linear and cyclic polyynes in the liquid phase using steady-state and ultrafast, temperature- and polarization-resolved optical and vibrational spectroscopy. We find highly delocalized ground states in both topologies, with softened Peierls distortion and reduced bond-length alternation relative to shorter chains. In contrast, the excited state singlet dipole depolarization mechanism and subsequent intersystem crossing are strongly dependent on chain length and topology. As in shorter polyynes, transient infrared spectroscopy shows that photoexcitation of long linear polyynes induces a cumulene-like excited-state geometry; however, this structural rearrangement is weaker and shorter-lived than in shorter analogues. Comparison with shorter-chain trends and theoretical predictions shows that the Huang–Rhys factor remains far below the ideal infinite-chain value at 48 carbons, suggesting that vibronic coupling grows more slowly at long chain length than expected from simple extrapolation. Our results reveal how topology influences the largely backbone-dominated electronic dynamics of long polyynes and refine our understanding of finite sp-carbon systems at longer chain lengths than previously accessible with such time-resolved methods.

articles.title: Enantioselective Three-Component Reductive Coupling of Aldehydes, Amines, and Alkynes via Ligand-Enabled Cobalt/Photoredox Dual Catalysis for Modular Synthesis of Allylic Amines
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Here, we disclose a catalytic strategy that merges visible-light photoredox with cobalt catalysis to realize a previously elusive three-component enantioselective reductive coupling of readily available aldehydes, amines, and alkynes. This transformation provides a direct, step-economical route to high-value chiral allylic amines with broad substrate scope and high chemo-, regio-, and enantioselectivity, while overcoming long-standing challenges, including parasitic single-electron over-reduction, competitive aldehyde–alkyne coupling, and the inherent regioselectivity issues of unsymmetrical internal alkynes, and circumventing the moisture sensitivity and limited scope of pre-isolated imines. Central to this breakthrough is the rational design of a chiral phosphoramidite ligand featuring a tricyclic tetrahydrobenzoquinoline core, which avoids coordination saturation at cobalt and establishes a unique electronic “push–pull” synergy with a coordinated iodide anion. Mechanistic studies support an anion-promoted, single-ligand catalytic model wherein a high-spin cobaltacyclopentene intermediate serves as the key stereocontrol element. The monodentate, π-accepting phosphoramidite functions as a flexible electronic buffer, mitigating Pauli repulsion and dramatically lowering the oxidative cyclization barrier. The synthetic utility is demonstrated by late-stage functionalization of complex bioactive molecules and a concise synthesis of the antiplatelet drug prasugrel.

articles.title: Evolution of Interfacial States Induced by Hydronium–Water Ordering on Au(111)
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Structured interfacial water can substantially modify charge transfer at solid–liquid interfaces, yet direct spectroscopic evidence for how water ordering reshapes interfacial electronic states remains scarce. Herein, using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), we identify parabolic interfacial states (IFSs) arising with the ordered water structures on Au(111), in striking contrast to the insulating nature of disordered water multilayers. Light exposure induces partial dissociation of H2O, and the resulting hydrated protons combine with residual H2O molecules to form ordered Eigen/Zundel-type hexagonal hydronium-water monolayers on Au(111) at 120–140 K. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations based on Eigen/Zundel-type motifs reproduce the experimentally observed IFSs and indicate that the states derive from the renormalized Au(111) Shockley surface state with a reduced effective mass at the water/gold interface. Annealing-driven transition from the Eigen-type to Zundel-type monolayers is evidenced by the distinct changes in the dispersions of the IFSs. These results establish a band-structure perspective for ordered water/metal interfaces and show that hydrated-proton-introduced excess electrons, when confined at a two-dimensional interface, can reshape the interfacial electronic landscape and charge transport.

articles.title: Magneto-Optical Studies on the Orbital Angular Momenta and Spin–Orbit Coupling in the Excited Triplet States of Octahedral Mo6 Clusters: Magnetic Circular Dichroism and Magnetic Circularly Polarized Luminescence
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The magneto-optical properties─magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) and magnetic circularly polarized luminescence (MCPL)─of octahedral hexanuclear [Mo6I8Y6]2– clusters (1, 2, and 3, possessing OPOPh2, N3, and CF3COO as the terminal Y ligands, respectively) were studied. In their MCD spectra, negative Faraday A terms corresponding to the S0 → Sn transitions were observed at ∼400 nm, reflecting the orbital angular momentum (OAM) and high symmetry of the molecular orbitals (MOs). In their highly concentrated solutions, positive Faraday A terms corresponding to the spin-forbidden S0 → Tn transitions were observed at ∼600 nm due to large spin–orbit coupling (SOC). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first direct observation of the spin-forbidden S0 → Tn transition in metal clusters by MCD. In their MCPL spectra, negative, strong phosphorescent MCPL signals (g ≈ 1.0 × 10–2 at 1.6 T) were observed at ∼690 nm, indicating that these Mo clusters are promising candidates for novel CPL materials. Time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations performed for the model cluster [Mo6I8Cl6]2– could reproduce UV–vis absorption and MCD spectroscopic properties. Especially, the MCD signals were evaluated by analyzing the SOC and the Zeeman effects of the OAM and spin angular momentum in the excited triplet state. TD-DFT gradient calculations indicated the geometrical distortion and stabilization of the lowest excited triplet [Mo6I8Cl6]2– and the destabilization of its Franck–Condon ground state, which explain the large red shift of phosphorescence. These results open new possibilities for understanding and functionalizing metal clusters.

articles.title: Mechanism-Guided Development of Thioacetylene Probes for Chemoproteomic Profiling of Cellular Protein Thiyl Radicals
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Protein thiyl radicals are transient reactive intermediates involved in oxidative stress and enzymatic catalysis. However, their proteome-wide, site-resolved profiling in living cells remains challenging due to the lack of suitable tools. Here, we report chemoproteomic probes enabling covalent capture and site-resolved identification of protein thiyl radicals in living cells. Designed to leverage sulfur-mediated stabilization of a vinyl radical intermediate, our thioacetylene-based probes selectively capture cysteine thiyl radicals while minimizing cross-reactivity with nucleophilic thiolates and nonradical amino acid residues. In vitro validation and live-cell chemoproteomic analysis established radical-dependent labeling and site-resolved detection of protein thiyl radicals. Notably, the probes enabled site-specific mapping of thiyl radical-associated cysteine residues in live E. coli, including Cys439 of ribonucleotide reductase A (NrdA), a canonical enzymatic thiyl radical site. Expanded residue profiling further confirmed cysteine-predominant labeling and detected probe modification at established and putative glycyl radical residues in PflB, NrdD, and YjjI, suggesting that the platform may extend beyond thiyl radicals to other protein-centered radicals. Application of the probe under oxidative and nitrosative stress revealed condition-dependent changes in cellular protein radical-associated labeling, including decreased labeling at established glycyl radical residues and bidirectional changes in cysteine radical-associated labeling. Together, these findings establish thioacetylene probes as a platform for site-resolved mapping and comparative monitoring of endogenous protein-centered radicals in living cells.

articles.title: Optical Access to a Molecular Nuclear-Spin Register in Catalytically Relevant Palladium(I) Complexes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Paramagnetic metal complexes are powerful tools in chemical catalysis and, increasingly, quantum information science, positioning them as ideal tools for quantum sensing within reactions themselves. However, this application requires an interface between spins and light in chemically relevant platforms. Here, we demonstrate that circularly polarized light can generate electron spin coherence in low-symmetry, catalytically relevant Pd(I) complexes. By measuring ultrafast changes in optical polarization with time-resolved Faraday rotation, we optically detect coherent superhyperfine interaction between the Pd(I)-centered electron spin and adjacent 31P nuclei from the ligand at ambient temperature in solution. The electronic origins of this behavior are attributed to excited-state orbital angular momentum through combined spectroscopic and computational analysis, and the optically measured coherence is benchmarked against pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance. Spin polarization is coherently exchanged between the electron spin and initially incoherent nuclear spins, constituting a rare example of optical access to a nuclear spin register in an ambient-temperature, solution-phase molecular system. Both reactivity and quantum spin function are mediated by the bisphosphine ligand; taken together with in situ detection of coherent Pd(I) spin dynamics directly in reaction mixtures, this work moves molecular qubits toward quantum sensing in chemical reactions.

articles.title: Solvent Cage Suppresses Dynamically Induced Entropic Pathways to Provide High Selectivity in Intramolecular Fe-Oxo Radical Rebound Reactions
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: For homogeneous transition metal reactions, it is generally assumed that when intermediates are formed, they are sufficiently long-lived for the surrounding solvent cage to fully equilibrate prior to product formation. However, some transition metal reactions generate a highly reactive and transient intermediate for which product selectivity is not governed by subsequent competing transition states but rather by dynamic effects during descent from the transition state that forms the intermediate. In such reactions, solvent reorganization may be slow relative to product formation, which could significantly impact reaction pathway selectivity. Here, we demonstrate the important role of the solvent cage and explicit solute–solvent interactions in determining pathway selectivity for the ultrafast-evolving radical pair intermediate generated during (PDP)Fe-oxo-catalyzed intramolecular sp3 C–H functionalization. Quasiclassical reactive trajectories showed that with only a continuum solvent model a mixture of oxygen rebound/hydroxylation, desaturation, and direct carboxylate rebound products are formed due to dynamically driven, entropically favored wandering, which is inconsistent with experiments. In contrast, trajectories in explicit solvent reproduced the experimental product selectivity and demonstrated that solvent controls the nonstatistical, motion-driven selectivity by acting as a nonequilibrated solvent cage that restricts access to entropically favorable wandering configurations. The solvent effectively guides the radical pair intermediate toward one dominant product pathway. These results demonstrate the important role of the solvent cage in reactions involving highly transient intermediates where dynamic effects control selectivity.

articles.title: Synergistic Interactions Enable Superior Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity in Compositionally Complex Nanocrystal–Nanosheet Hybrids
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Thiospinel nanoparticles are promising catalytic materials due to their compositional tunability, electronic conductivity, and structural stability. While significant gains in catalysis have been made through material engineering, one continuously developing route is through the use of support materials to enhance performance. Here, we report a simple, scalable, low-temperature method to coproduce colloidal multimetal nanocrystals (<20 nm in diameter) and In2S3-based nanosheets (<1 nm thick), forming compositionally complex hybrid nanocrystal–nanosheet heterostructures in situ. The in situ-formed heterostructures demonstrate enhanced catalytic activity in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in alkaline conditions; peak performance was achieved in heterostructures formed between (Ni,Co,Fe)3S4 nanocrystals and (In,Fe,Mn)2S3 nanosheets with overpotentials as low as 283 mV at 10 mA/cm2. Heterostructures can also be produced ex situ by introducing nanosheets, postsynthetically, to the nanocrystals, reducing the overpotential of (Ni,Co,Fe)3S4 nanocrystals from 362 mV to 312 mV with only a 5 wt % addition. This improvement highlights synergistic interactions in the heterostructures. These results suggest that an optimum nanosheet loading that maximizes effective nanocrystal–nanosheet interfacial coupling while preserving access to the Ni/Co-rich catalytic domains is the relevant design parameter. Our findings provide a low-temperature, colloidal route for synthesizing compositionally complex and highly uniform (<15% dispersity) sulfide nanocrystals, nanosheets, or heterostructures of the two with tunable structures and enhanced electrocatalytic performance. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a compositionally complex hybrid material that is able to enhance performance when formed both in situ or ex situ and the use of In2S3 as a scaffold for a support material for enhancing OER performance.

articles.title: Tailoring Three-Dimensional Porphyrin Hosts to Control Fullerene Recognition and Charge-Separation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Porphyrin–fullerene assemblies are widely regarded as model systems in artificial photosynthesis. However, attaining precise structural control over both fullerene binding and charge-separation behavior within a single, rigid three-dimensional porphyrin host continues to be a significant challenge in supramolecular design. Dihydroanthracene- and triptycene-functionalized tetraarylporphyrins are shown here to act as biconcave aromatic hosts for C60, forming 1:1 and 1:2 complexes with association constants up to 104 to 105 M–1, as evidenced by 1H NMR and fluorescence titrations, and electrospray ionization mass spectrometry. Key in the host design is the porphyrin β,β-substitution that generates a well-defined and encapsulating environment for C60. Triptycenoporphyrins exhibit more geometrically confined C60 binding than their dihydroanthracene analogues, highlighting the critical role of topological control in C60 recognition. Despite identical binding strengths in nonpolar toluene and polar benzonitrile, the corresponding C60@triptycenoporphyrins display pronounced solvent-dependent excited-state behavior. Charge-separated states are generated more rapidly in benzonitrile yet attain significantly longer lifetimes in toluene, as revealed by steady-state and time-resolved spectroscopic measurements. These results demonstrate that tailoring rigid three-dimensional porphyrin frameworks enables simultaneous enhancement of C60 binding and fine control over charge-separation and -recombination dynamics, establishing this scaffold as a versatile platform for artificial photosynthetic systems that require long-lived charge-separation.

articles.title: Unifying Polar and Hydrophobic Models of Ice Recognition by Antifreeze Glycoproteins
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Antifreeze glycoproteins (AFGPs) enable polar organisms to survive at subzero temperatures by inhibiting ice growth through selective association with specific crystallographic planes. However, the molecular basis of this interaction and its remarkable selectivity remain incompletely understood, and both polar and hydrophobic binding models have been proposed. Here, we combine the synthesis of AFGP variants with high-resolution NMR spectroscopy, antifreeze activity measurements, and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the molecular determinants of ice recognition. Minimally perturbative chemical modifications, including site-specific deuteration and fluorination, were used to probe the contributions of nonpolar and polar interactions while preserving the characteristic AFGP conformation. The combined structure–activity relationships and computational analyses support an integrative binding model that provides a unified and parsimonious interpretation of the experimental observations. Within this framework, our experimental evidence is consistent with the view that dispersive interactions involving peptide and carbohydrate methyl groups favor productive association with the ice surface, whereas carbohydrate hydroxyl groups, together with sugar- and backbone-associated water molecules, contribute polar interactions that promote selective and persistent binding. This model reconciles key aspects of previously proposed polar and hydrophobic descriptions and provides a molecular rationale for the characteristic plane selectivity of AFGPs and the conservation of specific sequence motifs. More broadly, our results highlight minimally perturbative isotopic substitution and fluorinated molecular editing as useful chemical strategies for probing weak dispersive contributions to complex molecular recognition processes while preserving native molecular architecture.

articles.title: Zeolite-Confined Triatomic Cu Oxides at Silanol Nests as Hydrogen Transport Channels for H2 Production from Methanol Steam Reforming
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Cu-based catalysts offer high methanol steam reforming (MSR) activity but are limited by unstable Cu+–Cu0 interconversions due to the redox and sintering labilities of Cu. Herein, we developed a universal amino-functionalized “gripper” strategy for firmly and precisely anchoring atomically dispersed metals (e.g., Cu, Co, Ni) within Beta-zeolite. Triatomic Cu oxide (Cu3Ox) sites lower the methanol dehydrogenation activation barrier, and the synergistic interplay with adjacent OH groups from silanol nests accelerates H2 evolution and the MSR reaction. Spatially decoupling Cu-mediated methanol activation from silanol-driven H2 evolution at silanol nests as proton transport channels within the confining zeolite framework also effectively protected Cu from sintering, achieving a high specific activity of 951 molH2·molCu–1·h–1 and over 600 h of stability under continuous regeneration. This work provides a universal strategy for synthesizing atomically dispersed metal catalysts and a new design principle for maintaining the Cu structure during MSR.

This review compares room-temperature exfoliation methods that peel layered crystals into ultrathin sheets, examining their yields, defect levels, and flake sizes. It proposes reporting standards and a decision flowchart to help researchers choose the right method for a given application and highlights hybrid processes, real-time monitoring, and AI-driven optimization as promising routes toward industrial production.

They identify a “super pause” DNA sequence near gene start sites that alone potently pauses RNA polymerase II, trapping it in a yet undescribed “sidetracked” conformation, showing how DNA sequence itself controls pausing.

Layer-Number-Controlled Symmetry Breaking and Surface-State Transport in Rhombohedral Graphene Multilayers
articles.abstract: Rhombohedral multilayer graphene hosts layer-polarized flat bands, providing an intriguing platform for correlated and topological states; however, how layer number governs symmetry breaking and surface screening remains elusive. Here, we prepare rhombohedral graphene multilayers and systematically conduct electrical transport measurements. We uncover an unconventional layer dependence of phase transitions: the critical displacement field Dc for the layer-antiferromagnetic-to-semimetal transitions remains nearly constant across tetralayer to hexalayer graphene, whereas Dc for the semimetal-to-layer-polarized-insulator transition increases with layer number, defying unscreened Coulomb interaction models. In hexalayer graphene, surface-state-dominated transport emerges with Landau levels and resistive peaks predominantly controlled by adjacent gates, revealing strong interlayer screening. High magnetic fields further reveal valley-layer-locked Landau levels and dissipative states associated with interlayer backscattering, highlighting the presence of decoupled surface states. Our findings establish the layer number as a key tuning knob for engineering correlated and topological phases in rhombohedral graphene multilayers.

articles.title: Magnetic Exciton-Based On-Chip Optical Attenuators Using CrSBr
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional magnetic semiconductors, in which excitonic resonances are coupled directly to the underlying spin order, offer a fundamentally distinct route to active photonic functionality unattainable in conventional dielectrics. The van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr exemplifies this class: its sharp excitons exhibit large oscillator strengths and energies that are continuously and reversibly tunable through the magnetic state of the material, producing dramatic field-induced changes in the permittivity. Here, we exploit this magneto-excitonic response to realize compact, magnetically tunable optical attenuators in standard silicon nitride waveguides. We demonstrate up to 2.5 dB/μm continuous attenuation from CrSBr flakes under in-plane magnetic fields below 1 T. We further show that the device response depends nontrivially on the CrSBr thickness through coupled-mode physics with the polarity of the field response inverting between the perturbative and strongly coupled regimes. This work highlights two-dimensional magnetic semiconductors as a promising materials platform for compact, continuously reconfigurable control of guided light.

articles.title: Measurement of Parity-Dependent Energy-Phase Relations in a Potential Artificial Kitaev Chain Utilizing a Transmon Qubit
articles.abstract: Artificial Kitaev chains have emerged as a promising platform for realizing topological quantum computing. Once the chains are formed and Majorana zero modes are braided/fused, reading out the parity of the chains is essential for verifying the non-Abelian property of Majorana zero modes. Here, we demonstrate a transmon-based microwave probe for a four-site quantum dot–superconductor chain based on a Ge/Si nanowire. One end of the chain is incorporated into a superconducting transmon circuit, enabling spectroscopic identification of the chain’s singlet/doublet ground state and thereby inference of its total Fermion parity. We also demonstrate that, for multiple-dot chains, there are two types of 0−π transitions between different charging states: the parity-flip 0−π transition and the parity-preserved 0−π transition. Furthermore, we demonstrate electrostatic tunability of the interdot coupling. This phase-sensitive microwave platform provides a tool for studying complex hybrid superconducting quantum dot systems and for future extended artificial Kitaev chains.

articles.title: Revealing Polar Walls in CsPbBr3: Herringbone Structure and Formation Pathway
articles.abstract: Domain walls in ferroic materials can host nanoscale functionalities absent from the periodic crystal, offering new opportunities to control electronic transport and polarization in semiconductor devices. Metal halide perovskites demonstrate important photophysical properties; however, their ferroic properties remain unclear. Here we discover a hierarchical herringbone network of polar walls within the nonpolar halide perovskite CsPbBr3 comprising ferroelastic twin walls and antiphase walls. Atomic-scale imaging reveals that both wall types comprise nanoscale regions whose inversion-symmetry is broken compared to the surrounding bulk lattice. In-situ heating experiments show that these interfaces form sequentially during symmetry-lowering phase transitions, revealing a different formation pathway compared with ‘conventional’ oxide perovskites. These polar nanowalls, together with their enclosed topology, may impact carrier transport. This reveals a previously unrecognized structural motif in CsPbBr3, providing new insights into their photophysical and optoelectronic behavior.

articles.title: Ultralow Electron Temperature Plasma for Damage-Reduced Processing of High-k/Metal Gate Films toward Vertically Stacked Nanosheet Devices
articles.abstract: In vertically stacked nanosheet devices, repeated plasma-processing steps are required to realize multiple threshold voltages (Vth), but such repeated exposure can accumulate plasma-induced damage (PID) in ultrathin high-k/metal gate (HKMG) stacks. Here, we demonstrate that ultralow electron temperature (ULET, Te < 1 eV) plasma generated using a DC-biased grid suppresses PID by controlling the electron temperature and ion energy distribution function (IEDF). Compared with conventional inductively coupled plasma processing at the same substrate bias (−100 V), ULET plasma reduces the mean ion energy from 131 to 101 eV and reduces the IEDF standard deviation by 44% (from 37.4 to 20.9 eV). Consequently, surface roughness decreases by up to 58%, fluorine incorporation decreases by up to 58%, and HfO2 Raman-band intensities are 1.32–1.81 times those under conventional ICP processing. These results establish electron-temperature control as a key parameter for minimizing PID in HKMG films relevant to vertically stacked nanosheet devices.

articles.title: Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis
articles.abstract: Brown adipocytes (BAs) are thermogenic cells that regulate energy homeostasis, and age-related declines in thermogenesis contribute to cold sensitivity1–5. We previously identified a BA subpopulation with low UCP1 expression (hereafter, BA-L cells) that coexists with the classical, high-UCP1-expressing BAs (hereafter, BA-H cells)6. Here we show that IL-1β secreted by neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby BAs in the BA-L state. Specifically, IL-1β stabilizes hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (H6PD) protein from degradation to ensure the generation of active glucocorticoids, which activate the glucocorticoid receptor (GR, encoded by Nr3c1) and increase the expression of its target gene, regulator of G-protein signalling 2 (Rgs2), thereby suppressing UCP1 expression. Cold exposure reduces IL-1β levels, depending on sympathetic innervation, leading to H6PD degradation and the conversion of BA-L cells to BA-H cells, thereby enhancing UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Rising environmental temperatures trigger the opposite events. BA-specific inducible deletion of Nr3c1 during cold exposure locks these cells in the BA-H state, leading to persistent thermogenesis and increased energy expenditure days after the mice return to room temperature. Notably, IL-1β is elevated in aged brown adipose tissue, resulting in a locked low BA-H/BA-L ratio and cold intolerance. Suppressing GR in aged mice restores the BA-H/BA-L ratio, resumes thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure. Our findings reveal a spatiotemporal neuronal–immune regulation of BA heterogeneity that governs thermogenesis and offers a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms underlying increased cold sensitivity in older individuals. IL-1β from neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby brown adipocytes in a low-UCP1 state; cold temperature reduces IL-1β via sympathetic nerves, leading to transition to a high-UCP1 state and increased thermogenesis, while higher temperatures have the opposite effect.

Projections that include severe drought predict that a majority of the 993 cactus species assessed will see large losses of suitable climatic area: more than 25% of species could lose at least 80% of it by 2100.

articles.title: Earth’s early history told by 3.9-billion-year-old rocks from northern China
articles.abstract: Ancient rocks in northern China reveal that by 3.95 billion years ago, surface-altered oceanic crust had been buried rapidly to depths greater than 50 kilometres and partly melted. This crust was derived from a mantle reservoir that had been left behind when the crust separated from the early mantle as early as 4.3 billion years ago. Zircon crystals found in some of Earth’s oldest rocks suggest that the source rock was once buried about 50 kilometres into the mantle.

articles.title: Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines
articles.abstract: The global transition towards sustainable energy systems has identified tidal power as a uniquely predictable and substantial renewable energy resource1. However, the highly unsteady sea environment subjects turbines to severe hydrodynamic loads, greatly increasing capital and maintenance costs2,3. Large-scale state-of-the-art turbines at present rely on complex, expensive active pitch systems to mitigate these fluctuations. Here we present a reliable, passive alternative: flexible rubber blades featuring chordwise trailing-edge deformation. We experimentally demonstrate that these flexible blades achieve an equivalent total energy yield over simulated tidal cycles compared with rigid blades with active pitch control, while mitigating high-frequency fatigue-inducing load fluctuations by up to one-third. This passive load regulation arises from aeroelastic deformation that flattens blade camber under load, enabling structural robustness without added mechanical complexity. These findings suggest that chordwise-flexible blades can enhance the durability and performance of tidal turbines, offering a promising pathway towards more reliable and cost-effective tidal energy generation. Flexible tidal turbine blades with passive trailing-edge deformation match the energy yield of active pitch-controlled blades while reducing fatigue-inducing load fluctuations by up to one-third, lowering maintenance complexity.

articles.title: Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks
articles.abstract: The scarcity of terrestrial rocks older than 3.9 billion years (Gyr) has hindered our understanding of Earth’s early evolution, fuelling persistent debates on how and when the first continental crust formed and plate tectonics started. At present, the only unequivocally documented >3.9-Gyr-old rocks are from the Acasta Gneiss Complex, Canada1–3. Here we report a 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss from eastern Hebei, North China Craton, in which primary magmatic zircon records elevated δ18O values (average +6.77 ± 0.23‰) and positive εHf(t) values (weighted mean +1.45 ± 0.27). This suggests a low-temperature altered basaltic source that originated from a mantle depleted in the Hadean. In contrast to the low-pressure origin inferred for the roughly 4.0-Gyr-old Idiwhaa unit in Acasta2, the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss reported here exhibits geochemical signatures attributed to a high-pressure origin4. Thermodynamic and trace element modelling demonstrate that its parental magma formed by means of low-degree (8–16%) melting of basaltic crust at >1.6 GPa and 740–820 °C, suggesting rapid burial of (near-)surface-altered oceanic crust to mantle depths along a cool thermal gradient. We propose that this rapid burial was most likely achieved through a transient subduction event. Analysis of a 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss from eastern Hebei, China, reveals a composition suggesting a low-temperature altered basaltic source, that originated from a mantle depleted in the Hadean, was most likely transported to mantle depths through a transient subduction event and partially melted to produce the trondhjemite.

articles.title: Conformationally driven negative chemotaxis in synthetic vesicles
articles.abstract: Chemotaxis—directed movement in response to environmental cues—is fundamental to biological systems but remains rare in artificial systems, where it typically relies on complex catalytic pathways or intricate adaptive designs. The molecular mechanisms underlying artificial chemotaxis are still scarce and poorly understood, posing challenges for the rational design of advanced artificial chemotactic systems. Here we present a minimal polymeric system that achieves negative chemotaxis through intrinsic conformational dynamics, enabling mechanical transduction and directional movement without the need for catalysis or external energy input. Our study uncovers a previously unrecognized molecular mechanism in which hydrophobic membrane domains dynamically reconfigure in response to chemical signals, triggering a cascade of events, from conformational rearrangements to interfacial tension alterations that generate self-sustained motile behaviour. By elucidating the interplay between membrane dynamics, interfacial forces and directional transport, our findings advance the molecular understanding of synthetic systems that emulate cytoskeletal remodelling in biological motility and establish a versatile framework for engineering functional artificial protocells with life-like behaviours. Achieving negative chemotaxis without catalytic designs remains challenging in artificial systems. Now it has been shown that intrinsic membrane conformational dynamics generate interfacial tension gradients, driving polymersomes away from a lactic-acid source without requiring external energy input.

articles.title: Switchable nucleophile-electrophile chemistry enables functional four-electron Li-I2 batteries
articles.abstract: Four-electron iodine redox chemistry offers a high theoretical specific energy of ~1324 Wh kgI−1, yet its practical realization is fundamentally limited by the conflicting demands of rapid I0/I+ oxidation, effective suppression of iodine shuttling, and stabilization of highly reactive I+ species. Here we report a redox-active, Lewis acid/base-tunable phthalimide that resolves these constraints through a single-molecule polarity-switching mechanism. Upon electrochemical oxidation, electrophilic phthalimideδ+ strongly interacts with nucleophilic iodine and polyiodide species, concurrently suppressing polyiodide shuttling and promoting their conversion to I+. The consecutively generated phthalimideδ− acts as a nucleophilic stabilizer for the resulting I+ species. This electrochemically driven polarity switching of phthalimide enables flexible four-electron Li-I2 pouch cells that deliver ~400 mAh gI−1 capacity, a specific energy exceeding 1200 Wh kgI−1, a high cathode-level specific energy ( ~ 883.4 Wh kg(cathode)−1), and stable cycling over 1000 cycles. The successful integration of these cells into wearable wireless charging and motion-sensing systems demonstrates the potential of polarity-switchable iodine chemistry for next-generation flexible energy-storage devices. Iodine multi-electron conversion is crucial for high-performance Li-I2 batteries. Here, authors introduce a polarity switchable phthalimide that promotes I − /I0/I⁺ redox via tunable Lewis acid/base interactions, enabling flexible cells with high capacity and good cycling stability.

articles.title: UMIche: a UMI-centric analysis platform for enhancing molecular quantification accuracy in bulk and single-cell sequencing
articles.abstract: Unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) are widely utilised in RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) technologies to eliminate polymerase chain reaction (PCR) duplicates, thereby improving the accuracy of molecular quantification. However, synthesis errors in UMIs during sequencing often compromise the reliability of UMI counting. While various computational methods have been developed for error correction, the lack of a unified benchmarking and validation framework impedes systematic evaluation and optimisation. Here, we present UMIche, an open-source, UMI-centric computational platform designed to enhance UMI-assisted molecular quantification. Its application to collapsing monomer and homotrimer UMIs across multiple bulk and single-cell sequencing protocols demonstrates effective PCR-duplicate removal. Across a broad spectrum of simulated and experimental datasets with ground truth, most UMI collapsing methods integrated into UMIche perform similarly under low-error conditions, whereas set-cover optimisation and majority voting show greater robustness as the UMI error profile becomes more pronounced. Together, these capabilities enable scalable UMI collapsing, systematic benchmarking, and method development to improve molecular quantification. Errors in unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) can distort molecule counts. Here, the authors present UMIche, a platform for benchmarking deduplication methods, and show that set cover and majority voting are more robust as barcode errors increase.

articles.title: An organic semiconductor-based photocatalyst sheet for overall solar-driven water splitting
articles.abstract: Splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen using sunlight offers a route to renewable fuel, but translating this reaction into systems suitable for industrial implementation remains difficult. Photocatalyst sheets can overcome key limitations of common direct water-splitting approaches (photoelectrochemical devices and photocatalyst dispersions), but existing photocatalyst sheets rely on inorganic semiconductor nanoparticles and processing techniques that can be difficult to scale. Here we show that solution-processed organic semiconductors can form water-splitting photocatalyst sheets by simply tailoring the charge extraction layer beneath the light-absorbing film. A single organic semiconductor active layer (deposited as a bulk heterojunction blend) drives either hydrogen or oxygen evolution depending on its underlying molecular contact, yielding photocathode and photoanode half-cells with well-matched photocurrents. Combining both reactions on one substrate using a microdomain-patterned molecular underlayer affords a photocatalyst sheet that achieves unassisted water splitting under simulated sunlight for over 2 h and generates hydrogen at a stabilized rate of 1.3 µmol h−1 cm−2, which corresponds to a solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 0.1%. Solar water splitting offers a route to renewable hydrogen, but developing photocatalyst sheets from scalable, solution-processable materials remains a challenge. Here the authors use underlayer engineering to build an organic semiconductor photocatalyst sheet that enables unassisted overall water splitting under simulated sunlight.

articles.title: PKA signaling controls ILC3 homeostasis and IL-23-mediated inflammation in the gut
articles.abstract: Group 3 innate lymphoid cells (ILC3s) are tissue-protective lymphocytes that are enriched in the healthy gut and depleted in gastrointestinal disorders. Here we created a single-cell atlas to define how ILC3s respond to distinct stimuli, observing that prostaglandin engages protein kinase A (PKA) to upregulate tissue-protective factors. In contrast, the canonical activator interleukin-23 (IL-23) decreased negative regulators of PKA, including PRKAR1A. Lineage-specific Prkar1a deletion reduced ILC3s and increased susceptibility to enteric infection in mice. PRKAR1A was not required in early life but continuously preserved ILC3 homeostasis in adults by restraining PKA activity. Overproduction of IL-23 was sufficient to reduce PRKAR1A in ILC3s and increase PKA signaling that provoked gut inflammation. Finally, ILC3s from the healthy human intestine expressed PRKAR1A, which was downregulated by IL-23 or in inflammatory bowel disease. These results demonstrate that regulated PKA signaling is essential for tissue-protective ILC3s, while IL-23 drives aberrant PKA signaling to elicit intestinal inflammation. Sonnnenberg and colleagues show that prostaglandin engages protein kinase A (PKA) and sustained PKA activation promotes the depletion of ILC3s. IL-23 can drive aberrant PKA signaling resulting in intestinal inflammation.

Normalized membrane ratio of TROP2 as a predictor of clinical outcomes with datopotamab deruxtecan in non-small-cell lung cancer
articles.abstract: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd)—a trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed antibody–drug conjugate—has demonstrated efficacy in patients with advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ± actionable genomic alterations. However, TROP2 expression by pathologist assessment using conventional immunohistochemistry with visual scoring does not predict response to TROP2-directed antibody–drug conjugates in NSCLC. We developed TROP2 quantitative continuous scoring (QCS)—a fully supervised computational pathology approach that quantifies TROP2 expression in individual NSCLC cells and subcellular components from immunohistochemistry-stained slides. Using QCS to determine TROP2 expression at the tumor cell membrane and cytoplasm, normalized membrane ratio (NMR) was developed (ratio of membrane relative to membrane + cytoplasmic TROP2) in the biomarker-evaluable population of patients with advanced NSCLC in the TROPION-PanTumor01 study ( n = 115). The TROP2 NMR cut-point was optimized and validated in patients with nonsquamous NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations (primary intended-use population, n = 221) in the biomarker-evaluable population ( n = 352) of the TROPION-Lung01 trial. Association with clinical outcomes was assessed. Progression-free survival was longer in Dato-DXd-treated (median 7.2 versus 4.0 months; hazard ratio 0.40, 95% confidence interval 0.25–0.64) but not docetaxel-treated (median 4.1 versus 4.4 months; hazard ratio 0.94, 95% confidence interval 0.59–1.49) patients with TROP2 NMR-positive versus TROP2 NMR-negative samples (treatment by biomarker status interaction P = 0.0098), indicating that TROP2 NMR may be a predictive biomarker for Dato-DXd.

articles.title: The expansion of kinase drug discovery: new targets, platforms and indications
articles.abstract: In the past 25 years, kinase drug discovery has grown into one of the most thriving areas in pharmaceutical research and development. What began as a field dominated by ATP-competitive small molecules has diversified into a broad therapeutic landscape that includes allosteric and covalent inhibitors, activators, proximity-induced modulators, targeted protein degraders and antibody-based therapies, with more than 150 regulatory approvals so far worldwide. In this Review, we provide a comprehensive analysis of the current kinase therapeutic landscape, including more than 2,100 kinase-targeting agents that have entered clinical development in more than 23,000 clinical trials. We cover drug platforms, new targeting approaches, the expanding target spectrum, approvals and clinical trends. Nearly half of the canonical human protein kinases have at least one clinical-stage agent, placing kinases among the most intensively explored drug target classes. Nevertheless, development remains highly concentrated around a small set of blockbuster kinase targets, such as EGFR. We also examine the features associated with successful kinase-targeting agents and causes of agent discontinuations and regulatory withdrawal. Over the past 25 years, kinase drug discovery has been one of the most active areas in pharmaceutical research and development. This article provides a comprehensive analysis of the kinase therapeutic landscape, covering drug platforms, new targeting approaches, the expanding target spectrum, approvals and clinical trends.

The copper catalyst buffers aryl radicals to prolong their lifetime and suppress side reactions, increasing the efficiency of the method.

articles.title: Catalytic enantioselective dual C–H cross-coupling enabled by a radical-buffering strategy

Mechanistic analysis reveals the copper catalyst acts as a buffer for the transient aryl radical intermediate, prolonging its lifetime and suppressing potential side reactions.

articles.title: Association between TyG‑BMI and repeat percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) risk: exploratory stratification by glucose metabolism status
articles.abstract: Most patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) are diagnosed with coronary heart disease (CHD). The triglyceride glucose‑body mass index (TyG‑BMI) has been reported to be associated with CHD. This study aimed to investigate the association between TyG‑BMI and the risk of repeat PCI among post‑PCI patients, with additional exploratory stratification analyses according to glucose‑metabolism status. Data for this study were derived from resident health‑record follow‑up records of Yipeng Community Health Service Center, covering January 2015 to January 2025. Logistic regression models and restricted cubic spline (RCS) were used to evaluate the association between TyG‑BMI and the risk of repeat PCI among post‑PCI patients, with exploratory stratification by glucose‑metabolism status. Logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analyses showed no significant linear or nonlinear association between TyG‑BMI and repeat PCI (OR=0.999,95%CI:0.994 ~ 1.003, P = 0.534; nonlinear χ2 = 0.91, df = 3, P = 0.8223). Stratified analyses by glucose metabolism status also revealed no significant correlation in any stratum(P > 0.05). No independent association between TyG‑BMI and repeat PCI was identified in post‑PCI patients, even within different glucose‑metabolism strata. Relevant findings require further verification in larger prospective cohorts.

articles.title: Colchicine use was associated with reduced all-cause mortality in patients with diabetic gout without prior coronary artery disease: A propensity-matched nationwide cohort study
articles.abstract: Colchicine has been associated with reduced cardiovascular events in secondary prevention, but evidence for primary prevention is limited. We examined the association between colchicine use and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and gout without prior coronary artery disease. From the Korean National Health Insurance Service database, we identified 48,295 patients with diabetes and gout without prior coronary artery disease between 2015 and 2019. We compared 28,964 colchicine users with 19,331 non-users by 1:1 propensity score matching, which produced 17,337 matched pairs. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and nonfatal stroke. The primary composite outcome occurred in 12.52% of colchicine users versus 15.03% of non-users (hazard ratio [HR] 0.71; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.66–0.75; P < 0.001). All-cause mortality was significantly reduced in colchicine users (8.01% vs. 11.07%; HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.53–0.62; P < 0.001). No significant differences were observed for myocardial infarction (HR 1.15; 95% CI 0.96–1.37; P = 0.121) or stroke (HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.81–1.01; P = 0.076). In a landmark analysis at 365 days that addressed immortal time bias, the associations with all-cause mortality (HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.62–0.73; P < 0.001) and with the composite outcome (HR 0.76; 95% CI 0.71–0.81; P < 0.001) remained significant, whereas stroke (HR 0.99; 95% CI 0.87–1.12; P = 0.823) and myocardial infarction (HR 1.15; 95% CI 0.95–1.40; P = 0.144) did not differ between the two groups. In patients with diabetes and gout without prior coronary artery disease, colchicine use was associated with lower all-cause mortality. The reduction in the composite outcome was driven by mortality rather than by myocardial infarction or stroke.

articles.title: Combined monophosphoryl lipid A and alpha-Galactosyl ceramide adjuvants enhance the systemic immune response to intranasal inactivated influenza vaccination in a murine homologous challenge model
articles.abstract: Inactivated influenza vaccines (IIVs) often fail to provide robust mucosal protection, necessitating the development of potent adjuvants for intranasal delivery. This study evaluated a novel adjuvant combination of Monophosphoryl lipid A (MPL), a TLR4 agonist, and alpha-Galactosyl Ceramide (α-GalCer), an NKT cell ligand, to enhance the efficacy of an intranasal inactivated A/PR8 (iPR8) influenza vaccine. In vitro results demonstrated that MPL+ α-GalCer increased the frequencies of CD4⁺ CD25⁺ , CD8⁺ CD25⁺ and CD4⁺ CD69⁺ T cells relative to both the vehicle control and either single adjuvant in splenocyte cultures, whereas in purified dendritic cell and macrophage cultures MPL+ α-GalCer was no more effective than MPL alone. Splenocyte supernatants showed higher elevated TNF- α, IL-2, IFN-γ, IL-4, and IL-13. This pre-activation drove robust allogeneic T-cell proliferation in a mixed lymphocyte reaction, indicating enhanced allostimulatory capacity rather than influenza-specific priming. In vivo, a single intranasal dose of iPR8+ MPL+ α-GalCer elicited high systemic IgG titers and was effective at inducing Th1-associated IgG2a alongside IgG1. Following an LD50-range PR8 challenge, the combined-adjuvant group showed 100% survival, which was not statistically significant and lower lung viral titers at 7 days post-infection. This group exhibited elevated post-challenge lung-associated antigen-specific IgA and a reduced viral burden, which was accompanied by lower inflammatory cell infiltration and cytokine levels. The protection of combination group was accompanied by increased frequencies of ex vivo antigen-responsive CD4+ and CD8+ T cells recovered post-challenge. Our findings suggest that the MPL+ α-GalCer combination enhances innate and adaptive immune responses, providing an effective adjuvant platform for homologous mucosal protection in a murine model.

articles.title: Computational evaluation of chromone–tetrazole hybrids as noncovalent inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 Mpro
articles.abstract: Emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants continue to demand orally tractable, non-covalent inhibitors of the conserved main protease (Mpro). Here, chromone-phenyl-tetrazole hybrids were prioritized using a multiscale computational strategy that connects drug-likeness, binding stability, free-energy ranking, conformational behavior, and quantum-level electronic features. The series showed favorable oral drug-like profiles and low-to-moderate predicted acute toxicity. Among the stable Mpro complexes, M2 displayed the strongest computed affinity (MM/GBSA ΔGbind = −38.8 kcal·mol ⁻ ¹), driven mainly by dispersion with limited desolvation cost, whereas M4 showed the most direct catalytic-dyad engagement through His41/Cys145-supported anchoring. DFT analysis rationalized these complementary profiles: M2 and M4 exhibited narrower HOMO-LUMO gaps (4.00 eV) and higher electronic softness, while ELF/NCI maps revealed heteroatom-centered electron reservoirs and weak intramolecular preorganization. The derived pharmacophore consists of a planar chromone π-platform bearing a carbonyl/phenolic acceptor-donor edge, a para-phenyl spacer for conjugation and hydrophobic occupancy, and a methoxy-tetrazole polar/π-rich head for Glu166/Phe140/His163 anchoring. Overall, M2 and M4 emerge as complementary lead chemotypes for experimental validation and structure-guided optimization against Mpro.

articles.title: Cooperative R&D contracts for power batteries under R&D outcome uncertainty and subsidies
articles.abstract: This paper examines a supply chain comprising a single new energy vehicle manufacturer (NEVM) and a single power battery supplier (PBS), considering government subsidies and R&D outcome uncertainty. An exponential function is employed to characterize R&D outcome uncertainty. The impacts of R&D subsidies and R&D capability on R&D investment, supply chain members, and their expected profits are examined. A comparative analysis of cost-sharing (CS) and revenue-sharing (RS) contracts is conducted. The findings reveal that: (1) R&D investment exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship with R&D capability and a positive relationship with R&D subsidies. (2) Under an RS contract, the expected profits of the supply chain and its members increase with higher R&D subsidies and enhanced R&D capability. Under a CS contract, the expected profits of the PBS and the supply chain increase with higher R&D subsidies and enhanced R&D capability; however, the NEVM’s expected profit exhibits a U-shaped relationship with R&D subsidies and R&D capability. (3) Compared with centralized decision-making, neither contract achieves the centralized benchmark for the supply chain’s expected profit. However, compared with decentralized decision-making, the CS contract increases the PBS’s R&D investment and expected profit; the RS contract increases the PBS’s R&D investment and expected profit as well as the supply chain’s expected profit. Both contracts can only improve the NEVM’s expected profit under certain conditions. These findings provide valuable theoretical insights and practical implications for decision-making by NEVMs, PBSs, and government agencies.
