Moreover, we show that image distinctiveness predicts the flipped relationship between H-ability and FA-ability in both behavior and neural activity, providing a unifying explanation of stimulus-specific memorability.

articles.title: A multi- tissue atlas of age-associated differential transcript usage in mouse reveals predominantly regulatory isoform switching across brain, liver, and adipose
articles.abstract: Alternative splicing is increasingly recognized as dysregulated in the aging process across tissues and affects proteome and other regulatory changes which can be biomarkers of aging. In this study, we aimed to identify differential transcript usage (DTU) and isoforms switch accompanied with functional annotation and structural analysis in mouse brain, liver and adipose tissue during natural aging and Ercc1 knock out mice. Age associated isoform switches affected both coding and non-coding transcript features. Across tissues, 36.5-42.6% of switches altered the predicted coding sequence, 31.2-36.5% involved non-coding alternative arms, and 11-18% involved transcripts encoding an identical protein. We observed overall 3'-UTR lengthening in the brain and shortening in the adipose. A single pan-organ isoform switch event in the gene Ighm, recurs in seven separate tissue samples. BioEMU modeling confirms feasibility for a minority of switches following a seven-fold eligibility cascade; the Cyth1 exemplar shows an intrinsically disordered N-terminal extension that does not change the shared SEC7 and PH domains. Together, these results distinguish age-associated isoform changes as predominantly regulatory in mechanism, with structural consequences restricted to tissue-specific events that form a tractable target for conformational ensemble modeling.

articles.title: A novel behavioral paradigm for characterizing anticipatory postural adjustments in mice
articles.abstract: Voluntary movements perturb the body's equilibrium, and the nervous system limits this disturbance by generating anticipatory postural adjustments (APAs) that redistribute body weight before and during movement. APAs have been characterized extensively in humans and larger animal models, but the absence of a tractable behavioral assay in mice has limited access to the genetic and circuit-level tools needed to investigate their neural basis. Here, we describe a force-plate behavioral paradigm in which freely moving mice stand on four independent load cells, receive an auditory GO cue and initiate locomotion voluntarily without task-specific training. Using force recordings, high-speed video and markerless pose estimation, we show that mice initiate a step with a stereotyped sequence of weight shifts: the center of pressure (CoP) moves anteriorly and then laterally away from the swing side, the swing forepaw and diagonally opposite hindpaw unload, and body weight is carried by the remaining diagonal pair. A single principal component explained approximately 80% of the variance in the average trial, compared with approximately 50% when paw identity was shuffled. Pressure recordings identified rapid swing-forepaw unloading beginning, on average, 87.9 ms before lift-off. Head and ear movement began approximately 200 ms before lift-off, and an operational multimodal estimate placed the interval between the earliest detected postural movement and the onset of forepaw rotation at approximately 160-180 ms. Neuropixels recordings from the pontine reticular nucleus (PRN) and supplementary motor area (SMA), monosynaptic tracing of inputs to reticulospinal PRN neurons, and preliminary cell-ablation experiments identify the PRN as a candidate node in the circuitry supporting anticipatory postural control. This paradigm provides a platform for circuit-level investigation of postural control and its disruption in disease.

articles.title: A protocol for cortical and deep-brain calcium imaging in freely moving mice with the Mini2P system.
articles.abstract: Two-photon calcium imaging has transformed our understanding of neuronal circuit function, yet conventional approaches require head fixation, limiting the study of neural activity during natural behavior. Miniaturized two-photon microscopy (Mini2P) overcomes this constraint by enabling calcium imaging in freely moving animals while preserving the optical single-cell resolution of conventional two-photon microscopy. However, its implementation requires the careful integration of multiple technically demanding procedures, presenting substantial challenges for laboratories adopting this approach. Here, we present a comprehensive, step-by-step protocol for implementing Mini2P calcium imaging in freely moving mice, emphasizing procedures that are unique to or particularly critical for successful implementation of this technique. This protocol covers system preparation and performance checks, optical alignment, field-of-view selection, baseplate installation, and strategies for maintaining imaging stability during microscope attachment and reattachment. We also address behavioral habituation, integration with behavioral tasks, imaging acquisition, quality control, and troubleshooting as a part of an integrated experimental workflow. Representative imaging data acquired through cranial windows in the primary visual and somatosensory cortices, and through a gradient-index lens in the medial prefrontal cortex, illustrate the applicability of this workflow across different brain regions and optical preparations. Designed for adaptation across brain regions and behavioral paradigms, the protocol provides practical guidance for identifying technical challenges and verifying successful implementation. By establishing clear decision points, validation criteria, and troubleshooting strategies at each stage, this workflow aims to improve reproducibility and facilitate the adoption of the Mini2P for investigating neuronal circuit dynamics during freely moving behavior.

articles.title: A ribosome-dependent small-ORF switch controls flagellar gene expression and virulence
articles.abstract: RNA structures are active regulators of bacterial translation. Here, we identified a naturally occurring translation-enhancing small open reading frame (tesORF) that controls the expression of the flagellar operon fliFGHIJK in Salmonella enterica and other motile Enterobacterales. Nucleotide-resolution ribosome profiling revealed this previously unannotated 54-nucleotide ORF immediately upstream of fliF. Genetic, transcriptomic, and biochemical analyses support a model in which tesORF translation counteracts an inhibitory RNA structure, exposing the fliF ribosome-binding site and promoting translation initiation independently of the encoded peptide sequence. Disruption of tesORF translation reduced expression of the downstream operon and impaired motility and virulence-associated phenotypes in Escherichia coli, Salmonella, and Yersinia. Together, our findings reveal how translation of a conserved small ORF regulates an entire flagellar operon through RNA structural remodelling, with consequences expending to the wider flagellar regulon, linking RNA structural dynamics to bacterial motility and virulence.

articles.title: Accessory B Chromosomes Alter Chromatin Accessibility and Gene Expression in Maize Pollen Nuclei
articles.abstract: B chromosomes in maize (Zea mays L.) are supernumerary, nonessential chromosomes that exhibit non-Mendelian inheritance through chromosome drive. During the second pollen mitosis, they undergo nondisjunction, resulting in their preferential transmission via B-containing sperm cells. Although their transmission mechanisms have been extensively characterized, the effects on chromatin organization and transcriptional regulation in gametophytic cells remain poorly understood. Here, we combined flow cytometric sorting of pollen nuclei with an assay for transposase-accessible chromatin sequencing (ATAC-seq) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) to investigate the impact of B chromosomes on chromatin accessibility and gene expression in mature maize pollen. Using pollen nuclei isolated from a maize inbred line B73 carrying zero and two B chromosomes, we generated high-purity datasets suitable for integrated chromatin and transcriptomic analyses. We identified extensive chromatin accessibility and transcriptional activity at B-chromosome loci. Importantly, the presence of B chromosomes was also associated with altered chromatin accessibility and gene expression on the standard A chromosomes, revealing regulatory effects extending beyond the B chromosome itself. Together, these findings contribute to a broader understanding of effects of selfish genetic elements in plants.

articles.title: Advanced meditation stabilizes cortical dynamics through inhibitory gain control linked to absorptive depth
articles.abstract: Advanced meditation can shift conscious experience from ordinary body- and world-centered awareness toward absorption, detachment and dissociation-like states, yet the neural mechanisms that stabilize these immersive states remain unclear. We studied 18 long-term meditators during eyes-open rest and Rajyoga meditation, a practice in which practitioners reduce bodily identification while enhancing inner self-awareness. We combined multidimensional neural approach including frontal EEG spectral power, temporal non-stationarity and corticothalamic neural-field modeling, because these measures probe underlying complementary levels of the brain state transition: the strength of neural activity, its temporal stability, and the circuit level inhibition-excitation gain mechanisms. This framework is especially relevant to meditation because oscillatory, temporal organization may distinguish stable meditative states, and corticothalamic dynamics are closely linked to arousal and conscious state regulation. We correlated meditation induced neural changes with subjective ratings of absorption and dissociation. Compared with rest, meditation was associated with higher beta1, beta2 and gamma power, with no change in the slower bands (delta, theta and alpha), and with lower beta-band temporal non-stationarity, indicating a more stable expression of fast cortical dynamics. Fitting the corticothalamic model to the EEG spectra showed stronger cortical inhibitory gain and lower effective intracortical gain, placing meditation in an inhibition-dominant regime, with lower gain in the loop between excitatory and inhibitory neurons within the cortex. During meditation, these model estimates were related to subjective absorption and showed trend level links with dissociation. Together, these findings suggest that Rajyoga meditation stabilizes cortical dynamics through inhibitory gain control, linking absorption (deep and steady attention on the meditation) to dissociation-like self-detachment.

articles.title: Affordable 96-parallel SPPS: hardware and software add-on for automated liquid handling platforms
articles.abstract: ParSynt-P is a hardware and software add-on that converts a liquid-handling robot already available in a proteomics laboratory (Tecan Freedom EVO) into a parallel plate-format peptide synthesizer for generating libraries of candidate peptide standards for targeted blood plasma proteomics. The manifold is milled from polytetrafluoroethylene and has ports for an inert gas and a vacuum line; a standard commercially available 96-well filtration plate is secured to it with an airtight seal. The software layer generates robot worklists from a table of peptide sequences and controls switching of the N?/vacuum lines, including pulsed gas mixing. The system performs up to 96 syntheses per run, and coupling of one residue takes 94 min. Workability of this 96-well format was verified on three fully loaded plates. The uniformity of synthesis conversion across the plate was measured quantitatively using a characterized NAT/SIL standard pair. The add-on cost $351, while the synthesis cost is $0.23 per coupling and $1.14 per milligram of crude product, an order of magnitude below the market price of custom synthesis.

articles.title: Binding mechanisms of therapeutic antibodies to human claudin-18.2
articles.abstract: Claudin-18.2 (CLDN18.2) is a tight junction component with highly restricted expression in the paracellular space of nonmalignant gastric epithelial cells. It becomes accessible on tumor cell surface during malignant transformation, making CLDN18.2 an attractive target for targeted therapies against gastric cancer. Recently, zolbetuximab has become the first FDA-approved monoclonal antibody that targets CLDN18.2 in advanced gastric cancer, and others like osemitamab have entered phase 3 clinical trials. However, the high-resolution structure of CLDN18.2 is lacking, and how CLDN18.2 is recognized by therapeutic antibodies remains undefined. Here, we report cryo-EM structures of human claudin-18.2 (hCLDN18.2) in complex with the Fab fragments of zolbetuximab and osemitamab, revealing the structure of hCLDN18.2 and its binding mechanism to the therapeutic antibodies. Further analyses reveal that three residues in the first extracellular loop of hCLDN18.2 that are different from human claudin-18.1 (hCLDN18.1) play a critical role in antibody binding. Our data elucidate the structural basis for selective binding of therapeutic antibodies to hCLDN18.2, which should aid rational design of next-generation immunotherapies targeting hCLDN18.2.

articles.title: Biological aging and comorbidities are linked to HIV 1 reservoir size despite suppressive antiretroviral therapy
articles.abstract: Background The HIV reservoir persists in long-living immune cells after antiretroviral therapy initiation. Proviral DNA integrates at preferential host DNA sites, while HIV transcription continues under treatment, with potential biological consequences. Treated people with HIV remain at increased risk for premature aging and non-AIDS comorbidities compared to people without HIV. Whether HIV reservoir size and activity impact health outcomes during treatment remains unclear. Methods We analyzed 1895 people with HIV using antiretroviral therapy from the 2000HIV cohort to study associations between the reservoir and historic and prospective virologic and immunological response markers, comorbidity outcomes and biological aging scores. The reservoir was assessed by quantifying total and intact proviral HIV DNA in circulating CD4+ T cells, along with measures of HIV transcriptional activity, including cell-associated HIV RNA. Results HIV reservoir markers were highly correlating and associated with older aging scores and adverse virologic outcomes, including quantifiable and residual viremia at study entry and during follow-up. Total HIV DNA, unlike the minor fraction of intact HIV DNA, correlated with prevalent cardiovascular disease, subclinical atherosclerotic disease, liver fibrosis and incident malignancies independent of circulating inflammatory markers and lowest CD4 nadir. Total HIV RNA associated with prevalent cardiovascular disease and liver fibrosis. Conclusion The HIV reservoir associated with older aging scores and long-term health outcomes in people with HIV using antiretroviral therapy, independent of inflammation and immune suppression history. Whether reservoir-reducing interventions lower the risk of non-AIDS comorbidities should be studied in people with high reservoir markers. Funding and trial registration ViiV Healthcare; 2000HIV ClinicalTrials.gov number: NTC03994835

articles.title: Boosting Single-Cell Methods Significantly Enhances Cell-type Classification
articles.abstract: Single-cell sequencing drives biological discovery by revealing key cellular processes, cell types, and cell states. Recent technological advances have accelerated atlas-scale data generation across laboratories. With the increasing amount of single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) data, new challenges emerge, including effective batch correction, cell-type annotation, rare cell-type and cell-state detection, as well as biological pathway discovery. Inspired by methods for boosting weak learners such as AdaBoost, here we present a novel paradigm, scBoost, that combines single-cell analysis methods using stacked ensembles to boost task performance beyond that of individual methods. We show that scBoost pretrained on Tabula Sapiens 2.0 dataset performs significantly better than existing methods in cell-type classification on the real-world Human Fetal Heart Map and Plaque Atlas. We also demonstrate that scBoost substantially improves the performance of cell-type classification and ranks at the top of the leaderboard on the OpenProblems benchmark, a standard-in-the-field. scBoost is modular and is adaptive to new single-cell methods, which will enable it to continue to serve as a resource to the community in the future.

articles.title: Catalytic domain-lipid interactions negatively regulate RhoA signaling by modulating conformational dynamics
articles.abstract: RhoA belongs to the Ras superfamily of small GTPases, regulates cytoskeletal actin organization and cell motility, and is implicated in cancer metastasis and neurodegenerative diseases. It is predominantly anchored to the cytosolic side of the plasma membrane (PM) via its prenylated C-terminus, but little is known about its PM organization, dynamics, and lipid interactions. In this work, we used extensive atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and simulations-guided experiments to study the molecular details and functional consequences of RhoA membrane targeting, interactions and dynamics. We found that both GDP- and GTP-bound RhoA adopt a well-defined, stable membrane organization and binding mode irrespective of initial conditions and bilayer lipid composition. RhoA membrane organization is determined by hydrophobic interaction of the prenylated C-terminus with the membrane, and a previously unknown, critical role of electrostatic interactions between cationic residues on the G-domain and N-terminus with anionic lipids in the PM. N-terminal interactions are mediated by a polybasic patch including residues R5, K6, and K7, and substitution of these residues with Ala increased RhoA-mediated F-actin accumulation and effector activation in cells. MD simulations suggest that the triple mutant retains the global membrane organization of wild type RhoA but alters key protein-lipid interactions. Specifically, we observe a loss of cooperative lipid engagement involving the polybasic patch and Switch II residues with amine-bearing lipids, and a rerouting of intra-protein dynamic networks that primes Switch I for effector recognition. These results suggest that the membrane serves not just as a scaffold but also as an allosteric partner of RhoA to fine-tune intra-protein dynamics in a functionally relevant manner.

articles.title: Chaperone mRNA secondary structure does not strongly track thermal adaptation in bacteria, but groL coding sequence shortens in its disordered C-terminal tail
articles.abstract: Ribosomal and transfer RNAs show clear compositional and structural signatures of adaptation to growth temperature, but messenger RNA does not, and the generality of this asymmetry at individual loci remains untested. We asked whether the two principal bacterial chaperone transcripts, dnaK and groL, encode systematically different mRNA secondary structures in thermophiles relative to mesophiles. Using a phylum-matched cohort of 50 bacterial strains (25 mesophiles, 25 thermophiles; balanced across Actinobacteria, Bacteroidetes, Firmicutes and Proteobacteria), we folded each coding sequence at 37{degrees}C and 55{degrees}C and compared fifteen thermodynamic and structural descriptors per gene. Raw folding metrics showed no significant group differences after multiple-testing correction. However, after controlling for dinucleotide composition with Altschul-Erickson shuffles, thermophile sequences, particularly groL, retained modestly more residual secondary structure than mesophile sequences. The strongest and cleanest signal was not structural: groL coding sequences are shorter in thermophiles (mean 1626.5 versus 1636.3 nt; Cliff's {delta} = 0.571, P = 5.1x10-4), a relationship that scales continuously with optimal growth temperature and persists after phylogenetic generalised least squares correction (n = 50, Pagel's {lambda} = 0.997, slope = -0.356 nt{degrees}C-1, P = 6.0x10-5). Protein-level alignment localised this difference: approximately three-quarters of the excess deletion signal falls within the terminal ~25 residues corresponding to the intrinsically disordered, glycine/methionine-rich C-terminal tail of GroEL. Thermal adaptation in these loci therefore appears to act primarily on a disordered peptide extension, with only a modest residual signature detectable in mRNA folding after composition is controlled.

articles.title: Comprehensive Characterization of Somatic Mutations and Gene Expression on TP53/PTEN DKO Murine Glioblastoma Cell Lines: Insights from Whole-Exome and RNA-seq Analysis
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive brain tumor characterized by genomic instability and transcriptional plasticity. To investigate the somatic evolution of GBM, we performed an integrated analysis using Whole-Exome Sequencing (WES) and RNA-seq on a murine glioblastoma model representing two stages: early-stage transformed neural stem cells (tNSC) and late-stage malignant GBM (mGB). The comparative analysis of mutational signatures provides evidence of a two-phase evolutionary path for tNSC and mGB. Variant calling in tNSCs revealed mutations in Pfdn2, Oip5, Trmt10a, Nabp2, Man2b1 with mGBs acquiring additional putative progression-associated genes such as Cdk4, Ubap2, Ccdc11, Errfil, and Tead2 associated with malignancy and Temozolomide (TMZ) resistance. Samples in tNSCs exhibited signatures associated with stress-(SBS4) and development-associated (SBS40) processes. In contrast, mGB samples exhibited an increase inmutation signatures, specifically associated with replication- (SBS5) and mismatch repair (MMR) processes (SBS26). Notably, SBS26 consistently ranked in the top five mutational signatures across all samples, indicating that there may have been an early, and sustained, loss of MMR. Ti/Tv ratio also revealed elevated transversions in tNSCs supporting early instability post TP53/PTEN knockout, while mGB demonstrated normal transition-to-transversion ratio. Gene ontology reveals activities in neurodevelopmental pathways in tNSCs such as neurogenesis, axon guidance, and synapse regulation while in mGB it shifts to cellular transformation and invasion, and epidermal development. Moreover, differential expression analysis showed extreme downregulation against control neural stem cells (ctrlNSCs) indicating genomic instability and then the partial restoration of expression in mGB, resembling ctrlNSCs but with a bias toward malignant upregulations. Together this suggests, early genomic instability disrupting developmental programs and blocking differentiation, and later on replication-driven mutations and cytoskeletal remodeling reprograms the tumor into a proliferative, invasive, and therapy-resistant state.

articles.title: DE-Rigor-Agent: An Agentic Workflow for Assumption-Aware Differential Expression Analysis of Bulk RNA-seq Data
articles.abstract: Differential expression (DE) methods for bulk RNA-seq differ in their statistical assumptions, input data requirements, and supported study designs. Large language model (LLM) agents can automate DE analysis, but they may default to popular methods without checking whether these methods are appropriate for the data. We introduce DE-Rigor-Agent, an assumption-aware agent that organizes DE analysis into three stages: input standardization, method filtering, and method execution. Before executing any DE method, the agent uses expert-curated criteria and dataset-specific diagnostics to evaluate six commonly used methods, documents the reasons for retaining or excluding each method, and executes all retained methods. We evaluated DE-Rigor-Agent on 140 simulated datasets spanning 14 challenging scenarios involving small sample sizes, zero inflation, expression outliers, pre-normalized inputs, and confounded batch effects. Benchmarks showed that method-dataset incompatibilities could lead to inflated false discovery rates (FDRs) or reduced statistical power. Two general-purpose LLM agent baselines, including one explicitly prompted to consider statistical assumptions, selected DESeq2 or edgeR for nearly all datasets. In contrast, DE-Rigor-Agent's filtering decisions closely matched the incompatibilities introduced in the simulations and remained consistent across random seeds, with little additional computational cost. These results demonstrate that DE-Rigor-Agent provides an automated approach to assessing method suitability, making DE analysis more rigorous and transparent.

articles.title: Denaturation-sensitive BRET probes enable intracellular thermal shift measurements across diverse protein targets and biomolecular complexes
articles.abstract: Thermal shift assays have revolutionized drug discovery, but can be limited in sensitivity and scalability. Combining the unique attributes of differential scanning fluorimetry (DSF) and cellular thermal shift (CETSA), we report the methodological framework for the bioluminescence resonance energy transfer shift assay (BRETSA). BRETSA utilizes denaturation sensitive BRET probes, in combination with luciferase-tagged target proteins, to track and longitudinally record thermal shift in living cells. Denaturation profiles were successfully measured for over 500 globular proteins, spanning 24 target families in diverse cellular compartments. Among these, target engagement was confirmed for over 200 proteins; including validated drug targets as well as understudied members of the kinase subfamily. Leveraging orthosteric, allosteric, and covalent ligands in potency studies, this method offers improved sensitivity and scalability compared to other thermal shift methods. We extend the utility of BRETSA to interrogate target engagement at biomolecular complexes and query cooperative binding for molecular glues and emerging tricomplex drug modalities.

articles.title: Desiccation stress enhances virulence potential of group B Streptococcus
articles.abstract: Streptococcus agalactiae (Group B Streptococcus, GBS) asymptomatically inhabits the gastrointestinal and female reproductive tracts but can also cause invasive diseases in susceptible individuals. Despite its clinical importance, relatively little is known about its ability to survive outside the host and whether environmental persistence contributes to transmission and infection. Here we investigate the GBS survival under nutrient starvation and desiccation, characterizing phenotypic and genomic adaptations associated with environmental persistence. GBS remained viable for 30 days during starvation at room temperature and for more than 80 days under desiccated conditions, with GBS grown to stationary-phase bacteria exhibiting greater survival than actively growing bacteria. Survival under desiccation was conserved among several clinically relevant GBS serotypes. Following rehydration desiccated GBS exhibited enhanced biofilm formation compared to control non-desiccated strains. Whole-genome sequencing identified mutations in genes involved in capsule biosynthesis, cell-envelope homeostasis, nutrient transport, and carbohydrate metabolism, suggesting that multiple adaptive pathways may contribute to environmental persistence. Importantly, desiccated GBS retained the capacity to colonize the vaginal mucosa and displayed increased invasion of reproductive tissues in a murine vaginal colonization model. In a systemic infection model, desiccated GBS exhibited enhanced virulence compared to control non-desiccated GBS, demonstrating that environmental survival does not diminish pathogenic potential. This environmental persistence may represent an underappreciated factor contributing to GBS transmission and the epidemiology of late-onset neonatal disease.

articles.title: DiffTernary: a Diffusion Model for Molecular Glue Ternary Complex Docking
articles.abstract: Molecular glues (MGs) modulate protein function by inducing or stabilizing protein interactions. However, accurately modeling MG ternary complexes remains challenging. Here, we present DiffTernary, a diffusion-based docking method for the joint prediction of relative protein arrangement and MG binding pose. We introduce Ternary-PDB, a dataset of 76,702 experimentally determined ternary complexes curated from the Protein Data Bank using structural filters and a release cutoff aligned with AlphaFold 3 (AF3). When trained on this dataset, DiffTernary achieved acceptable protein-protein interaction (PPI) predictions (DockQ > 0.23) for 50.0% of MGBench complexes with a single prediction, compared with 51.1% for AF3. In comparisons with AF3, OpenFold3, ESMFold2, Protenix-v1 and Protenix-v2, DiffTernary ranked second with a best-of-25 PPI prediction success rate of 78.4%, behind ESMFold2 (90.9%) and ahead of AF3 (72.7%). A separate DiffTernary model trained on TernaryDB achieved a mean DockQ of 0.306 on the 94 complexes in the TernaryDB MGD test set with a single prediction, compared with 0.228 for DeepTernary. Confidence-based selection among 40 samples yielded acceptable PPI predictions for 41.5% of complexes, compared with 30.9% for DeepTernary. An E2Former variant increased training and sampling throughput 6.90-fold and 4.37-fold, respectively, under the evaluated configurations. Together, DiffTernary and Ternary-PDB provide an efficient docking approach for MG complex prediction and a valuable structural resource for MG discovery and design.

articles.title: Differential regulation of myeloid Scavenger Receptor A (CD204) expression in humans versus mice in response to sepsis
articles.abstract: Sepsis is the number one cause of mortality in the critically ill patient. The underlying pathophysiology of sepsis is not fully understood. Scavenger Receptor A (SR-A) is a promiscuous receptor of myeloid cells that binds multiple pathogen associated molecular patterns (PAMPs). We have demonstrated that SR-A promotes mortality in murine sepsis. The present study sought to examine the effect of sepsis on myeloid SR-A expression in septic mice and compare it to sepsis patients. Leukocytes were isolated from mice after cecal ligation and puncture. Blood leukocytes were isolated from sepsis patients. Myeloid cells were isolated from healthy mice or human subjects and were treated with PAMPs. Leukocyte phenotype and SR-A expression were determined by flow cytometry. CLP increased SR-A expression when compared to sham operated animals on both neutrophils and monocytes/macrophages. In contrast, SR-A expression was not changed on either neutrophils or monocytes from sepsis patients when compared to healthy control subjects. Treatment of murine neutrophils and macrophages with Pam3CSK4 and treatment of macrophages with LPS increased SR-A expression. Human neutrophil SR-A expression was not altered by any PAMPs, and only treatment with C. albicans glucan increased SR-A expression on human monocytes. Myeloid SR-A expression is increased in septic mice, and this increase plays a detrimental role in the response to sepsis, while SR-A expression is not changed in leukocytes from septic patients and does not correlate with SOFA II scores. Thus, myeloid SR-A expression does not appear to play significant a role in the pathophysiology of human sepsis.

articles.title: Distinct binding modes shape exploitable asymmetries between echinocandin and triterpenoid resistance landscapes in Fks1
articles.abstract: Echinocandins are the first-line treatment for invasive fungal infections and work by inhibiting the fungal {beta}-1,3-glucan synthase Fks1. Recently, a first-in-class triterpenoid Fks1 inhibitor, ibrexafungerp, was approved for clinical use. The extent to which the difference between these drug classes alters the landscape of resistance mutations in Fks1 is unknown. We used deep mutational scanning (DMS) to quantify the effects of all single-amino-acid variants spanning 159 residues across the three canonical Fks1 resistance hotspots and flanking regions in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Drug selections revealed widespread position-specific cross-resistance and differential resistance, including an ibrexafungerp-specific resistance cluster downstream of hotspot 2 that defines a novel triterpenoid-specific resistance hotspot. We defined this as hotspot 4 and redefined the boundaries of the remaining three canonical echinocandin hotspots, based on the mutational landscape of our DMS analyses. Susceptibility testing of individual FKS1 variants of S. cerevisiae and Candidozyma auris strains confirmed conserved class-specific and cross-resistance patterns. Structure-guided ligand placement, molecular dynamics-based simulated annealing, and DMS-informed pose selection linked drug-specific phenotypes to distinct interaction networks, providing a molecular rationale for the observed differential resistance patterns. These data provide a framework for predicting antifungal resistance, informing treatment strategies and future drug design.

articles.title: Distinct input-output relationships between basal forebrain subnuclei underlie heterogeneous cholinergic modulation of the mouse cortex
articles.abstract: The basal forebrain (BF) supports many behavioral functions via its brain-wide projections, which can be recruited independently and task specifically. However, the anatomical underpinnings for this functional heterogeneity are poorly understood. Here, we compared two mouse BF subnuclei, the horizontal diagonal band (HDB) and the substantial innominata (SI), in terms of their anatomical connectivity and functional recruitment. Using anterograde and retrograde tracing, we show that they target largely segregated forebrain regions, but their input comes from a partially overlapping subset of regions. However, many neurons within each region project to just one of the subnuclei, suggesting they can be recruited independently. To test this, we combined optogenetics and widefield Ca2+ imaging and showed that stimulating prefrontal cortical projections to the HDB or SI results in distinct large-scale patterns of cortical activity via a cholinergic mechanism. Our results provide an anatomical basis for the flexible, area-specific cholinergic modulation of brain function.

articles.title: Elevational variation in gut microbial community composition and predicted functional potential across three Himalayan redstart species
articles.abstract: Environmental gradients and seasonal migration may influence host-associated microbial communities, yet their contributions to gut microbiome variation in montane birds remain poorly understood. We investigated gut microbial communities across 1,300 to 4,200 m in three Himalayan redstarts (Phoenicurus fuliginosus, P. leucocephalus, and P. frontalis) exhibiting contrasting seasonal movement strategies. Using 16S rRNA gene sequencing of 46 fecal samples, we characterized microbial diversity, community composition, distance decay relationships, co-occurrence networks, and predicted functional potential. Elevation was significantly associated with microbial community composition, explaining approximately 3% of variation, whereas host species showed no significant association after accounting for elevation. P. fuliginosus exhibited significant compositional differences among most sampled elevations, whereas P. leucocephalus showed significant positive distance decay relationships. Alpha diversity showed no consistent elevational trend, while core microbial taxa and co-occurrence networks varied among elevational groups. PICRUSt2 analyses identified 28 predicted KEGG Level 3 pathways differing significantly among elevations, including pathways associated with amino acid, lipid, glycan, carbohydrate, and bile acid metabolism. Together, these findings highlight elevation as a significant correlate of gut microbial community composition and predicted functional potential, with distinct patterns of microbial turnover among closely related Himalayan redstarts.

articles.title: Establishment of split-TurboID in Plasmodium falciparum facilitates identification of a PfAlba2 protein interaction network during late blood stage development
articles.abstract: Malaria parasites of the genus Plasmodium undergo complex multi-host lifecycles that require precise regulation of gene expression. Unlike model eukaryotes, Plasmodium spp. genomically encodes a limited repertoire of canonical transcriptional regulators, but possess a substantial complement of RNA-binding proteins (RBPs), highlighting the importance of post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms in regulating parasite gene expression. Among these RBPs are a family of DNA/RNA-binding proteins termed 'Alba' (acetylation lowers binding affinity) of which six have so far been identified in these parasites. Here, we investigated the localisation, functional importance and molecular associations of P. falciparum Alba protein PfAlba2 using two different endogenously tagged parasite lines. Using a GFP-FKBP tagged line, we demonstrated that PfAlba2 is expressed throughout asexual blood stage development and primarily localised in the cytosol. Conditional mislocalisation experiments indicated that PfAlba2 contributes to normal parasite growth. To overcome challenges in generating a miniTurboID proximity labelling line, we established a custom split-TurboID proximity labelling system for use in P. falciparum to characterise the PfAlba2 proxiome during asexual blood stage development. The split-TurboID system facilitated identification of 101 enriched PfAlba2 proximal proteins in schizont stage development, with significant enrichment for proteins involved in translation initiation, including two additional Alba family members, PfAlba1 and PfAlba4. Complementary RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing (RIP-seq) identified 380 PfAlba2-associated transcripts with significant enrichments including cytosolic ribosomes, rRNA-processing factors, PfAlba1, and egress and invasion-related transcripts (PfRALP1, PfRON4, PfRH1, PfRH5). Together, these findings implicate PfAlba2 in RNA metabolism and translational regulation, suggesting an important regulatory function for this protein during parasite blood stage development.

articles.title: Evolutionarily distinct dengue virus type 2 with a unique type-specific neutralization determinant
articles.abstract: Dengue viruses 1-4 (DENV1-4) mostly circulate in endemic cycles involving humans and Aedes mosquitoes. However, rare dengue outbreaks originate from non-human primates. These spillovers are caused by sylvatic virus genotypes that are closely related to endemic strains of the same serotype, but some are caused by strains that fall between the four canonical serotypes on phylogenetic trees. It is not clear whether these genotypic differences are reflected in corresponding antigenic differences. Here, we characterized the antigenic features of QML-22, a divergent strain most closely related to DENV2. On an antigenic map, QML-22 clustered with other globally representative DENV2 strains. QML-22 was not as well neutralized by antisera raised against endemic DENV2 and was better neutralized by antisera from DENV1, 3, and 4 infections than other strains of DENV2. QML-22 had a cluster of distinct amino acid residues in domain I of the envelope (E) protein, with only scattered point mutations elsewhere in the envelope. A potently neutralizing anti-DENV2 antibody that targets this site in domain I of the E protein, 3F9, had >1000-fold lower neutralization of QML-22 than other endemic DENV2 strains, whereas other cross-reactive and DENV2-specific antibodies neutralized QML-22 and endemic strains to similar titers. When antisera from non-human primates infected with QML-22 or DENV2 reference strain S16803 were depleted with the heterologous virions, homologous neutralization was unaffected but heterologous neutralization was reduced, suggesting homologous neutralization was due to distinct epitopes. Evolutionary analyses showed the 3F9 epitope was under relaxed selection pressure compared to other neutralizing epitopes and that QML-22 had unique amino acids in this epitope relative to the likely common ancestor of all DENV2. These findings provide insight into the antigenic diversification of DENV and the possible evolution of new serotypes.

articles.title: Exploring subacute effects of a DMT and harmine meditation retreat on the brain's control energy landscape
articles.abstract: Modeling the brain as a controllable structural network allows the estimation of the control energy (CE) required to reach functional states, where low-CE states are more accessible. Psychedelics are thought to acutely flatten the brain's CE landscape, broadening the repertoire of reachable states, but whether this reorganization persists into the subacute ``afterglow" window is largely unknown. This exploratory study uses rs-fMRI from a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (N = 39; 19 verum [N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT) + harmine, Ayahuasca-inspired formulation], 20 placebo) scanned before and after a three-day meditation retreat. We compute CE on a group human connectome project (HCP) structural connectome under two approaches that emphasize long and short timescale dynamics. Globally, we found no systematic shift in the distribution of CE between transitions, however mean CE increased in both groups at the long timescale approach. Surviving network effects emerge when a network's intrinsic timescale matches the stabilization regime. In the long timescale regime, the central executive network (CEN) showed an increase in post-retreat CE within the verum group that survived Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR-BH) correction. Although CE and functional connectivity are distinct, this higher CEN cost may relate to the reduced within-network connectivity previously reported subacutely after psilocybin. The default mode network (DMN) also showed a post-retreat CE increase in both groups, but neither change survived FDR correction. In the short timescale approach, the visual network (VN) showed a FDR-BH CE decrease within the verum group, consistent with reduced dynamical demand in a region acutely engaged by DMT. To examine whether changes were concentrated in less accessible states, we additionally analyzed rare brain states, defined by the top decile of information content. This analysis revealed a modest session x condition interaction in the long timescale approach. Overall, the two timescale lenses surface different network effects, that align with cortical timescale hierarchies. These findings point to network- and timescale-specific, rather than global, CE changes in the afterglow window, though effects are small and heterogeneous and require confirmation in larger samples. Characterizing whether and where psychedelic effects persist into the subacute window is relevant to psychedelic-assisted therapy, including safety, therapeutic timing, and durability of drug effects. More broadly, considering cortical timescale hierarchies may help identify network-specific CE changes that might be less apparent when networks are evaluated under a single dynamical timescale.

articles.title: Fast Pangenome Matching Statistics in Compressed Space with Move Structures
articles.abstract: Matching statistics and supermaximal exact matches (SMEMs) are key inputs for sequence homology search and classification. Methods such as MONI, PHONI, and ropebwt3 compute these statistics using compressed pangenome indexes, but are substantially slower than methods that compute approximations of matching statistics, such as pseudo-matching lengths (PMLs). PMLs can be computed quickly in a single pass, but SMEM computation can require overlapping forward or backward passes over the query. We present ms2, a suite of algorithms that use "move structures" to compute matching statistics and SMEMs efficiently in compressed space. Our four algorithms compose move structures for the LF, {Psi}, {varphi}, and {varphi}-1 permutations with additional longest common prefix (LCP) array summaries and samples. The algorithms offer different tradeoffs among speed, index size, and support for reporting SMEM offsets. They inherit the move structure's fast, constant-time operations and achieve high throughput by leveraging the move structure's locality of reference. Thanks to recent advances, move structures can be constructed in optimal time and compressed space, including the LCP information needed for "match recovery" during SMEM computation. On 100 haplotypes of human chromosome 22, ms2's fastest algorithm computes matching statistics 35 to 48 times as fast as PHONI's online approach, while using an index of similar size. On the 472-haplotype HPRC2 pangenome and human reads, three ms2 modes achieve speedups of at least 22, 19, and 15 times over ropebwt3, whose index is about 15% the size of ms2's fastest mode. When additionally reporting SMEMs and their offsets, ms2 achieves speedups of 25 to 34 times over ropebwt3. Together, these advances enable online computation of matching statistics and SMEMs at a throughput that supports real-time processing of approximately 21 PromethION nanopore flow cells on a single thread. The ms2 software is open source and available at https://github.com/langmead-lab/ms2. It builds on the open-source TeraTools suite (https://github.com/ucfcbb/TeraTools) and Orbit library (https://github.com/drnatebrown/orbit). Experimental scripts and other details are described in: https://github.com/langmead-lab/ms2-experiments.

articles.title: Functional characterisation and identification of a core interactome of Plasmodium regulatory protein Alba4
articles.abstract: Plasmodium spp. parasites have complex lifecycles that rely on strict regulation of gene and protein expression. Current evidence suggests that P. falciparum has a relatively limited repertoire of canonical transcriptional regulators and RNA interference (RNAi)-associated small RNAs compared to model eukaryotes, potentially reflecting a greater reliance on RNA binding protein (RBP)-mediated post-transcriptional regulation (PTR). Among these RBPs, the acetylation lowers binding affinity (Alba) family of DNA/RNA-binding proteins has been implicated in RNA metabolism and regulation of mRNA stability and translation. In Plasmodium spp. parasites, the Alba family has expanded to include up to six members, with sequence divergence and structural modifications beyond the conserved Alba domain leading to diversification of family members, some of which appear restricted to Plasmodium and related parasites. In this study, we were unable to truncate PfAlba4, but successfully generated an endogenously tagged PfAlba4 parasite line, representing the first successful instance of endogenous tagging of a PfAlba family protein. Utilising this transgenic line, we confirm ubiquitous expression throughout blood stage development and its predominantly cytosolic localisation. Conditional loss of PfAlba4 through the knock-sideways approach demonstrated an important role for PfAlba4 in blood stage development and proteomics analysis defined a protein interaction network of 67 significantly enriched proteins, with notable enrichment of proteins potentially involved in RNA processing and regulation. Further characterisation of one of these proteins, the uncharacterised protein PF3D7_0706500, revealed a partially overlapping network of proximal proteins enriched for RNA-regulatory factors, suggesting potentially shared roles in PTR. RNA Immunoprecipitation-Sequencing (RIP-seq) identified 692 PfAlba4 associated transcripts, with an enrichment of a pyrimidine-rich motif in their 3' untranslated regions, suggesting a potential sequence-dependent mechanism of RNA recognition. Integration of proteomic and RIP-Seq datasets in late blood stage parasites revealed a consistent association with RNA processing and regulatory pathways, implicating PfAlba4 in post-transcriptional regulation. Together these findings establish PfAlba4 as an important component of the RNA-regulatory landscape in P. falciparum and highlight the importance of PfAlba proteins for malaria parasite blood stage development.

articles.title: Genome-wide diversity across 130 years reveals drastic post-bottleneck genetic erosion in a recovering population of golden eagles (Aquila chrysaetos)
articles.abstract: Many wild populations have experienced severe human-induced declines, but the genetic consequences of such bottlenecks are often poorly understood. In Finland, as well as in many other countries, golden eagles were heavily persecuted during the 19th-20th centuries, disappearing from southern regions and reaching their lowest population size in the 1950-1960s. Although conservation efforts facilitated demographic recovery, the long-term genomic consequences of the bottleneck remained unknown. Here, we used whole-genome sequencing data spanning 136 years to evaluate patterns of genetic diversity in 26 Finnish golden eagles before, during, and after the mid-20th century bottleneck. We found substantial loss of genetic variation, including an 82% reduction in genome-wide heterozygosity, a 42% decline in nucleotide diversity, a 67% reduction in Watterson's theta, and a substantial loss of variable sites. Analyses of the site frequency spectrum and Tajima's D confirmed historical population contraction, and runs of homozygosity analysis indicated elevated post-bottleneck inbreeding. These results indicate strong genetic erosion in Finnish golden eagles despite the census size recovery. Therefore, incorporating genomic indicators in conservation monitoring and performing regional assessments are necessary to guide management and preserve biodiversity in line with the Global Biodiversity Framework's goal of maintaining genetic variation.

articles.title: HIV broadly neutralizing antibody precursor maturation induced by mRNA vaccination in nonhuman primates
articles.abstract: The induction of broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) is a principal goal of prophylactic HIV vaccines. For many bnAbs, priming ultrarare precursors from the naive B cell repertoire is the first major immunological hurdle. Previous studies have shown that the germline-targeting (GT) priming immunogen N332-GT5 delivered as adjuvanted protein to non-human primates (NHPs) activates bnAb precursor B cells for the human bnAb BG18 targeting the V3-glycan supersite on the HIV envelope (Env) glycoprotein. Here, we engineered N332-GT6 to improve binding affinity to diverse BG18-class precursor naive B cells by 9-fold. mRNA-LNP vaccines expressing N332-GT5 or N332-GT6 as membrane-bound (gp151) trimers were evaluated for their ability to prime BG18-class precursor B cells in NHPs across three related studies. Although N332-GT5 gp151 mRNA-LNP priming induced BG18-class precursor B cells in most animals after two vaccinations, the higher-affinity N332-GT6 gp151 induced responses more consistently after only one immunization. Sequential vaccination with two heterologous mRNA-LNP booster immunizations drove affinity maturation and induced BG18-class memory B cells capable of binding wildtype HIV Env. Together, these findings demonstrate that mRNA immunization can achieve GT priming, boosting, and early maturation of ultrarare bnAb-class B cells in NHPs.

articles.title: Heat-killed Latilactobacillus sakei D279 Attenuates Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Intestinal Inflammation and Barrier Disruption
articles.abstract: Intestinal barrier dysfunction and excessive inflammation contribute to the pathogenesis of various metabolic and gastrointestinal diseases. Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) induces systemic and intestinal inflammation, disrupts epithelial tight junctions, and impairs intestinal barrier integrity. Although heat-killed Latilactobacillus sakei D279 exhibits antiviral activity, its effects on intestinal barrier function remain unclear. In this study, we examined whether heat-killed D279 preserves intestinal barrier integrity and attenuates LPS-induced inflammatory responses in vivo (LPS-challenged mice), ex vivo (mouse peritoneal macrophages), and in vitro (IEC-6 intestinal epithelial cells). Cytokine and receptor gene expression in macrophages was measured to evaluate inflammatory responses. Furthermore, barrier function was assessed using transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER), and the expression of tight junction-related genes was assessed. D279 alleviated LPS-induced intestinal injury in LPS-challenged mice, as indicated by the attenuation of colon shortening and histopathological changes compared to those in the LPS control group. In peritoneal macrophages, D279 pretreatment suppressed LPS-induced expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-, IL-1{beta}, and IL-12{beta}), increased IL-10 expression, and reduced LPS-induced upregulation of MLCK expression. This postbiotic increased basal cell viability in a concentration-dependent manner in IEC-6 cells. Moreover, it enhanced epithelial barrier development (increased TEER) and upregulated tight junction gene expression. These findings demonstrate that heat-killed D279 primarily confers its benefits by attenuating LPS-induced cytokine responses, limiting the upregulation of MLCK expression, and partially preserving goblet cell abundance. This is consistent with its protective postbiotic role in intestinal homeostasis. Thus, this study introduces a candidate postbiotic for the promotion of intestinal resilience under systemic inflammatory stress.

articles.title: Hepadnavirus tropism determined by diversified NTCP functionality in Feline species
articles.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) exhibits a narrow host range, largely determined by sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptides (NTCP), a hepatic bile acid transporter acting as the HBV receptor. NTCP among animals appears to have evolved following trade-off mutations to lose its viral receptor activity while preserving its transporter function. Here, through profiling of the NTCP homologs from 23 mammalian species, we uncover unexpected functional heterogeneity of feline NTCPs. NTCPs derived from cat, tiger, and leopard supported viral preS1 binding and HBV infection, whereas lion-NTCP was deficient for preS1 binding and, notably, exhibited markedly reduced bile acid transport. Cat-NTCP was further demonstrated to have viral receptor function by productive infection in primary cat hepatocytes. Experimental mutagenesis identified double substitution at positions 191 and 268 as key determinants: introducing lion-type substitutions into cat-NTCP (G191R and T268A) abolished preS1 binding, whereas reciprocal substitutions in lion-NTCP restored receptor function. Molecular dynamics simulations suggested that lion-NTCP adopts conformation in which a transmembrane helix bending enlarges the whole bile acid tunnel and disrupts preS1 compatibility. Such differences also determined host susceptibility to another feline-infected domestic cat HBV. These findings reveal diversified NTCP functionality with evolutionary plasticity that acquires resistance to hepadnavirus infection at the expense of physiological transporter function.

articles.title: Herbivore and carnivore microbial signatures indicate diet and health variation in human gut microbiota
articles.abstract: Diet is a key factor shaping gut microbiota in mammals, with herbivores and carnivores harboring distinct microbial communities. However, despite humans being highly omnivorous, it remains unclear whether their gut microbiota more closely resembles that of herbivores or carnivores or how individual-level variations along this spectrum are associated with human health status. We compared gut microbiota profiles of 858 samples from 109 mammalian species and constructed a Herbivore-Carnivore (HC) index based on bacterial groups characteristic of each diet. The HC-index positioned humans between herbivores and carnivores and showed that traditional hunter-gatherers and nonhuman apes retained herbivore-leaning profiles, whereas urbanized humans exhibited a shift toward a carnivore-leaning state. By applying the HC-index to >72,000 participants across multiple cohorts worldwide, we found that elevated HC-index values were associated with plant-based and fiber-rich diets, greater microbial diversity, enhanced potential to degrade plant-derived carbohydrates, favorable clinical measures, and lower prevalence of self-reported disease. We demonstrated that the HC balance of gut microbiota captures a conserved diet-related gradient across mammals and provides an interpretable framework linking human diet, microbial function, and health.

articles.title: Hyperactivation of Mincle in exacerbated apical periodontitis in an autoinflammatory mouse model for cherubism
articles.abstract: Aims: To examine the role of Mincle, a C-type lectin (Clec) pathogen recognition receptor (PRR), in exacerbated apical periodontitis (AP) in an autoinflammatory mouse model for cherubism (CBM). Methodology: Patients with immune system dysfunction have higher prevalence of AP but the mechanism remains largely unknown. We studied a knock-in (KI) mouse model carrying a Sh3bp2 mutation for CBM. We performed pulp exposure in one lower 1st molar of 5- to 6-week-old mice to introduce pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMP)-induced endodontic infection. We determined the expression levels of Clec subfamily genes by qPCR. To suppress Mincle, we generated Sh3bp2+/+Mincle+/+, Sh3bp2+/KIMincle+/+, and Sh3bp2+/KIMincleKO/KO mice or injected Sh3bp2+/KI mice with a Mincle-binding DNA aptamer (AptMincle). Mice were analyzed 42 days after pulp exposure by micro-CT (mCT), qPCR and immunoblotting. Statistical analysis was performed by one-way ANOVA followed by post-hoc analysis with Tukey’s test or two-way ANOVA followed by Sidak correction. p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: Expression of Clec4e (Mincle) was significantly increased in Sh3bp2 mutant mice after pulp exposure compared to WT littermates (p<0.0001). Sh3bp2+/KIMincle+/+ and Sh3bp2+/KIMincleKO/KO mice had a comparable response to pulp exposure, including the degree of bone loss and induction of inducible NOS (iNOS), IL-1b, and TNF-a. Sh3bp2+/KI mice injected with AptMincle after pulp exposure for 21 days showed significant amelioration of bone loss compared to mice with vehicle injection (p<0.0001). Conclusions: These seemingly conflicting data of suppressing Mincle by crossing with Mincle KO mice and AptMincle injection suggest that Mincle has dual functions upon PAMPs stimulation, consistent with a previous study showing that Mincle enhances tissue destruction during the inflammatory stage and is subsequently needed for inflammation resolution. Fine-tuned suppression of Mincle significantly reduces the severity of AP in Sh3bp2+/KI mice. This study suggests that patients with CBM may benefit from more frequent dental examinations and early intervention to reduce or prevent severe progressive bone loss in periapical tissues.

articles.title: Hyperglycemia-responsive circRNA drives diabetic neuropathic pain by competing for PUM2 binding and promoting proNT3/CCL2 in DRG neurons
articles.abstract: Diabetic neuropathic pain (DNP), one of the most common and debilitating complications of diabetes mellitus (DM), remains poorly managed by conventional analgesics, highlighting the urgent need to explore its etiology-associated mechanisms. Here, we identified a novel conserved circular RNA, cRps6kb1, that is significantly upregulated in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons across multiple mouse models of type 1 DM and type 2 DM, as well as in human donors with DNP. Blocking cRps6kb1 upregulation attenuated the increases in DRG neurotrophin-3 mRNA (Nt3), its encoded proneurotrophin-3 (proNT3), and downstream C-C chemokine ligand 2 (CCL2) expression, as well as the persistence of nociceptive hypersensitivity under the conditions of streptozotocin-induced type 1 DM or high-fat diet-fed type 2 DM. Conversely, mimicking cRps6kb1 upregulation increased DRG Nt3, proNT3, and CCL2 levels and produced DNP-like symptoms in naive mice. In addition, high glucose increased the expression of cRps6kb1 and Nt3 in cultured DRG neurons from mice and human donors. Mechanistically, upregulated cRps6kb1 competed with the Nt3 3'-untranslated region (3-UTR) for the translational repressor PUM2 binding, releasing PUM2 from the Nt3 3-UTR and enhancing Nt3 mRNA translation and stability. Thus, cRps6kb1 is a key contributor to DNP and represents a promising therapeutic target for its treatment.

articles.title: Inferring chromatin looping interactions from microscopy-based measurements: opportunities and pitfalls
articles.abstract: Chromatin looping plays essential roles in several nuclear processes and live-cell microscopy has become a key method for studying how chromatin loops behave in time. Extracting dynamical parameters including looping probability, lifetime, and search time from live-imaging data requires inferring looping events from noisy 3D distance trajectories. By analyzing polymer simulation data with known ground truth, we show that with realistic localization precision, the common method of simple thresholding on 3D distance measurements can result in severe misestimation of looping probability, lifetime, and search time. We use simple statistical considerations to show that inference from simple thresholding becomes infeasible when localization error is comparable to the size of the interaction to be studied. Finally, we demonstrate how noise-aware methods can be used to estimate looping parameters more accurately in these regimes.

articles.title: Learned associations constrain anticipatory visual dynamics and enhance sensory and motor readiness to facilitate perceptual decisions
articles.abstract: Learned cue target associations can guide attention to facilitate perceptual decision making, yet how they shape the content and dynamics of neural activity, and whether this facilitation reflects anticipatory preparation, post-target sensory enhancement, or both, remains unclear. Here, we used magnetoencephalography while participants made living/nonliving judgments about visual objects (e.g., cat/violin) with left- or right-hand button presses. Cue category associations were established through repeated pairings: predictive cues always preceded one target category, whereas uninformative cues preceded both categories equally often. Predictive cues facilitated behavioral responses despite limited explicit awareness of the learned associations. Representational similarity analysis showed that prediction preactivated target-specific representations in the visual cortex resembling target evoked activity before target onset. Prediction also elicited anticipatory, response specific motor beta suppression. Together, these findings supported anticipatory preparation, with little evidence of enhanced posttarget visual specificity. Posttarget visual specificity and anticipatory motor preparation independently predicted response speed, with hierarchical drift diffusion modeling linking greater visual specificity to faster evidence accumulation and stronger motor preparation to shorter nondecision time (a model parameter reflecting sensory encoding and motor execution). Beyond representational content, prediction also constrained the evolution of anticipatory visual population activity, and more constrained, stable early visual trajectories predicted faster responses. These population dynamics were associated with faster evidence accumulation, lower decision thresholds, and shorter non-decision time. Together, these findings suggest that associative memory facilitates perceptual decisions by shaping the content and dynamics of anticipatory neural activity, with partially dissociable contributions from visual processing and motor preparation.

articles.title: Local goodness-of-fit measures for neural decoding
articles.abstract: State-space models are widely used to relate neural activity to internal states that cannot be observed directly, but assessing whether a given model is appropriate for a dataset remains difficult. Current approaches, such as cross-validation, summarize model fit across an entire recording. They can reveal that a model is imperfect, but not when during the recording it fits poorly. We therefore lack tools for targeted model refinement. Here, we develop local goodness-of-fit measures that ask whether each spike is consistent with the model's prediction based on all preceding spikes. Each spike, through the tuning of the neuron that fired, points to a range of likely states, just as the prediction does. A spike that narrows a broad prediction is consistent with it; one that points to states the prediction considers unlikely is not. Because the comparison needs only the prediction and the states each spike points to, it also applies to models that decode from unsorted spike waveforms. Using simulations in which model errors are known, we show that two consistency measures, based on the overlap of high-probability regions and on predictive checks, flag such inconsistent spikes, whereas the standard Kullback-Leibler divergence also flags spikes that merely narrow a broad prediction. We then apply the measures to a hippocampal recording from a rat performing a spatial foraging task. In these data, a model assuming continuous movement is expected to fail during immobility, when the hippocampal representation can jump to distant locations, so we compare it with a model that also allows such jumps. As expected, the overlap measure flags more spikes during immobility than during movement under the continuous model, and allowing jumps removes most of the continuous model's flags. The consistency measures thus show when during a recording a state-space model fits poorly, providing tools for its targeted refinement.

articles.title: Long-read analysis of complete human 5S rDNA arrays reveals a zoned organization with two-state unit methylation linked to chromatin architecture
articles.abstract: Despite the fundamental importance of the 5S ribosomal DNA (rDNA) to all cellular life, the landscape of its units by position along its array has remained poorly understood. Here, recent telomere-to-telomere long-read sequencing is used to resolve 5S rDNA arrays from flank to flank and to follow the state of each unit along single molecules. The array is zoned at both the sequence and the epigenetic level. Notably, methylation is bimodal at the level of the unit, and the combination of low-methylation and high-methylation units gives rise to the overall methylation pattern of the array. Moreover, the average number of low-methylation units remains relatively constant regardless of array length. Chromatin fiber sequencing (Fiber-seq) data further show that low-methylation units are more accessible, have lower nucleosome occupancy and are more frequently footprinted at the TFIIIB-binding site, consistent with analyses of ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq data from cell lines. Across species, this pattern is shared among apes, whereas other species show diverse patterns. These results provide a unit-resolved view of the human 5S rDNA array and reveal a zone-specific organization of unit methylation that is associated with chromatin architecture.

articles.title: Male-specific genome sequences for non-invasive sex identification in Nishikigoi (Cyprinus carpio)
articles.abstract: Nishikigoi, ornamental cultivars of the common carp ( Cyprinus carpio ), are economically valuable aquaculture teleosts in which mature females command significantly higher market prices due to superior body conformation and coloration. Consequently, early and non-invasive sex identification is highly desirable for commercial breeding. Although sex determination in common carp follows an XX/XY system, sex-chromosome-specific markers and field-applicable diagnostic methods for Nishikigoi have remained limited. In this study, we conducted sequence-based bulked segregant analysis using whole-genome shotgun sequencing of female and male pools in Kohaku, a representative Nishikigoi lineage. We identified male-specific candidate contigs and successfully developed PCR-based male-specific markers. Validation across multiple Nishikigoi varieties and wild common carp demonstrated that primary primer pairs achieved high diagnostic accuracy. Comparative genomic analysis revealed that these candidate contigs mapped to the genomic region on chromosome 25B containing the male-determining gene Pangu , with the primary marker located in immediate physical proximity to the gene. To enable field diagnostics, we combined non-invasive epidermal mucus DNA extraction, loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP), and chromatography-printed array strip (C-PAS) technology, establishing a rapid on-site detection workflow. Overall, this study provides highly reliable PCR markers associated with the sex-determination locus and establishes a non-invasive, field-applicable diagnostic platform to streamline commercial Nishikigoi breeding and sex-selected stock management.

articles.title: Maternal E-Cigarette Exposure Exacerbates Neonatal Ischemic Brain Injury Through the miR-30c-5p-Neurod1 Axis
articles.abstract: Background: Neonatal ischemic stroke is an important cause of mortality and long-term neurological morbidity in infants. Maternal smoking and e-cigarette exposure are recognized risk factors for adverse neonatal outcomes, but the mechanisms underlying increased susceptibility to ischemic brain injury remain unclear. This study investigated whether dysregulation of the miR-30c-5p-Neurod1 axis contributes to this susceptibility. Methods: Pregnant rats were exposed to e-cigarette aerosols from embryonic day 4 to 20. Studies were conducted in male offspring on postnatal day 10. Baseline molecular changes were assessed using microRNA sequencing, quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction, Western blotting, RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC) and luciferase reporter assays. Ischemic injury was evaluated following transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO). Flow cytometry and molecular analyses were performed to characterize associated cellular changes. The effects of in vivo miR-30c-5p mimic administration, Neurod1 knockdown, and miR-30c-5p inhibition were also investigated. Results: Maternal e-cigarette exposure increased tMCAO-induced infarct size and was associated with increased apoptosis and senescence-associated changes, together with reduced expression of markers of neurogenesis and synaptic development. Under baseline conditions, microRNA profiling and molecular analyses revealed increased miR-30c-5p expression and decreased Neurod1 mRNA and protein levels in the neonatal brain. RISC and luciferase reporter assays supported an interaction between miR-30c-5p and Neurod1 mRNA. In vivo administration of a miR-30c-5p mimic reduced Neurod1 expression and increased infarct size, whereas Neurod1 knockdown independently exacerbated ischemic injury and associated cellular changes. Conversely, inhibition of miR-30c-5p restored Neurod1 expression, reduced infarct size, and ameliorated associated pathological changes. Conclusions: Maternal e-cigarette exposure is associated with baseline dysregulation of the miR-30c-5p-Neurod1 axis and increased susceptibility to neonatal ischemic brain injury in male rats. These findings suggest that this regulatory axis may contribute to the effects of prenatal e-cigarette exposure on the developing brain and may increase susceptibility to neonatal ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Multi-Structure Segmentation of Type B Aortic Dissection from CT Images with U-Net
articles.abstract: Type B aortic dissection (TBAD) is a life-threatening condition in which a tear in the intimal layer separates the aortic wall into a true and a false lumen. Assessment of the lumen, the intimal flap, and false-lumen thrombosis from CT images is important for risk analysis and treatment planning. This work applied U-Net-based deep neural networks to the automatic segmentation of these structures in TBAD. We collected 46 CT scans from 20 patients, with voxel-wise annotations of three structures: the aortic lumen, the intimal flap, and the thrombus. We explored four models: two convolutional networks, nnU-Net 2D and 3D, and two transformer-based architectures, TransUNet 2D and 3D. We observed that (1) for both nnU-Net and TransUNet, the 3D models outperformed their 2D counterparts on all three structures. The difference was small for the aortic lumen but large for the thin flap and the thrombus. The best model, nnU-Net 3D, reached a DSC of 93.05% for the lumen, 50.22% for the flap, and 69.94% for the thrombus. (2) The intimal flap was the most difficult structure for all models. Even the best 3D models showed large thrombus boundary errors in a few scans. These results provide a baseline for developing more advanced models for accurate segmentation of these structures in TBAD.

articles.title: NON-NUCLEOSIDE REVERSE TRANSCRIPTASE INHIBITORS BLOCK THE INCORPORATION OF VIRAL GLYCOPROTEINS INTO HIV-1 VIRIONS
articles.abstract: Non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs) are a key component of antiretroviral therapy that block reverse transcription in newly infected cells. NNRTIs have also been reported to induce premature activation of the HIV-1 protease in virus-producing cells, an activity that has been optimized in a class of NNRTIs known as targeted activators of cell kill (TACK). In this study, we used the TACK compound Pyr01 to investigate how NNRTI-induced premature protease activation affects virion composition and infectivity. We found that Pyr01 treatment markedly reduces the incorporation of the HIV-1 envelope (Env) glycoprotein into virus particles in an Env cytoplasmic tail-independent manner. Pyr01 treatment also disrupts the virion incorporation of foreign viral glycoproteins and causes a substantial loss of the viral enzymes from virions. Virions produced from NNRTI-treated cells exhibit reduced membrane order. The defect in viral glycoprotein incorporation requires an active protease, implicating premature protease-mediated disruption of the Gag lattice and resulting changes in membrane properties as the primary mechanism underlying these effects. These findings reveal that NNRTI-induced premature protease activation during virus assembly fundamentally changes the protein composition and membrane order of HIV-1 virions to markedly reduce particle infectivity. These results have implications for the use of TACK compounds therapeutically and provide basic insights into the properties of the viral membrane that promote viral glycoprotein incorporation.

articles.title: Necroptosis is a targetable driver of severe coronavirus pathogenesis
articles.abstract: Human-pathogenic coronaviruses differ dramatically in pathogenicity but the underlying mechanisms are incompletely understood. Here, we demonstrate that highly pathogenic coronaviruses trigger necroptosis in the infected cells and lung tissues, whereas necroptosis is not detected in cells infected by seasonal coronavirus. Mechanistically, highly pathogenic coronaviruses produce Z-RNA, activate ZBP1 and initiates necroptotic cell death signaling, triggering necroinflammation and lung injury. In contrast, seasonal coronaviruses produce little to no Z-RNA, and do not activate necroptosis. Importantly, small-molecule inhibition of necroptosis attenuates inflammatory cytokine expression and markedly ameliorates lung damage in mice infected with all three highly pathogenic coronaviruses, independent of virus clearance. Overall, our study identifies necroptosis as a dominant mediator of coronavirus pathogenesis, and positions necroptosis blockade as a new therapeutic target against severe coronavirus diseases.

articles.title: Neuropathological assessment of cerebrovascular integrity in Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy
articles.abstract: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy neuropathological change (CTE-NC) is defined by perivascular deposits of phosphorylated tau, with lesions preferentially located at sulcal depths. We investigated whether CTE-NC is associated with structural changes to perivascular spaces (PVSs) or microvascular degeneration. Post-mortem middle frontal gyrus tissue from 11 CTE-NC cases and 11 age-matched controls was examined using immunohistochemistry. All CTE-NC cases exhibited pathognomonic lesions in this region. We quantified PVS width along with vessel lumen and PVS area, string vessel burden, pericyte density, and aquaporin-4 (AQP4) polarisation to the astrocytic endfoot. Total PVS width did not differ significantly between the groups in grey matter (P = 0.543) nor white matter (P = 0.468). Neither PVS area (sulcal depth, P = 0.097; gyral crest, P = 0.645) nor PVS-to-lumen area ratio (sulcal depth, P = 0.454; gyral crest, P = 0.307) differed significantly. Similarly, there were no significant differences in total microvascular length (p = 0.693), string vessel burden (p = 0.128), pericyte density (p = 0.589), or AQP4 endfoot enrichment (p = 0.538). We therefore found no evidence of large-scale PVS enlargement, lumen narrowing, capillary degeneration, pericyte loss, or altered AQP4 endfoot enrichment in CTE-NC at the locations and spatial scales investigated. Taken together, these findings suggest that the pathognomonic perivascular tau lesion is not associated with a classical small vessel degenerative phenotype in CTE-NC. However, that does not exclude more subtle molecular, functional, or ultrastructural changes at the interface between vessels, the perivascular space, and surrounding brain tissue.

articles.title: OligoFragger: spectrum graph-guided analysis of modified RNA oligonucleotides by mass spectrometry
articles.abstract: RNA modifications are widespread modulators of RNA function, but comprehensive identification remains technically challenging. This is especially true for densely modified RNAs such as tRNAs, where multiple modified residues and many possible chemistries occur within short sequence contexts. Tandem mass spectrometry provides direct chemical and positional evidence for modified oligonucleotides, but current database-search strategies struggle when dozens of candidate modifications must be considered simultaneously. Here, we present OligoFragger, a spectrum graph-guided computational tool that uses fragment evidence to constrain modified-oligonucleotide searches before full database scoring, enabling rapid and robust oligonucleotide identification. Using controlled RNA samples and tRNA datasets from E. coli and human cells, we demonstrate that OligoFragger increases identifications under stringent FDR control while recovering known modification patterns and supporting label-free quantification. This strategy enables sensitive, FDR-controlled identification and label-free quantification of modified RNA oligonucleotides in complex epitranscriptomic search spaces.

articles.title: PAMP: Continuous-to-Discrete Mutation Projection for Enzyme Engineering
articles.abstract: Efficient enzyme engineering requires translating quantitative turnover predictions into specific mutations that im- prove catalytic activity while reducing experimental search.
