Here, we demonstrate a multifunctional ITO/SnP2S6/Ti memristive neuron that combines reproducible volatile resistive switching and integrate-and-fire dynamics under electrical-pulse stimulation with wavelength-selective photoresponses and short-term optoelectronic synaptic plasticity. Leveraging these experimentally measured device characteristics, we construct a multimodal neuromorphic recognition framework that integrates volatile memristive neurons with programmable memristive synapses. Inspired by the parallel processing of visual features in the primate visual system, structural and color information are independently encoded and processed through separate electrical and optical pathways before being integrated for classification. Importantly, inference is implemented using experimentally measured neuronal firing statistics and programmed synaptic conductance states, rather than idealized device models, thereby establishing a direct link between device characteristics and system-level functionality. As a proof-of-concept, the framework is evaluated on a fruit-recognition task using a subset of the Fruits-360 image data set, achieving a classification accuracy of 94.9% through multimodal fusion and substantially outperforming recognition based on either modality alone. These results establish SnP2S6 memristive devices as a versatile platform for integrating electrical and optical neuronal functionalities and highlight their potential for hardware-realistic multimodal in-sensor neuromorphic computing.

articles.title: Attempts to Understand and Manipulate the Orientation and Retention of Peptides Inside Nanopores Expand the Toolbox for Nanopore-Based Proteomics
articles.abstract: Nanopore techniques have emerged as promising tools for deciphering complex proteomics from the single-molecule level by profiling individual peptides. The entry orientation of a peptide and its subsequent retention inside the nanopore are crucial for the analytical results but remain challenging to be properly defined, which limits the sensing capability of nanopore-based proteomics technology. Here, we propose that electrically driving peptide entry into α-hemolysin nanopores against opposing electroosmotic flows is a promising platform to guide the polypeptide with a preferential orientation. α-Hemolysin mutants with opposite ion selectivity have been engineered and employed to measure peptides at pH 3.8 and at alkaline pH exceeding 10.0. The impact of peptide charge distribution on the orientation has been investigated by simulating the peptide dipole moment and electrophysiology measurements. In addition, the retention position of the peptide has been altered by introducing tryptophan residues at position 125 within the β-barrel region of α-hemolysin, which increases the sensitivity for specific peptide region and enables the detection of initially inaccessible monomethylation modifications. Thus, we present a rational framework to investigate and manipulate the orientation and dwelling position of peptides inside the α-hemolysin nanopore, which can enhance our capability to profile polypeptides by using nanopore techniques.

articles.title: Biomimetic Nanozyme-Decoys Reprogram Immune Niches to Intercept Colitis-Carcinoma Transition
articles.abstract: Colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC) arises from chronic inflammatory niches characterized by persistent oxidative stress and dysregulated immune cell recruitment. Current anti-inflammatory therapies provide only transient symptom relief and fail to prevent malignant progression due to their inability to simultaneously mitigate oxidative injury and immune chemotaxis. Our analysis of clinical samples revealed markedly elevated C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 2 (CXCL2) in intestinal tissues from patients with inflammatory bowel disease and CAC, implicating the CXCL2-CXCR2 (C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 2) axis in driving excessive neutrophil and macrophage infiltration and fostering tumorigenesis. Herein, we report a biomimetic nanozyme (PB@ECM) that reprograms inflammatory immune niches to intercept CAC progression. PB@ECM integrates a Prussian blue nanozyme core with genetically engineered macrophage membranes, enabling concurrent scavenging of reactive oxygen species through superoxide dismutase- and catalase-like activities and sequestration of CXCL2 via membrane-displayed CXCR2 receptors. In murine models of colitis and CAC, PB@ECM significantly alleviated intestinal inflammation, suppressed neutrophil and macrophage infiltration, and effectively inhibited colitis-carcinoma transition. Notably, treatment with PB@ECM significantly prolonged survival compared with other groups. By disrupting the pathological crosstalk between oxidative stress and immune chemotaxis, this work establishes a biomimetic nanozyme strategy for preventing inflammation-driven carcinogenesis.

articles.title: Breaking the Capacity–Stability Trade-Off in High-Voltage LiCoO2 via Opposite Co/O Redox Activity
articles.abstract: LiCoO2 (LCO) suffers from daunting capacity–stability trade-off due to deeper Co oxidation and ensuing O oxidation (O2– → Co4+ electron transfer) at high-voltage (≥4.5 V). Aggressive Co4+ and O2/On– (0 < n < 2) species result in pronounced mechanical/chemical failure and fast capacity decay. Most of the state-of-the-art solutions partially resolve these problems yet sacrificing capacity. Herein, facilitated Co3+/4+ redox and effectively restrained O redox are simultaneously achieved by amplifying Co t2g electron density of states (DOS) near the Fermi level while reducing O 2p electron DOS. Consequently, the engineered cathode harvests a remarkable initial capacity of 212.1 mAh g–1 at 4.6 V (vs 212.9 mAh g–1 of bare LCO). Moreover, advanced multiscale X-ray/electron spectroscopy and imaging techniques reveal that mitigated O redox prevents irreversible phase transitions, lattice O loss, and undesirable surface parasitic reactions. As a result, the cathode has reinforced electrochemical (capacity retention of 88.4% within 330 cycles at 5C) and thermal stability thanks to fatigue-free (de)lithiation channels, less new-generated Co3O4 layer, and inorganic-rich cathode/electrolyte interphase (CEI) film. This work provides a valuable inspiration for the electronic structure engineer of robust LCO cathode toward high operation voltages.

articles.title: Bright Alkyl Quantum Defects Govern Early Carbon Nanotube Pharmacokinetics in Mice
articles.abstract: Fluorescent quantum defects in single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) are a major advance in nanocarbon research, owing to their bright, single-photon emission at telecom wavelengths and versatile conjugation chemistries for biomedical sensing and disease targeting. Here, we introduce an efficient, oxygen-free sonochemical route that generates long-chain alkyl defects, simultaneously shortening nanotubes and producing a bright, homogeneously emissive (6,5) SWCNT ensemble. Among 15 screened reactants, the branched-chain NiaproofⓇ 4, which molecular dynamics simulations show packs more densely and uniformly than linear surfactants, yields a 3.4-fold brightness enhancement and a sharp emission peak near 1108 nm. Single-particle spectroscopy reveals J-aggregate emission redshifts at high defect densities, and fibrinogen titration shows defect chemistry governs protein-driven coating displacement. Using a home-built short-wave infrared imaging system (25 mW cm–2, 989 nm excitation, 1150 nm long-pass collection), we show that these sparse defects (∼9–16 μm–1) drive different pharmacokinetics between NiaproofⓇ 4– and lipid-PEG–functionalized (6,5) at early time points, converging as protein-corona formation masks the underlying chemistry. Histology localizes the nanotubes within macrophages of mononuclear phagocyte system–associated organs. Intravenous administration (∼41 μg kg–1) causes no acute toxicity and a short ∼2-day retention. The NiaproofⓇ 4 group exhibits a reduced circulating myeloid-cell fraction following corona formation, which may reflect organ recruitment and sequestration, while the accompanying increase in CD3+ T cells may partly reflect a proportional shift in leukocyte composition.

articles.title: Charge-Induced Formation and Field-Driven Directional Motion of Vacancies in a Two-Dimensional Halide
articles.abstract: Controlling defect evolution in two-dimensional (2D) materials is essential for reliable nanoelectronic functionalities, yet selectively inducing defect formation and externally driven migration remains a key challenge. Here, we demonstrate two distinct mechanisms governing halogen vacancy formation and migration in a PbBr2 monolayer on highly ordered pyrolytic graphite using low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy combined with density functional theory calculations. We show that halogen vacancies reshape the local density of states and electrostatic potential beyond the immediate defect site. Crucially, electric fields and charge injection mediate distinct atomic-scale responses: tip-induced electric fields drive directional vacancy migration and coalescence, whereas charge injection from the tunneling current induces vacancy formation, with enhanced efficiency when coupling to shallow defect states. These results demonstrate that direct electrical stimuli can drive both vacancy motion and creation in a two-dimensional, predominantly ionic material system. Our findings establish a framework linking defect-induced electronic structure, local electrostatics, and externally driven atomic rearrangement under conditions relevant to device operation.

articles.title: Data-Driven Atomic Interplay Modulation Enables Dual-Functional High-Entropy Alloy Mediator for Li–S Batteries
articles.abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) have emerged as appealing candidates to achieve performance regulation in Li–S batteries. Nevertheless, the design principles and working mechanisms of HEAs for dual electrodes remain elusive because of their structural disorder and chemical complexity. Herein, we propose a data-driven maneuver to enable rapid and precise screening of a customized HEA nanocatalyst (FeCoNiCuVMn, 6E-HEAs) via a performance-oriented theoretical criterion in the realm of Li–S electrochemistry. The delicate modulation of atomic interplay in 6E-HEAs simultaneously accelerates sulfur redox kinetics and stabilizes lithium metal deposition. Consequently, Li–S batteries sustain favorable cycling performance at 1.0 C over 1000 cycles while affording a capacity decay rate of merely 0.067% per cycle. The pouch cell harvests a specific capacity of 884.8 mAh g–1 at 0.5 C with steady cyclic operation. Our study elucidates crucial roles of effective compositional gain in boosting bidirectional Li–S electrocatalysis, offering atomic-level insights into HEA design for electrocatalytic reactions.

articles.title: Overcoming Oral Environmental Barriers: Nanoengineering Strategies for Antimicrobial Peptides in Biofilm-Associated Oral Diseases
articles.abstract: Biofilm-associated oral diseases impose a substantial global health burden and are closely linked to systemic inflammation. Although antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) offer a promising alternative to conventional antibiotics, their therapeutic efficacy in the oral cavity is limited by barriers in the oral environment. Free AMPs are rapidly removed by salivary flow, destabilized by local proteases, and impeded by substantial diffusion barriers within mature biofilms. Nanoengineering provides a systematic approach to address these limitations. In this review, we present a barrier-oriented framework for AMP delivery and examine how nanomaterial design addresses the specific constraints of the oral environment. Interfacial engineering prolongs local retention, spatial protection preserves AMP stability, and microenvironment-responsive systems provide on-demand activation for effective biofilm disruption. Alongside these approaches, multifunctional nanosystems combining antimicrobial, immunomodulatory, and regenerative activities are discussed. Finally, key translational challenges, including biosafety, microbiome homeostasis, manufacturing, and regulatory barriers, are critically examined. This review traces the development of AMP nanoengineering from passive delivery vehicles toward precision therapeutic platforms that respond dynamically to the oral microenvironment.

articles.title: Self-Assembly of Two-Dimensional Open Structures with Adjustable Square Voids
articles.abstract: Self-assembly of anisotropic particles offers a powerful route to design materials with tailored microstructures. Here we investigate two-dimensional systems of patchy hard rectangles using Monte Carlo simulations and free volume theory, mapping their phase diagram across packing fractions and interaction strengths. Low attraction recovers excluded-volume phase behavior (isotropic–tetratic–smectic), while intermediate attraction strengths feature a broad isotropic–smectic coexistence region. For high interaction strengths our theory predicts, and simulations confirm, a highly ordered “weaver” phase characterized by a four-rectangle unit cell that forms a regular grid of square voids. Although the pure weaver phase forms only in a narrow window of packing fractions, it coexists with either the isotropic gas or smectic solid over a wide range of packing fractions. Patchy rectangles demonstrate how shape together with tunable interactions can be utilized to self-assemble porous materials with precisely adjustable void sizes and geometries and could be realized using DNA origami structures.

articles.title: Truly Asynchronous and One-Hot Constraint Probabilistic Potts Computing with Floating-Body Metal–Oxide–Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistors
articles.abstract: This work presents a truly asynchronous physical Potts node (TAPPN) using floating-body metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistors (FB-MOSFETs) to overcome the scalability and encoding overhead limitations of binary Ising-based probabilistic computing. The TAPPN enables native multistate representation without external random-number generators (RNGs) or complex digital arbitration by the intrinsic stochastic single-transistor latch (STL) effect and a drain-sharing configuration. The stochastic source and the one-hot constraint are realized by three transistors, and the node requires 25 transistors and 220 nW including the readout, compared with 2160 transistors and 52 μW for a self-contained digital node evaluated at the same boundary. Its truly asynchronous operation allows efficient exploration of the problem space in large-scale graph-coloring benchmarks. In simulations of the update rule, the Potts-based system achieves a higher success probability than simulated annealing (SA) and parallel tempering (PT) on graph-coloring benchmarks. For an integrated array assumed to operate at 5 MHz, the architecture is projected to reach a time-to-solution (TTS) of 3.4 μs and an energy-to-solution (ETS) of 504 nJ. This platform establishes a complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS)-compatible pathway toward large-scale, multistate combinatorial optimization.

articles.title: Ultrafast High-Photogain UV–Vis-NIR Broadband Photodetection in Parallelly Overlapped Stacking Type-I GaSe/MoTe2 Heterostructure
articles.abstract: Broadband photodetectors are important for next-generation optoelectronic applications, ranging from fundamental science, environmental monitoring, industrial detection to artificial-intelligence-enabled Internet of Things systems, where both high responsivity and fast response are critically demanded. Typically, a trade-off exists between the two in the photogating effect, making it challenging to achieve both simultaneously. This study reports a parallelly overlapped stacking GaSe/MoTe2 heterostructure with type-I band alignment (PSH-GM), which simultaneously realizes an ultrafast photoresponse of 523 ns and a high responsivity of 8.95 × 103 A·W–1, together with a noise equivalent power of ∼0.38 × 10–14 W·Hz–1/2 and a specific detectivity of 8.01 × 1011 Jones. Furthermore, PSH-GM exhibits a responsivity of up to 103 A·W–1 over a broad spectral range of 355–1100 nm, covering the ultraviolet (UV), visible (Vis), and near-infrared (NIR) regions. The underlying photodetection mechanism of the parallelly overlapped stacking type-I heterostructure is clarified using photocurrent mapping, and the origin of the dark current shift at different operation frequencies is elucidated, both of which offer insights into the design principles of two-dimensional heterostructures optimized to simultaneously achieve high responsivity and high response bandwidth. Imaging demonstrations are conducted at 355, 520, and 850 nm, and free-space optical communication is demonstrated at 115.2 kbit·s–1, which highlights the potential of PSH-GM for broadband UV–Vis–NIR photodetection, ultrafast data communication, high-speed imaging, and integration into advanced optoelectronic systems.

articles.title: Ultrafast Imaging of Dynamic Disorder in Superionic Chalcocite
articles.abstract: The optimal functionalities of matter often appear at emergent structural orders involving entangled changes in the lattice structures and the underlying atomic degree of freedom. Here, we report laser-induced, thermally driven dynamic structural orders evolving in the low- to high-chalcocite transition of copper(I) sulfide using time-resolved electron diffractometry in ultrafast electron microscopy. We filmed the complete phase trajectory of the transient atomic motions and the hierarchical decoupling of structural orders that unfold over time. Moreover, a transient, disordered state is unveiled. The disordered state emerges during the superionic diffusion of copper ions along a few-nanometer-thick lattice channels. Temporal gating of the various combinations of structure could expand the range of accessible functional states in matter.

articles.title: In situ multimodal X-ray imaging and crystal plasticity study of the intragranular stress and orientation distribution during necking in ductile deformation
Characterizing Fill Factor Limitations in Perovskite‐Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Monolithic perovskite‐silicon tandem solar cells have achieved power conversion efficiencies approaching 35%. However, a significant gap remains to their thermodynamic limit, primarily due to fill factor (FF) losses. This work presents a methodology to identify the underlying mechanisms of the losses. Electroluminescence characterization reveals the potential FF without series resistance losses but cannot fully explain the observed FF limitations. An additional loss mechanism is the photoshunt, a phenomenon which the parallel shunt resistance apparently reduces under illumination in perovskite solar cells. Using an analytical model, we show that the photoshunt originates from competition between charge extraction, governed by transport‐layer properties and electric field, and recombination in the absorber and at interfaces. An equivalent circuit model quantifies its impact on subcell and tandem FF. Additionally, the two‐diode property of the Si subcell can also influence the tandem FF losses. Measurements on tandem devices under spectrally independent LED illumination show that photoshunt losses can be hidden under bottom‐cell‐limited conditions, explaining the preference for slightly bottom‐cell‐limited tandem designs. Reducing the photoshunt through improved charge transport and reduced recombination could enable operation closer to current matching while minimizing FF and efficiency losses.

articles.title: Competitive Solvation Structure in a Deep Eutectic Electrolyte Enables High‐Voltage LiCoO2‐Based Pouch Cells With 5000‐Cycle Stability
articles.abstract: Anion‐rich solvation structures improve interfacial stability but often impede Li+ desolvation, limiting fast‐charging and low‐temperature performance in high‐voltage lithium metal batteries. Unlike conventional high‐concentration or weakly solvating electrolytes, we propose a deep eutectic electrolyte (DEE) using succinonitrile (SN) and dimethyl sulfone (MSM) with competitive coordination capability. This design shifts the Li+ solvation from aggregate clusters (AGGs) to a balanced AGGs/contact ion pairs (CIPs) distribution, which lowers the Li+ desolvation energy barrier, enhances the transport kinetics, and endows the DEE with an ionic conductivity of 3.87 mS cm−1 and a Li+ transference number of 0.81. MSM moderates excessive SN coordination, suppressing parasitic reactions on the anode, thereby enabling stable Li plating/stripping for 6800 h. A lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI)/lithium difluoro(oxalato)borate (LiDFOB) dual‐salt system further optimizes interfacial chemistry, yielding a bilayer solid electrolyte interphase comprising an inorganic‐rich inner layer and a flexible organic outer layer. LiCoO2||Li cells retain 97.1% capacity after 1000 cycles at 5C (3.0–4.5 V) and operate stably at −10°C. A 3.0 Ah LiCoO2||Li pouch cell further delivers a high energy density of 417 Wh kg−1, and LiCoO2||graphite pouch cells sustain long‐term durability over 5000 cycles. This competitive solvation strategy effectively harmonizes kinetics and interfacial robustness for high‐voltage, fast‐charging DEEs.

articles.title: Dual Metal Dopants Advance Near‐Room‐Temperature PbS‐based Thermoelectrics
articles.abstract: Low-cost lead sulfide (PbS) exhibits poor near-room-temperature (300–573 K) thermoelectric performance, limiting its practical applications. Here, Se/Te alloying coupled with dual-metal Zn/Ge co-doping is employed to enhance the near-room-temperature thermoelectric performance of n-type PbS. Se/Te alloying forms a single-phase PbS0.5Se0.35Te0.15 solid solution (PbS(Se/Te)), where alloy-induced mass and strain fluctuations enhance phonon scattering, reducing the lattice thermal conductivity from ∼2.09 W m−1 K−1 for PbS to ∼0.75 W m−1 K−1 at 300 K without compromising electrical transport. Zn/Ge co-doping further optimizes carrier transport by regulating lattice defects and tuning carrier density, achieving a high carrier mobility of ∼522 cm2 V−1 s−1 and an optimized carrier density of ∼1.03 × 1019 cm−3. The optimized PbS(Se/Te)+0.6‰Zn+5‰Ge sample exhibits an enhanced power factor of ∼20.23 µW cm−1 K−2 at 300 K, yielding a ZT of ∼0.54 at 300 K and an average ZT of ∼0.80 over 300–573 K. A seven-pair thermoelectric module achieves a maximum temperature difference (ΔT max) of ∼33.4 K at T h = 343 K, and a single-leg device reaches a peak conversion efficiency of ∼7.2% under a temperature difference of 300 K. These results highlight the potential of Zn/Ge co-doping for advancing n-type PbS-based materials toward near-room-temperature cooling and low-grade heat recovery.

articles.title: Efficient H2O2 Photosynthesis With Valorization by X‐Packing NDI Cocrystal Catalyst
articles.abstract: Solar‐driven photocatalytic H2O2 synthesis offers a sustainable and green alternative to the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. However, coordinated regulation of electron‐transfer (ET) and energy‐transfer (EnT) pathways for efficient H2O2 production remains challenging. Organic charge‐transfer (CT) cocrystals, which reconfigure the energy‐level structure through new intermolecular electronic states, provide a promising avenue to overcome this limitation. Herein, we report a CT cocrystal photocatalyst, DPNDI‐Py, prepared by liquid‐assisted grinding (LAG) of N, N′‐bis(4‐pyridyl)‐1,4,5,8‐naphthalenediimide (DPNDI) and pyrene (Py). The cocrystal harbors an X‐packed donor‐acceptor arrangement, with a crossing angle of 52° between the long axes of DPNDI and Py. Spectroscopic measurements confirm strong intermolecular CT, and transient spectroscopy supports CT‐related excited‐state dynamics and the formation of long‐lived triplet states, while theoretical calculations indicate electronic structure favorable for intersystem crossing (ISC). Mechanistic studies indicate that both EnT and ET pathways are utilized in photocatalysis. Under LED irradiation in air, DPNDI‐Py delivers an average H2O2 production rate of 18.47 ± 0.57 mmol g−1 h−1 coupled with an 83.7 ± 2.26% dehydroascorbic acid (DHA) yield from ascorbic acid (AA) oxidation. This work provides mechanistic insight into CT‐mediated photocatalysis, offering a design principle for organic photocatalysts.

articles.title: Lumped Circuits Modeling of Dynamic Energy Transfer in Triboelectric Nanogenerators with Nonlinear Electromechanical Coupling
articles.abstract: Powering autonomous electronics, sensors, and wearable systems using small‐scale daily mechanical energy is becoming increasingly important. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) offer a lightweight, flexible, and adaptable route for such applications, particularly when movements are involved. Here, we present a first‐of‐its‐kind unified dynamic energy‐transfer framework for TENGs, coupling their mechanical and electrical domains through a lumped element‐based equivalent circuit (LEEC) model. The framework captures time‐varying electrostatic behavior and key mechanical parameters, mass, damping, and stiffness, within a single predictive platform, enabling system‐level analysis of dynamic efficiency, impedance, resonance, and power transfer under different excitation conditions. The Thévenin equivalent model reveals that TENG performance is dynamically governed by excitation frequency, resonance, load matching, and surface charge density, approaching a time‐averaged theoretical efficiency of ∼54%. Experimental validation across devices with varied mechanical parameters shows close agreement with theory in electrical response and frequency‐dependent behavior. Furthermore, four borophene‐modified TENGs with different charge‐generation characteristics exhibit a systematic increase in electrical output and an estimated efficiency of up to 14.2% for the examined parameter space, supporting the model‐predicted dependence of energy‐conversion performance on surface charge density. The LEEC‐guided platform enables coupled energy and information harvesting through resonance‐enhanced capacitor charging and self‐powered road‐state sensing.

articles.title: Nonlinear Kinetic Optimization via Strong–Weak Cosolvent Synergy in Aqueous Zinc Batteries
articles.abstract: Cosolvent engineering for aqueous Zn metal batteries has traditionally emphasized thermodynamic stabilization, whereas the kinetic dimension of Zn2+ charge transfer—particularly in multi‐cosolvent systems—remains far less understood. Here we conduct a systematic study on a dual‐cosolvent electrolyte pairing a strong cosolvent (DMSO) with a weak cosolvent (DMC). Through spatial decoupling, the strong cosolvent directly coordinates to stabilize the primary solvation shell, while the weak cosolvent forms a dynamic outer‐shell buffer. This unique context modulates Zn–ligand binding, facilitates desolvation, and guides the formation of a regulated SEI. Consequently, this architecture preserves comparably high thermodynamic stability while unlocking a nonlinear kinetic optimization exclusive to the dual‐cosolvent regime. Using a multi‐descriptor framework, we demonstrate a ∼40% reduction in the charge‐transfer barrier relative to single‐cosolvent systems. This kinetic enhancement translates into robust practical performance, establishing strong–weak cosolvent synergy as a versatile design principle for next‐generation aqueous batteries.

articles.title: Synergistic Surface‐Bulk Induction of Uniform Out‐of‐Plane (100) Orientation for High‐Efficiency Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Perovskite thin films featuring out‐of‐plane oriented (100) crystallographic facets are pivotal for advancing the efficiency and stability of perovskite solar cells, owing to their superior charge transport properties and reduced deep‐level defect density. However, conventional single‐strategy modification approaches are typically constrained by limited control over crystal orientation and spatially heterogeneous orientation distribution, hindering the full exploitation of such beneficial facets. Herein, we present a surface‐bulk synergistic induction strategy that overcomes the limitations of single modification approaches, effectively promoting directional grain alignment and cooperatively guiding ordered out‐of‐plane growth during thermal annealing. Benefiting from the successful fabrication of a perovskite film with a uniform and predominant preferred orientation, the inverted perovskite solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.98% (certified 26.41%). Furthermore, the homogeneous texture and high intrinsic stability of the (100) facets enable the devices to retain 93.5% of their initial PCE after 1000 h of operational stability testing. This strategy effectively tackles the technical constraints of precursor solution regulation and solid‐state surface treatment, offering a novel research model for the precise modulation of perovskite thin film crystal facets and the secondary growth of polycrystalline thin films.

articles.title: 3D‐Printed Gradient Shape‐Memory Strain Sensors With Rewritable Gauge Factors
articles.abstract: The gauge factor (GF) of a flexible strain sensor is typically fixed during fabrication, constraining its dynamic range to a single operating window. Here, we report a material–structure co‐programming strategy that transforms GF from a static fabrication parameter into a dynamically reconfigurable sensing state. Using a polycaprolactone shape‐memory polymer/carbon black composite, thermomechanical programming allows a single unmodified device to access a continuum of gain states, tuning GF from 4.69 to 238.4 through preset strain. Thermal erasing resets the baseline state, enabling repeated rewriting of the sensing gain without altering material composition or electrical layout. To expand this design space, direct ink writing adds an independent architectural axis: printed hourglass and tapered tetra‐pyramid geometries concentrate strain into localized sensing zones, amplifying the programmed response and pushing peak GF beyond 1000. Recognizing that high GF is not universally optimal, we show that high‐gain states resolve faint physiological signals, whereas low‐gain states provide stable output under large‐amplitude motion. Finally, we demonstrate a rewritable dual‐channel interface that reassigns gain states across channels to re‐task a single sensor on demand.

articles.title: A Dragon‐Fruit‐Like Nanoplatform Containing Polydopamine‐Wrapped Selenium Quantum Dots Boosts Synergistic Chemo‐Photothermal Therapy for Triple‐Negative Breast Cancer
articles.abstract: Triple‐negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains a significant clinical challenge due to lack of targetable biomarkers and systemic toxicity of conventional chemotherapy. To address these hurdles, we engineered a bioinspired “dragon‐fruit‐mimetic” nanoplatform (GemSe@PDA), with selenium quantum dots (SeQDs) and gemcitabine (Gem) uniformly dispersed in polydopamine (PDA) matrix that acts as a functional photothermal carrier. This distinctive structural endows high drug loading capacity, and the PDA matrix degrades under lysosomal acidic conditions (pH ∼5.0), enabling stimuli‐responsive release of SeQDs and Gem. GemSe@PDA shows uniform morphology (174.8 nm in diameter) and excellent photothermal capability of raising local temperature to 48.3°C within 10 min. Functionally, the GemSe@PDA nanoplatform integrates three modalities of SeQD‐driven apoptosis, PDA‐mediated photothermal ablation under 808 nm NIR irradiation, and Gem‐induced chemotherapy. Mechanistically, RNA‐seq analysis revealed that SeQDs provoke apoptosis by regulating the Akt/caspase‐3 signaling pathway, while Gem triggers cell cycle arrest. In vivo studies demonstrated that GemSe@PDA markedly boosts tumor‐targeted accumulation and effectively suppresses tumor growth, lowering the tumor weight to merely 15.9% of the control group without systemic toxicity. By combining the structural advantages of a dragon fruit‐like design with bioactive SeQDs, this nanoplatform provides a versatile, biocompatible strategy for overcoming the therapeutic problems of TNBC.

articles.title: A Dual‐Functional Inherent Hydroxyl Chainmail on Defective La(OH)3 for Robust Electrocatalytic Hydrogenation in Extreme Aqueous Matrices
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic hydrogenation of carbon‐heteroatom bonds promises sustainable chemical synthesis and water remediation, yet practical deployment is challenged by both sluggish proton supply from water dissociation in alkaline media and rapid catalyst poisoning by dissolved organic matter (DOM). Herein, we show that the defective La(OH)3 nanorods bearing an inherent hydroxyl chainmail circumvent these two bottlenecks simultaneously. The chainmail is proposed to be capable of reconstructing the interfacial hydrogen‐bond continuum into a proposed proton‐relay highway that accelerates water‐dissociation‐limited proton delivery, while acting as a proposed biomimetic, multisite hydrogen‐bonding shield that sequesters macromolecular DOM to protect active sites from fouling. Demonstrated for the electrocatalytic hydrodechlorination reaction, the catalyst achieves highly effective dechlorination of florfenicol across pH 3.0–13.0 and sustains exceptional stability in high‐chemical oxygen demand (COD) matrices (1000 mg L−1 humic acid), outperforming most state‐of‐the‐art catalysts. Continuous‐flow treatment of real aquaculture and pharmaceutical effluents confirms sustained dechlorination efficiency and pronounced toxicity abatement. By revealing how this seemingly passive OH− chainmail orchestrates proton transfer and molecular sieving, this work establishes a broadly applicable design paradigm for fouling‐resistant electrocatalysts operating in complex aqueous environments.

articles.title: A High‐Performance Dibenzothiophene‐Terminated Self‐Assembled Hole Transport Monolayer for Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Self‐assembled hole transport monolayers (SAMs) have become indispensable components of high‐performance inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). SAMs not only govern the interfacial hole extraction kinetics but also influence the crystallization quality of the overlying perovskite film and the properties of the buried interface. In this work, we designed and synthesized a novel SAM featuring a terminal dibenzothiophene group, designated DBT‐4PACz. Our investigation reveals that, compared with the commercial benchmark Me‐4PACz, DBT‐4PACz forms denser and more uniform coverage on the substrate, exhibits higher conductivity, and demonstrates a more favorable energy level alignment with the perovskite. Moreover, the thiophene moiety in DBT‐4PACz enhances the interaction with the perovskite. This, combined with the denser SAM layer, improves the crystallization quality of the perovskite and reduces interfacial defects. Leveraging this molecular design, inverted PSCs employing DBT‐4PACz achieved a remarkable power conversion efficiency of 27.01% (certified 26.62%), significantly surpassing the performance of Me‐4PACz‐based control devices (26.16%). Furthermore, DBT‐4PACz‐based devices exhibit superior operational stability.

articles.title: A Microenvironment‐Feedback Cascaded Hydrogel for Regenerative Repair of Infected Diabetic Wounds
articles.abstract: Infected diabetic wound repair is hindered by a hostile microenvironment of heavy bacterial burden, persistent oxidative stress, toxin‐driven inflammation, and hypoxia. Here we report a microenvironment‐feedback cascaded hydrogel, termed HL‐10, for infected diabetic wound repair. HL‐10 is formed via dynamic Schiff base crosslinking between L‐arginine ‐modified chitosan and aldehyde‐functionalized F127, with erythrocyte membrane‐hybridized, polymyxin B‐modified and perfluorohexane (PFH)‐loaded liposomes (Rφ‐PLipo‐PFH) embedded within the hydrogel network. The chitosan‐based network first suppresses bacterial growth and biofilm formation. As the acidic and reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐rich conditions trigger matrix degradation, the hydrogel scavenges local ROS and generates nitric oxide to alleviate oxidative stress and inflammation. This degradation process simultaneously exposes the embedded liposomes, which neutralize bacterial toxins and reduce the LPS‐induced M1 macrophage phenotype, while the PFH core provides a sustained oxygen supply to counter hypoxia. In a Pseudomonas aeruginosa‐infected diabetic model, HL‐10 treatment accelerated wound repair and was accompanied by attenuation of AGE‐RAGE/PI3K‐Akt signaling, restoration of angiogenesis, and improved tissue remodeling, demonstrating a systematic biomaterial approach for managing refractory wounds.

articles.title: A Multifunctional Surface for Microplastic Trapping, SERS‐Based Molecular Sensing, and PFAS Breakdown Through Microdroplet Deposition
articles.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) and per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) co‐occur in natural and drinking waters, where they persist, accumulate, and pose risks to ecological and human health. Their mitigation demands integrated detection and remediation beyond single‐function platforms. Here, we report Ag@TiO2 nanobrushes (NBs), fabricated entirely by ambient charged microdroplet deposition, as a unified substrate for MP capture, SERS‐based sensing, and photocatalytic PFAS degradation. In a two‐step electrospray process, 1D Ag nanowire arrays (Ag NBs) were grown over large areas and overcoated with TiO2. During overcoating, a Marangoni‐type capillary rearrangement drives Ag nanoparticles to the wire periphery, yielding an Ag@TiO2 architecture with a percolated plasmonic network in a photoactive TiO2 scaffold. The 3D NB network traps MP beads, while dense electromagnetic 3D hotspots enable SERS detection of Rhodamine 6G (LOD ∼38 fM; EF ∼6 × 107) and 1 µm polystyrene beads (LOD ∼31.6 ng mL−1; EF ∼ 105) across DI, tap, and simulated seawater. The unmodified substrate drives photocatalytic degradation of perfluorooctanoic acid under ambient sunlight, confirmed by mass spectrometry. This is the first fully electrosprayed platform, integrating MP trapping, femtomolar‐level SERS detection, and PFAS photoremediation, thereby demonstrating ambient charged microdroplets as a scalable route to multifunctional nanostructures for water monitoring and remediation.

articles.title: A Nano‐Cocoon Platform Attenuates Osteoarthritis Progression via Chem‐Bio Coupled ROS Scavenging and Cartilage Lubrication Restoration
articles.abstract: Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, cartilage matrix degeneration, and impaired lubrication are central drivers of osteoarthritis (OA). However, poor matrix retention limits drug delivery to chondrocytes and lubrication restoration. Here, we develop a zwitterion-based, thioketal-crosslinked Superoxide Dismutase (SOD)-polymer complex (SOD-SADT) via in situ atom transfer radical polymerization, in which polymers grow from the enzyme surface and envelop SOD to form a nanoscale cocoon. The polymer shell exhibits cartilage-matrix affinity through van der Waals and electrostatic interactions with type II collagen and chondroitin sulfate. Accordingly, its zwitterionic hydration layer enables matrix-anchored lubrication, substantially reducing the coefficient of friction of OA-like cartilages. Meanwhile, SOD-SADT establishes a chem-bio coupling for ROS elimination that couples enzymatic·O2 − dismutation with thioketal-triggered chemical depletion of H2O2 and·OH, achieving up to ∼80% ROS scavenging. Notably, SOD-SADT achieves high chondrocyte uptake (∼ 91.7 ± 3.4%) and promotes lysosomal escape. This enhances intracellular utilization, thereby attenuating oxidative injury and restoring anabolic/catabolic balance. In a mouse model of OA, intra-articular SOD-SADT preserves cartilage structure and improves joint function, thereby markedly slowing OA progression. Overall, this work offers a dual-action strategy that couples intracellular antioxidant regulation with extracellular lubrication repair to address OA.

articles.title: A Sequential Photothermal‐Piezoelectric GBR Membrane for Cascading Anti‐Infection and Bone Regeneration in Periodontal Defects
articles.abstract: The effective regeneration of infectious periodontal bone defects remains challenging, as current commercial guided bone regeneration (GBR) membranes offer only passive barrier function. Here, we report an electrospun, multifunctional GBR membrane engineered for active therapy. Composed of poly (L‐lactic acid) (PLLA) and doped with silver‐polydopamine‐modified barium titanate (Ag@PDA@BTO) particles, this membrane integrates sequential photothermal and piezoelectric effects, thereby enabling on‐demand, stage‐specific therapy for infected periodontal bone regeneration. The PLLA/AgPBT membrane enabled a sequential therapeutic strategy: First, rapid, NIR‐induced photothermal heating (>60°C in 5 min) achieved > 99% immediate bactericidal activity; second, under ultrasound, it generated ∼800 mV to provide long‐term piezoelectric‐driven bacterio‐inhibition and macrophage polarization (M1→M2); third, it promoted osteogenic differentiation while simultaneously acting as a barrier against soft tissue ingrowth. In a Sprague‐Dawley rat model of infectious bone defects, the membrane significantly enhanced the differentiation of osteoblast‐lineage cells, ultimately facilitating new bone formation. Validated both in vitro and in an infectious rat bone defect model, this intelligent membrane transitions from a potent antibacterial barrier to a pro‐healing electroactive scaffold, dynamically adapting to the complex oral microenvironment and overcoming the static nature of traditional GBR.

articles.title: A Single‐Channel Humidity‐Pressure Dual‐Modal Decoupling Sensor for Assistive Geriatric Rehabilitation
articles.abstract: Against the background of global population aging and the growing need for elderly care, developing multi‐modal sensing platforms with high interference immunity, specifically for complex respiratory dysfunctions, has become a critical demand in the field of precision medicine. However, conventional multimodal sensors suffer from performance limitations and signal crosstalk due to excessive reliance on complex material synthesis and suboptimal structural design. A humidity–pressure dual‐modal sensor (HPDS) was designed by integrating polyimide, electrodes, and a heterogeneous conductive elastomer into a sandwich‐structured device. The HPDS exhibited good sensitivity over a wide pressure range (0.58–392 kPa), high mechanical stability exceeding 50 000 cycles, and a fast humidity response of 200 ms. An intelligent assistive training scheme combined with a lightweight one‐dimensional convolutional neural network (1D‐CNN) was further constructed for respiratory pattern discrimination and physical therapy assistance, achieving an accuracy of 98.9% in classifying the six core respiratory states. This work provided a universal design paradigm for next‐generation low‐coupling and high‐performance AI devices, showing great promise in the development of intelligent healthcare and home‐based rehabilitation.

articles.title: Active Learning For Tractable and Reproducible Pulsed Laser Deposition
articles.abstract: This paper shows how data‐driven machine learning approaches can improve growth control, reproducibility, and physical insight in the pulsed laser deposition (PLD) growth of correlated oxides. Despite well‐known relationships between growth conditions and material properties, consistently producing high‐quality films of complex materials like LaVO3${\rm LaVO}_3$ remains difficult due to the highly non‐equilibrium nature of PLD and the defects and competing phases that accumulate during growth. Here, we use an active learning framework based on Gaussian process Bayesian optimization that incorporates measured bulk and surface lattice properties along with impurity phase information to efficiently map the multidimensional growth space of LaVO3${\rm LaVO}_3$ by PLD. By tuning the relative weighting of these properties, the model identifies an optimized region where phase‐pure films of LaVO3${\rm LaVO}_3$ exhibit two‐dimensional surfaces, near‐ideal lattice parameters, and minimal sub‐bandgap optical absorption. The trained model reveals clear competition among different defect formation mechanisms that are connected to unseen parameters like supersaturation and surface mobility, thus giving insight into the highly non‐equilibrium process of PLD growth. Together, this demonstrates that property‐guided machine learning can accelerate materials optimization while providing a new way to address fundamental growth mechanisms in PLD that enable understanding and utilization of quantum phenomena found in complex oxides.

articles.title: Additively Manufactured Geometry‐Reconfigurable Soft Neural Probes With Monolithic Multifunctionality
articles.abstract: Developing neural interfaces that seamlessly integrate with the brain while enabling stable, multimodal sensing and stimulation is central to advancing neuroscience and neuroprosthetic technologies. Conventional metal‐ or silicon‐based probes suffer from mechanical mismatches with soft tissue, causing inflammation, signal instability, and limited long‐term performance. Recent efforts toward soft probes have improved compliance, yet their fabrication typically relies on complex lithography or modular assembly, limiting geometric customization, scalability, and multifunctional integration. Here, we present NeuroMAP, a multifunctional architected probe for neural interfacing, enabled by a three‐dimensional reconfigurable fabrication strategy that integrates conducting polymer hydrogel electrodes and embedded microfluidic channels within compact soft cylindrical architectures. Multimaterial direct ink writing followed by rolling‐ or wrapping‐based reconfiguration produces NeuroMAP and its miniaturized W‐NeuroMAP variant with integrated electrical and fluidic functions. The probes exhibit high compliance, stable electrochemical performance during deformation and extended immersion, and precise leakage‐free microfluidic delivery. This additive manufacturing strategy enables scalable multichannel integration with up to 30 electrically isolated electrodes. In vivo implantation in the mouse hippocampus demonstrates localized chemical neuromodulation, spatially resolved single‐unit recording, stable chronic stimulus‐responsive electrophysiology, and attenuated glial responses compared with rigid metal probes. This work establishes a customizable, mechanically compliant platform for multifunctional neural interfaces.

articles.title: Advancing CO2 Electroreduction Toward Multicarbon Products via Catalyst Engineering and Integrated Paired Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction (CO2RR) provides a compelling pathway for converting CO2 into value‐added multicarbon (C2+) products using renewable electricity, yet its technological translation remains limited by coupled challenges spanning catalyst chemistry, reaction microenvironments, reactor architecture, and cathode‐anode integration. This review develops a multiscale framework that connects molecular‐level C‐C coupling with device‐ and process‐level performance. Fundamental CO2 activation, reaction pathways, electrochemical metrics, and structure–activity relationships are critically examined, with particular emphasis on Cu‐based catalysts and emerging catalyst‐engineering strategies for selective C2+ synthesis. These catalytic principles are then linked to operando surface states, intermediate coverage, local microenvironments, mass transport, membrane behavior, and electrolyzer configuration under technologically relevant conditions. Beyond cathodic optimization, oxygen evolution and alternative anodic chemistries, including biomass‐derived alcohol oxidation and plastic‐derived stream valorization, are assessed within integrated paired‐electrolysis architectures. Their practical significance is benchmarked through matched current density, full‐cell voltage, carbon and electron efficiency, product concentration, crossover, separation, durability, and realistic feed compatibility. This framework exposes critical catalyst‐reactor‐process trade‐offs and defines design principles for scalable, durable, and economically credible CO2‐to‐C2+ electrosynthesis.

articles.title: An AIEgen‐Based Covalent Organic Polymer With NIR‐II Emission for 980 nm Excitable Tumor Phototheranostics
articles.abstract: Covalent organic porous polymers (COPs) represent an attractive platform for phototheranostics due to their structural tunability and extended conjugation. Nevertheless, achieving COPs that simultaneously exhibit efficient second near‐infrared (NIR‐II) fluorescence and long‐wavelength excitation remains a considerable challenge, limiting their applicability in deep‐tissue theranostics. In this study, we constructed a conjugated COP (BTTB‐PA) by integrating an aggregation‐induced emission luminogen (AIEgen) BTTB into a rigid imine‐linked framework. The confined environment within BTTB‐PA skeleton restricted molecular motion of the AIEgen, activating intense NIR‐II fluorescence. To further enhance photophysical properties, the dynamic imine bonds in BTTB‐PA were converted into planar thiazole linkages through post‐synthetic modification, yielding BTTB‐PSH with improved structural rigidity and conjugation. This transformation resulted in a pronounced prolong in absorption and exceptional photothermal conversion efficiency under 980 nm laser irradiation. As a result, BTTB‐PSH nanoparticles enabled high‐contrast NIR‐II fluorescence and photoacoustic imaging, guiding highly effective photothermal ablation of tumors. This work provides a strategic approach to developing structure‐engineered COPs for advanced cancer theranostics.

articles.title: Benzotriazole‐Functionalized g‐C3N4/NH2‐UiO‐66 Heterojunctions Enable Photothermal Self‐Healing and Durable Polyurea Protective Coatings
articles.abstract: Protective polymer coatings for marine and island infrastructures are expected to integrate resistance to mechanical damage, chloride attack, ultraviolet aging and fungal colonization, yet achieving these functions in a single dynamic coating remains challenging. Herein, an Oct‐CUPU coating is developed by embedding a benzotriazole‐modified g‐C3N4/NH2‐UiO‐66 heterostructure, denoted as Oct‐CU, into a disulfide‐containing polyurea network. The g‐C3N4/NH2‐UiO‐66 heterointerface provides photothermal conversion and interfacial reinforcement; the benzotriazole moiety improves UV shielding, and the dynamic polyurea matrix supplies reversible hydrogen bonding and disulfide exchange for damage repair. These coupled molecular and interfacial interactions enable localized light‐to‐heat conversion to activate chain mobility and network reconstruction, while the rod‐like heterostructure promotes stress redistribution and improves long‐term barrier stability. As a result, the optimized Oct‐CUPU coating exhibits rapid NIR‐triggered scratch healing and markedly enhanced corrosion‐barrier retention. It also maintains improved abrasion tolerance, UV‐aging resistance, and mold resistance compared with the unmodified coatings. This work presents a heterostructure‐assisted design strategy for adaptive polyurea coatings with integrated self‐healing, anticorrosion, anti‐aging, and antifouling‐related functions, offering potential for durable protection of metallic structures in marine, coastal, and outdoor environments.

articles.title: Bias‐Free Tactile Synaptic Ionogel With Viscoelastic Memory for Biomechanical Monitoring
articles.abstract: Endowing artificial skins with adaptation and sensory memory is essential for intelligent tactile perception. However, conventional transistor‐based neuromorphic systems rely on energy‐intensive, decoupled architectures that fundamentally constrain their structural flexibility and energy efficiency. In this study, we report a monolithic, bias‐free piezoionic tactile synapse that exhibits adaptive plasticity driven solely by mechanical stimuli. Learning and memory arise from stress‐induced piezoelectric polarization at the dynamic interface, which drives rapid ion separation, coupled with supramolecular confinement within the viscoelastic polymer network that retards cation backflow. This kinematic asymmetry induces pronounced ion transport hysteresis, directly translating mechanical inputs into cumulative postsynaptic potentials. Furthermore, the supramolecular network inherently affords autonomous self‐healing and conformal adhesion. Leveraging these features, we demonstrate a self‐powered electronic skin for the in situ quantification of neuromuscular coordination and biomechanical endurance. By unifying mechanotransduction and memory at the material level, this work establishes a novel paradigm for energy‐efficient biological‐machine interfaces.

articles.title: Bioinspired Ultralow‐Power Flexible Electro‐Optically Configurable Synaptic Transistors: An Integrated Perception‐Processing‐Tracking Visual Chain
articles.abstract: Biological visual tracking closely parallels the autonomous navigation that requires motion recognition, typically progressing through a cascade of optical perception, adaptive attention, and real‐time tracking. However, most efforts focus on low‐level perception and decoupled algorithms, while overlooking the crucial intermediate mechanism of in situ background suppression for salient target separation. Here, inspired by the Nile tilapia visual system, a perception‐processing‐tracking visual chain architecture based on flexible, electro‐optically configurable synaptic transistors is first proposed. Leveraging the sharp absorption edge of quantum dots (QDs), the device achieves prominent RGB‐NIR band recognition. Notably, the introduction of a phosphoric acid‐mediation strategy significantly enhances the stability of blue‐emitting CsPbCl3 QDs while preserving their excellent optical performance. Combined with a poly(vinylidene fluoride‐co‐hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF‐HFP) dielectric layer, the system enables efficient cross‐modal optoelectronic signal processing. Electric field tuning of photocarrier tunneling assigns an attention score as high as 95.88% to target regions and merely 3.79% to backgrounds, with the score gap widening over time. Assisted by reservoir computing (RC), the device classifies six target motion trajectories with 98.89% accuracy, operating at an ultra‐low energy cost of 0.011 fJ per synaptic event with exceptional mechanical flexibility. These attributes open up promising prospects for future autonomous driving applications.

articles.title: Bio‐Inspired Flex‐Rigid Design Enabling High‐Performance Multimodal Locomotion of Robots
articles.abstract: Biological locomotion often benefits from flex‐rigid architectures, where soft tissues coordinate with rigid skeletons or appendages to enable effective force transmission, versatile motion generation, and environmental adaptability. However, translating this paradigm to robotics remains challenging. Here, we present a bio‐inspired flex‐rigid robot (Bio‐FRR) that integrates a muscle‐like pneumatic actuating unit with a fin‐like rigid arched plate to achieve high‐performance multimodal locomotion. Unlike conventional rigid‐flexible hybrid robots in which rigid elements mainly serve as passive reinforcements or fixed appendages, the Bio‐FRR employs a deployable flex‐rigid mechanism, where a multi‐chamber pneumatic actuator actively drives rigid arched plates to fold and unfold, thereby converting local soft deformation into body‐level posture reconfiguration and locomotion‐relevant mechanical output. Such a design endows the Bio‐FRR with versatile and adaptive locomotion across various environments, realizing five high‐performance locomotion modes on land and in water without structural reconfiguration, including upright hopping, leapfrogging, terrestrial crawling, diving, and swimming. The Bio‐FRR reaches a maximum terrestrial speed of 1.23 body lengths per second (BL/s), a horizontal swimming speed of 0.42 BL/s, and an untethered driving speed of 48.67 mm/s. Bio‐FRR offers a robust blueprint for next‐generation amphibious soft robots, enabling versatile locomotion and enhanced adaptability.

articles.title: Br‐Mediated Interfacial Microenvironment Engineering Triggers Dual‐Site Oxide Pathway Mechanism for Stable Oxygen Evolution
articles.abstract: Steering the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) toward desired oxide pathway mechanism (OPM) is critical for reconciling catalytic activity and stability. However, rationally triggering the adjacent oxygen‐radical coupling involved in OPM remains highly challenging due to the complex intermediate evolution and the stringent requirement for adjacent dual sites. Herein, we report a Br‐mediated anode‐electrolyte microenvironment engineering to construct a high‐density active •O interface on NiFe oxide, enabling direct •O─O• radical coupling on Ni─Fe dual sites. Rather than simply tuning dual‐site spacing, Br species with large size and weak hydration ability act as interfacial regulators to enhance the Lewis acidity of Ni─Fe centers and reorganize the interfacial hydrogen‐bond network, accelerating OH− migration, adsorption, and •OH deprotonation. The promoted •OH deprotonation shifts the rate‐determining step to •OOH formation and creates a •O‐rich interfacial environment, promoting access to an additional OPM pathway, as verified by in situ ATR‐SEIRAS, DEMS, and DFT calculations. Consequently, NiFeOxBry exhibits an 89 mV reduction in overpotential at 10 mA cm−2 and requires a cell voltage of only 1.725 V to achieve 1 A cm−2 when employed in an anion exchange membrane electrolyzer. This work establishes interfacial microenvironment engineering as a pathway‐selective design principle for efficient and durable OER catalysis.

articles.title: Compositionally Tuned FeNiMnCuNbAgx High‐Entropy Alloy Nanoparticles With Enhanced ROS Generation and Photothermal Antibacterial Activity
articles.abstract: The development of multifunctional antibacterial nanomaterials is of considerable interest in combating antibiotic resistance and marine biofouling. Herein, Ag‐containing FeNiMnCuNbAgx high‐entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA‐NPs) with tunable composition were synthesized through a non‐equilibrium arc‐discharge plasma strategy. By introducing Nb to stabilize Ag within the alloy matrix, homogeneous HEA‐NPs with adjustable Ag content were successfully obtained. The resulting nanoparticles exhibited broad‐spectrum antibacterial activity, efficient photothermal conversion, and strong biofilm‐removal capability. In particular, FeNiMnCuNbAg0.25 HEA‐NPs achieved 99.99% elimination of planktonic Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteria at a low dosage of 15 µg·mL−1 (15 ppm), while under simulated solar irradiation (1 sun), the biofilm removal efficiency at 50 µg·mL−1 increased from 86% to 98%, demonstrating a pronounced photothermal enhancement effect. Mechanistic investigations combining electron spin resonance (ESR), density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and transcriptomic analysis revealed that the Ag incorporation altered the thermodynamic evolution of oxygen reduction intermediates and modulated reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation behavior. Meanwhile, transcriptomic results indicated that HEA‐NP treatment induced redox imbalance, respiratory dysfunction, and translational suppression in the bacterium. These findings highlight the potential of Ag‐containing HEA‐NPs as multifunctional antibacterial materials for biofilm control and antimicrobial protection in marine‐relevant environments.

articles.title: Concentration‐Dependent Self‐Assembly and Nanoparticle Maturation of Reflectins
articles.abstract: Cephalopods dynamically modulate coloration for camouflage and communication through iridophores whose Bragg reflector‐like ultrastructures contain high‐refractive‐index proteins known as reflectins. However, the mechanisms linking concentration, conformation, and nanoparticle stabilization in full‐length reflectins remain poorly understood. Here, coarse‐grained molecular dynamics simulations of Doryteuthis pealeii reflectin A2 (RfA2) across five concentrations are combined with dynamic light scattering (DLS) and circular dichroism (CD) measurements. The simulations reveal rapid initial protein aggregation followed by slower structural maturation, during which interprotein interaction energy and contact networks continue to evolve. A simulation‐derived concentration‐dependent crossover separates multi‐cluster vs single‐cluster regimes and DLS shows larger assemblies at higher experimental concentrations. The simulations further delineate region‐specific secondary‐structure reorganization and CD demonstrates concentration‐sensitive structural changes with a distinct secondary‐structure redistribution. Moreover, the simulations predict concentration dependence in the contribution of intermolecular contact network reorganization; the L1, L3, and L5 linker regions supplied many of these contacts, with L3 providing the dominant contribution. Overall, these findings establish a molecular‐level framework where concentration governs RfA2 self‐assembly and continued conformational and intermolecular reorganization during maturation, providing insight into sequence‐ and assembly‐level principles regarding iridophore optical function and reflectin‐based materials design.

articles.title: Confinement‐Enabled Epitaxy of Single‐Crystal InN Fins Enables Room‐Temperature Ohmic Contact to GaN
articles.abstract: Indium nitride (InN) combines the highest electron mobility and peak carrier velocity among the III‐nitrides with an intrinsically degenerate surface accumulation layer, making it an attractive but difficult material for electronic interfaces. Here, we show that geometric confinement increases local adatom supersaturation and enables the growth of single‐crystal InN by standard pulsed metal–organic chemical vapor deposition under conditions that otherwise do not support planar InN. This approach yields single‐crystal InN fins through selective‐area growth and supports versatile AlN/InN and GaN/InN heterostructures. The resulting selectively grown InN fins form abrupt GaN/InN and AlN/InN heterointerfaces and exhibit exceptionally low‐resistance, anneal‐free ohmic behavior. When integrated as epitaxial contact layers in AlGaN/GaN heterostructure FinFETs, they enable room‐temperature contacts that outperform conventional high‐temperature alloyed contacts while preserving interface crystallinity. These results establish confinement‐enabled InN epitaxy as a route to low‐thermal‐budget, gate‐first GaN processing and highlight a broader strategy for contact engineering and heterogeneous integration in advanced nitride electronics.

articles.title: Construction of Injectable Hydrogels Based on Cationic Porphyrins and Hyaluronic Acid for Wound Healing With Multimodal Antibacterial Therapy and Instantaneous Monitoring
articles.abstract: Although hydrogels with antimicrobial and monitoring have the potential for precision wound therapy, it is difficult to construct smart framework of hydrogels in molecular level. Herein, an in situ crosslinked antimicrobial conductive hydrogel (Au/HA‐TPP) based on 5,10,15,20‐tetra(4‐N‐(4‐boronobenzyl)pyridin) porphyrin (TBPP) and hyaluronic acid (HA) was prepared triggered by an alkaline solution containing Au(III) reduction catalysis with phenylboronic acid, (5,10,15,20‐tetra(4‐dihydroxyborylphenyl) porphyrin (TBP) and 5,10,15,20‐tetrakis‐(4‐N‐methylpyridyl) porphyrin (TMPyP)) as control. In the process of gelation, Au(III) was reduced into Au nanoparticles (Au NPs) and formed into nanoparticles and dispersed evenly in Au/HA‐TPP with fastest gelation time of 22 s and the best mechanical properties. The synergistic interaction of Au NPs and porphyrins can induce effective antibacterial photodynamic therapy (APDT) under visible light irradiation, and the photothermal effect caused by Au NPs had a fast temperature rise in seconds with good cycling stability. In addition, quaternized porphyrins in Au/HA‐TPP played a long‐term antibacterial and APDT effects. The dynamic change of the contact resistance between the hydrogel and wounds can reflect the wound healing to achieve instantaneous monitoring. Au/HA‐TPP hydrogels integrated multimodal sterilizations as well as the realization of intelligent wound detection, which could provide the diagnosis and treatment of infected wounds at different application scenarios.

articles.title: Continuous Heterodyne Microwave Sensing With van der Waals Spin Defects
articles.abstract:
Quantum sensing with solid‐state spin defects provides a powerful approach for microwave‐field detection, but conventional sensing protocols are often limited by narrow detection bandwidths. Here, we demonstrate continuous heterodyne microwave sensing using spin defects in hexagonal boron nitride, a van der Waals material with intrinsically broad spin resonances. By implementing a continuous heterodyne protocol that mixes a weak signal microwave field with a continuous auxiliary microwave field, we realize linear microwave‐field detection with a dynamic range from 192.5nT$192.5
obreakspace \mathrm{nT}$ to 12.8μT$12.8
obreakspace \mu \mathrm{T}$. The large inhomogeneous linewidth of the defect ensemble enables a detection bandwidth of 4MHz$4
obreakspace \mathrm{MHz}$, while single‐frequency measurements achieve sub‐hertz spectral resolution. In addition, the scheme supports simultaneous detection of multiple microwave frequencies and wide‐field imaging. These results establish van der Waals spin defects as a promising platform for broadband continuous‐wave microwave sensing, with potential applications in microwave spectral analysis, spin dynamics, and quantum‐circuit diagnostics.

articles.title: Copper Single Atoms on a Photothermal Heterostructure for Dual‐Field‐Driven Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Conversion
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic reactions involving multiple electrons and protons, such as nitrate reduction to ammonia, are constrained by sluggish interfacial charge-transfer and inefficient mass transport. Here, we propose a dual-field-driven strategy that integrates the local thermal field and the built-in electric field within a photothermal heterostructure, enabling concerted control over both atomic-scale active-site construction and the reaction microenvironment. Using a CeO2/Co3O4 composite as the platform, photogenerated electrons guided by interfacial band alignment drive the site-selective loading of single-atom Cu onto CeO2 domains, yielding an atomically precise Cu/CeO2/Co3O4 (Cu/CeCo) catalyst. Under near-infrared irradiation, the optimal catalyst provides an NH3 yield rate of 110.5 µmol h−1 cm−2 at −0.4 V vs. RHE and a high Faradaic efficiency of 95.8% at −0.2 V vs. RHE, both outperforming its dark-state performance. Mechanistic studies indicate that Cu single atoms anchored on CeO2/Co3O4 promote NO3 − adsorption and effectively inhibit the hydrogen evolution reaction. Furthermore, the dual-field accelerates the interfacial charge transfer and promotes the overall reaction kinetics. This work demonstrates that dual-field microenvironment engineering serves as a promising platform for advancing atomic-scale catalysis toward sustainable chemical synthesis.

articles.title: Correction to “Machine Learning‐Driven Molecule Additives for High‐Performance Perovskite Solar Cells With Bandgap Universality and Scalability”
Correction to “Multifunctional Reconfigurable Electromagnetic Metamaterials Based on Compression‐Torsion Coupling Structures for Transmission Modulations and Holographic Displays”
Coupling *CO Protonation on Cu Single Atoms With H2O Dissociation on Bi Nanoclusters for Synergistic CO2‐to‐Methanol Electrosynthesis
articles.abstract: The electrochemical reduction of CO2 to methanol (CH3OH) represents a promising strategy for mitigating global warming and energy shortages. However, the rational design of high‐performance electrocatalysts for selective CO2‐to‐CH3OH conversion remains challenging. Herein, we construct a dual‐site catalyst featuring Cu single atoms (CuSAs) and Bi nanoclusters (BiNCs) co‐anchored on a hierarchical porous nitrogen‐doped carbon (NC) support (CuSAsBiNCs/NC). It delivers a high CH3OH Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 73.6% with a stability of 120 h in an H‐cell, and reaches a CH3OH partial current density of 106.6 mA cm−2 with 82% FE in a flow cell. The excellent performance is attributed to a synergistic mechanism: CuSAs promote the generation and protonation of the key *CO intermediate, while BiNCs facilitate H2O dissociation to supply *H to adjacent Cu sites. Their electronic interaction strengthens *CO adsorption and lowers its protonation barrier at Cu sites, while accelerating H2O activation at Bi sites. Furthermore, the confinement effect of the hierarchical pore structure in the NC support facilitates the enrichment of *CO intermediate and stabilizes the catalyst. This work establishes a conceptual framework for developing synergistic electrocatalysts through precise atomic‐scale component integration, offering an appealing strategy to boost CH3OH production by simultaneously tuning *CO adsorption/protonation and H2O dissociation.

articles.title: Crystalline‐Amorphous Heterointerfaces Enable Elastic Peracetic Acid Activation for Resilient Remediation of Hypersaline Wastewater
articles.abstract: Hypersaline organic wastewater treatment is chronically impeded by mechanistic inhibition and rigid lattice inelasticity. Herein, we design a MnBiCoOx catalyst featuring crystalline-amorphous (C-A) heterointerfaces and propose a synergistic “remote electron pump-localized electronic depot” mechanism for peracetic acid (PAA) activation. This architecture leverages interfacial symmetry breaking and spin polarization to modulate eg orbital occupancy and d-d hybridization, establishing a resilient electronic structure with intrinsic charge-buffering capacity that ensures robust catalytic stability against hypersaline environments. Intriguingly, the presence of chloride ions (Cl−) induces a counterintuitive 2.58-fold kinetic acceleration, reframing halides as coordination-driven modulatory hubs that promote spin-polarized electron injection into PAA σ* antibonding orbitals. Quantitative contribution analysis identifies singlet oxygen (1O2) as the dominant matrix-tolerant species (65.47%), underscoring a mechanistic shift toward non-radical-mediated pathways. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the dz 2-mediated σ-bonding overlap, coupled with an upward shift of the d-band center, substantially reduces the activation barrier. Crucially, the MnBiCoOx/PAA system exhibits operational stability for 912 h in hypersaline wastewater, and life cycle assessment (LCA) confirms its exceptional environmental sustainability. This work provides mechanistic insights into rationally designing catalysts with structural resilience and electronic responsiveness for adaptive environmental remediation.

articles.title: Decouple and Synergize: D‐π Conjugation‐Enabled Remote Electronic Tuning of M‐O Sites for Enhanced C‐H/O‐H Cleavage in HMF Electrooxidation
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural oxidation reaction (HMFOR) is a green biomass valorization route, yet its scalability is constrained by the intrinsically sluggish hydroxymethyl oxidation on transition‐metal‐based catalysts, which, unlike aldehyde oxidation, requires concurrent C‐H/O‐H cleavage and C(sp3) → C(sp2) rehybridization. However, current strategies lack atomic‐scale precision to accelerate this kinetics and establish clear structure‐performance relationships. Herein, M3(HHTP)2 (M = Co, Cu) with atomically ordered and dispersed metal sites was designed to decouple intrinsic roles of M‐O sites in HMFOR. Building on this, bimetallic Co1.8Cu1.2(HHTP)2 was constructed, harnessing d‐π conjugation for precise bidirectional long‐range electronic communication between spatially separated M‐O sites: Cu‐O kinetically accelerates the sluggish hydroxymethyl oxidation on Co‐O, while Co‐O reciprocally mitigates Cu‐O poisoning from excessive HMF adsorption, establishing a self‐sustaining electronic synergy. Meanwhile, differentiated OH− adsorption on the dual sites optimizes the H‐bond network, accelerating electrochemical‐chemical cycle at Co‐O. Ultimately, Co1.8Cu1.2(HHTP)2 delivers a 2.7‐fold higher 2,5‐furandicarboxylic acid yield than Co3(HHTP)2 and enables gram‐scale production of 99.4%‐pure 2,5‐furandicarboxylic acid via 2,5‐diformylfuran and 5‐hydroxymethyl‐2‐furancarboxylic acid pathways. This work establishes d‐π conjugation as a general strategy to decouple and synergize specific roles of spatially separated sites to overcome the rate‐determining step, providing a novel paradigm for rational catalyst design in complex multi‐step reactions.

articles.title: Device–System Co‐Design of a Memristor‐Based 3D Convolutional Spiking Neural Network for Dynamic Vision Processing
articles.abstract: Dynamic image processing is a vital component of artificial intelligence and Internet of Things (IoT) applications. However, conventional image processing systems often suffer from high computational complexity and substantial power consumption. Memristors, as emerging nanoscale devices, offer promising advantages in terms of high‐density integration and energy‐efficient computing. In this work, we present a three‐dimensional convolutional spiking neural network (3D CSNN) system capable of efficiently processing dynamic visual data. A bio‐inspired spike encoder is implemented using volatile NbOx memristors, and its encoding characteristics are dynamically adjustable by introducing a time window strategy. In parallel, we introduce a high‐yield, stable anodic oxidation method for fabricating non‐volatile TaOx memristors. These devices are integrated into an array to perform 3D convolution operations, enabling effective extraction of both spatial and temporal features from dynamic input. By combining the low energy consumption of memristor‐based analog circuits with the high precision of digital logic, the digital‐analog hybrid system achieves a classification accuracy of 97% in gesture recognition tasks. This work establishes a scalable hardware paradigm for low‐power neuromorphic computing, providing new opportunities for next‐generation artificial vision and edge intelligence.

articles.title: Dual‐Dipole Synergy Breaks the Polarization‐Breakdown Trade‐Off for Ultrahigh Energy Density Flexible Capacitors
articles.abstract: A fundamental trade-off plagues dielectric capacitors: enhancing maximum polarization typically degrades breakdown strength, severely limiting energy density. Here we present a dual-dipole synergy strategy that resolves this contradiction. In layered perovskite films, we engineer an interlayer dipole driven by charge misalignment between functional layers, working in concert with the intralayer polyhedral dipole. Their synergy simultaneously amplifies polarization and strengthens the relaxor behavior and band gap that govern breakdown strength. Implemented in flexible SrBi5‑ x Pr x Ti4AlO18 capacitors, this design breaks the inverse coupling between maximum polarization and breakdown, delivering an ultrahigh energy density of 131.1 J∙cm−3 with 70.5% efficiency, a 179% enhancement over the unengineered counterpart. The capacitor retains excellent stability over 106 bending cycles. This work establishes a generalizable design paradigm wherein the vertical interlayer dipole acts as a new degree of freedom to independently tune polarization and breakdown in layered dielectrics, opening a transformative route beyond the classic trade-off.

articles.title: Dual‐Dipole Synergy Breaks the Polarization‐Breakdown Trade‐Off for Ultrahigh Energy Density Flexible Capacitors (Adv. Funct. Mater. 90/2026)
articles.abstract: Flexible Capacitors Dual‐dipole synergy breaks the polarization‐breakdown trade‐off in flexible layered perovskite capacitors. Pr doping drives site‐selective migration, generating an interlayer dipole that couples with the intralayer dipole. This synergy delivers an ultrahigh energy density of 131.1 J·cm−3 with 70.5% efficiency and robust stability over 106 bending cycles, offering a generalizable design paradigm for high‐performance dielectric energy storage. More details can be found in the Research Article by Yueshun Zhao and co‐workers (DOI: 10.1002/adfm.78265).

articles.title: Dual‐Spatial Confinement Engineered Mixed Matrix Membranes Toward Ultra‐Efficient Isobutanol Separation
articles.abstract: Metal-organic framework (MOF) based mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs) present significant promise for biofuel recovery. However, they are still plagued by key challenges for practical applications, including poor dispersibility of fillers and insufficient selectivity. Herein, a novel dual-spatial confinement strategy (D-SCS) to design ionic liquid (IL)-loaded graphene oxide (GO)/MOF-polymer MMMs is proposed. MOFs are first confined onto the surface of GO to promote their ordered dispersion in the polymer matrix. Subsequently, ILs are incorporated into the MOF pores to enhance the intermolecular interactions between MOF and isobutanol. By optimizing the alkyl chain length and content of ILs in the MOF pores, the hydrophobicity and free volume of the filler can be balanced. With the application of D‑SCS strategy, the resulting membrane delivered a high permeation flux of 5049.1 g·m− 2·h− 1 and a separation factor of 61.01 at 50°C, which were enhanced by 200.6% and 223.5%, respectively, in comparison with the pristine polyether block amide (PEBA, Pebax 2533) membrane. Moreover, theoretical calculations indicate that isobutanol shows higher adsorption selectivity and faster diffusion in GO/MOF‑808‑BMIM/PEBA membrane than in MOF‑808/PEBA and other MOF‑808‑ILs/PEBA membranes. This work provides a new approach for the construction of high-performance MMMs for efficient biofuel separation.

articles.title: Dynamic Matrix Competition Enables Host‐to‐Guest Reversal for Tailoring Carbon Dots Afterglow From Time‐Dependent Color to White Emission
articles.abstract: Room‐temperature afterglow carbon dots (CDs) materials, combining long‐lived emission, low toxicity, structural tunability, and ease of processing, hold significant application prospects in information encryption, anti‐counterfeiting, lighting, and sensing. However, existing boric acid (BA)‐based CDs afterglow systems generally suffer from issues such as single‐color emission, limited stimulus‐response dimensions, and unclear matrix regulation mechanisms. Herein, a BA/NaOH dual‐matrix system was developed, in which CDs afterglow can be precisely regulated by matrix ratio, achieving orange‐to‐green and orange‐to‐cyan time‐dependent color‐changing afterglow, and white afterglow. Through structural characterization of the composites, it was found that with increasing NaOH content, the confinement environment transitioned from a BA‐dominated B‐O network to a NaOH‐dominated borate structure, Na ionic bonds, and a deprotonated CDs surface. The specific regulatory mechanism of NaOH on each emission center in the composites was elucidated as promoting the generation and enhancement of short‐wavelength thermally activated delayed fluorescence while suppressing long‐wavelength room‐temperature phosphorescence.
