We tested serum for dengue NS1 antigen and IgM antibody by ELISA; positive NS1 samples underwent RT-PCR and serotyping. We estimated proportions with 95% confidence intervals (CI) and used logistic regression to examine adjusted associations. Results: Among 2,936 participants, 204 were NS1- and/or IgM-positive (6.95%; 95% CI, 6.05-7.93%): 31 were NS1-only, 161 IgM-only, and 12 dual-positive. Prevalence ranged from 3.88% (95% CI, 2.19-6.31%) at Kintampo to 12.32% (9.56-15.55%) at Atebubu, both in Bono East. Adjusted odds increased with age (aOR per five years, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.05-1.14). Eight of 43 NS1-positive samples contained dengue RNA: five DENV-1 from Bono East and three DENV-3 from Upper West. There was no clear rainy-dry season difference. Conclusions: Dengue NS1 and/or IgM were detected among febrile patients at all six facilities, and RT-PCR confirmed circulation of DENV-1 and DENV-3. These findings support including dengue in febrile illness evaluation and strengthening laboratory-supported surveillance in Ghana. Keywords: dengue, febrile illness, NS1 antigen, IgM, DENV-1, DENV-3, Ghana

articles.title: Detection of early-stage cancer using similarity-based classification of cell-free DNA fragmentation patterns
articles.abstract: Current cancer screening efforts face the dual problems of low patient adherence and a lack of available tests for many cancers, which motivates the development of less invasive multi-cancer early detection strategies. Such strategies will likely involve the use of liquid biopsies, which can analyze biomarkers found in blood for the presence of cancer. We introduce Blackjack, a new detection approach that focuses on the fragmentation patterns of plasma-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA). Blackjack characterizes a person's cfDNA fragmentation sites with a position probability matrix (PPM) that encodes information about the sequence context of the sites. For classification, Blackjack computes two features that represent the similarity of an individual's PPM to those of known healthy and cancer cohorts. With these two features, Blackjack then uses logistic regression to classify a new sample as being from a healthy individual or a person with cancer. In cross-validation experiments using two external whole genome sequencing datasets, Blackjack showed high performance, achieving a minimum area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.993 and minimum sensitivity (Sn) of 91.8% (at 98% specificity). This high performance was also present for stage I (AUC 0.991, Sn 89.8%) and stage II cancers (AUC 0.993, Sn 90.2%), and across eight different cancers (minimum AUC 0.985, minimum Sn 80.0%). We demonstrate that Blackjack's accuracy is stable at low simulated sequencing depths (~0.24x), and that tissue of origin prediction using Blackjack's similarity measures is high (minimum 82% accuracy of the top two predicted tissues). Our findings show that cfDNA fragmentation site contexts have valuable signals for early cancer detection, and that developing diagnostics with machine learning can benefit from a focus on having a small number of informative features.

articles.title: Displaced by a Volcano: Adolescent Well-Being in Uncertain Times in Iceland 2023-2026
articles.abstract: Aims: The November 2023 evacuation of Grindavik, Iceland, left families facing prolonged uncertainty about return. We examined adolescent well-being before and after evacuation and changes in gaps with national peers between 2025 and 2026. Methods: Repeated cross-sectional analyses used the 2023, 2025, and 2026 Icelandic Youth Study waves, adjusting for grade, gender, and non-Icelandic background. The town's single school in 2023 provided the pre-evacuation benchmark, with models accounting for national time trends. Adolescents who moved before evacuation provided a mobility benchmark. Results: In 2025, evacuees reported lower life satisfaction and school belonging, more psychosomatic symptoms, and higher odds of school absence and past-30-day substance use than the national reference group. The three well-being outcomes departed from the pre-evacuation pattern. Life-satisfaction and belonging gaps were larger among girls than boys in 2025, but these gender differences narrowed by 2026. Comparisons with prior movers suggested a distinct evacuation-related pattern in 2025 among evacuee girls, who reported lower life satisfaction and school belonging than prior-mover girls. In 2026, psychosomatic symptoms (B = 0.29, 95% CI [0.08, 0.49]), absenteeism (OR = 1.81, 95% CI [1.26, 2.60]), and substance use (OR = 2.59, 95% CI [1.75, 3.84]) remained higher relative to the national reference group. Life satisfaction and belonging were directionally lower, with intervals including zero. Change estimates did not establish narrowing of the gaps. Conclusions: The findings underscore the need for sustained educational and well-being support to address adolescents' social connections alongside their mental health during prolonged displacement, including in a Nordic welfare setting.

articles.title: Effect of starting metformin on severe and long COVID-19 among people living with type 2 diabetes in England: a new user cohort study in OpenSAFELY-TPP
articles.abstract: Introduction: Observational studies report lower COVID-19 mortality among metformin users, but most used prevalent-user designs comparing long-term survivors with heterogeneous controls. Randomised trials suggest little or no mortality effect. No large observational study has used a new-user design to estimate the effect of starting versus not starting metformin on severe and Long COVID outcomes in adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D). We aimed to estimate this effect on COVID-19-related hospitalisation or death, COVID-19 diagnoses, and Long COVID among adults with T2D in England. Research design and methods: Using OpenSAFELY-TPP linked NHS electronic health records, we conducted a population-based cohort study with a landmark new-user design. Adults aged 18-85 years newly diagnosed with T2D (August 2018-August 2019) were classified as starting metformin monotherapy within 6 months or not starting any antidiabetic drug, based on prescription data. Follow-up began 6 months after diagnosis and before the UK pandemic (avoiding immortal time) for up to 2 years. We estimated intention-to-treat and per-protocol effects using weighted Cox and pooled logistic regression, with negative (bone fracture) and positive (diabetes-related death) control outcomes. Results: Of 52,341 eligible people, 19,599 (37.4%) started metformin. For COVID-19-related hospitalisation or death, the maximally adjusted hazard ratio (HR) of metformin versus no antidiabetic was 1.17 (95% CI 1.02-1.35; 2-year risk difference 0.36%, 95% CI 0.09-0.62; intention-to-treat). The per-protocol HR for COVID-19-related hospitalisation or death was 1.11 (95% CI 0.96-1.29). The Long COVID estimate was imprecise (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.83-2.33; intention-to-treat). For bone fracture (negative control) the estimate was null (HR 1.00), but for diabetes-related deaths (positive control) it was elevated (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.09-1.81), indicating unmeasured confounding. Conclusions: The risks of severe and long COVID were slightly higher among people who started metformin, compared with those who did not start. These results plausibly reflect unmeasured confounding. These findings align more closely with randomised evidence than earlier prevalent-user studies and argue against a clinically meaningful benefit of starting metformin for COVID-19 prevention in newly diagnosed T2D.

articles.title: Ethical Risks and Governance of Consumer Electroencephalography-Based Neurotechnology: Qualitative Interview Study With Expert Stakeholders
articles.abstract: Background Consumer electroencephalography (EEG)-based neurotechnologies are rapidly expanding across commercial digital health delivery networks and wellness markets. Positioned at the intersection of non-medical self-monitoring and clinical applications, these consumer devices introduce complex challenges for device governance and digital bioethics regarding product claims, data privacy, evidential substantiation, and user protection. Objective This qualitative study examined expert stakeholder perspectives on the ethical, regulatory, and data governance challenges of consumer EEG neurotechnology, focusing on the allocation of responsibility across product lifecycles. Methods We conducted semi-structured interviews with 19 expert stakeholders spanning research, clinical practice, engineering, industry, ethics, law, and regulatory policy across North America, Europe, and Latin America. Interview data were systematically analysed using reflexive thematic analysis to examine how governance challenges, evidence burdens, and responsibilities are conceptualized across the neurotechnology ecosystem. Results Five interrelated themes emerged: (1) Regulatory Category Boundaries and Oversight; (2) Evidential Credibility and Claims-Related Harm; (3) Neurodata Privacy, Security, and Inference; (4) Layered Governance and Explicit Accountability; and (5) Participation, Global Equity, and Contextual Responsiveness. Participants identified major friction in applying traditional medical oversight to nonmedical digital health uses, linked unverified claims to user vulnerability, and expressed concern over downstream neurodata processing. A connecting synthesis demonstrates that oversight responsibilities span multiple actors and development stages rather than resting on a single regulatory mechanism. Conclusions Effective governance of consumer EEG digital health devices requires explicit allocation of duties for claims substantiation, data practices, and user safety, backed by inclusive stakeholder participation and contextual responsiveness.

articles.title: Excluded causal variants produce false discoveries in genetic fine-mapping
articles.abstract: Statistical fine-mapping seeks to distinguish causal genetic variants from correlated variants in linkage disequilibrium (LD). Although fine-mapping algorithms perform well in simulations, they are often applied in settings that violate their assumptions. In particular, genome-wide association study (GWAS) and quantitative trait locus (QTL) workflows routinely omit variants with minor allele frequency (MAF) below 1% and most insertions and deletions (indels), excluding many causal variants before fine-mapping begins. To assess this empirically, we compared filtered and unfiltered fine-mapping at 499 All of Us loci. Twenty percent of high-confidence calls after a 1% MAF filter, and 32% when indels were also omitted, lacked support in the unfiltered analysis. Errors were particularly enriched when tested variants tagged an omitted variant, so fine-mapping misassigned its signal to a proxy variant. At ABO, omitting the frameshift that defines blood group O gave near-certain posterior inclusion probabilities (PIPs) to linked single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). To address this disconnect, we developed SuSiE-OUT, which enables fine-mapping in scenarios with possibly omitted causal variants. Modeling infinitesimal effects did not reliably prevent these errors, whereas imputing omitted variants or modeling them with our SuSiE-OUT method prevented most errors. Overall, we find that common analysis workflows substantially increase false discoveries in fine-mapping analyses, and we demonstrate two approaches to mitigate this challenge.

articles.title: Exploring Data Augmentation for Stroke Severity Prediction: How Generative AI Enhances EEG Signal Classification
articles.abstract: In clinical datasets, data augmentation is often avoided because it can remove important unusual values, known as outliers, which are important for understanding diseases accurately. However, clinical EEG datasets often suffer from two key limitations: small sample sizes and class imbalance, which significantly reduce classification performance. To overcome these challenges, this study applies generative AI-based data augmentation techniques with a carefully designed hybrid pipeline that effectively enhances performance even on limited EEG data. Using EEG signals from 50 brain stroke patients, we investigate both traditional oversampling methods (SMOTE and ADASYN) and advanced generative models, including WGAN and WGAN-GP. Our proposed pipeline involves preprocessing EEG recordings, extracting comprehensive statistical and frequency-domain features, applying feature reduction, and evaluating multiple machine learning classifiers. Experimental results show that the combination of SelectKBest feature selection, SVM classifier, and WGAN-GP augmentation achieves the highest classification accuracy of 72%, outperforming other methods. This work introduces a novel hybrid approach for EEG-based stroke severity classification, demonstrating that generative augmentation, when integrated properly, can significantly improve performance on small clinical datasets. To the best of our knowledge, this combination of techniques has not been explored before on any dataset, providing a solid foundation for future research in automated EEG-based stroke diagnosis.

articles.title: Five Days of Acute Intermittent Hypoxia Is Safe and Improves Somatic Motor Function in Persons with Multiple Sclerosis
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES Walking impairment affects up to 75% of persons with multiple sclerosis (MS), and the benefits of rehabilitation are constrained by limited capacity for training-induced neuroplasticity. Acute intermittent hypoxia (AIH), brief repeated exposures to low inspired oxygen, triggers serotonin-dependent spinal plasticity that enhances motor output. In spinal cord injury, daily AIH paired with walking training has produced larger walking gains than training alone, positioning AIH as a promising primer for rehabilitation. Before AIH can be combined with training in MS, its safety and stand-alone effects with repeated daily dosing must be established in a population with demyelinating disease. We therefore conducted the first multi-day AIH trial in persons with MS to characterize safety and tolerability and to evaluate preliminary effects on ankle strength and walking. METHODS Twenty-three ambulatory adults with MS (Expanded Disability Status Scale [EDSS] 3.0-6.5; 15 relapsing-remitting, 8 secondary-progressive) completed a randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled crossover trial. Participants received AIH (15 x ~60 s episodes; FiO2 = 0.09; SpO2 target 84-88%) and Sham in a counterbalanced order, separated by a washout of at least 4 weeks. Assessments at pre-intervention, post-intervention, and follow-up included ankle plantarflexion and dorsiflexion torque, 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT), Timed 25-Foot Walk (T25FW), and MS Walking Scale-12 (MSWS-12). Treatment effects were estimated using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) with participant as a random effect. RESULTS No serious adverse events related to the intervention were reported, and follow-up MRI showed no new MS activity in either arm. Mean nadir SpO2 during AIH was 84.7 +/- 0.2%, and cardiovascular parameters returned to baseline within minutes of each session completion. Ankle plantarflexion torque was significantly greater following AIH than Sham (beta = 8.74 Nm, p < 0.001), with mean increases of 17.5% at post-intervention and 29.2% at follow-up. Six-minute walk distance was also significantly greater after AIH (beta = 10.14 m, p = 0.039). Dorsiflexion torque (p = 0.202), T25FW time (p = 0.239), and MSWS-12 score (p = 0.564) did not differ significantly between conditions. Greater elevation in heart rate during hypoxic episodes was associated with larger strength gains at follow-up (r = 0.58, p = 0.009). CONCLUSIONS: Daily AIH sessions are safe and well tolerated in persons with MS across a clinically heterogeneous disability range and produce significant improvements in ankle plantarflexion strength and walking endurance. These findings support combining AIH with task-specific gait training in future trials.

articles.title: Handheld, quantitative phase imaging probe for skin evaluation at subcellular resolution in vivo, in real-time, and in 3D
articles.abstract: Skin cancer is the most common malignancy in the United States. The gold standard for diagnosis of skin cancer is histopathological analysis via tissue biopsy. However, identifying which lesions to biopsy remains a significant clinical challenge, particularly at early stages of disease. In this work, we present a volumetric quantitative oblique back-illumination microscopy (qOBM) probe, a highly maneuverable, handheld imaging system capable of providing high-resolution, 3D visualization of the skin microstructure. We show the probe is capable of visualizing the dynamic, layered microstructure of the epidermis and the top of the dermis across all Fitzpatrick skin types in human skin in vivo. The easy maneuverability of the probe is highlighted by imaging anatomically challenging areas typically hard to reach for bulkier systems. Finally, we present additional case studies in ex vivo murine models and in vivo human nevi that further illustrate the potential clinical applications of the volumetric handheld probe. These results establish a low-cost, easy to use, high-resolution, compact system that combines the strengths of its predecessors -- the excellent maneuverability of the widely-used dermatoscopes and 3D, high-resolution imaging of prior bulkier systems -- to improve screening of dermatological lesions at the bedside.

articles.title: Higher platelet counts are associated with migraine risk across three cohorts among more than 21,000 cases
articles.abstract: Objective We assessed potential associations between migraine and complete blood cell count (CBC) data in three large population-based studies. Background Platelets are thought to be involved in migraine pathology through increased activation during an attack. Migraine attacks are often treated with NSAIDs that inhibit platelets, or triptans that target serotonin receptors, with serotonin being most highly expressed in circulation within platelet granules. However, the exact role of platelets in migraine remains unclear. Methods The UK BioBank (UKBB) has CBC data available from baseline blood samples and migraine diagnoses were obtained through self-report and electronic health records. CBC and migraine data from the 1999-2000, 2001-2002, and 2003-2004 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) study were obtained during single exam visits. CBCs were obtained from Framingham Heart Study (FHS) participants. Migraine history was assessed through clinical diagnostic impressions. The UKBB sample (18,919 cases (4,580 incident); 448,339 controls) was the primary discovery cohort for CBCs, with replication meta-analysis done in NHANES (1,887 cases; 7,242 controls) and FHS (395 cases (229 incident); 3,172 controls). Our primary model adjusted for age and sex, with secondary analysis adjusting for additional factors. Sex-stratified, sex-interaction and ancestry-stratified (UKBB only) analyses were also performed. Results Migraine was associated with platelet count (PLT) in the UKBB (OR=1.058, 95% CI [1.043,1.073], p=2.09E-14) and was replicated in the NHANES-FHS meta-analysis (OR=1.074, 95% CI [1.025,1.126], p=0.003). PLT also drove multiple significant signals of PLT-involved CBC ratios. While neutrophil counts and hemoglobin were associated with migraine in UKBB, these did not replicate in FHS-NHANES meta-analysis. Conclusion Higher platelet count is associated with an increased likelihood of migraine. Further studies with longitudinal assessments of CBCs and migraine attacks are needed to further understand the role of platelets in the onset of migraine attacks.

articles.title: How Many Time-Critical Emergencies? A Population-Based National Estimate of Attended Events per 100,000 US Residents
articles.abstract: Objectives. To estimate how many time-critical emergencies fire and emergency medical services (EMS) crews attend each year per 100,000 US residents. We counted events in which a crew reached a living patient or a trapped person whose outcome plausibly depends on how soon effective treatment starts. Methods. For 30 medical conditions, we took annual counts from US registries and datasets, or multiplied a national incidence count by the share of patients EMS attended. A condition was Tier A when a published study linked a measured delay, from minutes to a few hours, to death or major disability. Conditions whose time sensitivity rests on guidelines or expert consensus were Tier B. Fire and rescue events came from twelve months of National Emergency Response Information System public data, scaled to national totals. We removed double counting between conditions. Results. Crews attended an estimated 589 time-critical events per 100,000 residents a year (494 to 697 with every condition at its low or high value), equal to 4.3% of 9-1-1 EMS activations. Medical conditions accounted for 583 after removing overlap. Of these, 350 were Tier A, led by ischemic stroke (120.2) and EMS-treated cardiac arrest (78.7). Opioid overdose (123.4) led the 233 Tier B events. Those three conditions made up 55% of the medical total. Fire and rescue events added 6. Conclusions. At national rates, a US community of 100,000 can expect its fire and EMS crews to attend about 589 events a year in which time to treatment may change the outcome. That is roughly 11 a week, nearly all of them medical. The count measures how often response time can matter in the events crews attend, and it gives a denominator for valuing a faster response.

articles.title: Inactivating mutations in polyadenylation factor CSTF2 disrupt intronic polyadenylation patterns and are associated with intellectual disability.
articles.abstract: Alternative polyadenylation contributes extensively to transcript diversification and is particularly prominent during neuronal differentiation; however, its contribution to monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders remains incompletely understood. CSTF2 encodes an RNA-binding subunit of the cleavage stimulation factor complex and has previously been associated with X-linked intellectual disability through a single Asp50Ala missense variant with increased RNA-binding activity. Here, we identify seven rare CSTF2 variants in ten hemizygous male probands with intellectual disability, global developmental delay and/or autism spectrum disorder, including missense, nonsense, splice-site, and frameshift variants. Functional analysis of selected variants using RNA sequencing and 3'-end-proximal sequencing in CSTF2-depleted cells identified Phe19Leu, Gln543ter, Leu555Ser as strongly functionally impairing variants. These variants predominantly reduced usage of intronic polyadenylation sites while increasing usage of downstream sites within terminal 3'UTRs. Suppressed intronic sites were enriched for GU-rich sequence elements, were more evolutionarily conserved, and showed higher predicted polyadenylation-site strength, consistent with preferential impairment of CSTF2-dependent polyadenylation. In contrast, the previously reported Asp50Ala variant produced an opposing pattern, with preferential activation of intronic polyadenylation sites, consistent with its increased RNA-binding activity. These findings indicate that both reduced and increased CSTF2 activity disrupt the balance of polyadenylation-site usage and can result in neurodevelopmental disorder. Our data provide genetic and functional support for CSTF2 as an X-linked neurodevelopmental disorder gene, identify inactivating CSTF2 variants as a disease mechanism, and implicate dysregulation of intronic polyadenylation in human intellectual disability.

articles.title: LLM Embeddings Complement Theory-Driven Language Features and Cognitive Scores for APOE4 and Aβ Prediction
articles.abstract: Spontaneous language offers a scalable, noninvasive approach for identifying biological indicators of preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD). We examined prediction of APOE4 carrier status and cerebral amyloid-beta burden using Cookie Theft picture descriptions from two cohorts of Hebrew- and English-speaking participants (IRAP, N=134; WRAP, N=1,541). Amyloid-beta burden was classified using lowest-quartile, median, and highest-quartile cutoffs, capturing accumulation below conventional amyloid-positivity thresholds. We compared embeddings from pretrained large language models (LLMs) with standard cognitive test scores, reflecting conventional clinical assessment, and theory-driven linguistic features, reflecting traditional language analysis. Embedding-based models achieved the highest F1 scores among constituent models in five of eight tasks involving APOE4 status and global amyloid-beta burden. High prediction disagreement suggested complementary signals across approaches. An any-positive ensemble significantly outperformed every constituent model and a prior-informed random baseline across all eight tasks, and significantly outperformed all constituent models in 21 of 24 regional amyloid-beta tasks. These findings highlight the complementarity of LLM-based, theory-driven, and cognitive measures for predicting AD-related genetic risk and amyloid pathology, and support further investigation of their potential for early screening approaches.

articles.title: Lamina Cribrosa Strain as a Glaucoma Prognostic Factor: The STRAIN Study Methodology and Initial Outcomes
articles.abstract: Objective: To estimate the lamina cribrosa (LC) strain response to intraocular pressure (IOP) change in open angle glaucoma (OAG) patients and examine associations between LC strain and demographic and clinical characteristics relevant to OAG in an ongoing longitudinal study. Design: Cohort study Participants: Adult patients with OAG (205 eyes of 119 patients) Methods: The STRAIN study is an ongoing longitudinal study designed to determine whether LC biomechanical strain is associated with present, prior, and future OAG damage. In this initial analysis, patients either temporarily stopped [≥] 1 eye drop, initiated an eye drop, or underwent selective laser trabeculoplasty to produce IOP change. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans of the optic nerve head (ONH) acquired before and up to several weeks after IOP change were analyzed using digital volume correlation (DVC) to estimate LC strain. Strain measurements were compared with age, race, sex, axial length, central corneal thickness (CCT), corneal hysteresis, optic disc area, years of known OAG, retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness, and visual field mean deviation (MD). Main Outcome Measures: LC strain estimated by DVC from OCT scans acquired before and after IOP alteration. Results: Axial LC strain (Ezz) was tensile with IOP decrease and compressive with IOP increase. Maximum principal strain was tensile (mean Emax = 1.09%), and maximum shear strain was positive (mean{Gamma} max = 1.16%) in the radial-axial plane. Both increased quadratically with the IOP change. Older age was significantly related to greater tensile circumferential strain (p = 0.02) and lower{Gamma} max (p = 0.01). Sex, CCT, corneal hysteresis, and optic disc area were not significantly associated with LC strain. In combined multivariable models adjusting for IOP change, demographics, and accounting for correlations between eyes from the same patient, eyes with thinner inferior-quadrant RNFL had smaller{Gamma} max for a given IOP change (p = 0.02). Conclusions: LC strain in patients with OAG is associated with the degree of neuronal loss, age, and axial length, supporting a relationship between the LC biomechanical response and factors relevant to glaucomatous damage.

articles.title: Large Language Models to Label CT Radiology Reports for Incidental Findings Found in Lung Cancer Screening: A Comparative Analysis
articles.abstract: In this study, LLM and prompting strategies for labeling Specific Incidental Findings (SIFs) occurring during lung cancer screening, in radiology reports were compared. In this retrospective study, 300 CT reports from a Dutch academic hospital were included between 19th March 2003 and 28th December 2020. GPT-5, GPT-4-Turbo, Llama-3.1-8B-INST, MedGemma-4B-IT, a keyword-based search method, and a radiologist labelled the reports for the presence or absence of nine SIFs. The radiologist's scores were the reference standard. Each LLM was evaluated with four different prompting strategies: two without Chain-of-Thought (CoT), and two with CoT (one zero shot, one few shot). The automated labelling methods were evaluated against the radiologist primarily using Cohen's Kappa, and additionally sensitivity, specificity, and F1 scores. GPT-5 achieved substantial or almost perfect agreement for seven out of nine SIFs: aortic valve disease, bronchiectasis, consolidation, coronary artery calcification, emphysema, abnormality in mediastinal lymph nodes, and thyroid abnormalities, with Cohen $\kappa$ values of 0.81 (0.70, 0.93), 0.97 (0.93, 1.00), 0.71 (0.62, 0.82), 0.92 (0.87, 0.96), 0.91 (0.84, 0.97), 0.71 (0.62, 0.80), and 0.92 (0.86, 0.98) respectively. For the remaining two SIFs, moderate LLM agreement was obtained with MedGemma-4B-IT and with GPT-4-Turbo with Cohen $\kappa$ values of 0.48 (0.40, 0.60), 0.42 (0.31, 0.58) for interstitial lung abnormalities and mediastinal mass respectively. The highest agreement was obtained with the non-CoT prompt strategies for most SIFs. This study demonstrated that LLMs can automatically label radiology reports with agreement ranging from almost perfect to moderate, but not one LLM -- prompt combination achieved the highest agreement across all SIFs.

articles.title: Lipidome-wide analysis of concurrent and longitudinal blood pressure patterns in school-aged children
articles.abstract: Background: Elevated blood pressure (BP) in childhood is associated with cardiovascular risk, but its molecular lipid correlates remain poorly characterized. We investigated the association of plasma lipid species and patterns with concurrent and longitudinal BP phenotypes in school-aged children. Methods: In the Belgian ENVIRONAGE prospective birth-cohort, 195 children aged 9 to 12 years were examined between July 2021 and September 2024. A total of 1,232 plasma lipid species were quantified using liquid chromatography-electrospray ionization-tandem mass spectrometry. Associations with systolic and diastolic BP percentiles were examined using multivariable linear regression with permutation-based family-wise error rate (FWER) correction. Lipid-set enrichment analysis, with P values from sample permutation to account for correlation among lipid species, evaluated coordinated associations. Significant findings were examined across longitudinal BP patterns in 177 children with BP measured at ages 4-6 and 9-12. Findings: Each 1-SD increase in triglyceride (TG) 58:9 fatty acyl (FA) 22:4 was associated with 7.36 higher systolic BP percentile points (95% CI=3.91-10.80; P_FWER=0.03). TG 58:9 FA 22:4 was associated with incident (OR=2.78; 95% CI=1.33-5.79) and persistent (OR=2.14; 95% CI=1.22-3.77), but not resolved elevated BP vs stable-normal BP. Among lipid sets, species with a total carbon number of 38, mainly PC and PE, were inversely enriched with diastolic BP percentile. Interpretation: Childhood BP was associated with higher levels of a highly polyunsaturated long-chain TG, closely related to current BP elevation and not elevated among children whose BP had normalized.

articles.title: LungAI: An AI Biomarker that Refines Lung-RADS v2022 Triage of Screen-Detected Pulmonary Nodules
articles.abstract: Background: The Lung-RADS algorithm standardizes the management of screen-detected pulmonary nodules, but its risk assessment is driven chiefly by nodule size and attenuation. This misallocates a meaningful fraction of patients: a nontrivial share of small malignancies receive 12-month surveillance while large benign nodules proceed to invasive workup. Artificial intelligence (AI) may supply risk information independent of the imaging features Lung-RADS already uses. Methods: We validated LungAI, an investigational deep learning nodule malignancy classifier not yet cleared by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), on the held-out NLST test partition of Ardila et al. (2,747 low-dose CT examinations from 1,244 patients with at least 1 solid or part-solid 4-30 mm nodule; 89 pathologically confirmed cancers, prevalence 3.2%). We compared discrimination against Sybil, mean nodule diameter, and estimated nodule volume. A board-certified radiologist assigned Lung-RADS v2022 categories to a positives-enriched random subset (226 eligible examinations; 78 cancers), projected to the full cohort by contingency weighting. A per-category reclassification algorithm shifted patients along the existing Lung-RADS management ladder using a-priori score cutpoints. We evaluated a separately locked follow-up configuration on examinations with a prior scan. Results: LungAI achieved AUROC 0.92 (95% CI 0.88-0.95) and AUPRC 0.47 (0.35-0.61), outperforming Sybil (delta AUROC 0.07; delta AUPRC 0.18), diameter (delta AUROC 0.14; delta AUPRC 0.34), and volume (delta AUROC 0.14; delta AUPRC 0.38; all P<0.001). Against Lung-RADS v2022 scored ordinally on the weighted annotated subset, LungAI improved AUPRC (delta AUPRC 0.31, P=0.003) but not AUROC (delta AUROC 0.03, P=0.20). LungAI added discriminative information independent of diameter (likelihood-ratio chi squared = 161, P < 10e-36; delta AUROC 0.10) and, on follow-up examinations, independent of delta diameter, volume doubling time, and new-nodule status (chi squared = 79, P < 10e-18). Integrated with Lung-RADS, LungAI reduced cancers on the slowest (12-month rescan) pathway by 46% (3.1 --> 1.6 per 1,000 examinations) and benign biopsy referrals by 20% (32.7 --> 26.2 per 1,000 examinations) at approximately unchanged total biopsy volume (51.0 --> 50.1 per 1,000). Assuming full adherence to recommended follow-up, the combined approach yielded 25 months of net diagnostic lead time, an estimated net cost saving of ~$2,200, and 6.5 fewer benign biopsies per 1,000 examinations; accounting for published adherence rates, it yielded 1.6 additional cancer diagnoses within 1 year per 1,000 examinations. Conclusions: LungAI contributes malignancy-risk information orthogonal to the size- and growth-based features underlying Lung-RADS and improves the allocation of screening patients across the existing management spectrum while potentially decreasing invasive procedures for benign lesions. Multi-site, multi-geography validation is required to demonstrate practical generalizability.

articles.title: Measuring community building in group antenatal care: Evidence from a randomized trial in Malawi
articles.abstract: Improving the quality of antenatal care is essential for reducing persistently high maternal and neonatal mortality in Malawi. Group antenatal care has demonstrated improvements in quality, satisfaction, health behaviors, and outcomes. However, the impact of community building, one of the model’s core components, has not previously been quantitatively assessed. This study examined the measurement properties of two community building measures, assessed the impact of group antenatal care on these measures, and explored their potential role as mediators of health outcomes. This secondary analysis used quantitative data from the parent study testing the effectiveness of group antenatal care at seven clinics in Blantyre District, Malawi. The Perinatal Peer Support Scale and the Provider Connectedness subscale of the Pregnancy Related Empowerment Scale were used to measure community building and were validated using factor analyses. Results supported a two-factor structure for perinatal peer support (relational support and peer network) and a unidimensional structure for provider connectedness. Using generalized linear modeling, we found that participation in group antenatal care was associated with significantly stronger community building across all measures when compared to usual individual antenatal care. Women in group antenatal care demonstrated higher relational support score, peer network, and provider connectedness scores compared with women in individual antenatal care (p < 0.001). However, we found no evidence that community building had direct or indirect (mediating) effects on maternal psychological distress or infant birthweight. This study strengthens the evidence base for group antenatal care by validating measures of community building and showing that relational support, peer networks, and provider connectedness are important benefits of participation. Although community building did not mediate the outcomes examined here, the findings highlight the need to further test of theoretical pathways linking group antenatal care to maternal and child health outcomes.

articles.title: Metabolome-derived kidney function scores as prognostic readouts of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic health.
articles.abstract: Kidney disease is a rapidly growing global health concern, tightly linked to cardiovascular and metabolic disease within the recently defined cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome. Routine clinical assessment of kidney function primarily relies on creatinine-based estimated glomerular filtration rates (eGFRcr) which can be affected by non-renal factors and declines only after substantial kidney damage. Using data from the MetaCardis study (N=1,723), we derived metabolomic kidney function gaps (mKFGs)-the difference between metabolome-predicted eGFRcr and measured eGFRcr. A physiology-guided feature-selection strategy - anchored on three cardiometabolic markers (haemoglobin, albumin and the Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio) that associate with mKFGs but not with eGFRcr - yielded compact sex-stratified metabolite panels (40-98 out of 1,514 metabolites) that tracked cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk. Machine-Learning models revealed distinct metabolic signatures, including biomarkers of meat consumption and androgens, highlighting potential sex-specific pathways linked to CKM health. External validation in the general-population Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging (N=9,958) and German Chronic Kidney Disease Study (N=5,113) cohorts revealed that mKFGs added incremental predictive value for future CKM events and all-cause mortality beyond eGFRcr and established risk equations. Our findings open new avenues for personalised risk stratification for CKM disease progression and targeted interventions based on metabolically defined kidney health.

articles.title: Natural-language cohort queries on a hospital data platform: accuracy and provenance in a real-world evaluation
articles.abstract: Background: Accessing routinely collected clinical data for research remains technically demanding across heterogeneous hospital systems. This proof-of-concept study aimed to evaluate the accuracy and query-level traceability of a commercial natural-language (NL) data-query platform implemented at a university hospital. Methods: An on-premises data integration platform with an NL query interface (AIRE; Briya, Tel Aviv, Israel) was connected to the institutional health data platform across three tertiary-care hospitals under an approved pseudonymization and governance framework. Implementation comprised regulatory and governance approval, and IT deployment. Twenty-five NL prompts addressing cohort identification and characterization in an adult ICD-10 C71-coded brain-tumor cohort (n = 1,594) were evaluated against manually written reference SQL and checked for a corresponding executed query in the exported log. Responses were classified into five categories. Prompts with unanswered or incorrect responses were re-posed in a new thread. Results: The platform was implemented over two years. Fifteen of 25 responses were exact (n = 11), concordant after definition alignment (n = 1), or incorrect but traceable from the logged SQL (n = 3); six were plausible but incorrect without a logged query, and four remained unanswered. No incorrect unlogged result recurred in a new thread. Across the initial and repeat evaluations, 22 of 23 logged responses were correct or traceable, whereas all eight unlogged responses were incorrect. Conclusions: Implementation was feasible but required substantial local institutional preparation. The NL interface reproduced SQL-derived results when definitions were explicit, while query-level provenance and verification of the displayed result were critical for identifying unreliable outputs.

articles.title: Accelerating CO2 Biocatalysis through Multimodal AI-Guided Enzyme Prioritization and Spatial Confinement
articles.abstract: Direct biological conversion of CO2 into value-added chemicals is severely restricted by sluggish enzyme kinetics and inefficient intracellular carbon flux. Here, we address these catalytic bottlenecks by synergizing multimodal deep learning, mechanistic enzyme engineering, and synthetic organelle assembly. Using CASKP, a TransKP-guided candidate-prioritization framework that integrates sequence representations with a docking-derived scalar feature, we prioritized and experimentally identified a highly active β-carbonic anhydrase, PbCA, for improving intracellular CO2 supply. Structural analysis and molecular dynamics simulations guided the design of the R71A and V112A variants. The R71A–V112A variant displayed a specific activity of 26.1 U/mg and increased the intracellular 13C-labeled 3-phosphoglycerate ratio 4.9-fold. The simulations were consistent with a more hydrated active-site environment and a strengthened Tyr108-centered hydrogen-bond network. To overcome diffusion and thermodynamic limitations, these optimized biocatalysts were encapsulated into hybrid carboxysomes and coupled with an ATP-generating carboxykinase. 13C tracing confirmed incorporation of inorganic carbon into l-malate, with 95.2% of malate detected as 13C-labeled isotopologues. Subsequent promoter optimization yielded an l-malate titer of 22.7 g/L. This multiscale approach provides an integrated strategy for heterotrophic CO2-incorporating biocatalysis.

articles.title: Catalytic Stereoselective Inverse Electron Demand Formal Aza-Diels–Alder: Access to Highly Congested Molecular Bowl-Shaped 3D Tertiary Amines
articles.abstract: Diastereoselective sp3-rich heteroatom-based bowl-shaped polycyclic molecules are a key structural scaffold in various bioactive molecules. Due to the inherent steric congestion of these structures, achieving precise stereochemical control remains a significant challenge in contemporary synthetic chemistry. We herein disclose a practical iron-catalyzed assembly of an indole-derived tertiary amine-based pentacyclic molecule through an intermolecular, iminium-triggered dearomative inverse electron-demand formal aza-Diels–Alder (IEDFADA) reaction. Detailed computational and deuterium labelling experiments strongly suggest that the diastereoselective formation of this complex core involves a stepwise in situ generation of a short-lived, highly reactive azadiene. Moreover, the negative slope (ρ = –0.29) from the Hammett plot indicates the formation of a partial positive charge and that the electron-donating groups enhance the reaction rate. Notably, the concise tagging of drug molecules and downstream synthetic transformations with good yields and diastereoselectivity should highlight the potential applications of this methodology in drug discovery settings in medicinal chemistry.

articles.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Accelerated Discovery of Doped Spinel Co3O4 Catalysts for the Oxygen Evolution Reaction
articles.abstract: The discovery of doped spinel Co3O4 electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is hindered by the large catalyst design space and the high computational cost of density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Here, we establish a hierarchical interpretable machine learning (ML) framework that decouples electronic structure prediction from catalytic activity prediction. By starting with predicting the electronic descriptor (d-band center) from readily accessible structural descriptors and subsequently predicting adsorption energetics, the framework removes the need for expensive electronic structure DFT calculations during catalyst screening while preserving physical interpretability. A random forest model was trained on adsorption free energies of OH*, O*, and OOH* from 144 representative active sites and achieved a test mean absolute error of 0.21 eV. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified surface energy, active site undercoordination, and the d-band center as the dominant descriptors governing adsorption energetics. To avoid additional DFT calculations of the d-band center during screening, a second ML model predicted it directly from structural and elemental descriptors with a test mean absolute error of 0.23 eV. The resulting framework enabled rapid evaluation of OER overpotentials across 252 active sites, while subsequent targeted DFT calculations identified Al-, Ca-, Fe-, and Mn-doped Co3O4 as promising candidates. Targeted DFT calculations and electrochemical measurements further validated the improved OER activity of Al- and Fe-doped Co3O4. This work establishes an interpretable and computationally efficient strategy for connecting structural descriptors, electronic properties, adsorption energetics, and experimentally measurable catalytic activity, thereby accelerating the discovery of high-performance spinel oxide catalysts.

articles.title: Structural Insights and Functional Expansion of an Aerobic Skatole Synthase
articles.abstract: SktA from the cyanobacterium Nostoc punctiforme NIES-2108 belongs to the versatile heme oxygenase-like domain-containing nonheme oxidase superfamily, whose natural function is to transform 5-bromotryptophan (5-Br-Trp) to 5-bromoskatole in an oxygen-dependent manner. As SktA is also capable of transforming tryptophan (Trp) to skatole, this enzyme represents a skatole synthase that operates under aerobic conditions. Here, the crystal structure of SktA and its complex with 5-Br-Trp and Trp are reported. The amino acids responsible for the substrate binding and the diiron cluster formation were revealed, and their roles in the catalytic reaction were examined via mutagenesis experiments. In addition, we found that SktA is capable of transforming 7-bromotryptophan and 5,7-dibromotryptophan to yield 7-bromoskatole and 5,7-dibromoskatole, respectively, and resolved the crystal structures of SktA in complex with these alternative substrates to elucidate the plasticity of the substrate-binding pocket. Finally, we show that combining SktA and regiospecific self-sufficient Trp halogenases in one-pot reaction systems efficiently transforms Trp to 5-bromo-7-iodo-skatole or 5-iodo-7-bromo-skatole. In summary, this study reveals the structural information, substrate scope, and potential applications in synthetic biology as a module to generate differentially halogenated skatoles of SktA.

articles.title: Tuning Supported Fe-Ag Catalysts for Selective Acetylene Hydrogenation: A Combined Experimental and Computational Study
articles.abstract: The selective hydrogenation of acetylene is a key reaction step for purification in ethylene production, as trace amounts of acetylene can poison downstream polymerization catalysts. Industrial acetylene hydrogenation is currently performed almost exclusively using palladium-based catalysts, motivating the search for more abundant alternatives. In this study, supported Fe-Ag catalysts with different Fe:Ag ratios were synthesized and evaluated for the selective hydrogenation of acetylene under industrially relevant front-end conditions. The catalysts were characterized by XRD, N2-physisorption, TPR, XPS, STEM-EDX, ICP-OES and XRF, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations on idealized local Fe-Ag surface motifs were used to investigate composition-dependent trends in adsorption energetics. Catalyst characterization revealed no evidence for the formation of an extended Fe-Ag alloy phase after air exposure. Instead, Fe- and Ag-rich domains were found to coexist in close nanoscale proximity providing a structural basis for considering possible local Fe-Ag interactions. Accordingly, the DFT calculations were performed on idealized local Fe-Ag surface motifs to investigate how the local chemical environment around adsorption sites affects the adsorption energetics of reaction intermediates. DFT calculations predict a gradual weakening of adsorption strength with increasing local Ag content, while the experimental catalyst series independently shows a decrease in ethane selectivity with increasing Ag loading. Under CO-containing front-end conditions, catalyst selectivity increased further due to competitive adsorption effects, while the influence of catalyst composition became less pronounced. The combined experimental and computational results indicate that changes in the local Fe-Ag environment influence adsorption energetics and may contribute to the composition-dependent catalytic behavior in acetylene hydrogenation. These findings provide design principles for the development of palladium-free hydrogenation catalysts based on earth-abundant metals.

articles.title: Dual-Solvent Screening for Nondestructive In-Situ Optical Patterning of CsPbX3 QDs/PMMA
articles.abstract: Perovskite quantum dot (PQD)-polymer composites are widely pursued for display devices due to their excellent film-forming capacity, low cost, and favorable process compatibility. However, interfacial incompatibility between PQDs and polymers from mismatched surface chemistry triggers PQD aggregation and severe photoluminescence quenching, hindering microdisplay applications. Herein, a dual-solvent screening strategy is demonstrated for I-184-initiated crosslinked PQD-PMMA photoresists to balance solubility and lead-ion coordination strength. Undesired lead-solvent intermediate formation and residual solvent accumulation are suppressed to homogenize PQD dispersion and preserve optical performance. The 20 μm green patterned film retains 93% of the initial photoluminescence quantum yield with no photoluminescence peak shift and a narrow full width at half-maximum of 16.6 nm. The PQD pattern presents sharp pixel edges, 7.10% critical dimension deviation, 97.1% replication rate, and intersection over union of 0.92. This solvent engineering enables the revitalization of conventional polymers and addresses bottlenecks in photolithographic patterning of PQD-polymer composites.

articles.title: A Flexible Complementary Memristive Synapse for Convolutional Neural Network Applications
articles.abstract: The memristive artificial synapse, which typically operates on the basis of various filamentary conductance-update mechanisms, has been extensively utilized to implement hardware neural networks for brain-inspired computing. However, the stochastic conductance-switching characteristics that arise from uncontrollable filamentary evolution within the two-terminal device have long hindered hardware neural networks from achieving training and recognition performance comparable to their software neural network. Here, we propose a flexible complementary memristive synapse that achieves highly linear conductance-update behavior while preserving a large dynamic range. This synapse consists of a homogeneous bilayer of two amorphous indium–gallium-tin oxide (a-IGTO) films deposited under different oxygen partial pressures: an oxygen-deficient, VO-rich layer formed without O2 supply and an oxygen-supplied, VO-poor layer formed with O2 supply, exhibiting incremental and decremental conductance-update behaviors, respectively. The distinct oxygen-vacancy-related states and filament-evolution characteristics of the two layers suggest vacancy-mediated layer-to-layer redistribution, which can mutually compensate the nonideal conductive filament evolution of the two different layers, thereby facilitating more gradual modulation of the net conductance. The proposed flexible synapse exhibits robust mechanical stability and durability after 12,000 bending–release cycles, as confirmed by electrical characterization while maintained in the bent state at a bending radius of 2 mm. Finally, the applicability of the proposed flexible synapses to HW-NNs is evaluated through a VGG-8-based CIFAR-10 image recognition simulation using experimentally measured synaptic characteristics for weight updates in the two fully connected layers.

articles.title: Bacteria-Derived Micro/Nanoparticles for Vaccine Design
articles.abstract: Vaccines have profoundly reduced the global burden of infectious diseases and are increasingly being explored for cancer immunotherapy. However, developing vaccine platforms capable of simultaneously achieving efficient antigen delivery, precise immune modulation, and durable protective immunity remains a major challenge. Bacteria-derived micro/nanoparticles (BPs) have recently emerged as promising vaccine platforms that integrate the structural advantages of nanomaterials with the intrinsic immunostimulatory properties of bacterial components. Their micro-to-nanoscale dimension, pathogen-mimicking architecture, and capacity for multivalent antigen presentation facilitate efficient lymphatic trafficking, antigen-presenting cell targeting, and coordinated activation of both innate and adaptive immunity. Moreover, the endogenous pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) within BPs serve as built-in adjuvants, potentiating antigen cross-presentation, inducing trained immunity, and eliciting robust T-cell and B-cell responses. These unique structure–function relationships have accelerated the clinical translation of BP-based vaccines, with several candidates now in clinical trials or already commercialized. In this review, we discuss the fundamental mechanisms, engineering strategies, and clinical research progress of BPs in vaccine development, while critically emphasizing the current challenges in safety, mechanistic elucidation, and scalable manufacturing. We further outline future opportunities for harnessing BPs as precision-tailored platforms for next-generation immunization paradigms.

articles.title: Kinetic Control of Symmetry-Broken Spin Architectures of Azafullerene on [10]Cycloparaphenylene Templates: From Frustrated 2D Lattices to Quasi-1D Chains
articles.abstract: Supramolecular host–guest complexation provides a powerful strategy for stabilizing organic radicals and organizing them into functional spin architectures. Here, we investigate the kinetic pathways for on-surface complexation of spin-1/2 azafullerene radicals (C59N•) within templated [10]cycloparaphenylene ([10]CPP) nanohoop monolayers on Au(111), revealing a strongly anisotropic energy landscape that governs radical migration and encapsulation. Migration of isolated C59N• along the [10]CPP rims proceeds via relatively low energy barriers (∼0.45 eV), leading to preferential confinement at the nanohoop periphery prior to azafullerene encapsulation. C59N• relocation to the global energy minimum at the [10]CPP center requires overcoming substantially higher barriers of at least ∼0.8 eV, with interfullerene interactions raising these barriers further. High C59N• mobility and relaxed lateral confinement at [10]CPP template edges also activate an alternative assembly pathway in which azafullerene intercalation induces in-plane exfoliation of [10]CPP lines from the 2D [10]CPP array, creating a reconstructed two-dimensional superlattice composed of alternating zigzag chains of azafullerenes and linear rows of encapsulated C59N•⊂[10]CPP complexes. This edge-driven reorganization gives rise to anisotropic lattices of encapsulated radicals with one-dimensional structural motifs. The control over the rich energy landscape of C59N•⊂[10]CPP complexation thus enables access not only to geometrically frustrated two-dimensional lattices but also to quasi-one-dimensional chain motifs of spin-1/2 carrying radicals within a single supramolecular platform.

articles.title: Layer-Dependent Variation in Raman Modes of MoS2
articles.abstract: Raman spectroscopy is used widely to probe phonon properties and layer thickness in two-dimensional MoS2. However, relative peak heights of the out-of-plane (A1g) and in-plane (E2g1) Raman modes can vary with layer numbers. The explanation for origin of this variation has remained elusive. In this work, we show through statistical analysis of hundreds of Raman spectra on hundreds of samples that the A1g/E2g1 peak height ratio is ∼1.4 for monolayer and <1.0 for bilayer MoS2. However, in tri- and four layered MoS2, the A1g/E2g1 ratio can be both above or below 1.0, and gradually rises with thickness – approaching a saturation value of ∼1.3. We find – based on measurements on different dielectrics and at multiple temperatures down to 8 K – that the peak height ratio is modulated by the A1g line width, which depends on both substrate-dependent electronic effects and thermally activated contributions associated with interlayer-related phonon scattering. In monolayer MoS2, the anomalous area ratio originates from suppression of the E2g1 peak area and depends on excitation energy, suggesting the influence of its distinct electronic structure. Our results show that the variation of the A1g/E2g1 peak height ratio arises from the coupling of line width and monolayer-specific Raman response.

articles.title: Machine-Learning Dynamics of Redox-Active Materials: Polaron Diffusion on the TiO2(110) Surface
articles.abstract: In redox-active materials, atoms dynamically change their oxidation states in response to excess charge and electronic transport, with the potential for novel technologies spanning electronics, catalysis, and energy storage and conversion. Despite the remarkable progress of modern artificial intelligence methods in accelerating atomistic simulations, capturing the quantum-mechanical nature of charge transport and dynamically varying oxidation states remains a fundamental challenge, limiting scientific and technological progress. In this work, we introduce a machine-learning-based molecular dynamics framework capable of explicitly tracking the oxidation state dynamics arising from small-polaron hopping (excess charges trapped on single lattice sites that diffuse upon thermal activation). Our model uses descriptors augmented with charge localization information at each time step and is trained on density functional theory data to capture signatures of polaronic diffusion. We apply our method to the rutile TiO2(110) surface, which is a prototypical reducible oxide. Our simulations reveal that charge-carrier diffusion is highly sensitive to the local surface environment: polarons preferentially localize near oxygen vacancies, whereas their interaction with hydroxyl groups is weaker. These results provide a microscopic interpretation of experimental observations, highlight strategies to tune charge-carrier mobility through surface engineering, and demonstrate the applicability of our approach to investigating charge transport in complex materials.

articles.title: Modulation of MOF Catalytic Activity to Exploit Cystine Dependency for Immunometabolic Therapy
articles.abstract: Tumor immunometabolism plays an important role in tumor progression and immune cell activity and is therefore critical to the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy. Modulation of immunometabolism to boost cancer immunotherapy is mostly based on targeting tumor cell metabolism, which often fails to address the tumor-promoting functions maintained by stromal cells. In contrast, targeting a metabolic checkpoint shared by tumor cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) can potentially overcome this limitation but has been relatively underexplored. Herein, a locally delivered, ultrasound activatable nanocatalytic platform is reported for immunometabolic cancer therapy. The platform is composed of sulfasalazine and a gallium-modified Fe-TCPP metal–organic framework nanozyme codelivered in an oxidized sodium alginate-based hydrogel. Ultrasound-activated gallium-modified Fe-TCPP boosts electron transfer, peroxide activation, and reactive oxygen species production while disrupting iron balance. Simultaneously, sulfasalazine inhibits SLC7A11-mediated cystine uptake in CAFs and tumor cells, reducing matrix remodeling and weakening the tumor’s antioxidant defense. This dual approach increases oxidative stress, reshapes the tumor microenvironment, induces immunogenic tumor cell death with ferroptotic traits, matures dendritic cells, and strengthens CD8+ T-cell responses. Consequently, it suppresses tumor growth in an immunocompetent osteosarcoma model and remains effective in a patient-derived OSCC xenograft model. Together, these findings demonstrate that targeting shared SLC7A11-mediated cystine dependence integrates stromal remodeling, tumor redox disruption, and antitumor immune activation.

articles.title: Nanoarchitecture of Cobalt Phthalocyanine for Enhanced Chloramphenicol Hydrodechlorination through Direct Electron-Transfer Mechanism
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic hydrodechlorination (ECHD) provides a sustainable method for treating water polluted with chlorinated organic compounds under ambient conditions. Cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc) represents a molecular catalyst with economic benefits and high selectivity, although its performance is limited by significant molecular stacking. To this end, we constructed ordered CoPc nanotubes (CoTs) for ECHD studies, alongside conventional CoPc single molecules and disordered aggregates as reference systems. All materials catalyzed ECHD via a direct electron transfer (DET) route on the CoPc active state under turnover conditions. The ordered CoT architecture accelerated interfacial and internal electron transfer, boosting the intrinsic activity. Degradation involves simultaneous reduction of terminal nitro and chloro groups, and the latter is suggested to follow an energetically favorable remote attack pathway. At full chloramphenicol (CAP) conversion, CoTs delivered an ECHD ratio of 83.9%, which is superior to recent benchmarks. For practical use, a flow-cell system achieved a treatment flux of 6.79 L h–1 g–1, which is 5 times that of a standard H-cell. This work underscores the pivotal role of molecular ordering in enhancing ECHD and offers design guidelines for non-noble metal heterogeneous electrocatalysts.

articles.title: Recombinant Humanized Collagen V-Engineered Implant Interfaces Drive in situ Low-Thrombogenic Vascular Repair via Selective Bioadhesion
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular implants (e.g., vascular stents, occluders) face persistent challenges of thrombosis, immune activation, and delayed endothelial healing. Moreover, functional surfaces that can synergistically balance the demands of antithrombosis and pro-endothelialization remain suboptimal. Here, we develop a genetically engineered, recombinant humanized collagen V (rhCol V) that promotes vascular endothelial cell proliferation via the αvβ3-FAK pathway and induces smooth muscle contractile transition. Proteomics indicates reduced platelet adhesion via αIIbβ3 inhibition, thereby reducing thrombogenicity. In rabbit models, rhCol V-coated stents outperformed drug-eluting stents in long-term endothelial repair and remodeling, while suppressing acute thrombosis and immune activation. This engineered biomaterial has the potential to enhance the safety and efficacy of cardiovascular implantable devices.

articles.title: Slit-Confined Self-Assembly of Cellulose Nanocrystals for Long-Range Ordered Cholesteric Architecture
articles.abstract: Long-range ordered cellulose nanocrystal (CNC) architectures are vital for photonic applications, but conventional self-assembly predominantly yields defective, multidomain nanostructures. Herein, this study proposes a slit-confined self-assembly (SCSA) strategy to construct a scalable CNC cholesteric liquid crystal structure with a single orientational domain. Distinct from conventional methods relying on extreme external fields or drying protocols, SCSA utilizes a simple glass slit to steer CNC assembly through synergistic physical effects: gravity drives tactoids sedimentation and interfacial hydrogen bonding enforces preferential alignment. Concurrently, the geometric constraint effectively suppresses the nucleation and propagation of topological defects, enabling the formation of centimeter-scale monodomain cholesteric architectures. As a result, brilliant structural color in aqueous CNC suspensions is achieved without external fields or active stimuli, enabled solely by the synergistic effects of geometric confinement, gravity-driven sedimentation, and interfacial hydrogen-bond anchoring. The resulting highly ordered architecture achieves an exceptional orientation factor of 0.98 and a structural color dissymmetry factor (g) as high as 1.3, accompanied by reversible structural reassembly behavior. Furthermore, upon coassembling with luminescent guests, the system exhibits a giant circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) dissymmetry factor (glum) reaching −1.1. Collectively, this work establishes a robust, straightforward, and scalable route for highly controllable liquid crystal self-assembly, offering promising avenues toward high-performance photonic applications.

articles.title: Stiffness Directs Intracellular Fate and Intercellular Transport of Nanoparticles
articles.abstract: Nanoparticles have been developed as delivery vehicles to achieve uniform distribution of drugs in the tumor, but they are still not optimal for deep tumor penetration due to the hindrance by the dense extracellular matrix. Enabling active transport via tumor cells has been explored as a solution, which has been achieved by tuning the size and surface chemistry of nanoparticles. Here, we show that particle stiffness is another key determinant. Using positively charged polyglycerol nanogels with matched size, charge, and composition, we found that stiff nanogels preferentially enter cells via clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME), undergo lysosomal processing, and are efficiently exocytosed, enabling transcellular transport. In contrast, soft nanogels are taken up mainly by macropinocytosis, accumulate in the Golgi apparatus, and exhibit prolonged intracellular retention. Finally, the efficient CME and subsequent exocytosis of stiff nanoparticles contribute to the enhanced transcytosis efficiency, allowing them to penetrate 3D tumor spheroids. This stiffness-dependent cellular itinerary operates without additional surface modifications, revealing a general design principle whereby intrinsic mechanical properties can control intracellular and intercellular transport behavior of nanoparticles.

articles.title: Toward Generalized Dynamic Metasurface Holography with Learned Real-Momentum-Locked Evolution
articles.abstract: Dynamic holography is pivotal for next-generation displays with critical applications in augmented reality, virtual reality, and beyond. While metasurfaces have emerged as powerful approaches for dynamic holography, existing works remain largely confined to intensity-only modulation, restricting the available channels for display and information storage. Herein, we realize a generalized platform applicable to major types of dynamic holography (monochromatic, color, 3D, and vectorial) by introducing a learned metasurface and aperture synthesis framework (LMAS). This paradigm extends Fourier duality from the intrinsic static real-momentum mapping relationship into the dynamical regime and establishes a learned mapping between real-space aperture displacement and momentum-space holographic evolution via gradient optimization. Crucially, the aperture’s inherent field-agnostic nature provides a universal physical interface that unifies diverse optical degrees of freedom, allowing us to demonstrate four distinct types of dynamic meta-holography. The LMAS approach establishes metasurfaces as a generalized, compact, and scalable architecture for holographic evolution within a minimalist system configuration, offering broad potential in advanced displays, optical storage, and information multiplexing.

articles.title: Martensitic vs strain glass transformation in Ti–Nb alloys mediated by oxygen and nitrogen interstitial site reconfiguration
Data‐Driven Host Microstructure Design Toward Efficient and Durable Room‐Temperature Sodium–Sulfur Batteries
articles.abstract: Porous carbon materials are critical hosts for chalcogen‐ and halogen‐based conversion‐type cathodes, as they govern the activity and durability of electrochemical reactions. Understanding how their microstructures regulate electrolyte‐electrode interactions remains challenging given multiple coupling factors and dynamic changes during electrochemical cycling. Herein, machine learning was first used to screen three pore structure parameter windows relevant to electrochemical features from a large experimental dataset (23 carbon hosts and 1055 specific‐capacity data points). Based on these screened windows, three representative carbon hosts, namely micropore‐rich carbon, balanced carbon, and meso/macropore‐rich carbon, were synthesized as model systems. We reveal that pore structure governs sulfur species evolution, thereby dictating the competition between polysulfide‐mediated reactions and solvent self‐decomposition. The resulting spatial‐compositional differences of the cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) were found to profoundly impact energy efficiency, reversibility, and rate performance. The balanced carbon cathode with optimized inorganic‐organic distribution delivers an initial capacity of 1249.4 mAh g−1 and retains a capacity of 784.8 mAh g−1 after 500 cycles. This work not only proposes a data‐driven strategy for identifying CEI‐relevant pore structure windows, but also provides mechanistic insight into how physical metrics of porous carbon modulate multi‐step complex reactions and ultimately influence electrochemical performance.

articles.title: Renewable Intermittency Redistributes Catalyst Recovery and Membrane Degradation in Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Renewable intermittency is widely regarded as a durability stressor in water electrolysis, yet its impact on competing degradation and recovery processes within the cell remains unclear. Here, we show that realistic intermittent operation redistributes catalyst recovery and membrane degradation in anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE). A Ni–Fe‐based AEMWE single‐cell was operated under high‐resolution, solar‐mimicking load profiles that reproduce day–night intermittency without external buffering. Electrochemical diagnostics reveal reversible changes in activation, Ohmic, and mass‐transport losses, indicating partial performance recovery during zero‐current intervals. In situ X‐ray absorption spectroscopy attributes this behavior to reversible oxidation‐state and coordination changes of Ni and Fe, associated with the reversible formation and relaxation of amorphous (oxy)hydroxide surface layers. In contrast, hydrogen crossover measurements reveal increased crossover under low‐current operation, while post‐mortem membrane analyses provide independent evidence of membrane deterioration, identifying a critical system‐level limitation. These results show that intermittency does not uniformly mitigate degradation but redistributes it across cell components, enabling catalyst self‐restoration while exacerbating membrane vulnerability. This work establishes intermittency as a double‐edged operational parameter and provides a framework for designing materials and operating strategies for durable, battery‐free AEM water electrolysis.

articles.title: Understanding Charge Acceptance Limitations During Extreme Fast‐Charging of Li‐ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Extreme fast charging in lithium‐ion batteries is limited by their poor charge acceptance at high C‐rates. We use overpotential component analysis to decouple ohmic, kinetic and transport voltage losses during fast charging. The concentration gradients are identified as the primary culprit in poor charge acceptance, so we study carbonate electrolytes that utilize acetonitrile, a low viscosity, high dielectric liquid, as a co‐solvent to improve ion transport. Our results indicate acetonitrile co‐solvent successfully reduces fast charging concentration gradients and therefore improves charge acceptance at high C‐rates, particularly when used in combination with interface‐stabilizing additives. Molecular dynamics simulations show that ACN enhances Li+ transport through a combination of reduced bulk viscosity and increased solvation‐shell lability, with shorter solvent residence times and faster coordination exchange producing transport gains beyond those expected from viscosity reduction alone. Finally, we use three‐electrode cells to deconvolute overpotential at each electrode, and the specific LiNi0.8Mn0.1Co0.1O2 (NMC811) electrode architecture and loading used in our study is found to have much higher overpotentials than our graphite electrode. In particular, the significant differences in NMC811 concentration gradients between electrolytes with or without acetonitrile indicate that the design of electrode architecture is crucial for extreme fast charging applications.

articles.title: A Dual‐Locked and H2S‐NO Tandem‐Activatable NIR‐II Nanoagent for Colon Cancer Theranostics
articles.abstract: Dual‐locked activatable theranostics have been emerging as a promising cancer therapy platform. However, most of the reported dual‐locked systems only restricted to enzyme‐responsive probes, new molecular tools with other biomarker‐responsiveness still remain challenging. Moreover, optical manipulation in the second near‐infrared (NIR‐II) window can potentially boost the theranostic efficacy, but having rarely been explored. In this study, we report a dual‐locked and gas tandem‐activatable NIR‐II nanoagent for colon cancer theranostics. Water‐dispersible nanoparticles containing a nitrated organic small molecule (CTBN) and an acid‐responsive NO donor (NONOate; CTBNN‐NPs) are fabricated, displaying negligible emission in visible‐NIR region. Upon uptake by colon cancer cells, CTBNN‐NPs can be tandemly activated by the overexpressed H2S and the in situ released NO, thus turning on NIR‐II emission extending to 1200 nm. Moreover, the activated CTBNN‐NPs also demonstrate augmented NIR absorption as well as robust photothermal and type‐I photodynamic performance, achieving NIR‐II fluorescence imaging‐guided efficient photo‐elimination of colon cancer together with NO gas therapy, while exhibiting limited efficacy in the tested cervical and breast cancer models. This work provides a new molecular design approach to dual‐locked and H2S‐NO tandem‐activatable nanoagents with gas‐responsive and NIR‐II active capabilities, highlighting the exciting potential for cancer theranostics.

articles.title: Bismuth‐Mediated Zinc Extraction‐Induced Carbon Defects Boost Fe Single‐Atom Catalysis for Efficient Oxygen Reduction
articles.abstract: Fe single‐atom catalysts with Fe‐N4 configurations typically suffer from excessive adsorption of oxygenated intermediates, leading to intrinsic limitations in catalytic efficiency. Here, we propose a Bi‐mediated Fe‐adjacent Zn extraction strategy to create defects adjacent to Fe‐N4 moieties on ZIF‐8‐derived carbon support, thereby tailoring the local microenvironment of Fe single atoms. The resulting Fe‐N‐pCd catalyst exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity in alkaline electrolyte, delivering a half‐wave potential of 0.918 V versus RHE along with excellent durability. The assembled quasi‐solid‐state Zn‐air battery using Fe‐N‐pCd as the air cathode catalyst affords stable operation for over 3000 h at −40°C. Mechanistic investigations demonstrate that the formed carbon defects adjacent to Fe‐N4 sites redistribute the local electron density and favor the formation of an axial *OH‐bound Fe state under ORR conditions. This defect‐modulated coordination environment lowers the Fe d‐band center and alleviates the overly strong Fe‐*OH coupling, thereby changing the potential‐limiting step from *OH removal to *OOH formation and accelerating ORR kinetics. This study provides a neighboring‐template extraction route for engineering defect microenvironments adjacent to metal single atoms, opening new opportunities for the design of efficient ORR electrocatalysts.

articles.title: Correction to “Colorful Electrochromic Displays With High Visual Quality Based on Porous Metamaterials”
Defined Matrices Reveal Epithelial‐ and Mesenchymal‐Specific Responses to Stiffness and Adhesion in Human iPSC‐Derived Intestinal Organoids
articles.abstract: Human intestinal organoids (hIOs) are powerful models for studying development and disease, yet dissecting how physical and matrix cues shape epithelial and mesenchymal responses remains challenging due to reliance on ill‐defined matrices. Here, a fully defined hIO workflow was developed in which Matrigel was replaced by recombinant human substrates during pluripotent stem cell differentiation and by polyethylene glycol (PEG) hydrogels during 3D culture, while maintaining organoid viability and epithelial cytodifferentiation. Transcriptomic analyses show that both PEG‐ and Matrigel‐cultured hIO epithelial cells are most similar to human duodenal reference populations, and have greater transcriptional similarity to fetal than adult duodenal references. Despite this overall similarity, PEG culture is associated with subtle shifts in epithelial differentiation‐associated gene expression, together with altered mesenchymal ECM‐remodelling and integrin‐associated programs. Increasing matrix stiffness produces modest effects in epithelial cells, including increased MUC2‐positive cells, whereas mesenchymal transcriptional responses to stiffness are limited. Together, these findings establish a fully defined hIO platform that retains responsiveness to inflammatory stimulation while enabling controlled investigation of how matrix composition and stiffness shape epithelial and mesenchymal cell states in models of intestinal development and fibrosis.

articles.title: Designing a Thermochemically Active Hydrogel With In Situ‐Formed Ceramic–Carbon Hybrid Barrier for Suppressing Thermal Runaway Propagation
articles.abstract: Preventing thermal runaway propagation (TRP) is critical for the safety of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). While hydrogel interlayers actively cool through water evaporation, their mechanical reinforcement with conventional fillers dilutes the water-rich matrix and reduces enthalpy. Here, we propose a paradigm-shifting strategy by using boric acid (BA) as a thermochemically active cross-linker in a poly(AMPS) hydrogel. BA reconstructs the hydrogel network through dual N─H⋯O hydrogen bonding and B⋯O═C coordination, simultaneously enhancing compressive strength by 567%. Upon thermal runaway, the composite provides dual-mode protection: (1) synergistic heat absorption (volumetric enthalpy > 2000 J cm− 3) via water evaporation and BA stepwise dehydration, accompanied by flame-inhibiting SO2 release. (2) In situ formation of a highly insulating ceramic–carbon hybrid barrier. Post-test analysis reveals a critical BA content of 25 wt%, where tetrahedral boron coordination (63.3% BO4) maximizes covalent B─O─C bonds that chemically “weld” B2O3 to carbon.
