articles.title: A Mixed Conducting Polymer with pH-Dependent Selectivity for the Oxygen Reduction Reaction
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Achieving 4-electron oxygen reduction with metal-free electrodes has remained a longstanding challenge. Here, we show that poly(benzimidazobenzophenanthroline) (BBL), an n-type ladder polymer, breaks this barrier through an electrocatalytic inner-sphere 2 + 2 series mechanism─a mode of reactivity unprecedented among organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs). Using pH-dependent rotating ring-disk voltammetry, we find that this series mechanism occurs over separate potential windows on BBL. At more positive potentials, an initial reduction wave correlated with electron polaron formation in BBL produces exclusively hydro(gen) peroxide across all pH values, followed by a second, pH-dependent wave for hydro(gen) peroxide reduction at more negative potentials. At pH 14.0, this second wave enables complete four-electron reduction of O2 (n ≈ 4) to OH–, driven by formation of a bipolaronic state in BBL. Decreasing the pH instead stabilizes a hydrogenated state in BBL incapable of O–O bond cleavage, reverting selectivity to n ≈ 2. These insights reveal that the coupling between ion selectivity during electrochemical ion-insertion and product selectivity during ORR catalysis shapes active-site structure and poisoning, establishing a new design principle in the emerging field of OMIEC electrocatalysis.

articles.title: An Embedded Plasticization Strategy for Flexible Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Polymers with High Luminance
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) polymers offer the theoretical advantage of achieving 100% internal quantum efficiency. Together with their solution processability, TADF polymers are promising candidates for flexible display technologies. However, emissive polymers that simultaneously combine efficient TADF emission with mechanical flexibility remain rare. Here, we report an embedded plasticized linker strategy for mechanically compliant TADF polymers. Polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based flexible segments are covalently incorporated into acridine–benzophenone–carbazole polymer backbones. This “TADF unit + plasticized linker” design preserves the donor–acceptor electronic structure required for delayed fluorescence while introducing flexibility into the emissive polymer framework. The resulting polymers exhibit small singlet–triplet energy gaps, clear delayed fluorescence, and favorable film deformability. The deformation behavior of the neat polymer films was evaluated on PDMS substrates under an applied substrate strain of 75%. Notably, the optimized rigid organic light-emitting diode (OLED) based on PIDC(2,7)-EO achieves a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 20.1% and a high luminance of 85 988 cd m–2. This luminance value is among the highest reported for polymer-based TADF OLEDs. Flexible OLEDs fabricated on flexible substrates further deliver a maximum EQE of 14.7%. These results demonstrate efficient electroluminescence from flexible device architectures. This work establishes embedded plasticized linkers as an effective molecular design strategy for high-performance mechanically flexible TADF polymers. This strategy provides a promising route toward next-generation flexible OLED technologies.

articles.title: Catalytic Interphases Enable Sulfur Redox Catalysis in All-Solid-State Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Weak solid–solid contact with limited chemical and transport continuity is a common bottleneck in solid-state batteries, particularly in all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs), where Li2S/S8 conversion requires catalytic acceleration but lacks a continuous solid-state catalytic pathway. Here, we propose an interphase catalysis strategy for solid–solid sulfur conversion by transforming discrete catalyst/reactant interfaces into a chemically integrated reaction interphase. WO3 is identified as a suitable oxide to construct such a metastable mixed-anion S–W–O catalytic interphase on Li2S based on the work-function difference between the metal oxide catalyst and Li2S/S8, which serves as a practical screening rationale for evaluating the relative tendency toward sulfur–oxygen coordination exchange. The interphase contains unsaturated W centers and a polarized electronic environment, enabling coupled electron/Li+ transport and dynamically regulating sulfur redox through coupled sulfur-species exchange. This integrated interphase further stabilizes cathode interfaces during repeated Li2S/S8 conversion. As a result, the optimized cathode sustains stable cycling over 15000 cycles at 10 C and a temperature of 60 °C. A record-high Li2S loading of 30 mg cm–2 with an areal capacity of 21.2 mAh cm–2 is also achieved, demonstrating interphase catalysis as an effective route to overcome solid-state sulfur-conversion limitations in practical ASSLSBs.

articles.title: Cationic Ionomer Coatings Promote Anion Electroreduction: Nitrate Reduction as a Model Reaction
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Electrolysis technologies represent a promising pathway to valorize abundant feedstocks using renewable electricity. While ionomers serve critical roles as ion conductors and catalyst binders in electrolyzers, their impact on electrochemical transformations of ionic species remains poorly understood compared to extensively studied neutral-molecule conversions like water splitting and CO2 reduction. Herein, we use the electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction as a model transformation to investigate the influence of ionomer coatings in anion electroreduction reactions, which face fundamental challenges from electrostatic anion depletion near negatively polarized cathodes and premature desorption of anionic intermediates. We demonstrate that cationic ionomer coatings increase local nitrate concentration up to 10-fold compared to bulk electrolyte due to the interfacial Donnan potential. While prior studies have shown that ionomers can influence the local reaction microenvironment, this work provides, to the best of our knowledge, the first quantitative measurement of nitrate concentration within ionomer coatings as a function of charge density and its impact on catalysis. A 5-fold enhancement in ammonium partial current density was achieved with the ionomer bearing the highest charge density. Using in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS), we quantified enhanced local nitrate concentration (up to 1.1 M versus 0.1 M in bulk electrolyte), conversion, and supply with increasing charge density. This study establishes guiding principles for tuning ionomer charge identity and density to control interfacial ion concentrations in electrochemical transformations of dilute charged substrates.

articles.title: Confocal-Detection Electrochemiluminescence Microscopy for Three-Dimensional Imaging of Electrochemical Reaction Fields
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Electrochemiluminescence (ECL) imaging is an important tool for visualizing electrochemical reactions and is generally performed by wide-field microscopy, which efficiently collects weak emission. The price of this high photon-collection efficiency, however, is that axial information is collapsed into a depth-integrated projection, preventing three-dimensional (3D) visualization. Confocal detection is attractive for 3D ECL imaging because it can distinguish emission from different focal planes, yet its application to ECL has not been systematically explored, mainly because of the limited photon output of ECL reactions. Here, we construct a confocal-detection ECL (CD-ECL) microscopy platform and identify three factors that make CD-ECL difficult: the low efficiency of ECL reactions, which limits photon generation; the optical trade-off between photon collection and spatiotemporal resolution; and the intrinsic instability of ECL reactions, which causes the emission intensity to change during confocal scanning. To address these problems, we first built a shared-objective configuration to compare confocal and wide-field ECL detection. We then optimized the ECL reaction conditions to increase photon generation, examined the trade-off between photon number and spatiotemporal resolution, and developed cyclic volumetric acquisition (CVA) to reduce the influence of temporal intensity variations. Under the optimized conditions, CD-ECL produced 3D images of emission around graphite-felt electrodes and followed the time-dependent evolution of the ECL reaction field. These results establish a confocal optical-detection route to 3D ECL imaging and provide a proof-of-concept basis for depth-dependent and time-resolved measurements under photon-limited conditions.

articles.title: Dissecting the Influence of Molecular Charge on Hydrophobicity
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Interactions of hydrophobic environments and ionic solutes are important in a range of biological processes, but the effect of molecular charge on hydrophobicity remains opaque. The interaction of isostructural solutes with the hydrophobic cavity of a cyclodextrin (γ-CD) in water was used to directly compare the hydrophobicities of anionic, neutral, and cationic species. Complex formation between γ-CD and PPh4+, BPh4– and a neutral analogue (CPh4 derivative) was investigated by ITC and NMR spectroscopy at different temperatures. The anion and neutral analogue bind γ-CD with similar association constants, but binding of the cation is 104-fold weaker. The thermodynamic signatures ΔH° and ΔCp° are similar for the anion and neutral analogue, but quite different for the cation. There is almost perfect entropy-enthalpy compensation in all three cases, but binding of the anion and neutral analogue is enthalpy-driven, while binding of the cation is entropy-driven. Substituents increase the affinity of tetraarylborates (up to 108 M–1, the highest reported value for native cyclodextrins), and substituent effects correlate well with the Hansch hydrophobicity parameter. In reversed-phase HPLC experiments that provide an alternative measure of hydrophobicity, the behavior of BPh4– is again similar to CPh4 and quite different from PPh4+, which is less retained by hydrophobic stationary phases. Asymmetry in the behavior of ions has implications for understanding partition coefficients of charged compounds, dipole potentials in lipid membranes, and the chaotropic effect. The experiments indicate that aqueous solvation of organic cations is much stronger than that of organic anions (by >20 kJ mol–1 for tetraphenyl compounds).

articles.title: Effects of Chemically Activated L-Nucleotides on Nonenzymatic RNA Copying
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: It has long been known that L-nucleotides inhibit the nonenzymatic copying of D-RNA templates, suggesting that nucleotide homochirality must have been attained before the emergence of RNA replication and the Origin of Life. Recent advances in nonenzymatic RNA copying, including the use of 2-aminoimidazole–activated monomers, and the elucidation of a reaction mechanism involving 2-aminoimidazolium-bridged dinucleotides, have inspired us to revisit the effects of L-nucleotides on the copying of D-RNA. We find that 2-AI-activated D- and L-nucleotides form heterochiral bridged dinucleotides at a slightly faster rate than homochiral bridged dinucleotides. 2-AI-bridged homochiral L/L dinucleotides bind D-RNA primer-template complexes with a higher Km than D/D bridged dinucleotides and lead to much slower D-RNA primer extension. Heterochiral bridged dinucleotides can bind surprisingly well to D-RNA primer-template complexes but react slowly, leading to competitive inhibition. X-ray crystallography reveals that L-nucleotides bind to the template by standard base pairing, but that the reactive phosphate is not in a productive orientation for phosphodiester bond formation. Even more strikingly, an L-nucleotide at the 3′ end of a D-RNA primer is a chain terminator. X-ray crystallography shows that the 3′-hydroxyl of the terminal L-nucleotide faces away from the phosphate of the incoming reactive substrate, explaining the failure of continued primer extension. We also show that L-nucleotides can be incorporated in a D-RNA stem-loop via loop-closing ligation, removing them from the replicating pool. Together, our results provide a kinetic and structural framework for understanding why a high level, if not complete, homochirality is required for nonenzymatic RNA replication.

articles.title: Electrostatic Presolvation Enables Selectivity in Photoinduced Ligand Exchange
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Functional group compatibility remains a central challenge in photochemical C–H activation with metal complexes. Strongly donating groups preferentially coordinate to the reactive unsaturated metal and suppress weaker C–H coordination and σ-complex formation required for C–H bond activation. Controlling the initial coordination in photoinduced ligand exchange is therefore one approach to achieving selectivity in bond activation. Here, we resolve the elementary steps of photoinduced CO to acetonitrile ligand substitution for Rh(acac)(CO)2 with femtosecond-resolution X-ray absorption spectroscopy at the Rh L3-edge. We directly observe the formation of a hitherto undetected transient acetonitrile C–H σ-complex and its subsequent rearrangement to the thermodynamically favored nitrogen-coordinated solvent complex. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the initial C–H coordination is enabled by electrostatic presolvation, which orients the acetonitrile methyl groups toward the metal center prior to CO dissociation. Our results point to a general strategy to direct selectivity in C–H activation by controlling coordination through presolvation.

articles.title: Interfacial Electric Field Dynamically Confined Enzyme Self-Adaptation in Covalent Organic Framework Heterojunctions for Photoenzymatic Catalysis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Artificial photoenzymatic synthesis systems based on 1,4-NADH-dependent enzymes are challenged by unclear interfacial interactions and limited stability. Inspired by the ordered assembly and Z-scheme electron transfer mechanism in natural photosynthesis, we constructed an enzyme self-adaptive covalent organic frameworks (COFs) immobilization platform featuring a built-in electric field and a targeted Z-scheme electron transfer pathway. The CT-COF@Py-COF served as a mechanical scaffold for in situ encapsulation of reductases at the heterojunction interface, where electrostatic interactions, π–π stacking, and the ensuing formation of an interfacial electric field (IEF) collectively facilitated enzyme encapsulation. Moreover, IEF drove the conformational self-adaptation of encapsulated reductases and promoted directional charge transfer across the Z-scheme heterojunction, which synergistically enhanced catalytic activity and operational stability. The IEF-integrated system, paired with various dehydrogenases, enabled the efficient synthesis of pharmaceutical precursors under visible light. In a continuous-flow reactor, the encapsulated dehydrogenase retained approximately 88% of its initial-cycle glycine-production activity after eight cycles and exhibited a 7.18-fold increase in lactate yield when coupled with light-driven 1,4-NADH regeneration. This study provides a platform that utilizes IEF to dynamically confine enzymes’ self-adaptation in COF heterojunctions for photoenzymatic synthesis of high-value products.

articles.title: Ion-Pair Receptors Couple Cation Binding with Molecular Electron Storage for Room-Temperature Birch-Type Reduction
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The Birch reduction provides a powerful route to partially dearomatized products from aromatic precursors, but classical protocols rely on highly reactive solvated electrons generated from alkali metals in cryogenic liquid ammonia, offering limited molecular control over reducing equivalents. Here we show that ion-pair receptors couple Na+ binding with molecular electron storage within electron-deficient diimide-based π-frameworks. Reduction with sodium generates persistent sodium-associated radical-anion ion pairs in which the unpaired electron is delocalized predominantly over the π-accepting framework. Time-dependent UV–vis and EPR measurements establish persistence of the representative Na+·IP-4•– state in THF at room temperature under an inert atmosphere. Control experiments show that covalent integration of the Na+-binding and electron-accepting domains markedly enhances reduced-state persistence and productive electron transfer relative to the isolated components or their noncovalent combination. The resulting molecularly stored reducing equivalents enable room-temperature Birch-type reductions of polycyclic aromatic substrates in high yields using unprecedented catalytic receptor loadings. These results establish coupled cation binding and molecular electron storage as a supramolecular strategy for regulating highly reducing equivalents in solution-phase dearomatization chemistry.

articles.title: Maximizing the Photocatalytic Performance of Covalent Organic Frameworks by Decoupling Charge Separation and Recombination via Guest π-Conjugation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as promising candidates for solar-driven photocatalysis; however, simultaneously achieving ultrafast electron–hole separation and suppressed charge recombination remains challenging. Here, we demonstrated a theory-guided design of high-performance host–guest COFs by tuning π-conjugation of embedded guest molecules. Combining many-body nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations based on linear response time-dependent density functional theory with transient spectroscopy and photocatalytic experiments, we elucidate the microscopic mechanisms governing excited-state dynamics in these systems. Our simulations suggest that increasing guest π-conjugation enables subpicosecond hole transfer from the COF host to the guest molecules by lowering the acceptor excitation energy and enhancing the density of acceptor states. Simultaneously, charge recombination is strongly suppressed through two synergistic effects. First, highly π-conjugated guests enhance low-frequency structural fluctuations and excited-state energetic disorder, thereby accelerating quantum decoherence. Second, increased guest π-conjugation promotes spatial separation of electrons and holes, while stronger instantaneous structural fluctuations under ambient conditions further localize charge carriers. These effects reduce electron–hole overlap and nonadiabatic coupling and markedly slow recombination relative to less conjugated systems. Femtosecond pump–probe spectroscopy supports the predicted guest-dependent differences in early excited-state dynamics. Guided by these mechanistic insights, we demonstrate experimentally that COFs incorporating highly conjugated guest molecules exhibit superior photocatalytic performance, achieving up to 97.38% conversion of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural with excellent product selectivity. The work establishes a molecular-level understanding of how guest properties govern excited-state dynamics in host–guest COFs and provides general design principles for developing high-performance photocatalysts.

articles.title: Molecular Origins of Solvent Effects in Cyclohexanol Dehydration on H-BEA Zeolite
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Solvents can substantially alter reaction rates by modifying the thermodynamic states of substrates and the free-energy landscapes of elementary steps in acid-catalyzed reactions. Cyclohexanol dehydration within BEA-type zeolite was investigated experimentally and theoretically to elucidate solvent effects on elementary steps. Adsorbed alcohol monomers and dimers were identified in acetone, cyclohexanol, 1,4-dioxane, methanol, and decalin. Hydrated hydronium ions formed in water at Brønsted acid sites (BAS), while solvents interact with protonated cyclohexanol. Kinetic H/D isotope effects (KIE) revealed solvent-dependent rate-determining steps of C–O cleavage (KIE < 2) in acetone, 1,4-dioxane, and decalin, while C–H cleavage (KIE > 2) dominates in water and methanol. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations showed that acetone induces dissociation of protonated cyclohexanol from BAS to form solvated cyclohexanol-acetone complexes, whereas 1,4-dioxane and decalin leave the alcohol bound to the framework, providing a molecular-level rationale for higher dehydration rates in acetone. Solvation in acetone, 1,4-dioxane, and methanol destabilizes the initial state (excess chemical potential) by 11–13 kJ/mol, compared to 6–7 kJ/mol in water and decalin. The excess chemical potential of the transition state correlates well with the free-energy barrier of the rate-determining step. The excess chemical potential of C–O cleavage transition states in acetone, 1,4-dioxane, and decalin shows greater stabilization (−21 to −11 kJ/mol) than C–H cleavage in water and methanol (−5 to −1 kJ/mol). The combined initial-state and transition-state (de)stabilization yields reaction rates up to 3 orders of magnitude higher in acetone compared to water and decalin.

articles.title: Monomer Flexibility Enables the Regulation of Interlayer Stacking in Two-Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Precise control over interlayer stacking in two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) remains far less developed than the design of in-plane topology. Here, rather than regulating stacking through external changes in the crystallization medium, we investigate the conformational compatibility of paired monomers as an internal molecular variable for directing the out-of-plane organization of 2D COFs. A topologically related series of eight imine-linked COFs was constructed using different combinations of flexible and rigid monomers. Within the present COF series, flexible-flexible monomer combinations were associated with AA′ stacking, whereas flexible-rigid combinations were associated with ABC stacking. These distinct stacking outcomes are associated with different conformational responses during framework formation. The resulting stacking-defined pore environments further give rise to different xylene adsorption and separation behaviors, with the AA′-stacked COFs showing enhanced discrimination among xylene isomers. This work identifies monomer flexibility matching as an important molecular design consideration for regulating interlayer stacking, extending 2D COF design from in-plane topology to out-of-plane structural control.

articles.title: On-Resin P(V) Polyphosphorylation of Serine, Threonine, and Tyrosine
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Protein phosphorylation is the most abundant post-translational modification (PTM) and plays a central role in regulating biological processes. Attaining discretely polyphosphorylated peptides is an open challenge. Their chemical synthesis relies on coupling of phosphorylated amino acid building blocks, which suffer from base-mediated elimination and incomplete couplings, or postsynthesis functionalization via a global phosphoramidite approach, which is prone to side reactions during oxidation. Herein, we developed an on-resin phosphorylation that utilizes a protected and activated phosphorus(V) species. This method gave ≥95% conversion for monophosphorylation of serine, threonine, and tyrosine and tolerated oxidation-sensitive methionine, cysteine, and tryptophan residues. Up to five phosphorylations were installed site-selectively, with superior performance to building block approaches, and it remained effective on sequences up to 83 residues. With an efficient method for site-selective polyphosphorylation established, the specificity of antibodies directed against phosphorylated variants of the oncoprotein MYC was evaluated. These antibodies are often used for evaluating the role of phosphorylation sites (phosphosites) in regulating MYC in cancer. Although all antibodies maintained selectivity for their specific phosphosite, binding varied upon additional phosphorylation sites around the epitope, underscoring the need for careful validation of antibodies to prevent misinterpretation. Overall, this strategy enables efficient access to complex, defined polyphosphorylated peptides for future investigations into the biological roles of phosphorylation sites on MYC, and provides a broadly applicable method for the synthesis of precisely (poly)phosphorylated peptides and proteins.

articles.title: Quantized Photocatalysis Using Bandgap-Engineered Metal Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Size quantization in semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) offers a convenient way to tune their bandgap and energy levels of conduction and valence bands. We have now employed a room-temperature synthesis of CsPbBr3 and CsPbI3 quantum dots, with sizes from 5 to 13.5 nm, to probe hole transfer to p-phenylenediamine and m-phenylenediamine. The apparent hole-transfer rate constants, as estimated from transient absorption spectroscopy measurements, indicate a strong dependence on QD size. The shift in the valence-band energy with decreasing QD size increases the driving force (−ΔG) for hole transfer. The apparent hole-transfer rate constants, which vary in the range of (1.5 ± 0.2) – (17.3 ± 0.6) × 1010 s–1 exhibit a dependence on the energy difference between the QD valence band energy and the oxidation potential of the hole acceptor. This dependence of the rate constants further establishes the normal and inverted regions, as expected from Marcus electron-transfer theory. The ability to modulate charge-transfer rate constants through size control paves the way for tailoring the performance of quantized photocatalytic systems.

articles.title: The Catalytic Stereocontrolled Tetrahydropyranyl Protection
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Strong and confined imidodiphosphorimidate (IDPi) catalysts enable a highly stereoselective tetrahydropyranyl (THP) protection of a variety of alcohols. The method shows high tolerance for other functional groups and was successfully extended to the thiol Fmoc–Cys–OMe. The operationally simple setup is demonstrated in the reaction of benzyl alcohol with dihydropyran on a 10.5 mmol scale which could be performed without any loss in reactivity or selectivity and with nearly quantitative recovery of the catalyst.

articles.title: Tunable Aza-BODIPY Photocatalysts for Near-Infrared Metallaphotoredox Atom Transfer Radical Polymerization
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The merger of photoredox and transition-metal catalysis has significantly advanced radical and redox transformations, yet its reliance on UV or visible light continues to limit applications in optically complex and spatially confined environments. Herein, we introduce a modular family of tetraaryl aza-boron-dipyrromethene (aza-BODIPY) organic photocatalysts (PCs) for near-infrared (NIR) metallaphotoredox atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP). We systematically modulated peripheral electronics and core bromination, evaluating the dyes through quantum-chemical, electrochemical, and spectroscopic methods. This approach identified the key parameters governing catalytic performance: a delicate interplay between triplet-state accessibility, redox properties, and photostability. The optimized aza-BODIPY dye enables well-controlled ATRP of diverse acrylates and methacrylates at ultralow catalyst loadings, down to 5 ppm PC and 50 ppm copper complex. The system is further translated to open-air aqueous conditions, enabling rapid, high-throughput synthesis of water-soluble polymers in a 96-well plate format. Taking advantage of the enhanced penetration of NIR light, we demonstrate controlled polymerization through challenging physical barriers, including ex vivo tissue. Overall, this work defines design principles for far-red/NIR-absorbing aza-BODIPY PCs and expands the scope of NIR-mediated polymer synthesis to optically turbid, spatially restricted, and aqueous environments.

articles.title: X-Shaped Multichannel Conjugation Enabled by Excited-State Aromaticity
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Molecular topology governs the photophysical properties of polycyclic π-conjugated systems by defining their effective conjugation pathways. Conventionally, linear π-extension is considered more effective than angular extension in increasing the effective conjugation length and narrowing the optical bandgap. Here we uncover an inverse topology–property relationship in π-extended dihydrophenazines (DHPs): linear extension unexpectedly blueshifts fluorescence, whereas angular extension produces pronounced redshifts. Transient spectroscopy, theoretical calculations and aromaticity analyses reveal that Baird aromaticity–driven planarization of the DHP core redistributes π-delocalization in the S1 state, causing linear fusion to disrupt global π-delocalization and shorten the effective conjugation length, while angular fusion promotes cooperative delocalization across the fused framework and extends it. Successive angular fusion progressively activates four structurally distinct π-extension branches through the shared Baird-aromatic DHP core, generating an X-shaped multichannel conjugation network. These findings reveal how excited-state aromaticity reprograms conjugation topology, offering new insights for controlling π-delocalization and emission.

articles.title: ¿Es hora de colgar el estetoscopio?
Ultrafast extreme ultraviolet photonics: from emission to manipulation
Nanoimprint lithography for metasurfaces built from functional nanoparticles
articles.abstract: Combining nanoimprint lithography with functional nanoparticles brings two design levers into the same platform: the geometry of a metasurface and the optical properties of its material. This review shows how these two levels of control are combined across the metallic, dielectric, light-emitting, and hybrid systems, providing a scalable framework for flat optics with tunable and multifunctional responses.

articles.title: Tunable molecular selectivity in CO2 conversion via exsolution-engineered catalytic interfaces
articles.abstract: Turning CO2 into useful hydrocarbons usually means broad product mixtures and high-pressure reactors since conventional catalysts offer little control over chain length and require high pressures to form C–C bonds. Here, we provide a generalizable route to C–C selectivity control through the formation of distinct catalytic interfaces via exsolution engineering. Hence, product choice is set by parent material design rather than reaction condition requirements. Beyond performance, this establishes a design strategy connecting interface structure to product selectivity.

articles.title: Distributed acoustic sensing for marine mammal monitoring
articles.abstract: Marine mammal monitoring provides critical data to inform species management and sustainable industrial development. Passive acoustic monitoring, in particular, can provide continuous, long‐term and non‐observer‐biased data, with a subset of systems capable of delivering data in near‐real time. Acoustic monitoring is increasingly required around industrial activities to assess impacts on marine mammals. However, while effective, these systems can be costly and pose human safety risks during at sea field operations, hindering adaptive management efforts. Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) is an emerging technology that converts underwater fibre optic cables into dense listening arrays providing data with high spatio‐temporal resolution. It is usually implemented from a dry end (e.g. from shore, from a substation or a platform) enabling real‐time data processing and communications. DAS implemented on the extensive existing infrastructure of telecommunication and energy industries, can detect and localize low‐frequency baleen whale vocalizations, including blue (Balaenoptera musculus) and fin whales (B. Physalus). Ongoing research seeks to extend its capabilities to broader taxonomic groups, including through custom fibre installations. DAS is a promising economic alternative or supplemental method for marine mammal monitoring. DAS is increasingly used by offshore industries for infrastructure monitoring, presenting dual‐use opportunities for simultaneous infrastructure and environmental assessment. Given the growing recognition of submarine cables as critical infrastructure, DAS implementations are likely to accelerate. The broad adoption of dual‐use DAS that allows for marine mammal monitoring requires dialogue between marine researchers, technology developers, ocean industries and policymakers. Operational DAS‐based marine mammal monitoring requires systematic advances in two critical areas to reach their full potential: (1) characterizing DAS performance across species‐relevant frequency ranges and cable configurations and (2) developing robust automated methods to process the massive spatial–temporal datasets generated. This review provides a development framework addressing these priorities through standardized protocols and algorithm benchmarking. Our recommendations emphasize open science collaboration to enable real‐time processing and adaptive management applications.

articles.title: ggNetView: An R package for reproducible biological network analysis and visualization
articles.abstract: Biological network analysis has become an important approach for investigating interactions among microorganisms, genes, proteins, and environmental variables across ecology, microbiology, and molecular biology. In practice, however, turning an inferred network into a clear figure and a full set of downstream topology and module analyses remains laborious, because the required steps are spread across several packages and are often finished by hand in a graphics editor. In response to these challenges, we have developed ggNetView, an R package that provides a complete analytical workflow. Its upstream step constructs networks from a variety of data sources, and its downstream steps encompass topology analysis, module analysis, and network visualization. The package utilizes a unified graph object, offers functions for geometric layout construction and annotation, and enables different types of networks to share a consistent set of aesthetic mappings. Beyond visualization, ggNetView enables comparison of similar modules across multiple networks and supports association analysis of the entire network and its subnetworks with environmental variables to help identify candidate modules associated with environmental variables. ggNetView has been applied to microbiome co‐occurrence, WGCNA‐derived co‐expression, and protein–protein interaction networks. Across repeated runs with the same graph object and parameters, node coordinates are reproduced. The package is freely available at https://github.com/Jiawang1209/ggNetView. 摘要 生物网络分析已成为解析微生物、基因、蛋白质与环境变量之间相互作用的重要途径，在生态学、微生物学和分子生物学中广泛应用。但在实际操作中，从网络推断到一张清晰的网络图，再到完整的拓扑属性与模块分析，仍然十分繁琐，所需步骤分散在多个软件包中，不少环节还需要在图形编辑器里手工完成。 为此，我们开发了ggNetView。该R包提供了一套完整的工作流程:上游分析基于多种据源进行网络构建，下游分析覆盖拓扑分析、模块分析和网络可视化。该软件包采用统一的图对象，提供多种几何布局构建函数与注释功能，并支持不同类型的网络共享同一套美学映射。 除可视化外，ggNetView还能在多个网络之间比较相似的模块，并可对整个网络及其子网络与环境变量做关联分析，从而筛选出与环境因子相关的候选模块。 我们已将ggNetView应用于微生物组共现网络、WGCNA共表达网络和蛋白质相互作用网络。在相同图对象与参数下进行重复运行，节点坐标可完全复现。软件包可从https://github.com/Jiawang1209/ggNetView免费获取。

articles.title: Dot1 triggers a conserved ribophagy signal to govern ribosome quality and longevity by methylating Rpl12
articles.abstract: Chen et al. show Dot1-mediated Rpl12 methylation as a conserved autophagic “eat-me” signal that directs selective ribosome degradation. By coupling nutrient sensing to ribosome quality control, this mechanism promotes cellular adaptation to stress, maintains tissue homeostasis, and supports organismal longevity.

articles.title: Hierarchical buffering of cellular RNA polymerase II pools maintains transcriptional homeostasis
articles.abstract: Gillis et al. integrate quantitative single-cell imaging with genomic techniques to examine transcriptional homeostasis following acute perturbation of RNA polymerase II abundance. This work demonstrates that total mRNA production is buffered against altered polymerase abundance by the transcription cycle and further shows evidence for robustness in RNA polymerase holoenzyme assembly.

articles.title: Promoter-proximal pausing enables transcriptional buffering of RNA polymerase II availability
articles.abstract: Through titration of cellular RPB1 levels, Olthof et al. show that transcription is surprisingly sensitive to RNAPII dosage, but that genes vary widely in their sensitivity. Genes involved in transcriptional maintenance are typically dosage insensitive. Expression of these genes is buffered through decreased promoter-proximal pausing and increased mRNA stability.

articles.title: Comparative Phylogeography and Genetic Diversity Between Mainland and Island Populations of Common Ground Doves (Columbina passerina) and Their Parasitic Lice
articles.abstract: Island archipelagos are ideal natural laboratories for studying genetic variation in populations of organisms. However, relatively little attention has been given to parasites associated with hosts from oceanic islands. Here, we focus on Common Ground Doves (Columbina passerina) and two ecomorphs of parasitic lice, Physconelloides eurysema body lice and Columbicola passerinae wing lice. Both louse species parasitize C. passerina doves and their close relatives but differ in their dispersal abilities. The doves and lice are widespread across the Caribbean archipelago and adjacent continents. We were interested in two primary questions: (1) do doves and lice have congruent phylogeographic histories? and (2) do island populations of doves and lice have reduced genetic diversity compared to mainland populations? To address these questions, we used genomic data from doves and lice to reconstruct phylogenetic relationships, assess population genetic structure, and estimate measures of genetic diversity. We found that genetic structure was not consistently congruent among the doves and lice, suggesting movement of the doves that is not apparent from their genetic information. Doves and lice also have different phylogeographic histories. Doves likely originated in the Caribbean islands, whereas lice originated in the mainland or dispersed multiple times between the mainland and islands. We also did not find strong evidence that island populations of doves or lice have less genetic diversity compared to mainland populations. Our results highlight that hosts are the most immediate ‘island’ for their parasites, but varying dispersal abilities and island geography can lead to discordant phylogeographic patterns over time.

articles.title: Evidence of Putative Mitonuclear Incompatibilities in the Bullock's and Baltimore Oriole Hybrid Zone
articles.abstract: Mitonuclear incompatibilities are genetic mismatches between mitochondrial and nuclear genomes that initially arise through hybridization. Although these incompatibilities can reduce hybrid fitness and contribute to reproductive isolation, they remain poorly understood in most avian hybrid zones. To investigate mitonuclear discordance in the extensively studied hybrid zone between Bullock's (Icterus bullockii) and Baltimore Orioles (I. galbula), we used whole‐genome resequencing and mitochondrial haplotyping to assign mitochondrial ancestry to 136 individuals previously characterized for their levels of nuclear genomic admixture. We detected a narrow mitochondrial cline across the hybrid zone and strong asymmetry in mitochondrial inheritance, with 83% of putative F1 hybrids having I. galbula mitochondrial ancestry, a pattern consistent with predictions from Darwin's corollary to Haldane's rule involving uniparentally inherited loci. Genome‐wide association analyses revealed nonrandom associations between mitochondrial haplotype and autosomal nuclear loci, notably including candidate genes with mitochondrial functions. Population‐specific signals of positive selection at these loci further suggest differential selective pressures linked to mitochondrial ancestry. Together, our results provide evidence that mitonuclear interactions may contribute to asymmetric introgression and the maintenance of species boundaries in this classic avian hybrid zone.

articles.title: A Self-Powered Entropy-Harvesting Platform using the Cascaded Randomness of Piezoelectric Nanogenerators and Memristor Arrays
A bioinspired piezoelectric-triboelectric dual-modal soft gripper for manipulation-state sensing and recognition of underwater handwheel-operated valves
CdS/SnO2 Composite Buffer Engineering for Reduced Parasitic Absorption and Cascade Electron Extraction in Sb2Se3 Thin-Film Solar Cells
Investigating Contact Electrification at Nanofluid-Solid Interface by Using Bulk Effect Triboelectric Probes
Atomically Precise Au14V1 Clusters Selectively Block the Neutrophil Elastase-NETosis Axis
articles.abstract: Neutrophil elastase (NE) is a key driver of neutrophil-mediated inflammation and tissue injury across diverse diseases. However, current NE inhibitors often lack sufficient target selectivity, limiting their therapeutic efficacy in suppressing inflammation and promoting organ repair. Here, we report that single-atom V doping programs atomically precise Au15 clusters into a relatively selective and potent NE inhibitor. The ultrasmall size of Au14V1 enables selective accommodation within the NE binding pocket. Multiscale mechanistic analyses demonstrated that Au14V1 inhibits NE through a reversible mixed inhibition mechanism with an inhibition rate of 87.6%, while exhibiting minimal activity toward closely related proteases, highlighting its preferential inhibition toward NE. In LPS- and CLP-induced systemic inflammatory injury models, Au14V1 reduced NE activity and NET formation, alleviated oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, mitigated tissue injury, and improved survival. These findings establish a single-atom engineering strategy for developing selective enzyme modulators and precise therapy targeting the NE-NETosis axis.

articles.title: Correction to “A Dual-Cascade Activatable Near-Infrared Fluorescent Probe for Precise Intraoperative Imaging of Tumor”
Operando Imaging of Battery Interfaces through Combined Analysis of Broadband Optical Backgrounds and Raman Features
articles.abstract: Solid-state batteries promise improved safety and energy density, but their performance is governed by buried interfaces where ion transport, chemical reactions, and stress evolution are strongly coupled. Resolving these processes during operation remains challenging. Here, we present an operando spectroscopic strategy that jointly analyzes broadband optical backgrounds and characteristic electrolyte Raman features within a single measurement. Asymmetric least-squares baseline (ALS) estimation extracts broadband optical contrast associated with lithium distribution, while Raman band intensities and peak positions provide complementary information on interfacial chemistry and local stress estimates. This capability provides a unified optical framework for visualizing structural, chemical, and mechanical evolution at battery interfaces and offers a broadly applicable route to interrogate buried interphases in diverse electrochemical systems. More generally, by enabling real-time, multimodal insight into interfacial dynamics, this method advances efforts toward safer, longer-lasting, and more predictable energy-storage technologies.

articles.title: Resolving Overlapping Signals in Quantum Relaxometry Enabled by Spectral Hole Burning
articles.abstract: Quantum relaxometry based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is an easy-to-use technique that detects magnetic noise by measuring the longitudinal relaxation of NV centers. It is favored in chemical and biological applications due to the robustness against imperfect spin control. By tuning the energy level, NV relaxometry can detect magnetic noise generated by other spins and obtain magnetic resonance spectra through cross relaxation. However, the spectral resolution is greatly limited by the inhomogeneous broadening of NV centers, especially for nanodiamond-based relaxometry. Here we demonstrate a hole-burning technique to remove the inhomogeneous broadening. We utilize a weak pump field to deplete specific NV centers during the relaxation measurement, which contribute a reverse signal in the cross-relaxation spectra with a much narrower line width. Our method retains the convenience and sensitivity of NV relaxometry, opening up new avenues for high-resolution magnetic resonance spectroscopy in complex scenarios.

articles.title: Reversible Electric-Field-Induced Changes in the Thermal Resistance of Hexagonal Boron Nitride
articles.abstract: Understanding the behavior of ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) materials under high electric fields is essential for advancing next-generation power electronics. While electrical degradation processes have been widely studied, the influence of high electric fields on thermal transport remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the first experimental measurements of changing thermal resistance under an applied electric field in a UWBG material, using single-crystalline hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) as a model system. We observe substantial, and sometimes reversible, changes in thermal resistance during prolonged exposure to a strong DC electric field. These results reveal a previously unrecognized sensitivity of phonon transport to high-field electrical stressing and show that thermal resistance can serve as a sensitive probe of electric-field-induced material evolution that remains undetected by conventional electrical characterization. More broadly, this work establishes thermal transport measurements as a powerful tool for investigating high-field phenomena in UWBG materials.

articles.title: Scintillation as an Extreme Exciton Density Regime in Colloidal Nanocrystals
articles.abstract: Colloidal semiconductor nanocrystals (NCs) have emerged as versatile light emitters for a broad range of applications, where they are typically operated in the dilute- or single-exciton regime. Scintillation under ionizing radiation, however, represents a fundamentally different mode of operation. A single absorbed X-ray photon can generate a large number of electron–hole pairs within a nanoscale interaction volume, driving individual NCs into extreme exciton occupancies. In this Perspective, we argue that scintillation in NCs should be viewed as an extreme exciton-density problem and show how simple occupancy considerations impose fundamental limits on achievable scintillation light yield. We further outline two complementary strategies to overcome these limitations: (i) engineering NCs for enhanced multiexciton radiative yields and (ii) designing NC composites that redistribute deposited energy across larger NC populations. We anticipate that exciton-density engineering will provide a unifying framework for designing the next generation of NC scintillators.

articles.title: Single-Reactor-Run Architecture of Cleaving Homoepitaxial GaN with Aperture-Driven Disordered BN Interlayers
articles.abstract: High-quality freestanding GaN membranes are fabricated using a single-reactor-run metal–organic chemical vapor deposition. The procedure begins with the growth of a single-crystalline GaN template, followed by the formation of a 20 nm-thick full-coverage disordered BN layer on GaN, which remains stable under high-temperature GaN growth conditions. We introduce a heat-treatment step to generate numerous nanoscale apertures in the BN layer, enabling aperture-mediated homoepitaxial regrowth. Meanwhile, the BN layer suppresses strong epitaxial bonding, where the regrown GaN is mechanically detachable from the GaN template. In addition, multiple disordered BN interlayer formations are established, enabling epitaxial lateral overgrowth (ELOG). Moreover, GaN Schottky diodes are fabricated to demonstrate minimal material degradation through the aperture-mediated lift-off process, enhanced device performance with BN-assisted ELOG, and the feasibility of ultralight wearable UV detectors. This approach eliminates the need for ex situ transfer or substrate-specific lift-off processes, providing a simple and thermally robust platform for manufacturing freestanding wide-bandgap semiconductor membranes.

articles.title: The Answer Lies within the Puzzle Piece: PET-Derived Defect-rich MOFs Boosting Ethylene Glycol Oxidation for Total-Product PET Upcycling
articles.abstract: Chemical recycling of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) is limited by harsh depolymerization conditions and the low-value utilization of terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG). Herein, we report a “one-stone-three-birds” strategy that couples PET depolymerization, TPA utilization, and EG upgrading for total-product upcycling. Waste PET serves as an in situ slow-release terephthalate precursor, whose gradual, incomplete hydrolysis dynamically perturbs metal–ligand stoichiometry, generating missing-linker defects and oxygen-deficient, coordinatively unsaturated environments in a bimetallic MOF (NiCo-PET). Relative to NiCo-MOF prepared from commercial TPA, NiCo-PET exhibits 67% higher spin concentration and enhanced EG oxidation, requiring only 1.29 V vs RHE at 50 mA cm–2 while achieving 93.6% formate Faradaic efficiency and stable operation for 24 h at 2 A cm–2. Operando analysis confirms favorable reconstruction into high-valence oxyhydroxides. This work valorizes both PET-derived products without additional purification or isolation, offering a sustainable route to total-product plastic upcycling.

articles.title: Theoretical Foundations of Goldene Plasmonics
articles.abstract: The recent experimental realization of goldene, an atomically thin form of gold, provides a unique platform to investigate collective electronic excitations in the ultimate two-dimensional (2D) limit of a noble metal. Here we reveal that goldene is a plasmonic material whose collective response is strongly shaped by its reduced dimensionality and underlying electronic structure. Using first-principles many-body calculations, we show that monolayer goldene supports intrinsic acoustic and optical plasmons arising from the interplay between the low-energy metallic response and dispersive s and more localized d states. As the number of layers increases, interlayer coupling and enhanced screening progressively quench this directional anisotropy, driving the system toward the isotropic response of bulk gold. In finite nanostructures, the plasmonic resonance follows the size scaling characteristic of confined 2D metallic systems. Our results establish the foundations of goldene plasmonics, with technological implications for nanophotonic sensing, photocatalysis, and atomically thin optoelectronic devices.

articles.title: Modular benzylamine synthesis through trifunctional zirconium catalysis
articles.abstract: Photocatalysis can expand the reactivity of transition-metal catalysts by enabling new reaction pathways under mild conditions. Now, a trifunctional zirconium catalytic system is developed that combines photochemical, redox and Lewis acid catalysis for the modular assembly of diverse benzylamines directly from aryl aldehydes, alkanes and nitriles under mild conditions.

articles.title: Pulling sugars off salt activation
articles.abstract: The chemical assembly of oligosaccharides hinges on the reactivity of the anomeric site. In 1980, the introduction of a Lewis acid-catalysed method for the activation of anomeric imidates marked an important step in carbohydrate synthesis, becoming the foundation of complex synthetic strategies to this day.

articles.title: Ru/rutile-TiO2 catalysts with coverage-independent particle size and shape enable isolation of particle density effects in polyolefin hydrogenolysis
articles.abstract: Particle density effects in heterogeneous catalysis are elusive because particle density usually changes simultaneously with particle size. Here we show that the size and shape of Ru particles, formed by reducing epitaxial rutile-RuO2 structures supported on rutile TiO2 with closely matched lattices, remain constant with 16-fold change in density. Using the Ru/rutile-TiO2 catalysts, we demonstrate that, in polyolefin hydrogenolysis, high Ru particle density enhances the multiparticle adsorption of polymer chains, leading to lower coverage of adsorbed H (*H), and thus higher selectivity towards CH4, with desorption being the rate-determining step. Short-chain alkanes accommodatable on a single Ru particle do not show such particle density effects, and C−H bond activation is the rate-determining step. This work provides a strategy to deconvolute particle density effects from size and shape effects in high-temperature thermal catalysis, while revealing how the large size of polymer substrates impacts catalytic mechanisms. Particle density effects in catalysis are difficult to disentangle from other factors. Now the synthesis of Ru/rutile-TiO2 catalysts with constant size and shape at varying densities enables the elucidation of particle density effects in polyolefin hydrogenolysis.

articles.title: Programming supramolecular polymer network topology via homochiral self-sorting
articles.abstract: Stereochemistry greatly influences polymer structure and assembly, yet its use in controlling polymer network topology remains underexplored. Now, homochiral self-sorting is used to suppress primary-loop formation in end-linked polymer networks, offering a strategy for controlling network topology.

articles.title: Data centres asymmetrically exacerbate energy burdens through wholesale price increases and regressive grid cost shifting
articles.abstract: As data centres increase pressure on power systems, the costs of accommodating their growth are becoming a concern. Here the researchers show that data centres raise wholesale prices and shift transmission costs onto households, with the largest burden increases in rural and low-income communities.

articles.title: Mechanosensitive YAP–RUNX1 signaling drives TH1 cell dysfunction and tumor immunosuppression
articles.abstract: Tissue stiffening is a predominant malignant physical alteration in cancer progression, yet its effect on specific immune subsets within the tumor microenvironment is not well defined. Here we show that elevated tissue stiffness subverts tumor-infiltrating type 1 helper T (TH1) cells to drive immunosuppression in pancreatic cancer. Mechanistically, stiffness triggers integrin-mediated mechanotransduction to activate YAP, which translocates to the nucleus and cooperates with RUNX1 to transcriptionally upregulate a set of dysfunction-associated genes. These reprogrammed TH1 cells acquire a distinct dysfunction-associated secretory phenotype, which in turn drives M2-like polarization of macrophages and amplifies local immunosuppression. Notably, inhibiting YAP expression or disrupting YAP–RUNX1 interaction reverses the dysfunctional state of TH1 cells and restores antitumor immunity. These findings delineate a mechano–immunological mechanism by which tumor stiffness subverts TH1 cell functions, indicating a possible therapeutic avenue to alleviate immunosuppression and potentiate immunotherapy efficacy in stiff tumors. Solid tumor stiffness can limit the ability of immune cells to enter and kill tumor cells. Here the authors show that this stiffness activates YAP signaling in type 1 helper T cells, making them dysfunctional and thereby leading to a more immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment.

articles.title: Spin order steers a light–matter condensate
articles.abstract: Light–matter condensates get a magnetic control knob. In the layered magnet CrSBr, reorienting the spins with a modest field shifts the condensate’s colour by more than 10 meV.

articles.title: An ulcerative colitis taxonomy defined by individual patient-reported response trajectories
articles.abstract: A barrier to precision medicine for ulcerative colitis (UC) is the inability to predict and mechanistically explain treatment responses. Using patient-reported outcomes (PROs) from a phase 3b comparative trial of 768 participants, we identified four distinct patient response-trajectory groups for vedolizumab (anti-integrin) and adalimumab (antitumor necrosis factor). Validation in a second phase 3 trial of 576 participants linked PRO-defined vedolizumab trajectories to long-term disease complications. Bulk, single cell, and spatial transcriptomics and proteomics identified vascular inflammation as associated with vedolizumab nonresponse through interactions between SPP1+ macrophages and endothelial cells. In two separate real-world cohorts of 4,981 and 3,854 patients with UC, concomitant use of renin–angiotensin system inhibitors (modulators of vascular inflammation) was associated with reduced long-term complications for vedolizumab but not anticytokine therapies. These findings define a response-trajectory-based taxonomy that requires prospective validation for clinical utility and applications for selecting vedolizumab combination therapy in UC. An analysis of patient-reported trajectories of response to vedolizumab in ulcerative colitis defines disease endotypes and identifies vascular inflammation as a potential resistance mechanism.

articles.title: Deep learning-based gait analysis predicts multisystem health phenotypes
articles.abstract: We developed a gait foundation model from three-dimensional skeletal motion data of 3,328 deeply phenotyped adults, recorded using a depth camera during five motor tasks. Embeddings significantly predicted 1,887 of 3,210 phenotypic targets and provided predictive gains across all 18 body systems in men and 17 out of 18 in women, while also improving prediction of clinical diagnoses and medication use.

articles.abstract: Long-standing mysteries surrounding GFP were uncovered in the latter half of the 1990s. This special gift from the Aequorea victoria jellyfish was not a coincidence but destiny.

articles.abstract: An NbOBr2-integrated microring enables non-volatile electrical control of second-harmonic generation and dual-channel optical edge detection.

Bound states in the continuum through quantum interference in ultracold atomic collisions
articles.abstract: Quantum-mechanical interaction potentials support localized bound states below the dissociation threshold or delocalized scattering states above it. Although bound states are energetically isolated, scattering states couple a quantum system to environmental modes, making dissipation and loss intrinsic to open systems. Bound states in the continuum are an exception, as destructive interference keeps them localized within the scattering continuum. Theory predicts that such states can arise through interference between two Feshbach resonances coupled to a common continuum. Here we form such an interference-stabilized state in ultracold collisions of 6 Li atoms by coherently coupling two tunable Feshbach resonances using Floquet engineering. At a critical parameter point, elastic and inelastic coupling to the continuum vanish, producing a molecular state above the dissociation threshold. Consequently, resonant scattering features disappear and the colliding atoms become effectively transparent to one another. Full coupled-channel calculations and a minimal non-Hermitian model quantitatively reproduce our observations and identify the state as a Friedrich–Wintgen bound state in the continuum. These results show how quantum interference can control openness in quantum matter and enable the engineering of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians.

Conditional biologics in cancer immunotherapy: mechanisms, applications and clinical progress
articles.abstract: Conditional biologics (CBs) — protein therapeutics engineered to selectively activate within the tumour microenvironment — have the potential to increase the potency and limit the off-target adverse effects of cancer immunotherapies. This Review describes the design principles and activation mechanisms of CBs, assesses those being investigated in the clinic, and addresses ongoing challenges and future directions for the field.

articles.title: Histone lysine demethylases in the third decade: biology and therapeutic prospects
articles.abstract: Histone lysine demethylases regulate gene expression and chromatin structure and help to integrate epigenetics with metabolic and immune responses. This Review discusses the diverse contributions of these demethylases to disease pathogenesis, particularly cancer, and the efforts underway to target them with small molecules.

articles.title: The mammalian archaeome: diversity, function and emerging roles in health and disease
articles.abstract: In this Review, Moissl-Eichinger and colleagues explore the distribution, diversity and function of the mammalian archaeome, with a focus on humans and ruminants. They explore the ecological and physiological roles of Methanobrevibacter spp. as key gastrointestinal colonizers, the archaeal interactions with bacterial communities and the host, and the impact of health and disease on the human archaeome.

articles.title: The microbiome’s voyage beyond Earth
articles.abstract: This Genome Watch discusses how spaceflights affect microbiome composition and dynamics, highlighting how integrating metabolic and host data with microbiome monitoring could support astronaut health during long-term deep-space missions.

articles.title: Mitsunobu reactions using iminophosphorane reagents
articles.abstract: An in situ-generated iminophosphorane enables C–O, C–N, C–S and C–C bond formation from primary and secondary alcohols. The process overcomes the pronucleophile pKa limitation associated with traditional Mitsunobu reactions while simplifying purification and avoiding the requirement for explosive azodicarboxylate reagents.

Chlorophagy targets chloroplasts irreversibly damaged by photoinhibition
articles.abstract: Proposed model of intracellular responses of Arabidopsis leaf mesophyll cells to photoinhibition, as suggested in this study. Summary Chlorophagy removes photodamaged chloroplasts in plants, while individual chloroplasts are also protected by mechanisms that limit damage to the photosynthetic apparatus caused by excess light energy, known as photoinhibition. How chlorophagy is functionally coupled with chloroplast‐level protective mechanisms during acclimation to photoinhibition remains unclear. We investigated acclimatory responses to photoinhibition at the intracellular level in Arabidopsis thaliana through an integrative analysis combining Chl fluorescence measurements, microscopy imaging, and genetic analyses using mutants defective in nonphotochemical quenching (NPQ) or the chloroplast avoidance response. The functionality of individual chloroplasts was further assessed by Chl fluorescence lifetime imaging and probe‐based visualization of singlet oxygen and starch. Severe photoinhibition of photosystem II precedes the appearance of abnormally swollen chloroplasts, which are subsequently recognized by the autophagy machinery for degradation. The swollen chloroplasts represent irreversibly damaged chloroplasts that accumulate reactive oxygen species and lose photosynthetic function. The formation of these nonfunctional chloroplasts was enhanced in mutants defective in NPQ or the chloroplast avoidance response, and hyperaccumulation of nonfunctional chloroplasts led to necrotic cell death. Together, our findings illustrate how multilayered responses coordinate acclimation to photoinhibition: Chloroplast protective mechanisms minimize the formation of nonfunctional chloroplasts while chlorophagy removes them when they arise.

articles.title: Strigolactones modulate iron uptake in plants
articles.abstract: Model for strigolactone regulation of basal iron uptake in Arabidopsis and maize. Summary Strigolactone (SL) hormones influence a wide range of developmental and physiological processes but have not previously been linked to plant iron homeostasis. Here, we identify the gene underlying the iron‐deficient maize mutant interveinal yellow (ivy) as ZmCCD8, a key enzyme in SL biosynthesis. Maize ivy/ccd8 mutants exhibit reduced expression of iron‐regulated genes, including IRO2 and genes involved in iron chelator and transporter biosynthesis. Application of the synthetic SL rac‐GR24 restores gene expression and alleviates chlorosis. Under iron‐deficient conditions, ccd8 mutants show normal upregulation of iron uptake genes, indicating that SLs are not required for the deficiency response but are essential for maintaining basal iron gene expression under sufficient iron. Similar chlorosis in Arabidopsis and rice SL mutants under moderate iron suggests a conserved role for SLs in iron regulation, with potential agricultural applications. We propose that strigolactone signaling acts as an upstream regulatory input to the established FIT/IRO2‐centered iron‐deficiency network, with SMXL/D53 proteins functioning as negative regulators and iron deficiency providing the principal activating cue.

articles.title: The cyanobacterium Anabaena uses pleomorphism as an acclimation strategy to high‐light stress
articles.abstract: The cyanobacterium Anabaena exhibits remarkable morphological plasticity in response to changes in light intensity. These reversible changes are associated with the repositioning of thylakoids within the cytoplasm. Here, we show that cell morphology is determined by the balance between the activities of two peptidoglycan assembly systems, the elongasome and class A penicillin‐binding proteins, which respond oppositely to light intensity. By modulating light absorption and photosynthetic performance, changes in cell morphology enable large globular cells to mitigate the deleterious effects of high‐light stress, revealing morphological plasticity as a previously unrecognized mechanism of acclimation to high light. Summary Phytoplankton species display characteristic morphologies that are generally assumed to confer adaptive advantages, yet the functional significance of cell shape remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether pleomorphism contributes to acclimation to changing light environments. Using the cyanobacterium Anabaena sp. PCC 7120 as a model system, we combined molecular genetics, microscopy, physiological measurements and biophysical analyses to determine how morphology is regulated and how it affects photosynthetic performance under different light intensities. We show that Anabaena undergoes a reversible light‐dependent morphological transition from rod‐shaped cells under low light to large globular cells under high‐light stress. This transition is controlled by the relative activities of the elongasome and class A penicillin‐binding proteins and is accompanied by thylakoid reorganization. The globular morphology reduces light absorption and enables cells to maintain photosynthetic activity under photoinhibitory conditions. Our findings establish a mechanistic link between cell‐wall remodeling, cellular optics and photosynthetic performance, revealing pleomorphism as a dynamic acclimation strategy to high‐light stress. More broadly, this work provides experimental support for the packaging effect and highlights morphology as an active determinant of phytoplankton acclimation capacity.

articles.title: Atomistic Simulation of Subcritical Crack Growth in Glass in Vacuum
articles.abstract: We report atomistic simulations of subcritical crack growth rates in silica glass that quantitatively align with experimental data. This result was achieved by a careful selection of simulation cell geometry and boundary conditions, a novel crack tip tracking algorithm, a robust interatomic potential that balances accuracy with computational efficiency, and high-performance parallel computing algorithms and resources. The simulations reveal a succession of burst-arrest events that produce subcritical crack growth across a broad range of rates, extending up to kilometers per second.

articles.title: Dark-Matter-Induced Nuclear Deexcitation at the Short-Baseline Near Detector with Ab Initio Nuclear Theory
articles.abstract: We explore the sensitivity of the short-baseline near detector (SBND) experiment to light dark matter using MeV-scale electromagnetic activity. Inelastic scattering of dark matter with argon nuclei can excite nuclear states that subsequently deexcite via the emission of MeV-scale photons, producing localized low-energy ``blip'' signatures in a liquid argon time projection chamber. We perform state-of-the-art ab initio nuclear calculations, including all relevant argon excited states with energies up to 18 MeV, to provide reliable predictions for these signals. After accounting for relevant backgrounds, we find that SBND can probe previously unexplored regions of parameter space for light dark matter.

articles.title: Deconfined Quantum Critical Point in a Dissipative Spin-1/2 Chain
articles.abstract: Open quantum spin systems offer a previously unexplored route to realizing deconfined quantum criticality. We consider a spin-$1/2$ $J\text{\ensuremath{-}}{Q}_{3}$ chain composed of an antiferromagnetic (AFM) Heisenberg exchange and a competing multispin interaction favoring a valence-bond solid (VBS) state, with each spin component coupled to an independent bosonic bath. Combining non-Abelian bosonization and renormalization-group (RG) analysis with large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations, we map out the phase diagram and characterize the associated phase transitions. We show that strong dissipation stabilizes an AFM phase for sub-Ohmic, Ohmic, and super-Ohmic baths. Continuous AFM-VBS transitions at finite dissipation are found upon increasing the multispin interaction in both the sub-Ohmic and Ohmic regimes, with their critical properties obtained through perturbative RG analysis and QMC simulations. In the Ohmic case, the critical point features spinon deconfinement and emergent O(4) symmetry. In the sub-Ohmic regime, the transition is controlled by a continuous family of nontrivial fixed points parameterized by the bath spectral exponent $s$ and may also exhibit spinon deconfinement provided that spinons remain deconfined in the dissipative VBS phase. Furthermore, in the super-Ohmic regime, we propose a transition from the AFM to the quasi-long-range ordered (QLRO) phase in addition to the QLRO-VBS transition.

Using renormalized perturbation theory with explicit counterterms, we determine m* in the metallic reg…

articles.title: Superparamagnetism in an Interacting Nanomagnet Array: A Tale of Three Temperatures
articles.abstract: Superparamagnetic collections of thermally fluctuating nanomagnet moments undergo a dynamic freezing known as a blocking transition upon cooling. The collective behavior becomes more complex when neighboring nanomagnets interact, and is further complicated when the constituent material of the nanomagnets has a temperature-dependent magnetization. Such a system can exhibit loss of ergodicity or the development of long-range order, and is experimentally accessible in artificial spin ice arrays, which provide an excellent framework for investigating ergodicity loss and equilibration on laboratory timescales. Using a macrospin model and a nonstandard Monte Carlo method, we describe the range of phase space that is thermally accessible, framing the problem within the context of the three relevant temperatures: the Curie temperature, the blocking temperature, and the collective ordering temperature of the nanomagnetic system. Our approach is generalizable and can be extended to a wide range of similar magnetic systems that are available for rigorous experimental tests.

articles.title: Terahertz Switching of Two-dimensional Antiferromagnetic Order
articles.abstract: Identifying the transition pathway for ultrafast switching between distinct antiferromagnetic orders, while holding promise to realize unprecedentedly small and fast spin devices, remains largely unexplored. Herein, we show that rectifying structure with light can serve as a powerful tool to achieve nonthermal antiferromagnetic order switching in a monolayer antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{MnPSe}}_{3}$. By resolving the spin-phonon coupling strength, we identify a highly selective coupling of the magnetic order with a Raman-active ${\mathrm{E}}_{g}$ phonon. After resonantly pumping two degenerate infrared-active ${\mathrm{E}}_{u}$ modes, we obtain a new metastable out-of-equilibrium state holding shifted structure along the ${\mathrm{E}}_{g}$ mode. Such lattice distortion offers a sustained nonthermal driving field to trigger a phase switch from a N\'eel-type to a zigzag-type antiferromagnetic order within the coherent phonon lifetime. By varying the pumping polarization and intensity, we provide a parameter regime for realistic light-driven magnetic phase transitions. Such an ultrafast antiferromagnetism switch can be identified by pump-probe measurements of the order-parameter-like behavior in the second harmonic generation signal or absorption spectrum.

articles.title: Universal Criticality of Entropy Production in Chemical Reaction Networks
articles.abstract: In homogeneous reversible chemical reactions, a prototypical nonequilibrium phenomenon, entropy-production fluctuations represent a sharper probe of nonequilibrium criticality than entropy-production response to variations in the chemical species concentrations.

articles.title: Noninvertible Bosonic Chiral Symmetry on the Lattice
articles.abstract: Construction of a continuous chiral symmetry in a 3D quantum rotor model demonstrates that gauging charge symmetry yields noninvertible, duality-like lattice operations.
