Aortic blood pressure and overall ETCO2 remained largely stable during stepwise PEEP titration, but decreased over the course of resuscitation. This association may indicate that at higher PEEP levels cardiac output exceeds ventilation, resulting in the prolonged time to peak ETCO2. Ongoing analysis will quantify the dose-dependent effects of PEEP on ventilation metrics (AOI, COM, and peak ETCO2), along with indicators of cardiac output (aortic blood pressure and the area under the capnography waveform curve). These findings may inform PEEP as a modifiable ventilation parameter during CPR to optimize airway management and resuscitation outcomes.

articles.title: Abstract P2019: Mental Health Outcomes After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Population-Based Cohort Study Comparing Adult Survivors with Other Critically Ill Patients
articles.abstract: Background: Psychiatric morbidity is common after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), yet whether survivors carry excess risk relative to other critically ill patients or instead share post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) mechanisms remains unclear. Hypothesis: OHCA survivors experience excess new-onset mental health and addictions (MHA) risk compared with matched critical illness survivors, beyond what is explained by pre-existing psychiatric history and sociodemographic vulnerability. Methods: Population-based retrospective cohort study (ICES, Ontario, Canada; 2007-2022). Adults surviving ICU admission for non-traumatic OHCA were matched to non-OHCA critical illness survivors by age (±3 years) and admission date (±3 days). Primary outcome: time to first new-onset MHA diagnosis within 15 years of discharge, from validated physician-coded inpatient, emergency department (ED), and outpatient records. We fit flexible parametric (Royston-Parmar) survival models with death as a competing risk and used logistic regression to compare inpatient versus outpatient care intensity, adjusting for sex, comorbidities, prior healthcare use, and neighbourhood marginalization. Results: Among 6,034 OHCA survivors matched to 16,461 controls (mean follow-up 4.7 years), 2,740 OHCA survivors (45.4%) received a new MHA diagnosis: anxiety/mood (33.9%), substance-related (7.8%), and psychotic disorders (2.7%); 20.0% required inpatient psychiatric admission. Incidence peaked within six months post-discharge. Composite MHA hazard was similar between cohorts (aHR 0.95; 95% CI 0.89-1.02). OHCA survivors had lower hazards for outpatient anxiety/mood (aHR 0.91), psychotic (0.74), and behavioural disorders (0.62); any inpatient psychiatric admission (0.85); inpatient mood disorders (0.69); and deliberate self-harm (0.73). The strongest predictor of new MHA outcomes was pre-existing psychiatric diagnosis (aHR 2.22; 95% CI 1.97-2.49); high pre-arrest ED use, younger age, female sex, and residence in racially marginalized or high-density neighbourhoods also independently predicted risk. Conclusions: Contrary to our hypothesis, OHCA survivors did not exhibit excess MHA risk versus matched critical illness survivors and showed lower hazards across several subcategories, suggesting shared post-ICU rather than arrest-specific psychiatric mechanisms. Nevertheless, nearly half developed a new MHA diagnosis, concentrated in the first six months and driven chiefly by pre-existing psychiatric history. These findings support integrating OHCA survivors into unified post-ICU mental health pathways, with early screening and targeted outreach for those with prior psychiatric diagnoses, high ED use, or residence in disadvantaged communities.

articles.title: Abstract P2020: Adolescent and Young Adult Survivors’ and Parent Co Survivors’ Lived Experiences of Pediatric Out of Hospital Cardiac Arrest Survivorship
articles.abstract: Background: Survival following pediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) has improved, yet there is a paucity of research about the long-term outcomes and experiences of survivors and their families. Understanding their experiences will help shape survivor- and co-survivor-centered interventions and outcomes that focus on long-term recovery and well-being. Research Question: What is the lived experience of adolescent/young adult survivors (AYA) of OHCA and their parent co-survivors in survivorship? Aims: This study primarily sought to: (1) gain a deeper understanding of AYA survivors’ and their parents’/legal guardians’ perceptions of life after a CA in survivorship and (2) understand how survivors’ and co-survivors’ needs have changed over time since arrest. Methods: The study was conducted at a large pediatric healthcare system in Southern California using a qualitative phenomenological design. Participants were recruited using purposive, snowball, and convenience sampling. Eligible AYA were aged 10 to 24 years, English-speaking, experienced OHCA between ages 10-18, survived greater than 6 months post-arrest, and were able to verbally articulate their experiences. Parents/legal guardians of eligible AYA were also invited to participate. Each participant completed two semi-structured interviews between October 2025 and March 2026, which were audio-recorded and transcribed. Data were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis informed by the hermeneutic circle. Coding was performed independently by two researchers, resolving discrepancies through consensus. Recruitment continued until thematic saturation was achieved. Results: Nine participants, including both survivors (n=3, 33.3%) and co-survivors (n=6, 66.6%), participated. Survivors were aged 18 to 24 years, and co-survivors were aged 40 to 59 years. Four (44.4%) self-identified as Hispanic or Latino. Five (55.5%) identified as White, two (22.2%) as Asian, and two (22.2%) as Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander. Among participants, four (44.4%) preferred “she” as their gender pronoun, three (33.3%) preferred “he,” and two (22.2%) preferred not to state. Five overarching themes about survivorship were identified: survivorship (a) is a new normal, (b) means being there, (c) is a physical embodiment, (d) means letting go, and (e) is what meaning we want to give it. Survivors emphasized challenges with self-concept and social reintegration, which is critical in their development stage. Parents described persistent anxiety, adjustment challenges, and advocacy burdens. Both groups highlighted discordance between acute care received and long-term support. Conclusions: AYA survivors of OHCA and their parents experience enduring psychosocial and functional impacts. Findings underscore the need for structured, family-centered, and individualized support throughout survivorship.

articles.title: Abstract P2021: Temporal Trends in Hospitalization and Survival After Out of Hospital Cardiac Arrest: Insights from the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival (CARES)
articles.abstract: Background: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains a major public health challenge, with persistent variation in outcomes across demographic and clinical subgroups. Evaluating recent trends in hospitalization and survival may identify disparities and inform targeted improvements in resuscitation systems of care. Methods: We conducted a retrospective trend analysis using the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival (CARES) from 2019-2024. We evaluated temporal changes in (1) proportions of hospitalized OHCA patients across demographic and clinical characteristics and (2) survival to hospital discharge stratified by hospitalization-related factors.Generalized linear models with a Poisson distribution and log link were applied separately for each subgroup, with calendar year modeled as a continuous predictor and population at risk included as an offset. Deviance-based corrections accounted for overdispersion. Annual percentage changes with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated, with p<0.05 indicating statistical significance. Results: Significant shifts in OHCA hospitalization patterns were observed. The proportion of hospitalized female patients declined by 0.60% per year (95% CI, –0.76% to –0.45%; p<0.0001), while male hospitalizations increased by 0.37% per year (95% CI, 0.28% to 0.46%; p<0.0001). Hospitalizations among Black patients decreased modestly (–1.30% per year; 95% CI, –2.56% to –0.03%; p=0.045), whereas Hispanic/Latino patients demonstrated a substantial increase (4.94% per year; 95% CI, 2.17% to 7.79%; p=0.0004).Clinically, the proportion of patients achieving sustained return of spontaneous circulation declined (–2.58% per year; 95% CI, –4.41% to –0.72%; p=0.0066), while hospitalizations without sustained ROSC increased modestly. The proportion pronounced dead in the emergency department decreased significantly (–6.26% per year; 95% CI, –10.24% to –2.10%; p=0.0035).Despite these shifts, no subgroup demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in survival to discharge. Overall survival increased by 1.54% per year (95% CI, –2.18% to 5.39%; p=0.42), with similarly non-significant findings across arrest characteristics and hospitalization factors. Conclusions: From 2019 to 2024, OHCA hospitalization patterns shifted across demographic and clinical subgroups, with persistent disparities and declining sustained ROSC. Despite these changes, survival to hospital discharge has not significantly improved. These findings highlight ongoing inequities and underscore the need for targeted, system-level interventions to improve OHCA outcomes.

articles.title: Abstract P2022: Functional Recovery After Cardiac Arrest Understanding Paths and Potential
articles.abstract: Introduction: Survivorship after cardiac arrest includes cognitive, emotional, and physical aspects of recovery. Domain specific recovery trajectories are individualized and under-reported in the literature. Understanding recovery capacity is critical for optimizing goal setting when counseling patients and their caregivers. Methods: We performed a retrospective analysis of comatose cardiac arrest survivors enrolled in our single-center acute brain injury repository between 2/5/2022 and 12/11/2025. We excluded patients who died prior to hospital discharge or who had no follow up modified Rankin Scale score (mRS). Patients were followed prospectively, and mRS was determined using patient and family interviews. Patients discharged alive with at least one follow-up mRS at any of the four time-points (3-month, 6-month, one year, two years) were included in the analysis. Good outcome was defined as mRS 0-3; longitudinal mRS changes were assessed with a Sankey plot. Results: Among the 56 patients [mean (SD) age 57.7 (16.8) years] included, 89.3% (n=50) were out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. The most common arrest etiology was cardiac (n = 36, 64.3%), of which the majority (n = 26, 72.2%) had a shockable rhythm, followed by respiratory (n = 15, 26.8%). Median (IQR) length of stay was 14 (9-22) days. The most common discharge locations were home (n=31, 55.4%) and short-term rehabilitation (n=14, 25%). Median (IQR) number of mRS assessments was 2 (2-3). Good outcome increased from 23 patients at three months to 26 patients at one year. There was one patient with poor outcome at one-year (mRS 4) who improved to good outcome at two years (mRS 0). In a sub-analysis of patients with an mRS at both 3-months and 1-year (n=11), 4 (36.4%) patients with mRS 2-3 improved to mRS 0-1. Conclusion: Functional neurologic recovery following cardiac arrest varies over time. Understanding recovery trajectories and factors associated with improvement are critical to maximizing survivorship potential. Our preliminary findings convey that recovery can be delayed, and possible up to two years following arrest.

articles.title: Abstract P2023: Hospital Readmission and Mortality in Cardiac Arrest Survivors Discharged with Favorable Neurologic Outcome
articles.abstract: Introduction: Even among cardiac arrest survivors discharged with favorable neurologic outcomes, the risk of subsequent cardiac and non-cardiac complications, hospital re-admission, and mortality remains substantial. A better understanding of the causes and predictors of post-discharge re-admission and death is essential to developing targeted follow-up strategies, optimizing long-term recovery, and improving cardiac arrest survivorship. Methods: We performed a retrospective analysis of cardiac arrest survivors enrolled in a single center cardiac arrest recovery program (CARP) between 1/19/2024 and 5/9/2026. The CARP program follows all in-hospital (IHCA) and out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients from index hospitalization admission to discharge, at which point those who awaken and were following basic commands were enrolled. Enrollment included an evaluation for psychological and cognitive symptoms, as well as post-discharge neurology clinic appointment (on average three months post-discharge). Amongst enrolled patients, hospital re-admissions and mortality occurring prior to post-discharge neurology clinic visit were tracked. Results: Of 105 enrolled patients, 34 (32.4%) underwent hospital readmission. The median [interquartile range] time from index cardiac arrest discharge to re-admission was 16 [8-99.8] days. Eight (7.6% of all patients, 24% of re-admitted patients) died at a median of 71.5 [20-160] days from index hospital discharge. The most common cause of death was withdrawal of life sustaining therapy (50%, n=4), followed by recurrent arrest without ROSC (25%, n=2). Amongst those who survived the readmission, the median [IQR] length of stay was 4 [2-10] days and the most common admission diagnoses included cardiopulmonary dysfunction (n=13, 38.2%) and neuropsychiatric symptoms (n=11, 32.4%). Patients requiring readmission were more likely to have suffered an IHCA, were younger, had longer length of stay, and were less likely to be discharged home (Table 1). Conclusion: Cardiac arrest survivors experience a heightened risk for readmission and mortality, even after discharge with good neurologic outcome. The most common causes for readmission were cardiopulmonary and neurologic symptoms. Further work to help identify those at highest risk for readmission and to evaluate the impact of a nurse navigator on readmission rate and mortality should be prioritized.

articles.title: A “Significant” Shift in Statistical Interpretation in Ecology and Evolution: A Helpful Guide for Authors and Reviewers
articles.abstract: “Statistical significance”, wherein the deviation of some measure of a sample population is greater than an expected threshold (usually p > 0.05) is a concept and practice strongly embedded in the life sciences. However, the use of “statistical significance” has been deprecated by the American Statistical Association (ASA), and that news has been slow to spread across disciplines. The result of this misuse is that many authors are wrongfully claiming “no effect” of a variable when p > 0.05 or confidence intervals (CIs) overlap zero. To ensure scientific rigor in Ecology and Evolution, we offer this brief guide to authors and reviewers and strongly encourage authors to use the ASA statement on p‐values. The ASA suggests that authors report effect sizes and attendant error in ways that let users judge support for the hypotheses represented in a model, avoiding the binary “true or false” of p = 0.05 or overlapping CIs. Furthermore, we encourage authors to acquaint themselves with numerous other common mistakes in statistical interpretation highlighted by the ASA and subsequent authors. By incorporating these principles into statistical reporting and results, information and patterns that might otherwise be overlooked remain available for readers to evaluate. We recognize that changes in reporting practices will not occur overnight, so our aim is to help authors adopt ASA principles: to that end we describe potential problems and offer guidelines for authors and reviewers to follow, to avoid incorrect statistical interpretations and spurious conclusions.

articles.title: Broad‐Scale Landscape Structure and Fine‐Scale Microhabitat Jointly Shape the Distribution of the Jeju Salamander, Hynobius quelpaertensis
articles.abstract: Species distribution models often assume that species occupy all environmentally suitable space, but low-dispersal amphibians may track landscape structure that has persisted over long periods as well as current local conditions. We examined how broad-scale landscape structure and fine-scale microhabitat jointly shape the distribution of the Jeju salamander, Hynobius quelpaertensis, on Jeju Island, Republic of Korea. Using 85 spatially thinned occurrence records and 10,000 background points sampled on land, we compared a broad-scale predictor set (terrain at ≥ 1 km, drainage position and long-term climate, used as a proxy for a long-term topographic-hydrological template) with a fine-scale set (microtopography, wetness, insolation and canopy). Weighted elastic-net models were evaluated by spatial block cross-validation with block-bootstrap confidence intervals, and a generalized additive model (GAM) with broad-scale suitability as an offset tested whether microhabitat refined occupancy within broadly suitable space. The broad-scale and fine-scale models discriminated occurrences equally well (ROC AUC = 0.79 and 0.78), but the broad-scale model was better calibrated (Tjur's R 2 = 0.16 vs. 0.12), and the combined model performed best (ROC AUC = 0.81; Tjur's R 2 = 0.20). Both sets identified drainage position: occurrence increased with upstream drainage area and local wetness and was higher in hollows and valley bottoms. Within the broad-scale core, fine-scale smooth terms doubled Tjur's R 2 (0.14 to 0.28): occurrence rose with canopy shade and valley depth and declined on exposed south-facing slopes, although the gain in discrimination was uncertain. Areas suitable only at the fine scale covered 24% of the island but had one-sixth the presence rate of areas suitable at both scales. Valley drainage structure thus sets the template for the distribution of H. quelpaertensis, and shaded, moist microhabitat refines occupancy within it. Conservation should maintain drainage networks together with their forest cover, and candidate unoccupied areas should be surveyed in the field.

articles.title: Comparative Chloroplast Genomics Reveals Phylogenetic Relationships Among Korean Dioscorea Species
articles.abstract: Crop wild relatives represent important sources of genetic variation for crop improvement, particularly as climate change and increasing global food demand require the development of more resilient and productive crop varieties. However, genomic information on many wild Dioscorea species in East Asia remains limited. In this study, we sequenced and assembled the complete chloroplast genomes of six Dioscorea species native to Korea, including the first reported complete chloroplast genome of D. coreana. The assembled genomes exhibited a conserved quadripartite structure with similar gene contents and GC compositions across species. Despite this overall conservation, comparative analyses revealed localized sequence variation, particularly in noncoding regions. Several loci, including ndhF and ycf1, exhibited increased nucleotide diversity, indicating their potential as informative markers. In addition, simple sequence repeats were composed mainly of A/T‐rich motifs and predominantly distributed in the large single‐copy region. Phylogenetic analysis based on concatenated chloroplast protein‐coding gene sequences provided a well‐resolved framework for the studied taxa and clarified the relationships among Korean Dioscorea species. Furthermore, the close genetic relationship between cultivated yam and its wild relatives was supported. These results provide new genomic data for previously underrepresented Korean taxa, including the first chloroplast genome of D. coreana, and offer a basis for future studies on genetic diversity, species identification, and the utilization of wild germplasm.

articles.title: Conservation Implications of High Population Genetic Structure Detected in a Parasitic Fluke of Diamondback Terrapins
articles.abstract: Parasites are increasingly utilized as surrogates for investigating host ecology. Digenean trematodes (“flukes”) have been identified as promising bioindicators because they have obligate multi‐host life cycles that often include an abundant and accessible gastropod intermediate host and one or more vertebrate definitive hosts. Definitive vertebrate hosts are typically the mechanism for dispersal by flukes, thus driving congruent patterns in population genetic structure between host and parasite. This suggests that flukes can function as surrogates for understanding dispersal of their vertebrate hosts. Here, we investigated the terrapin fluke Pleurogonius malaclemys as a surrogate for its definitive diamondback terrapin host Malaclemys terrapin. This parasite is reliant on its intermediate host, the eastern mudsnail Ilyanassa obsoleta, as well as terrapin final hosts. We hypothesized that there would be high population genetic structure across fluke populations, reflecting the limited dispersal rates and low population connectivity of terrapin hosts. Specimens of Pleurogonius malaclemys were sampled from mudsnails (internal first‐intermediate and external cyst stages) and from terrapins (adult stage) across their co‐occurring range from Massachusetts to northeast Florida. Fluke mitochondrial DNA was extracted and sequenced, and a 620 bp fragment was used for population genetics analyses. Asexually reproducing larval fluke stages were rare within mudsnails (often 0%, but never exceeding 3.85%), while external cysts were common on mudsnails (up to 74%). About 45% of terrapins from southern New Jersey harbored adult flukes. Genetics analyses revealed high diversity and population genetic structure in flukes, broadly consistent with reported patterns for terrapins. Our study provides baseline genetic data and a foundational understanding of the biogeography and diversity of the terrapin fluke, thereby identifying a promising surrogate for terrapin population ecology and subsequent conservation efforts.

articles.title: Relationship Between Predicted Habitat Suitability and Population Density of Game Mammals Under a Sharply Continental Climate
articles.abstract: This study evaluates the relationship between MaxEnt-predicted habitat suitability and departmental estimates of population density for 14 game mammal species in the Pavlodar Region. Model performance varied substantially among species (Test AUC = 0.538–0.992; TSS = 0.220–0.984), and extremely high AUC values for some species with small samples were interpreted cautiously. For 41 territorial units, habitat suitability was aggregated as the mean MaxEnt value within each polygon and compared with density using Spearman's rank correlation. Spearman's r s ranged from 0.288 to 0.738; in the initial analysis, a statistically significant positive relationship was detected for 13 of the 14 species, whereas the relationship was not statistically significant for the steppe polecat (r s = 0.288; p = 0.068). Residual spatial autocorrelation assessed with Moran's I was non-significant for 11 species; for wolf, bobak marmot, and roe deer, an additional spatially constrained permutation analysis was performed. After this analysis, the relationship remained significant for wolf (r s = 0.714, p = 0.0007) and roe deer (r s = 0.488, p = 0.0198), whereas for bobak marmot it remained positive but was not statistically significant after accounting for spatial structure (r s = 0.467; p = 0.0615). The results indicate that habitat suitability reflects the environmental potential of an area but is not a direct measure of population density.

articles.title: Siblings in Flight: Unravelling Reproductive Barriers Between Two Butterfly Sister Species
articles.abstract: Understanding how reproductive isolation is maintained between closely related taxa is a central question in evolutionary biology. Here, we investigate the mechanisms underlying divergence and isolation between two sister butterflies, Erebia palarica and Erebia meolans, which occur in sympatry in the Cantabrian Mountains (N Spain) and in allopatry elsewhere. Using an integrative approach, we combine genetic, genome synteny and cytogenetic analyses, Wolbachia screening, and geometric morphometrics to assess their evolutionary history and elucidate potential reproductive barriers between these species. The phylogeographic pattern suggests that both species diverged in allopatry, coming into secondary contact along the Cantabrian Mountains after the last glacial maximum. Both mitochondrial and nuclear markers recover reciprocal monophyly, indicating the absence of recent hybridisation. The identical chromosome numbers in both species (2n = 28), the absence of major chromosomal rearrangements or straightforward genitalia differentiation, and the presence of the same Wolbachia strain in all infected individuals suggest that neither chromosomal rearrangements nor Wolbachia‐induced incompatibilities contribute to their reproductive isolation in sympatry. In contrast, morphometric analyses show a significant divergence in wing size consistent with asymmetric character displacement: sympatric populations of E. palarica exhibit larger wings relative to both allopatric conspecifics and sympatric E. meolans, whereas E. meolans shows little size variation across northern Spain. Our findings point to wing size divergence in E. palarica as a response to sympatry with E. meolans. Overall, this study provides novel empirical evidence for morphometric character displacement in the family Nymphalidae, highlights the importance of multidisciplinary approaches for understanding species differentiation, and sets a framework for future genomic studies of speciation and reproductive isolation between closely related taxa.

articles.title: Thermoregulatory strategy shapes physiological responses to dormancy in animals: A meta‐analysis
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Dormancy allows animals to persist through prolonged periods of unfavourable environmental conditions by entering states of extreme metabolic depression. However, physiological responses to dormancy vary substantially across taxa and can involve changes in redox balance, immune function and endocrine adjustments. A key unresolved question is whether this variation reflects fundamental differences in how endotherms and ectotherms regulate metabolic depression and subsequent reactivation, with implications for understanding animal life histories and responses to climate change. Here, we conducted a meta‐analysis to test whether physiological responses to dormancy differ between endothermic and ectothermic animals. We synthesised 2464 effect sizes from 106 studies across 57 species, quantifying redox, immune and glucocorticoid status during dormant and arousal states relative to active, non‐dormant state, under cold‐ and heat‐induced dormancy. In endotherms, dormant and arousal states were associated with reduced oxidative damage and reactive oxygen species production, together with increased antioxidant and redox‐regulatory activity, indicating robust maintenance of redox homeostasis across metabolic transitions. In contrast, ectotherms experienced increased oxidative damage during the dormant state under both cold‐ and heat‐induced conditions, with little evidence for compensatory antioxidant responses. Immune function also diverged across thermoregulatory strategies: while endotherms showed no overall suppression of immune function during dormancy and an increase in innate immune responses during arousal, ectotherms tended to downregulate both innate and adaptive pathways during the dormant state. By contrast, glucocorticoid levels did not show consistent changes across dormancy states in either group. Our study shows that the physiological consequences of animal dormancy vary across thermoregulatory strategies. Endothermy seems to buffer the oxidative and immunological challenges associated with metabolic depression, whereas dormancy in ectotherms is associated with physiological trade‐offs that may limit adaptive capacity to changing conditions. Our synthesis highlights metabolic depression as a key axis linking thermoregulation to variation in physiology, with implications for the evolution of life histories and prediction of species responses to ongoing environmental change. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Deadwood Mitigates Declines in Soil Food‐Web Energy Fluxes in Canopy Gaps
articles.abstract: Across forests worldwide, frequent climate extremes and intensified timber harvest are reshaping forest structure by increasing tree mortality and canopy opening, threatening terrestrial biodiversity and ecosystem sustainability. In unmanaged forests, natural disturbances create canopy gaps and leave substantial deadwood on site, whereas timber harvesting creates gaps through the removal of living trees, thereby limiting the accumulation of deadwood. However, how these disturbances and management practices affect ecosystem functioning, especially of the belowground system, remains little understood. Here, we reconstructed 116 soil animal food webs in a full‐factorial experiment manipulating forest gaps and deadwood addition. We quantified energy fluxes of soil food webs as an integrative measure of belowground ecosystem functioning and investigated their network architecture 2 years after establishment of the experiment. Forest gaps reduced total food web energy fluxes by 13.4%, decreased network connectance, and shifted energy flow towards the bacteria‐dominated “fast” channel, indicating simplified soil food webs, impaired soil functioning, and reduced energy retention belowground. However, compared to gaps without deadwood, the presence of deadwood in gaps increased total energy flux by 37.4%, primarily through enhanced fungivory and wood‐feeding pathways, and restored network connectance and cycling rates to levels comparable to those in closed‐canopy forests. Our results demonstrate that deadwood acts as a key structural component that mitigates the detrimental effects of canopy gap formation on belowground ecosystem functioning, underscoring deadwood retention after timber harvest as a practical strategy to safeguard soil functioning in a more disturbance‐prone future.

articles.title: Projected Climate Change Impacts on Deep‐Sea Corals of the Red Sea
articles.abstract: Ocean warming, acidification, and deoxygenation, among other co‐occurring factors, are shifting species ranges throughout the marine environment. Mesophotic and deep corals are understudied in their response to climate changes, particularly in the Red Sea, which has relatively high temperatures and salinities and is projected to undergo major changes in the future, with little assessment of the impacts to date. Ecological niche modelling can be used to explain the known distribution of a species, predict its current range, and estimate future range shift under changing ocean scenarios. Here, we estimate the area of suitable habitat for four mesophotic and deep‐sea corals (Acanthogorgia spp., Stylaster tritoni, Bathypathes thermophila, and Madracis interjecta) across the whole Red Sea under present conditions and under different scenarios of future environmental changes (years 2090–2100). We found variations in the responses of these corals, but two of the four taxa are projected to lose significant amounts of their current habitats, while the other two lose a smaller portion. In particular, the scleractinian coral M. interjecta is likely to lose the largest proportion of its habitat, while the black coral B. thermophila may experience the least change. Deeper areas may become suitable for these corals, but colonisation will depend on their ability to disperse. We also assessed the potential biodiversity hotspots both now and in the future, finding the northern Red Sea to be one ecologically important area. These results enable marine spatial planning in support of an effective long‐term conservation action to protect these important habitats.

articles.title: Beyond the safety thresholds: Contrasting drought responses in Mediterranean seeders and resprouters revealed by hydraulic and leaf turgor safety margins
articles.abstract: We evaluated drought‐induced damage, resistance and recovery in several Mediterranean woody species spanning contrasting regeneration strategies. By integrating hydraulic and leaf turgor safety margins, foliar damages, mortality and non‐structural carbohydrates, we identified three drought‐induced functional phases. Mortality and recovery diverged between obligate seeders and resprouters, showing that crossing physiological safety thresholds does not necessarily translate into equivalent mortality outcomes. Abstract The Mediterranean region is warming around 20% faster than the global average, and models project declines between 10% and 30% in precipitation by the middle of the century. Increasing drought and heat stress conditions are causing massive climate‐driven forest decline and mortality episodes around the world, especially exacerbated in water‐limited ecosystems. Therefore, it is critical to understand species‐specific physiological thresholds underlying drought‐induced mortality. We experimentally compare drought resistance and short‐term resilience of Mediterranean woody species with contrasting post‐disturbance regeneration strategies (obligate seeders vs. resprouters) along a controlled drought stress gradient. Our aim is to unravel the physiological mechanisms behind drought‐induced mortality and assess variations in the safety thresholds of both plant regeneration strategies. We quantify hydraulic safety margins (HSM), leaf turgor safety margins (LTSM), leaf damage, mortality and non‐structural carbohydrates (NSC). Both HSM and LTSM decline as the drought intensifies, but their relationship with mortality differs from a simple threshold avoidance pattern. Mortality increases with decreasing HSM and LTSM in both regeneration strategies. Seeders show substantially higher mortality around HSM = 0, while resprouters frequently operate beyond HSM = 0 with lower mortality. Leaf damage emerges as a strong predictor of mortality, with a more severe response in seeders, while declining NSC concentrations were associated with a marked increase in mortality in seeders, but not in resprouters. Our results reinforce current mortality models that invoke dual thresholds, loss of stem conductivity and safety margins, and carbohydrate depletion as decisive predictors of drought‐induced mortality in plants. Synthesis. Our findings present key insights into the role of plant regeneration strategy and physiological characteristics in enhancing resilience to drought and identify different drought‐induced functional phases defined by the interaction between HSM and LTSM. These results emphasize the importance of promoting mixed communities of these co‐occurring strategies in the conservation and adaptive management plans of Mediterranean forest ecosystems in the context of global change. Resum La regió mediterrània s'està calfant aproximadament un 20% més ràpid que la mitjana mundial, i els models projecten una disminució de les precipitacions d'entre el 10% i el 30% per a la mitat de segle. L'augment de les condicions de sequera i estrès tèrmic està provocant episodis massius de declivi i mortalitat forestal induïts pel clima a tot el món, situació especialment agreujada en ecosistemes amb limitacions hídriques. Per això, resulta fonamental comprendre els llindars fisiològics específics de cada espècie que estan subjacent a la mortalitat induïda per la sequera. Comparem experimentalment la resistència a la sequera i la resiliència a curt termini d'espècies llenyoses mediterrànies amb estratègies de regeneració post‐pertorbació contrastants (espècies que es regeneren obligatòriament a partir de llavors enfront d'espècies rebrotadoras) al llarg d'un gradient controlat d'estrès hídric. El nostre objectiu és desentranyar els mecanismes fisiològics que expliquen la mortalitat induïda per la sequera i avaluar les variacions en els llindars de seguretat de les dues estratègies de regeneració vegetal.…

articles.title: Declines in dryland woody vegetation following an extended dry decade
articles.abstract: Two large‐scale field surveys, a dry decade apart, show decreases in woody vegetation cover, particularly in drier Mediterranean regions. However, species diversity provides critical resilience. Plant communities with high species richness‐maintained stability, effectively buffering drought impacts and preventing vegetation loss. Abstract Changes in temperature, rainfall regimes and water availability, as part of global climate change, lead to increased drought stress, especially in dry ecosystems. Yet empirical evidence of how woody vegetation responds to such climate drying remains scarce. We examined changes in woody cover and species composition across 71 woodland and shrubland sites, spanning the east Mediterranean climatic gradient, resurveyed a decade apart (2008–2009 and 2018–2019). The studied decade was characterized by reduced rainfall and a shorter rainy season combined with consistent warming, resulting in increasing aridity. Woody cover declined in 52% of sites and increased in 24% of them. The magnitude of decline was greatest in arid regions and was strongly predicted by mean annual precipitation. Model selection identified species richness as a stabilizing factor: sites with high species richness experienced smaller losses or maintained stable woody cover. At the species level, we identified seven dominant tree, shrub and sub‐shrub species. Of these, Quercus coccifera var. calliprinos showed consistent increases in cover, correlated with the rainfall gradient, whereas the cover of Pistacia lentiscus, Calicotome villosa, Cistus spp., and Sarcopoterium spinosum declined. The cover of Phillyrea latifolia and Rhamnus spp. was relatively stable. However, climatic variability explained only a small portion of the change in cover of each of the dominant species. Synthesis. Our results reveal a shift from the well‐documented trajectory of secondary woodland regeneration towards regional declines in woody cover under intensifying aridity. Our findings provide rare field‐based evidence that species richness enhances vegetation resistance to climate drying. תקופת יובש ממושכתאחר דעיכת הצומח המעוצה ל שינויים בטמפרטורה, במשטר הגשמים ובזמינות המים כחלק משינוי האקלים העולמי מובילים לעלייה בעקת יובש לצמחים במיוחד במערכות אקולוגיות יובשניות. עם זאת, עדויות אמפיריות לגבי האופן שבו צמחייה מעוצה מגיבה לעלייה בעקת יובש כזו נותרו מועטות. של מזרח הים התיכון, אשר נסקרו פעמיים בהפרש של עשור (2008–2009 ו‐2018–2019). העשור שנחקר אופיין בירידה בכמות הגשמים ובהתקצרות עונת הגשמים, בשילוב עם התחממות עקבית, מה שהוביל לעלייה ביובשנות. במחקר זה בחנו שינויים בכיסוי המעוצה ובהרכב המינים ב‐71 אתרי צומח טבעי ‐ חורשים, שיחיות ובתות, המשתרעים לאורך המפל האקלימי הכיסוי המעוצה ירד ב‐52% מהאתרים ועלה ב‐24% מהם. עוצמת הירידה הייתה הגדולה ביותר באזורים היבשים יחסית ונמצאה קשורה לכמות המשקעים השנתית הממוצעת. עושר המינים נמצא כגורם מייצב: השינוי בכיסוי הצומח היה קטן יותר או נשמר יציב באתרים בעלי עושר מינים גבוה. שעיר ומרווני, וסירה קוצנית ירד ברוב האתרים. הכיסוי של בר‐זית בינוני הראה עלייה כללית בכיסוי ומתאם למפל הגשם בעוד שהכיסוי של המינים אלת המסטיק, קידה שעירה, לוטם ברמת המין, זיהינו שבעה מיני עצים, שיחים ובני‐שיח דומיננטיים. מתוכם, האלון המצוי היה יציב יחסית. עם זאת, השונות האקלימית הסבירה רק חלק קטן מהשינוי בכיסוי של כל אחד מהמינים הדומיננטיים ואשחר א"י ונקוד. סינתזה :תוצאותינו חושפות תפנית מהמסלול המתועד היטב של סוקציה משנית לעבר דעיכה בכיסוי המעוצה עקב התגברות היובשנות. בנוסף, ממצאינו מספקים עדות נדירה מן השדה לכך שעושר מינים מגביר את עמידות הצמחייה לתהליך העלייה ביובשנות.

articles.title: Ambipolar Electrochemical Doping of CsPbBr 3 Nanocrystals
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Electronic doping underpins many semiconductor applications but has remained elusive for lead halide perovskite nanocrystals because their high density and low formation energy of defects easily compensate introduced dopants. Here, we use electrochemical doping as a strategy to avoid doping compensation. Electrochemical injection of electrons or holes into the nanocrystal is compensated by surface-adsorbed electrolyte counterions, therefore not compromising crystal structure. We accomplished ambipolar (n- and p-type) doped CsPbBr3 nanocrystals with charge carrier concentrations ranging from intrinsic up to 4.8 × 1017 cm–3 (corresponding to 0.25 charges per nanocrystal). We show that electrochemical doping is reversible and stable at these free carrier concentrations. The extent of doping and stability are enabled by the use of lecithin, a zwitterionic ligand that strongly binds to the surface of the CsPbBr3 nanocrystals while still allowing ion and electron transfer. Lecithin stabilizes the surface atoms by shifting the potentials for Pb2+ reduction and Br– oxidation outside of the bandgap. The inferred surface-chemistry design rules for stable electrochemical doping can also serve as a guideline for developing CsPbBr3 nanocrystals stable under high free-carrier concentrations in optoelectronic devices, such as light-emitting diodes or electronically triggered quantum light sources.

articles.title: CHARMM-Compatible Molecular Mechanics Force Fields for Multiscale Modeling of HIV-1 Replication Inhibitors
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Molecular dynamics simulations provide insight into inhibitor-protein interactions and support rational drug design; however, their accuracy depends on reliable molecular mechanics force field parameters and coarse-grained representations that retain relevant molecular features. Although force field parameter sets for biomacromolecules are well established, the chemical diversity of small-molecule inhibitors often requires the development of system-specific parameters. Here, we present a parametrization framework integrating quantum mechanical optimization, experimental benchmarking, and small-molecule coarse-graining, demonstrated using HIV-1 inhibitors targeting multiple stages of the viral replication cycle. We provide a curated data set of CHARMM-compatible force field parameters for 12 HIV-1 inhibitors and the HIV assembly cofactor inositol hexakisphosphate (IP6), together with geometry-optimized atomic structures and ligand restraint files. The resulting parameters are validated against experimental structural and thermodynamic benchmarks, including lenacapavir binding free energy estimates, through inhibitor-bound complex simulations. We demonstrate applications of the parameter data set by quantifying inhibitor-protein interactions, including the free-energy profile of an integrase strand transfer inhibitor interacting with the viral capsid lattice, and the binding energetics of an allosteric integrase inhibitor. Furthermore, we extend the all-atom inhibitor parameter data set through a novel coarse-graining strategy for small molecules that preserves key electrostatic features. The HIV-1 inhibitor force field parameter data set is a publicly available resource that establishes a unified framework for multiscale modeling of HIV-1 inhibitors and facilitates computational and structural biology studies of drug resistance and inhibitor design. More generally, the framework presented here is broadly applicable to small-molecule parametrization and multiscale simulations in other therapeutic and biomolecular contexts.

articles.title: Effects of semaglutide on cardiac structure and function in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity: a pre-specified cardiac magnetic resonance substudy of the CAMEO-SEMA trial
articles.abstract: As presented at the 2026 AHA Scientific Sessions, a cardiac magnetic resonance substudy of the CAMEO-SEMA trial showed that semaglutide significantly improved cardiac structure and function, including left atrial reservoir strain and left ventricular filling dynamics, in individuals with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity.

articles.title: Hemodynamic effects of semaglutide in individuals with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity: a placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial
articles.abstract: As presented at the 2026 American Heart Association Scientific Sessions, in a placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial, semaglutide significantly improved pulmonary artery wedge pressure and other hemodynamic parameters during low-intensity exercise in individuals with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity.

C2H2 zinc‐finger transcription factor FveJAG cooperates with SIMPLE LEAF1 to regulate compound leaf morphogenesis in strawberry
articles.abstract: Proposed model for the regulatory network of FveJAG governing leaf shape in woodland strawberry. Summary Leaves play a vital role in photosynthesis, respiration, and transpiration, significantly impacting a plant's adaptability and crop yield. Strawberry plants develop trifoliate compound leaves, the molecular regulatory pathways of which are not well‐understood. Here, we identified a woodland strawberry (Fragaria vesca) mutant, designated simple leaf 2 (sl2), which exhibits the complete suppression of the two lateral leaflets. The causal gene encodes a C2H2 zinc‐finger transcription factor that is homologous to JAGGED and is named FveJAG. A point mutation located within the intron triggers alternative splicing and generates a premature stop codon. The prior key transcriptional regulator of leaflet initiation, SIMPLE LEAF1 (SL1), directly targets the promoter of FveJAG to activate its transcription. The synergistic interaction between sl1 and sl2 indicates that SL1 and FveJAG function within the same regulatory pathway. Genetic and expression analyses suggest that FveJAG also acts downstream of FveMYB117a during leaflet initiation. Taken together, our results uncover a direct SL1 target gene and elucidate a complex regulatory network involving SL1, FveJAG, and FveMYB117a in strawberry compound leaf morphogenesis, offering further mechanistic insights into the genetic regulation of leaf complexity.

articles.title: PGCopilot: an AI‐assisted research agent for plant functional genomics
articles.abstract: System architecture of PGCopilot. The system architecture comprises four layers: (1) data sources, including locally built resources (Botanical Knowledge Base using ChromaDB and Qwen3‐embedding; Multi‐Database Resources with 1.83 M records across seven plant species) and runtime‐accessed external resources (PubMed via NCBI E‐utilities); (2) an MCP Tool Layer with 31 specialized tools built on the FastMCP framework, including locally developed tools implemented with FastMCP and the official STRING MCP service; (3) PGCopilot Core integrating prompt governance, LLM reasoning engine (DeepSeek‐V3.2), and evidence integration modules; and (4) a Query & Response Interface providing entity grounding, ID mapping, multi‐database retrieval, and conflict reporting. Summary The exponential expansion of multi‐omic data presents a major bottleneck for researchers seeking to derive biological insights from heterogeneous genomic resources. Although large language models (LLMs) enable natural language interaction with scientific knowledge, general‐purpose LLMs are not designed to reason over plant‐specific biological issues and frequently produce hallucinated or oversimplified outputs. We developed PGCopilot, an AI‐assisted research agent tailored for plant functional genomics. It integrated task planning, identifier disambiguation, and tool orchestration to actively retrieve and synthesize evidence across heterogeneous biological databases using the Model Context Protocol. Built on a knowledge base of 1.83 million records, together with online access to PubMed titles and available abstracts covering over 33 million indexed articles and STRING protein–protein interaction data, it could plan retrieval strategies and integrate evidence into grounded responses, reducing unsupported outputs and addressing data fragmentation and identifier discrepancies. In expert‐guided benchmarking, PGCopilot achieved higher performance than the evaluated baseline LLMs, demonstrating advantages in task relevance, evidence integration, hallucination control, and research utility, and providing more verifiable citations and explicit reporting of cross‐database inconsistencies. As an autonomous agent supporting multiturn tool interaction, it streamlined cross‐database evidence integration from labor‐intensive search‐and‐retrieval to automated analysis‐and‐synthesis. This approach streamlines cross‐database navigation and evidence integration, allowing researchers to focus more on hypothesis formulation, experimental design, and critical interpretation of comprehensive evidence.

articles.title: Alchemically Transferable Parameters for Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
articles.abstract: Machine-learned circuit parameters could remove one of the main bottlenecks of variational quantum eigensolvers: the classical optimization loop, with its typical barren plateaus, local minima, and costly energy and gradient evaluations, is replaced by a direct prediction. Prior work showed that machine-learning models paired with a structured circuit design can transfer across system size and structure within hydrogenic systems. The next step: Extending them to organic molecules would seem to require re-training on use-case-specific training sets. In this work, we show that this is not necessary by establishing an alchemical approach. A geometric projection places surrogate hydrogen atoms along the bond directions of the target molecule and so maps its local bonding environment onto small hydrogenic fragments. Existing hydrogenic solvers can then be reused as they are. The only new quantity is a single projection radius per bond type, which is fitted once on a small reference molecule and reused unchanged thereafter. We demonstrate the approach on the separable-pair circuit designs that have been used in prior work and extend the approach to multi-circuit approaches that span effective bases for quantum subspaces.

articles.title: Surface-Engineered BiVO4 Photocatalyst Enables Selective Water Oxidation for Water Splitting via a Photocatalysis–Electrolysis Hybrid System
articles.abstract: Selective water oxidation in the presence of thermodynamically favored competing oxidation reactions remains a major challenge for photocatalytic systems. BiVO4 is one of the most efficient visible-light-responsive photocatalysts for water oxidation and exhibits high activity in Fe3+-mediated water-oxidation systems. However, although accumulated Fe2+ can introduce competing oxidation pathways under strongly acidic Fe3+/Fe2+ redox conditions, effective strategies for suppressing these processes and maintaining selective water oxidation remain largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate a surface-engineering strategy that overcomes this limitation in BiVO4. Systematic investigation revealed that the poor activity of BiVO4 under strongly acidic Fe3+/Fe2+ conditions arises not only from catalyst degradation but also from competition with Fe2+ oxidation reactions. Surface modification of BiVO4 with W species, originally intended to improve acid durability, not only suppressed catalyst dissolution but also mitigated Fe2+-related performance losses, resulting in a marked enhancement of photocatalytic water oxidation. The activity enhancement correlated with highly dispersed surface W species localized near the outermost region of BiVO4. Notably, the highest activity was obtained before or near the onset of detectable WO3 crystallization, suggesting that the surface state of W species in this temperature range is more closely associated with the enhanced activity than crystalline WO3 domains under strongly acidic Fe3+/Fe2+ conditions. The optimized photocatalyst maintained efficient water oxidation while suppressing Fe2+-related performance losses, achieving an apparent quantum yield of 63% under Fe3+-based conditions and approximately 30% even under strongly acidic and concentrated Fe(ClO4)3 conditions relevant to hybrid water splitting. The optimized photocatalyst maintained selective water oxidation even as Fe2+ accumulated to approximately 100 mM, enabling nearly quantitative Fe3+-to-Fe2+ conversion under strongly acidic conditions. When incorporated into a photocatalysis–electrolysis hybrid system, the enhanced photocatalytic activity was directly translated into approximately 1.5-fold higher water-splitting performance than that of the benchmark H-Fe-Cs-WO3 system. These findings demonstrate that selective water oxidation can be maintained even in the presence of thermodynamically favored competing oxidation reactions through appropriate photocatalyst surface engineering, providing a useful strategy for photocatalysts operating in redox-mediated reaction environments, including photocatalysis–electrolysis hybrid water-splitting systems.

articles.title: Unseen but Avoidable: How Impurities Bias Electrocatalysis from Interface to Interpretation
articles.abstract: Impurities exert profound effects on electrocatalytic measurements and interpretations. Trace levels of contaminants introduced through electrolytes, electrodes, gases, or cell materials routinely generate false activity signals, accelerate degradation, and alter product selectivity. This review categorizes impurity effects by functional impact, including misleading activity, compromised stability, and shifted selectivity, and offers strategies to recognize, isolate, and mitigate these influences. We argue that reliable and reproducible electrocatalytic data require an impurity-aware approach, integrating both experimental protocols and systems engineering. By intentional design, impurities can be transformed from hidden liabilities into controlled variables, ensuring that reported advances in electrocatalysis reflect intrinsic catalyst properties and translate into durable energy technologies.

articles.title: Structural Evolution of State-Dependent Kinetics during Potassium Storage in Layered CrSe2
articles.abstract: Layered CrSe2 reversibly accommodates approximately one potassium (K) per formula unit, but the structural origin of its rate-dependent capacity remains unresolved. Operando synchrotron X-ray diffraction (SXRD) reveals the sequential P-3m1-R3m-C2/m phase pathway during cycling at different current rates. The P-3m1/R3m transformation exhibits the lattice discontinuity and becomes incomplete when increasing the current rate, as directly observed by operando SXRD. Chemical K deintercalation and state-resolved impedance measurements provide complementary evidence for sluggish kinetics near the fully deintercalated regime. Restricting the upper cutoff voltage will sacrifice some capacity but will improve electrochemical cycling capacity retention. These findings identify a particularly rate-sensitive structural region and show how phase-resolved characterization can guide voltage-window selection for layered potassium-storage electrodes.

articles.title: Antiambipolar and Bidirectional Photoresponse in Ternary van der Waals Heterostructure Transistors
articles.abstract: Next-generation nanoelectronics require device architectures that integrate high density, multifunctionality, and low power consumption. Antiambipolar transistors (AATs) are promising candidates for multivalued logic and intelligent sensing, yet conventional two-dimensional (2D) AATs suffer from low peak-to-valley current ratios (PVRs) and unidirectional self-driven photoresponse. Here, we report a multifunctional AAT based on a MoS2/Ta2NiS5/MoTe2 double van der Waals heterostructure (vdWH). The device exhibits outstanding antiambipolar transport characteristics, achieving an ultrahigh PVR of 1 × 107 and a peak current of 1.2 μA, surpassing those of most previously reported 2D AATs. By introducing Ta2NiS5 as an intermediate layer, a back-to-back type-I band alignment is established, enabling efficient modulation and reversal of interfacial band bending under different bias conditions. Simultaneously, under 635 nm illumination, the device exhibits a gate-tunable bidirectional photocurrent response, with responsivities of +2.94 and −0.65 A/W at Vgs = +40 and −40 V, respectively. Furthermore, the device is demonstrated in ternary logic inverters, in-sensor image convolution processing, and multimodal information encoding. These results demonstrate the potential of van der Waals heterostructure-based antiambipolar transistors for integrated and reconfigurable optoelectronic systems.

articles.title: Biscoordinated Strontium–Phenolic Networks for Bidirectional Repair of Dentin Hypersensitivity
articles.abstract: Dentin hypersensitivity (DH) is a widespread dental disease characterized by transient and sharp pain affecting routine oral activities, with a reported prevalence that can exceed 70%. While remineralization offers a promising therapeutic strategy to address the anatomical basis of exposed dentinal tubules, achieving long-term efficacy remains challenging due to mechanical abrasion and cariogenic biofilms. Herein, strontium–phenolic network nanoparticles (Sr-EGCG NPs) are developed via a facile, one-pot aqueous process for DH treatment. Unlike conventional transition-metal-based metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), the assembly of Sr-based MPNs is found to be dependent on alkaline conditions, yielding a distinct biscoordinated structure. When applied to exposed dentin, Sr-EGCG NPs exhibit rapid and stable adhesion mediated by abundant galloyl groups, maintaining tubule occlusion ratios exceeding 91.8% after simulated oral challenges, especially surpassing commercial Duraphat in thermocycling (Duraphat: 2.0%), while simultaneously reducing live bacterial coverage by over 97.5% at day 3. Crucially, Sr-EGCG NPs enable bidirectional dentin repair: in situ remineralization (achieving complete mineralized occlusion by day 7 both in vitro and in vivo) and the induction of tertiary dentin formation via the CaSR-mediated MAPK signaling pathway. Overall, this work provides insights into the rational design of Sr-based MPNs and expands the framework for developing biomaterials targeting DH.

articles.title: Coordinating Photoacid Generators Enable Site-Defined Metal–Oxo Cluster Lithography
articles.abstract: Lithographic patterning, which employs the solubility switch of photoresists to convert optical signals into nanostructures on the substrate, constitutes the primary top-down approach for high-precision nanomanufacturing. However, the stochastic defects arising from inhomogeneous reaction sites in photoresists pose a formidable challenge to reconciling the precision of sub-10 nm lithography. In this study, we present a coordinating photoacid generator (cPAG)-driven lithography strategy that has achieved a performance breakthrough through precise spatial control of acid sites. The resulting zirconium-oxo cluster photoresists, operating via cPAG-triggered precoordination and cluster cross-linking, demonstrate a two-orders-of-magnitude decrease in UV exposure dose. Furthermore, electron beam lithography has been demonstrated to achieve a sub-10 nm line width, underscoring its suitability for high-resolution and high-sensitivity applications. This strategy is versatile across cPAGs with diverse structures and is also applicable to other metal oxide photoresist systems, including titanium-oxo and zinc-oxo clusters. This work introduces a cPAG design tailored for cluster-based photoresists and validates their ability to overcome the intrinsic trade-off in resolution, line edge roughness, and sensitivity, providing a framework for developing next-generation photoresists.

articles.title: Quantum Dot Colloidosomes as Triggerable Microlasers
articles.abstract: Quantum dot (QD) supraparticle lasers are promising platforms for microscale light sources and photonic labeling, yet their optical properties are set during assembly. Here, we introduce QD colloidosomes, liquid-core/solid-shell supraparticles that combine whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) optical feedback with stimulus-triggered structural collapse. Intact QD colloidosomes exhibit narrow, cavity-defined emission consistent with WGM-assisted lasing from 4.2 mJ/cm2, with line widths of 2.2–3.7 nm, demonstrating light confinement without a solid core. We identify shell continuity as a critical determinant for WGM feedback and lasing by exploring a morphological continuum of suprastructures comprising solid supraparticles, colloidosomes, and microporous hollow shells. Intact colloidosomes support narrow cavity modes, whereas porous shells remain broadband even at high pump fluence. We show that colloidosomes can be driven to rupture and release payload through well-defined pathways, including meniscus-driven capillary failure, uniform heating, and localized near-infrared activation, thereby configuring their optical response from cavity-defined lasing to broadband emission. These results establish QD colloidosomes as stimuli-responsive microlasers that couple optical-state switching and triggered release within a single self-assembled platform.

articles.title: Self-Dissociating Albumin Nanoclusters for Passive Lymph Node-Targeted Inverse Vaccination in a Rheumatoid Arthritis Model
articles.abstract: Engineering lymph node-targeted tolerogenic nanomaterials requires simultaneous antigen–drug coloading and efficient lymphatic transport. However, conventional biocompatible nanoparticles with static architectures often face a size-dependent trade-off: larger particles enable cargo coloading but drain inefficiently to lymph nodes, whereas smaller particles favor lymphatic transport but have limited cargo versatility. Here, a size-transformable, self-dissociating albumin nanocluster inverse vaccine is introduced to address this materials design trade-off. Citrullinated peptide antigens are conjugated to human serum albumin, and rapamycin (RAPA) is coloaded using ball-milling technology to generate 200–300 nm nanoclusters. After subcutaneous injection, the nanoclusters dissociate into sub-10 nm albumin-based units, enabling passive lymphatic transport and accumulation in draining lymph nodes while maintaining coordinated antigen–RAPA codelivery. In vitro mechanistic studies show that the nanoclusters induce a tolerogenic dendritic cell phenotype and promote antigen-specific immune regulation. In a collagen-induced arthritis mouse model, weekly administration attenuates synovial inflammation, humoral autoimmune responses, bone erosion, and cartilage degradation while expanding Foxp3+ regulatory T cells. These findings establish self-dissociation-mediated size transformation as a functional materials strategy for lymph node-targeted antigen-specific immune tolerance and tolerogenic nanomedicine.

articles.title: Unusual CD-ee Dependence in Self-Assembled Chiral Nanocomposites through Nanoparticle-Mediated Interactions
articles.abstract: Supramolecular self-assembly can produce a linear or a positive nonlinear CD versus enantiomeric excess (ee) relationship. Negative “racemate rules” behavior is rare. In this work, we report an unusual nonlinear CD-ee dependence in a coassembly system comprising chiral perylene diimide molecules and gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). In contrast to the linear majority-rules behavior observed for pure PDI molecules, the introduction of AuNPs induces a tendency toward heterochiral coaggregation, leading to a negative CD-ee correlation at low temperature (278 K) and a positive correlation at high temperature (318 K). Even both positive and negative CD-ee correlations can coexist and be tuned within a single self-assembling system. Combined molecular dynamics simulations and preassembly control experiments demonstrate that the nanoparticles reshape the chiral recognition pathway of PDI molecules through alkyl chain–chain van der Waals interactions, while the assembly temperature further modulates the majority-rules behavior. This work reveals a mechanism by which nanoparticles act as regulatory units in supramolecular chirality, offering a design strategy for programmable chiral materials.

articles.title: Vitamin E-Engineered Anti-Inflammatory Lipid Nanoparticles for Safer mRNA Delivery
articles.abstract: Great strides have been achieved in lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-mediated mRNA delivery. However, traditional LNPs can induce undesirable side effects such as inflammatory reactions. Oxidative stress damage arising from ionizable lipids within LNPs is regarded as a major underlying cause of these adverse effects. Herein, we propose incorporating endogenous vitamin E (VE) into the tail moiety of commercial ionizable lipids to improve biosafety. Proof-of-concept investigations using SM-102-derived W3 confirm that this endogenous antioxidant modification substantially mitigates the inflammatory toxicity of mRNA-loaded LNPs. Following intravenous administration, W3 LNPs markedly decrease the levels of multiple pro-inflammatory cytokines, demonstrating an improved safety profile compared to SM-102 LNPs. Further analysis reveals that W3 LNPs significantly reduce intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, alleviate oxidative stress damage, thereby inhibiting the activation of key inflammatory pathways such as NF-κB. Of note, the optimized formulation, sW3 LNPs enable efficient mRNA delivery to the spleen, with stronger antitumor efficacy and higher safety than SM-102 LNPs. In summary, W3 lipid confers minimal inflammatory adverse effects while preserving excellent delivery capability, which indicates that the VE-engineered LNPs possess great potential to serve as powerful and multifunctional platforms for next-generation mRNA therapeutics.
