Anchoring LiZn Nanocrystals With Oligomer Binders for Enhanced Interfacial Stability in Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Lithium (Li) metal batteries have emerged as one of the most promising candidates for next‐generation energy storage systems due to the potentially high energy density. Nevertheless, repeated interfacial breakdown causes a short lifespan and poor safety. Inspired by the role of plant root systems in anchoring soil, an oligomer‐anchored LiZn nanocrystal composite interphase is constructed on the Li metal anode via a simple spray‐coating strategy, simultaneously enhancing the electrochemical stability and thermal safety of Li metal batteries. The LiZn alloy in the composite interphase restructures the interface energy distribution and reduces the local current density, thereby facilitating uniform lateral Li deposition. The oligomer serves as a binder to glue LiZn particles together and preserve the structural integrity of the interphase. A Li||LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 coin cell with the composite interphase exhibits a lifespan of 700 cycles at 1 C with a high cathode loading of 3.06 mAh cm−2. The 1.38 Ah Li||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 86% after 200 cycles. When the cycled pouch cells undergo forced thermal runaway, the composite interphase elevates the trigger temperature from 124°C to 191°C. This interphase design provides novel insights to enhance the service lifespan and thermal safety of high energy density batteries.

articles.title: Differentiated Interfacial Proton Delivery for Durable CO2‐to‐Formate Electrosynthesis
articles.abstract: Interfacial ion and water organization critically influence proton-coupled electrochemical reactions, yet their coupled regulation under high-rate CO2 electroreduction remains poorly understood. Here, we construct a mosaic-and-gap-confined poly(dimethylsiloxane)-modified Bi (Bi-PDMS) interface that reorganizes the catalyst–electrolyte solvation environment. Atomistic simulations indicate altered near-surface cation accessibility and a less persistent extended hydrogen-bond environment, while slow-growth proton-transfer calculations show a substantially larger energetic penalty for selected extended proton-delivery pathways than for local proton transfer to *OCHO. Operando spectroscopy and mass spectrometry measurements further reveal potential-dependent interfacial water restructuring, suppressed hydrogen evolution, and enhanced formate-related pathway response. Bi-PDMS-30 sustains ∼90% formate Faradaic efficiency (FE) at −0.2 A cm− 2 for ∼200 h with substantially reduced surface-deposit accumulation. Together, these results support differentiated interfacial proton delivery within a reorganized ion–water environment as a useful framework for selective and durable CO2-to-formate electrosynthesis.

articles.title: Dual Suppression of Triplet Exciton and Energetic Disorder via Organic Room‐Temperature Phosphorescent Additive to Reduce Energy Loss in Organic Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Non‐radiative energy loss originating from triplet exciton generation and intrinsic energetic disorder severely restricts the efficiency breakthrough of organic solar cells (OSCs). To address this dual bottleneck, herein, two benzodiimide‐based solid additives with distinct photophysical properties, namely fluorescent HPmDI and room‐temperature phosphorescent (RTP) BrPmDI, are developed to simultaneously suppress triplet exciton dissipation and mitigate energetic disorder for high‐efficiency OSCs. Both additives construct favorable intermolecular interactions with the D18 donor and L8‐BO acceptor, optimizing active layer molecular packing, enhancing film crystallinity, and reducing Urbach energy to alleviate intrinsic energetic disorder. Benefiting from the unique long‐lived triplet exciton characteristics of organic RTP BrPmDI, an efficient Dexter energy transfer (DET) pathway is additionally enabled, which effectively inhibits non‐radiative decay channels, including intersystem crossing and charge recombination‐induced triplet exciton formation. Consequently, the optimized D18:L8‐BO‐based OSCs modified with BrPmDI achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 20.52% with a low non‐radiative energy loss of 0.217 eV, far outperforming the pristine device (19.01% and 0.226 eV) and HPmDI‐modified device (19.70% and 0.219 eV). This work reveals the dual regulatory mechanism of organic RTP additives on triplet exciton dynamics and energetic disorder, providing a facile strategy for the design of high‐efficiency additive materials toward low‐energy‐loss and high‐performance OSCs.

articles.title: Fully Roll‐to‐Roll Coated Large‐Area Perovskite Solar Modules on Indium‐Free Microgroove Substrates
articles.abstract: Perovskite photovoltaics offer a promising route to low‐cost, low‐carbon solar energy, but progress toward largescale deployment is limited by manufacturing scalability, stability, and dependence on scarce materials. We demonstrate fully roll‐to‐roll coated, large‐area back‐contact perovskite photovoltaic modules based on a microgroove architecture that removes the need for transparent conductors such as Indium Tin Oxide (ITO). Devices are continuously manufactured on flexible substrates using scalable embossing, vacuum deposition, solution printing, and encapsulation. Modules with active areas up to 48.2 cm2 achieve record power conversion efficiencies exceeding 12.5 % and are further scaled to panels larger than 1000 cm2. The first comprehensive stability study of fully roll‐to‐roll coated perovskite modules is presented, including ISOS‐compliant accelerated ageing and up to five months of outdoor operation. Nanoscale x‐ray fluorescence tomography identifies key degradation pathways within the microgroove architecture. In addition to scalable fabrication, the architecture enables intrinsic bifaciality, improved angular response, and linear shading tolerance, enhancing real‐world energy yield and supporting sustainable largescale deployment beyond conventional photovoltaics.

articles.title: Non‐Planar Chlorine‐Coordinated Activation of Triatomic Ruthenium Sites for Efficient Oxygen Reduction
articles.abstract: The intrinsic electronic structure of Ru-based catalysts exhibits strong adsorption of oxygen-containing intermediates, which runs counter to the adsorption requirements of the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), limiting their ability to achieve high activity. In this study, we employed a spatial confinement-pyrolysis strategy to develop a chlorine-doped triatomic Ru catalyst (Ru3ClNC), whose active center consists of a Ru3ON6Cl unit stabilized by both Ru─Ru bonds and Ru─N/O/Cl coordination bonds. Ru3ClNC delivers a high alkaline half-wave potential (E 1/2) of 0.90 V and an acidic E 1/2 of 0.79 V; the assembled zinc-air battery demonstrates excellent performance in terms of energy density and durability. In situ experiments and theoretical calculations have demonstrated the superiority of Ru3ON6Cl as the electrocatalytic ORR active site. The non-planar coordination effects and electronic effects of the Cl atom, in synergy with the triatomic site, disrupt the high symmetry, trigger charge redistribution, and significantly optimize the localized electron density at the active site. Importantly, the rearranged electronic structure breaks the linear scaling relationship in the d-band, enabling the catalyst to simultaneously optimize the rate-determining step of Ru3NC and OH* desorption, thereby enhancing reaction kinetics. This provides a new design concept for Ru-based catalysts to overcome the thermodynamic limitations and thereby improve the ORR activity.

articles.title: Rational Terminal‐Group Engineering of Guest Acceptors for 20.7% Efficient Organic Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Achieving higher efficiency in organic solar cells requires simultaneous control over energy-level alignment, acceptor aggregation, and active-layer crystallization. Herein, two guest acceptors, S-SMA and AS-SMA, were designed by stepwise replacing the fluorinated terminal group of L8-BO with a weaker electron-withdrawing 2-(3-ethyl-4-oxothiazolidin-2-ylidene)malononitrile (CN-Rh) unit. This terminal-group engineering upshifts the acceptor energy levels, enables cascade the lowest unoccupied molecular energy levels among D18, the guest acceptor, and L8-BO, and regulates blend morphology. In situ spectroscopic analysis reveals that both guest acceptors accelerate the liquid-to-solid transition during film formation and promote tighter molecular packing. Compared with symmetric S-SMA, asymmetric AS-SMA enables a more favorable morphology and device operation, as reflected by suitable domain sizes, suppressed trap-assisted recombination, and more balanced charge transport. Consequently, the ternary D18:L8-BO:AS-SMA device delivers the best overall photovoltaic performance, achieving a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.71% with an open-circuit voltage (V OC) of 0.930 V and a fill factor (FF) of 80.62%. These results demonstrate that asymmetric terminal-group engineering is an effective strategy for coordinating energy-level tuning, crystallization kinetics, and morphology optimization in high-performance ternary organic solar cells.

articles.title: Synergistic Crystallization Regulation and Defect Suppression via Dual‐Site Molecular Coordination for Efficient Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Defects in polycrystalline perovskite films induce carrier ion migration and recombination, restricting the efficiency and durability of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Conventional additive strategies based on ammonium salts often provide insufficient defect passivation and poor long-term stability. Herein, (1H-benzo[d]imidazol-2-yl)methanamine hydrochloride (BMHCl) serves as a multifunctional molecule regulator to cooperatively regulate defect evolution and crystallization kinetics through dual-site molecular interactions in inverted PSCs. Benefiting from the coordinated interactions of the protonated amino group (─NH3 +) and electron-rich nitrogen atoms with defective [PbI6]4− octahedra, BMHCl effectively regulates crystallization kinetics, suppresses defect formation, and alleviates residual lattice strain. Consequently, the BMHCl-modified perovskite films exhibit enhanced crystallinity, enlarged grain sizes, optimized vertical orientation, and reduced trap density. These combined microstructural improvements facilitate charge carrier transport while suppressing non-radiative recombination. BMHCl also produces more favorable energy-level alignment and faster interfacial charge extraction. Consequently, the champion PSC achieves the conversion efficiency of 26.50% while demonstrating excellent operational and damp-heat stability, retaining 87.49% and 80.52% of its initial efficiency after 1000 h at 85°C and 800 h at 85°C, 85% relative humidity, respectively. This work demonstrates a practical molecular-interaction strategy for efficient and durable inverted PSCs based on multifunctional, dual-site passivation and crystallization regulation.

articles.title: Ultra‐High Ionic Conductivity Sulfide‐Based Composite Membranes Paired With Stable Interfacial Layer Enables High‐Energy‐Density All‐Solid‐State Batteries
articles.abstract: Intrinsic properties of sulfide solid‐state electrolytes (SEs) are crucial for achieving all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) with high safety and high energy density, yet it is challenging to fabricate high‐performance sulfide SE films in a scalable approach. Furthermore, the inevitable side reactions between sulfide SE and lithium metal anodes exacerbate interfacial incompatibility, causing degradation in the cyclic stability. Here, a high‐performance sulfide SE (Li5.4PS4.4Cl0.8Br0.8) was selected as the base phase to compensate for the loss of electrochemical performance during the dry film‐forming process. It was then combined with Polytetrafluoroethylene binder to prepare a high‐ionic‐conductivity composite membrane (HICCM). To mitigate side reactions between HICCM and the anode, a LiF‐rich interfacial layer forms in situ on the lithium metal surface, and the assembled symmetric cell achieves a high critical current density of 1.3 mA cm−2 and stable cycling for 2000 h (0.2 mA cm−2). For electrochemical performance, HICCM exhibits fast ion transport kinetics and electrical insulation, allowing the ASSB configured as FeS2//HICCM//LiF‐Li to achieve an energy density of 416.5 Wh kg−1 at a high loading of 3.4 mAh cm−2. This work demonstrates that by combining HICCM with a stable interface design, ASSBs can achieve longevity and high cell‐level energy density.

articles.title: Use of Biologics and Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors During Pregnancy in Patients with Systemic Autoimmune Diseases and Cancer
articles.abstract: Biologics and immune checkpoint inhibitors have transformed the treatment of autoimmune conditions and cancers. However, safety data regarding use during pregnancy are limited. Clinicians are left to weigh the potential benefits of treatment with frequently unknown risks to the pregnant patient and developing fetus. These therapies do not cross the placenta during the first trimester; thus, they are unlikely to cause teratogenicity. Use later in pregnancy has the potential to immunosuppress the neonate, which could lead to infection and inadequate vaccine response. These large molecules are minimally transferred into breastmilk and are mostly compatible with nursing.

articles.title: Differential Regulatory Activities of Potassium and Aldosterone in the Distal Nephron: A Resolution to the Aldosterone Paradox
articles.abstract: Aldosterone has long been viewed as a master regulator of fluid and electrolyte homeostasis, acting through the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) to stimulate electrogenic Na + transport via the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) in the distal nephron. This primary effect is thought to drive both K + secretion and Cl − reabsorption; however, the underlying mechanism has remained obscure and the dual regulation has generated an enigma often referred to as the aldosterone paradox. Here we propose a model for regulated K + secretion centered on local regulation of ENaC in the late distal convoluted tubule and early connecting tubule. In this segment, the MR is constitutively activated by glucocorticoids rather than by aldosterone, and yet ENaC activity and K + secretion through the renal outer medullary K + channel (ROMK) are not constitutive but, rather, are highly regulated. The model holds that the key regulatory step for K + secretion involves a cell-autonomous mechanism through which local interstitial [K + ] stimulates mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2)-dependent phosphorylation of the ENaC regulatory serum- and glucocorticoid-induced kinase 1 (SGK1); the K+-sensing kinase augments this phosphorylation by serving as a scaffold to enhance the physical interaction of mTORC2 with SGK1. Aldosterone acts further downstream to stimulate ENaC primarily in the late CNT and cortical collecting duct, in which ROMK apical expression is relatively low and Na + -Cl − reabsorption is favored. This revised paradigm resolves the aldosterone paradox and has important implications for hypertension, potassium disorders, and potentially medical therapies.

articles.title: What's Coming Up Next? The Physiology of Gastroparesis and GLP-1 Agonists
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is an incretin to regulate glycemia, activates peripheral and central neural pathways to control appetite, and inhibits upper gut transit to reduce food intake. Peptide and nonpeptide GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), as well as a combined GLP-1 and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), agonist are approved for type 2 diabetes, weight reduction, and other indications. GLP-1RA therapy can be complicated by upper gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms, including nausea and vomiting. Delayed gastric emptying secondary to GLP-1RAs may be influenced by drug pharmacokinetics, associated neuropathy, and development of tachyphylaxis with repeated dosing. A theoretical risk of pulmonary aspiration from retained gastric contents is concerning for patients undergoing anesthesia before endoscopy or surgery. Managing upper GI complications of GLP-1RA therapy includes diet modifications, antiemetic medications, and treatments that stimulate gastric emptying. Newer agents in testing include nonpeptide GLP-1RAs and GLP-1RAs acting in concert with GIP, glucagon, or other receptor-mediated pathways.

articles.title: Proteolytic dissection of eIF4G reveals that closed-loop mRNP formation is dispensable for bulk translation in mammalian cells
articles.abstract: The "closed-loop" mRNP, in which the 5' cap and 3' poly(A) tail are bridged by eIF4E-eIF4G-PABP interactions, has been proposed to drive efficient translation. Direct rigorous tests of this model in mammalian cells have remained elusive. Using auxin-inducible degrons to acutely deplete eIF4G1, we find that global translation is only partially reduced and recovers without restoration of eIF4G1 levels. We identify eIF4G3 as an underappreciated contributor to basal translation that buffers translational output upon eIF4G1 loss. eIF4G1 mutants reveal that PABP binding by eIF4G1 is dispensable for bulk protein synthesis. Further, PABP depletion has no immediate effect on protein synthesis but instead destabilizes poly(A) mRNA. In contrast, the N-terminal enteroviral cleavage product (2A-cpN) is a potent, dominant translational repressor that requires both PABP- and eIF4E-binding domains for inhibition. These findings suggest that the eIF4G-PABP closed-loop architecture is not required for productive initiation but may be actively co-opted for translational silencing.

articles.title: ROP GTPases are required for YUC transcription and auxin-mediated root hair growth in Arabidopsis
articles.abstract: The ROP subfamily of Rho GTPases act as a key signaling switch in response to the phytohormone auxin, impacting auxin response and transport in plant growth and development. It remains unknown whether auxin biosynthesis is regulated by ROP. Using Arabidopsis root hairs as a system to study cell growth, we found that ROP2/4/6 GTPases act redundantly in root hair growth via control of YUC-dependent auxin biosynthesis. The rop2/4/6 mutant reduced root hair growth, auxin accumulation and transcription of all 11 YUC auxin biosynthesis genes. External auxin and overexpression, root hair specific or shoot-specific expression of YUC2/8 fully restored rop2/4/6 root hair growth. A phosphomimetic (S5D) mutation in the C-terminal domain (CTD) of RNA polymerase II RPB1 increased YUC2/8 expression and hair growth in rop2/4/6, linking the Pol II CTD phosphorylation code to ROP-mediated YUC transcription. Our results reveal auxin biosynthesis as another important regulatory layer for ROP function during cell growth.

articles.title: The FERONIA receptor kinase is required for high-humidity responses in Arabidopsis
articles.abstract: High humidity greatly influences plant growth and development and triggers adaptive physiological responses such as leaf hyponasty (elongation of the leaf petiole and upward leaf movement). Cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channels 2 and 4 (CNGC2/4), calmodulin-binding transcription activators 2 and 3 (CAMTA2/3)-dependent transcription, and ethylene signaling acting through EIN2 and EIN3/EIL1 are required for high-humidity response in Arabidopsis. However, upstream regulators controlling these steps remain unknown. Here, we show that the receptor-like kinase FERONIA and its co-receptor LORELEI-LIKE GPI-ANCHORED PROTEIN1 (LLG1) are required for a large portion of high-humidity-associated Arabidopsis transcriptomic changes, including CNGC2, CAMTA-regulated genes, and cell wall remodeling genes, and for high-humidity-induced leaf hyponasty. High humidity triggers petiole-localized Ca2+ waves that precede hyponastic leaf movement. The petiole-localized Ca2+ signals were also significantly altered in the fer-4 mutant. Thus, the FERONIA receptor kinase is a critical early regulator of plant responses to high humidity.

articles.title: Atomic-Scale Insights into Electron-Driven Ag Migration and Growth Across Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-8/Ag2SeO3 Interfaces: A Theoretical and Experimental Study
articles.abstract: The ZIF-8/Ag2SeO3 heterostructure was designed to combine the adsorption capacity and porous architecture of zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) with the multifunctional response of Ag2SeO3 (ASO), seeking synergistic interactions that could yield a material with enhanced, complementary functionalities. We report the synthesis and interfacial evolution of ZIF-8/ASO heterostructures and the in situ formation of metallic Ag nanoparticles (NPs) under electron irradiation. X-ray diffraction confirms the coexistence of cubic ZIF-8 (I43m) and monoclinic ASO (P21/c) phases, with a microstructure consisting of ZIF-8 NPs uniformly anchored on ASO microrods in intimate interfacial contact. Time-resolved electron microscopy directly captures the nucleation and growth of Ag NPs on the ZIF-8 surface during electron irradiation, as confirmed by HRTEM-SAED and elemental maps, indicating spatially confined cubic Ag NPs with exposed (111) and (200) planes. Photoluminescence measurements show pronounced emission quenching and spectral redistribution, indicating modified optoelectronic behavior following heterostructure formation. First-principles calculations identify the ZIF-8/ASO(010) interface as a favorable configuration, characterized by strong interfacial interaction and significant charge redistribution. These results are consistent with the experimentally observed localized formation of Ag NPs and suggest that interfacial electronic interactions contribute to Ag+ reduction. Overall, the ZIF-8/ASO heterostructure provides an electron-responsive platform for localized Ag NP formation and interfacial optoelectronic modulation, offering insights into electron-beam-induced processes in ZIF-8-based heterostructures.

articles.title: Descriptor Logic for Disorder in High-Entropy and Compositionally Complex Fluorite Oxides: A Critical Assessment
articles.abstract: No single scalar captures disorder in high-entropy and compositionally complex fluorites. This Perspective evaluates compositional and structural descriptors by physical meaning, reference frame, covariance, and transferability. Pairwise cation mismatch contains the same information as size variance, whereas host-referenced misfit adds a reference-dependent mean-radius offset. Analysis of twenty-four published compositions from three systematic datasets illustrates the limits of configurational entropy and size variance as independent descriptors of phase formation and transport. With equal Hf, Zr, and Ce fractions, changing the host reference reverses misfit rankings and alters the host-offset term up to 78-fold. In twelve dual-phase zirconates and mixed zirconate-hafnates, the nominal rA/rB ratio correlates with phase fraction but describes neither coexisting phase, whereas measured phase compositions give non-overlapping fluorite and pyrochlore values, distinguishing descriptor limitations from inappropriate evaluation frames. Structural observables are assessed by specificity, reproducibility, and relevance. Together, these criteria and the compositional analysis define a framework that distinguishes compositional inputs, multiplicity and crystal-chemical mismatch, from their structural realization. Its purpose is to test descriptor relevance and limits rather than predict untested compositions.

articles.title: Template-Guided Crystal Chemical Design of Eu2+-Activated La2Ca3[Si4N4O8] Oxonitridosilicate Phosphor
articles.abstract: Template-guided crystal-chemical design offers a route to oxonitridosilicates, but transfer of an oxide topology requires compatible cation coordination and charge balance. Here, we report the synthesis and structural characterization of the 6-ring host La2Ca3[Si4N4O8], designed by considering [SiN]+ for [AlO]+ substitution in the Ca3[Al2O6] template together with aliovalent La3+/Ca2+ substitution. The idealized structural description contains isolated rings of corner-sharing [SiN2O2] tetrahedra and partially occupied or vacant cation sites. The nominal substitution scheme, 3Ca2+ → 2La3+ + VCa, provides a charge-balanced crystal-chemical rationale for the cation deficiency. Theoretical calculations reveal that the aliovalent substitution induces cation vacancies accompanied by local charge redistribution and coordination rearrangement, which may alleviate the lattice strain arising from the cation-size mismatch. Eu2+ activation produces broadband orange emission centered near 600 nm, with a reported photoluminescence quantum yield of 29.3%. The phosphor was further applied to a white LED by combining it with multiple phosphors. This work illustrates how cation composition and occupancy can be considered alongside the topology in template-guided exploratory synthesis.

articles.title: The Future of Light-Emitting Materials
Genetic Structure of Harbour Seals Phoca vitulina vitulina Along the Coast of Norwegian Mainland: Implications for Management
articles.abstract: Alignment between biologically meaningful units and stock boundaries is one or the requirements for sustainable resource management. In Norway, harbour seals (Phoca vitulina vitulina) are managed at the county level and, when local populations are deemed sufficiently large to support harvesting, hunting is permitted under a quota corresponding to 5% of the counted individuals. An assessment of population structure along the entire Norwegian coastline based upon 16 microsatellites revealed significant overall differentiation (F ST = 0.036, p < 0.001) consistent with a pattern of Isolation by Distance, in agreement with the estimated effective migration surface (EEMS). Pairwise differentiation among sampling sites challenged the current stock outline. Specifically, (a) geographically large counties (e.g., Finnmark, Nordland) could warrant subdivision into smaller management units, whereas (b) no differentiation was detected across the four south-eastern counties (Agder, Vestfold, Telemark and Østfold). Positive and statistically significant spatial autocorrelation detected at distances of 0–300 km invoked larger genetical similarity than expected by chance and agreed with the fine-grained population structure revealed by former tagging studies. The absence of evidence for recent bottleneck events suggests that populations remain at mutation-drift equilibrium.

articles.title: Resolving the graphite compatibility boundary with an electrolyte-native anion 19F NMR descriptor
Soil Microbes Mediate Contrasting Effects of Plant Diversity on Biotic Resistance and Invasional Meltdown
articles.abstract: Biological invasions are intensifying worldwide as a major component of global change, with soil microbes increasingly recognized as key regulators of invasion outcomes. Yet how soil microbes interact with biodiversity to determine whether communities resist or facilitate invasion, particularly through their effects on plant growth and species interactions, remains unclear. Here, we conducted a two‐phase feedback experiment in which soils were conditioned across a diversity gradient of native or invasive plant communities. We characterized soil fungal communities and quantified microbial effects on plant growth and species interactions between phylogenetically paired native and invasive species. Biodiversity generated contrasting invasion outcomes depending on community origin, driven by distinct microbial pathways. In native‐conditioned soils, increasing diversity reduced invader dominance (biotic resistance), primarily mediated by microbial effects on interspecific competition that enhanced native competition strength while reducing that of invaders. In contrast, in invasive‐conditioned soils, increasing diversity facilitated invader dominance (invasional meltdown), primarily driven by enhanced invader growth and suppression of natives. These patterns were associated with shifts in key microbial groups. Putative pathogen richness increased with increasing plant diversity and was negatively associated with native growth, whereas AMF richness declined with increasing plant diversity in native communities but increased with increasing plant diversity in invasive communities, promoting invader growth and competition strength. By integrating biodiversity‐ecosystem functioning, biotic resistance, invasional meltdown, and competitive interactions within a plant–soil feedback framework, our study advances invasion ecology. It identifies soil microbes as central mediators that link biodiversity to ecosystem invasibility through distinct pathways affecting plant growth and species interactions.

Divergent associations of plant functional composition and species richness with above‐ and below‐ground multitrophic organization in a desert steppe
articles.abstract: In a desert‐steppe biodiversity experiment, legume biomass proportion was associated mainly with leaf‐trait reorganization, whereas species richness showed more consistent associations with nematode faunal indices and footprint metrics. Measured leaf traits differed in predictive importance between herbivore feeding guilds. Positive associations between piercing‐sucking insect abundance and selected nematode indicators suggested a potential connection between above‐ground and below‐ground communities. Abstract Plant functional composition and species richness may be associated with different aspects of above‐ and below‐ground communities. Distinguishing these relationships is important for understanding how biodiversity‐related patterns extend across trophic levels. However, their respective associations with plant traits, herbivore feeding guilds and below‐ground food webs remain unclear in resource‐limited desert steppes. We sampled 64 plots during the fourth growing season of a desert‐steppe biodiversity experiment. We examined associations of realized legume biomass proportion and plant species richness with community‐weighted plant traits, chewing and piercing‐sucking herbivores, and nematode faunal indices and footprint metrics derived from relative sequence composition. Analyses combined joint regressions, direct feeding‐guild comparisons, random‐forest analyses and theory‐informed piecewise structural equation modelling. Higher legume biomass proportion was associated with lower community‐weighted leaf mass per area and higher density‐normalized leaf punch strength and trichome density. Several plant traits showed relatively high predictive importance for chewing insects but consistently low importance for piercing‐sucking insects. However, the direct mixed‐effects comparison did not detect a significant difference between guild‐specific responses to legume biomass proportion. Plant species richness was positively associated with the nematode structure and enrichment indices and negatively associated with the composite footprint metric (MF), whereas legume biomass proportion showed no significant conditional associations with these measures. Piercing‐sucking insect abundance was positively correlated with the herbivore footprint metric after multiple‐testing correction and showed positive conditional associations with the nematode structure index and MF in the piecewise SEM. Synthesis. Legume biomass proportion was linked primarily to above‐ground leaf‐trait reorganization, whereas plant species richness showed more consistent associations with below‐ground nematode faunal organization. Piercing‐sucking insect abundance showed positive associations with the nematode structure index and the composite and herbivore footprint metrics, suggesting a potential cross‐realm connection involving this feeding guild. Together, these findings indicate that plant functional composition, species richness and consumer feeding guilds represent different but connected dimensions of multitrophic organization in resource‐limited grasslands.

Chromosome Evolution in Amniote Vertebrates: A Comprehensive Atlas of Karyotypic Diversity From Ancestral States to Rapid Turnover
articles.abstract: The evolution of the amniote genome is characterized by a striking dichotomy between extreme karyotypic stasis and rapid structural innovation. To identify the mechanisms governing this variation, we provide a comprehensive synthesis of chromosome number and karyotype data across non‐avian reptiles, birds and mammals, integrating a century of classical cytogenetics with modern chromosome‐scale genomics. Amniote chromosome numbers span a range from 2n = 6 to 142 and have been shaped primarily by chromosomal fusions and fissions rather than by polyploidization common in non‐amniotes. Recent ancestral state reconstructions suggest a highly fragmented ancestral amniote karyotype of 2n = 88 with a bipartite organization of macro‐ and microchromosomes. They also support environmental sex determination as the plesiomorphic state. We explore the evolutionary mechanisms facilitating chromosomal turnover, including lineage‐specific transposable element activity, hybridization‐driven genomic instability and genetic hitchhiking, alongside the canalization model and the position‐effect hypothesis as primary responses to environmental transitions. Social structure, such as polygynous harem systems, can further contribute to rearrangement fixation via genetic drift in some, but not all, lineages. Chromosomal divergence across these lineages serves as a useful cytotaxonomic marker and, in some cases, a barrier to gene flow, as in the postzygotic incompatibility of equid and cervid hybrids. In contrast, introgression persists across karyotypically divergent rock‐wallabies and crocodilians, indicating that the reproductive consequences of karyotypic divergence are lineage‐specific rather than a fixed function of karyotypic distance. This synthesis presents an updated atlas of amniote chromosomal evolution and provides a conceptual framework for understanding how molecular mechanisms, ecological shifts and behavioural factors interact to shape genomic structure.

articles.title: Evidence for Local Adaptation Associated With Temperature Despite Weak Latitudinal Structure in a Temperate Seagrass
articles.abstract: Understanding genetic diversity and structure in natural populations is important for conservation and developing resilience into restored populations for the future. Populations at the lower latitude (or northern) range edges tend to have lower levels of genetic diversity and are poorly connected, although they may be locally adapted to warmer environments. The temperate seagrass, Posidonia sinuosa, occurs across a latitudinal gradient along the Western Australian coastline. Some meadows have experienced significant decline due to industrialisation and urbanisation of coastal areas. We investigated spatial genetic diversity, structure, and local adaptation using single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). All meadows had similarly low levels of genetic diversity with high levels of inbreeding, despite high clonal diversity. Weak genetic structure was consistent with genetic connectivity, enabled by sea‐surface seed dispersal. Approximately 6.1% of SNPs were identified as putatively adaptive and most were associated with temperature variables. Allelic turnover was associated with < 1.4°C temperature change, suggesting plants may be sensitive to small temperature changes. Meadows are currently growing in temperatures below their thermal optima, so may tolerate future projected temperatures up to a point. Importantly, this temperature increase is below the 1.5°C–2.0°C goal of the Paris Agreement and plants are unlikely to tolerate current projections for 2100, which equate to +3.2°C, in addition to extreme heatwave events. Conservation of fragmented, northern, warmer‐adapted meadows will be important to assist recovery and persistence of damaged meadows into the future, as translocation of putatively warmer‐adapted genotypes that have exhibited historic connectivity may be a viable strategy for restoration of impacted higher latitude meadows.

articles.title: Symbiont‐Derived Key Innovations Across the Diversity and Diets of Herbivorous Insects
articles.abstract: With prodigious biomass and diversity, herbivorous insects are among the world's most successful animals. It is widely believed, however, that some plant‐based diets do not meet the needs of insect metabolism. Microbial symbionts may balance such deficits through diverse biochemistry. Here, we consider whether obligate nutritional symbioses between insects and microbes support large portions of insect herbivore diversity. In doing so, we assess the evidence that these highly integrated relationships are key innovations, circumventing nutritive shortfalls within particular plant tissues. Toward these ends, we compile nutrient data for 20 plant‐ and non‐plant foods, plus data on diet and symbiosis across 874 families of insects—both herbivorous and non‐herbivorous. Our results reinforce widely believed, but often uncited evidence that several insect taxa have long‐consumed plant tissues with low concentrations of B‐vitamins, nitrogen, or accessible carbon. Emerging as symbiont‐enriched are seed‐feeders, which face insufficient quantities of several B‐vitamins in their food. Experimental and genome assessments show how symbionts surmount these B‐vitamin shortcomings, showing also where this same challenge, and those of high fibre or low amino acid content are surmounted through symbiosis on other diets. We thus show where symbiont services are key innovations. Over half of the world's insect herbivores persist without nutritive assistance from obligate symbionts. This is largely because many consume leaves, which are reasonably good sources of amino acids and B‐vitamins. Lateral transfer of microbial genes encoding plant cell‐wall degrading enzymes has helped to overcome high fibre content, defusing the most challenging nutritive aspect of leaf‐chewing diets.

articles.title: A zwitterionic dye cathode enables ultra-stable and scalable aqueous organic redox flow batteries
Advancing Moisture-Enabled Electric Generators: Ion Synergy, Technical Roadmap and Battery Hybridization Toward Real-World Self-Powered Systems
Contact-electro-catalysis: From contact electrification to interfacial redox chemistry
Synergistic dual-interfacial regulation via H2O-poor EDL and inorganic-rich SEI for long-life zinc anodes with high depth discharge
Defect-Initiated Anisotropic Oxidation in Two-Dimensional GaSe
articles.abstract: Oxidation governs the stability and functional conversion of two-dimensional semiconductors, yet its propagation through layered crystals remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the thickness-dependent oxidation of GaSe using optical spectroscopy, cross-sectional microscopy, and first-principles calculations. Experiments reveal concurrent top-down and edge-initiated oxidation, accompanied by Se redistribution and transient Ga2Se3 formation. Calculations identify Se vacancies as favorable sites for O2 adsorption and activation, which weaken neighboring Ga–Se bonds and promote oxygen incorporation. Molecular O2 faces a 4.03 eV barrier when penetrating a monolayer Ga2O3 model, compared with 0.54 eV along a GaSe van der Waals gap. This contrast supports interlayer diffusion as a plausible pathway for lateral oxidation, consistent with the pronounced thickness dependence and spatial anisotropy observed experimentally. Oxidation also yields a progression from p-type GaSe through ambipolar Ga2O3/GaSe heterostructures to n-type Ga2O3, whose devices retain stable characteristics after 300 °C air annealing.

articles.title: Emergent Giant Topological Hall Effect at the van der Waals Ferromagnet/Topological Insulator Interface
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) magnet-based heterostructures provide a vital platform for manipulating magnetic ground states and hosting complex spin textures. The topological Hall effect (THE) is a powerful tool for probing these textures in such systems. However, achieving a sizable THE in 2D vdW ferromagnets remains challenging due to the absence of broken inversion symmetry and sufficiently strong spin–orbit coupling (SOC). Here, we report an emergent giant topological Hall resistivity of 6.9 μΩ·cm at 10 K by interfacing the 2D ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2 (FGT) with the topological insulator BiSbTeSe2 (BSTS). Systematic temperature- and thickness-dependent studies suggest the origin of this pronounced signal to be the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI). Furthermore, temperature-field mapping reveals the coexistence of two distinct phases that we identify as having opposite topological charge. Our results establish these vdW ferromagnet/topological insulator heterostructures as a robust platform for enhanced interfacial THE, opening new avenues for high-efficiency topological spintronics.

articles.title: Photoinduced Carrier Doping of α-RuCl3 through Interlayer Charge Transfer
articles.abstract: Controlling doping density in correlated quantum materials offers a route to tuning their electronic states, but chemical doping can introduce disorder and limits dynamic control. Here, we demonstrate optically tunable electron doping of the layered Mott insulator α-RuCl3 through photoinduced interlayer charge transfer in MoS2/α-RuCl3 heterostructures. Photoluminescence and transient absorption measurements support electron transfer to α-RuCl3, leaving holes in MoS2. The layer-separated carrier population persists for more than 100 ps with an estimated doping density tunable through the excitation fluence. Selective excitation of α-RuCl3 further reveals hole transfer to MoS2. Transient absorption microscopy yields an early time effective hole diffusion coefficient of approximately 100 cm2 s–1 in the heterostructure, supporting a predominantly unbound carrier population. These results establish photoinduced charge transfer as a means of dynamically controlling carrier doping in α-RuCl3, providing a route toward optical manipulation of correlated electronic states.

articles.title: Photoluminescence-Driven Quasi-BICs in Photonic Nanomembranes for Active Refractometric Sensing
articles.abstract: Quasi-bound states in the continuum (quasi-BICs) offer a powerful platform for refractometric sensing by combining narrow resonances with strong electromagnetic confinement, promising high spectral resolution and large figures of merit (FOM). In practice, however, these advantages are often compromised by stringent angular alignment in passive transmission/reflection interrogation. Here, we demonstrate an active sensing platform that couples the defect-related photoluminescence (PL) of a freestanding silicon nitride nanomembrane to quasi-BIC modes. The substrate-free architecture suppresses radiation leakage and sustains tightly confined high-Q resonances, while emission-based readout bypasses stringent angular alignment. The resulting PL resonances exhibit line widths of 0.17 nm (Q ≈ 4000) in air and 0.26 nm in water. In aqueous sensing, the platform achieves a FOM of 250, substantially exceeding representative values reported for passive quasi-BIC sensors in the visible regime. This synergy translates the high-Q advantage of quasi-BICs into a practical active platform for high-performance refractometric and surface-binding sensing.

articles.title: Ultralow-Loss Femtosecond Laser Slicing of Lithium Niobate Enabled by Anisotropic Thermal Dissipation-Guided Vector Scanning
articles.abstract: Lithium niobate (LiNbO3) crystals have been widely used in photonic and electronic devices owing to their outstanding intrinsic optoelectronic properties. However, fabricating hundreds-of-micrometer-thick LiNbO3 wafers remains dominated by diamond wire sawing, which causes substantial material loss. Although ultrafast laser processing offers a promising alternative, the intrinsic noncentrosymmetric lattice, spontaneous polarization, and anisotropic photothermal response of LiNbO3 severely hinder high-quality laser cutting. Here, a thermal dissipation-guided vector scanning technology is proposed to realize ultrafast laser slicing of LiNbO3 crystals for the first time. By tailoring the scanning direction according to the anisotropic thermal dissipation, we achieve crystal exfoliation with an ultrathin subsurface damage layer of 10 μm and an exceptionally high-quality separation surface. The results establish vector scanning technology as an innovative route for high-quality femtosecond laser processing and low-damage separation of anisotropic crystals.

articles.title: Ultrathin SrTiO3 Capping Stabilizes the Surface Chemistry of Brownmillerite Ferrites during Reduction
articles.abstract: Redox processes in oxides are central to materials synthesis and functionality, but their control is often hindered by surface instabilities. Using ambient-pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, we show that a nominally 1 nm-thick SrTiO3 (STO) cap markedly enhances the surface stability of La0.05Sr0.95FeO2.5-δ (LSFO) thin films during H2 reduction by suppressing the formation of a secondary metallic Fe0 phase. Kinetic analysis indicates that the STO cap reduces the effective Fe0 formation rates by more than 6-fold at both 250 and 350 °C. These findings highlight ultrathin capping layers as an effective strategy for stabilizing oxide surfaces during redox.

articles.title: Antagonistic second-messenger signalling coordinates Pseudomonas aeruginosa surface colonization and virulence
articles.abstract: Second messengers cAMP and c-di-GMP regulate surface behaviours and virulence in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Here, the authors show how the bacteria switch between attachment and surface movement by coordinating the two signalling systems, allowing distinct bacterial populations to work together to colonise and damage human airway tissue.

articles.title: CO2 responsive nanoscopic and macroscopic materials directed by peptides
articles.abstract: Stimuli responsive assemblies can offer precise control over behaviour, but use of gases for this control is rare. Here, the authors report the use of carbon dioxide for tuneable nanoparticle response, directed by changes in peptide structure.

articles.title: Coupling electrolyte mechanical reinforcement and interfacial stress relaxation for near-ambient sulfide all-solid-state lithium metal batteries
articles.abstract: All-solid-state lithium metal batteries can suffer from dendrite growth and interfacial stress at low pressures. Here, authors couple a self-polymerizable composite sulfide electrolyte with a porous carbon current collector, enabling stable near-ambient condition cycling at high areal loading.

articles.title: Fully Integrated Deep-Ocean Flexible Temperature–Depth Sensor with Neural Network Compensation
articles.abstract: Marine pressure monitoring helps reveal ocean dynamics and assess human impacts. This work reports a self-contained low-power flexible marine temperature depth (FMTD) sensor featuring wide range, high precision and restrained temperature drift.

articles.title: Nanofluid wetting of Cu enables thin lithium negative electrodes for high-energy and long-cycling lithium metal batteries
articles.abstract: Lithium metal batteries face trade-offs between energy density and cycling life owing to lithium processability and plating challenges. Here, authors develop a nanofluid-wetting method to fabricate thin Li foils down to 800 nm, which enables anode-lean pouch cells with 498 Wh kg–1 / 1,142 Wh L–1 and stable cycling over 250 cycles.

articles.title: Selective depolymerization of poly(ethylene terephthalate) for economical closed-loop recycling of mixed textiles
articles.abstract: Recovering polymerization-grade monomers from waste textiles remains challenging. Here the authors report that the depolymerization of PET from thermally treated mixed textiles via methanolysis can be achieved in a rapid yet highly selective manner under mild conditions.

articles.title: Topological Josephson trijunctions as a Majorana source and path
articles.abstract: Majorana bound states (MBSs) are zero-energy localized states in topological superconductors, obeying non-Abelian braiding statistics. Manipulation of mobile MBSs, encompassing their on-demand generation, propagation, and fusion, is essential for braiding MBSs and operating topological qubits. We show that the manipulation is enabled by a trijunction formed on a topological insulator in a perpendicular magnetic field, where three Josephson junctions meet. While the superconducting phases at the trijunction center evolve to cross a boundary between topological and non-topological phase domains, the trijunction offers two distinct dynamics, source/sink and path, depending on the phase boundaries. At a source/sink boundary, two MBSs are pairwise generated at the center, and one of them is ejected to a Josephson junction. The reverse, pair annihilation by collision of two MBSs, can also happen. At a path boundary, an MBS moves from a Josephson junction to the trijunction center or vice versa, without involving other MBSs. Exploiting the two dynamics, fusion and braiding of MBSs can be operated in a trijunction network. We illustrate this with a double trijunction setup, where non-Abelian state evolutions associated with MBSs can be manipulated without dynamical control of the setup and detected by Josephson emission spectroscopy. Manipulating Majorana bound states is a key requirement for topological quantum computation. Here, the authors propose a topological insulator Josephson trijunction in a magnetic field that enables the generation, transport, and fusion of Majorana bound states through static control of superconducting phases.

articles.title: WASH orchestrates phagosomal maturation and bacterial killing in neutrophils through syntaxin 19-mediated lysosomal fusion
articles.abstract: Neutrophil phagocytosis is crucial for combating infections, yet the actin-mediated regulation of vesicular trafficking during late phagosomal maturation remains obscure. Using neutrophils lacking the actin nucleation regulator Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome Protein and Scar Homolog (WASH), we identify a mechanism linking actin remodeling, lysosomal fusion, and bacterial killing. Although WASH is dispensable for particle internalization, WASH deficiency impairs lysosome-phagosome fusion and intracellular bacterial killing. Lysosomes from WASH-deficient neutrophils show decreased association with actin comets and impaired dynamics. Rac1 activation rescues lysosomal trafficking but not phagosomal maturation. Mass spectrometry of phagolysosomes and TR-FRET identify atypical syntaxin 19 (STX19) as a WASH binding partner, and WASH recruits STX19 to phagosomes. Reconstituting WASH in primary neutrophils rescues phagocytosis, STX19 interference impairs phagosomal maturation, while STX19 overexpression enhances it. WASH is thus a central mediator of phagosomal maturation through STX19-mediated membrane fusion and actin-driven lysosomal dynamics, revealing how dysregulated trafficking contributes to immunodeficiency. How actin regulates late phagosomal maturation and microbial killing in neutrophils remains unclear. The authors here show that WASH drives actin-dependent lysosomal dynamics and STX19 recruitment to phagosomes, enabling lysosome fusion and bacterial killing.

articles.title: Bringing Rapid Reperfusion to More Patients with Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
Discontinuing Statins in Older Adults without Cardiovascular Disease
Early Days, Late Nights
Equity in Maternal–Fetal Medicine — Technological Advances and a Potential Path Forward
Hyperaldosteronism Remission after Extended Aldosterone Synthase Inhibition
Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Patients with Previous Ischemic Stroke
Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes
Interleukin-6 Inhibition with Ziltivekimab for Atherosclerotic Disease
Lung Hernia with a Chest-Wall Hematoma
Mass Surveillance with Artificial Intelligence — A New Determinant of Health?
