Prehospital Extracorporeal Life Support in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
[Articles] Cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (DAPT-SHOCK-AMI): a randomised, double-blind trial
articles.abstract: To our knowledge, this is the first randomised trial to compare P2Y12 inhibitor strategies specifically in patients with AMI-CS. Cangrelor achieved effective platelet inhibition more frequently than crushed ticagrelor at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. Non-inferiority of cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor was not demonstrated for the primary 30-day clinical endpoint. These trial findings can inform future trials of P2Y12 inhibition strategies in patients with AMI-CS.

articles.title: The Five Phases of cancer cells
articles.abstract: Beyond identifying individual malignant hallmarks, the central challenge in cancer biology is to uncover the fundamental organizing principles that underlie the interactive nature of cancer cell behavior. Here, we transform the ancient Wuxing theory into a mechanistically grounded, hypothesis-generating biological framework that conceptualizes cancer cell biology around five mutually interacting processes: Pliability, Hybridity, Aggressivity, Sociability, and Evolutivity (PHASE). By engaging in the circuit of mutual promotion and restriction, these phases form an integrated regulatory system that provides a rationale for organizing diverse malignant properties. Within this framework, cancer traits emerge as context-dependent manifestations of the proposed core interactions. Collectively, PHASE offers a complementary perspective for understanding disease progression that could advance interaction-guided therapeutic strategies to target human cancers.

articles.title: A Witness for Quantum Correlations Using Nonlinear Spectroscopy
articles.abstract: The ability to detect and quantify entanglement in molecular systems is essential for understanding their quantum correlations and to evaluating molecules as platforms for quantum technologies. Here we show how signals from existing spectroscopic techniques can provide sufficient information to witness entanglement. The main ingredient is a spectroscopic map from admissible quantum states to a finite-dimensional space of signal coefficients, which are expectation values of state-independent effective observables. The molecular response model and measurement protocol determine the effective observables for a fixed system bipartition, and the spectroscopic map defines sets of joint expectation values compatible with all admissible quantum states and their separable subset. We illustrate the construction of the effective observables and their expectation value sets using rotational invariants and the spectral structure of optical signals. Fluorescence dynamics and photon coincidences provide a complementary example. Our findings provide a theoretical basis for entanglement certification with established spectroscopic techniques.

articles.title: Can AI Agents Reliably Optimize Computational Chemistry Codes?
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) approaches have opened new possibilities in computational and theoretical chemistry. AI agents can now execute computational workflows autonomously, and their use in scientific software development represents another promising direction. Herein, we present a general strategy for the controlled optimization of scientific software using a dual-agent harness. By using separate worker and controller agents for optimization and evaluation, respectively, we find that this approach can reduce computational costs while preserving numerical accuracy for the computational chemistry methods examined. We apply this strategy to TIP4P water simulations in LAMMPS, as well as to Coulomb and exchange matrix construction and linear-response time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations in PySCF. Among these applications, the largest speedups are obtained for TDDFT. We then extend this strategy from optimizing established packages to developing efficient parallel CPU- and GPU-accelerated implementations of an initially serial molecular dynamics code, resulting in speedups of two to three orders of magnitude. Finally, we apply the protocol to open-ended algorithm development by constructing an adaptive self-consistent field approach that coordinates the use of multiple solvers. We find that the resulting approach can converge some challenging systems and occasionally reach lower-energy solutions than those obtained with the standalone solvers tested. These applications demonstrate that a strategy developed for improving code efficiency may also support the systematic development of computational methods. Overall, our benchmark study provides an example of AI-assisted advances in computational chemistry.

articles.title: Coupled plasmonic Fabry-Perot resonances modulating electromagnetic enhancement at a silver nanowire-nanoparticle junction proved by surface-enhanced fluorescence spectroscopy
articles.abstract: We investigated the surface-enhanced fluorescence (SEF), which is the broad background spectrum underlying the surface-enhanced resonant Raman scattering of dye molecules, emitted from junctions between silver nanoparticles (NPs) and nanowires (NWs). We found that the electromagnetic enhancement factors (FR) derived from the SEF exhibited spectral modulation, such as complicated oscillatory structures. This property became clearer when the emission polarization was perpendicular to the long axis of the NWs. The FR spectra of the long and short NWs exhibit fine and broad oscillatory structures, respectively, when the NPs are positioned near the NW centers. When the NPs were near the NW ends, a combination of fine and broad structures was observed. Numerical calculations of the position-dependent FR spectra successfully reproduced these properties, indicating that the spectral properties originated from the interaction between two plasmonic Fabry-Perot (FP) resonators within the NW, separated by a NP. Based on this result, an analytical model of coupled FP resonators was developed to evaluate these spectral features using experimentally measured NW lengths and NP positions while varying the inter-resonator coupling efficiency. This analysis revealed that the interference and superposition of the two FP resonances resulted in these complex spectra, the energy of which was radiated by the localized plasmons of the NPs.

articles.title: Delta-Corrected Shot Reduction for Bypassing Optimization Plateaus in Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
articles.abstract: The variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) remains a cornerstone hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for quantum simulation, yet its scalability is fundamentally constrained by heavy measurement overheads. While strategies such as variance-preserved shot reduction (VPSR) mitigates this cost, they suffer from convergence instability and optimization stagnation caused by finite-sample bias in limited pilot shots. To overcome this limitation, we introduce delta-corrected shot reduction (DCSR), an analytically enhanced shot allocation strategy that rigorously mitigates finite-sample instability. Utilizing the multivariate delta method, we derive explicit higher-order bias correction terms for the empirical reduction factor. Both theoretical analysis and numerical simulations reveal that incorporating higher-order statistical moments, such as skewness and kurtosis, provides the gradient resolution necessary to bypass noise-induced barren plateaus. DSCR significantly accelerates convergence compared to standard VPSR across diverse noise and resource regimes while matching or decreasing cumulative measurement costs, establishing a mathematically rigorous framework for variance-stabilized shot allocation on near-term hardware.

articles.title: Molecular Photoionization Spectra from Signed Dyson Orbitals and Anharmonic Nuclear Motion
articles.abstract: Molecular photoelectron bands couple changes in nuclear structure to the energy-dependent scattering of the departing electron. Band intensities require both nuclear transition moments and electronic continuum amplitudes. We present SPARKS (Scattering and Photoionization: Amplitudes, Response Kernels and Spectra), a molecular photoionization approach that connects signed Dyson orbitals to complex molecular dipole amplitudes and harmonic or anharmonic nuclear transition moments. Compact B-spline and finite-element discrete-variable representations support spectral and sparse outgoing-boundary solvers. Independent molecular checks reproduce a reference H$_2^+$ spectrum and CO continuum amplitudes, while analytic hydrogen photoionization tests establish the continuum normalization. For H$_2$O/H$_2$O$^+$, electronic derivatives activate a Franck--Condon-dark fundamental and enter the same nuclear operator used in harmonic, perturbative and internal-coordinate variational calculations. Furan extends the nuclear treatment to all 21 vibrational coordinates in a selected configuration-interaction window, including low-lying out-of-plane states. Four epichlorohydrin ionization channels show how orbital mixing reshapes cross sections and angular distributions at similar Dyson norms. Energy conservation is imposed separately for every vibronic transition at fixed photon energy. The resulting spectra retain vibrational assignments and electronic interference, connecting weak-band activation, anharmonic spacings and photoelectron angular distributions within one physical description.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal Energy Consistency Enables Reliable Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics from Diffusion Models
articles.abstract: Coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) extends molecular simulations to length and time scales inaccessible to atomistic models, but building thermodynamically faithful CG potentials remains a longstanding challenge. Energy-based diffusion models (EBDMs) provide a promising route for learning CG potentials through their zero-time energy. However, CGMD driven by diffusion-learned potentials can produce equilibrium ensembles that deviate substantially from the target distribution. We show that the zero-time distribution error is bounded by the sum of the spatial score error and temporal energy-derivative error, whereas conventional diffusion objectives directly supervise only the spatial component. Based on this finding, we introduce Spatiotemporal Energy Consistency (STEC) supervision, which complements spatial score matching by explicitly constraining temporal energy derivatives. We derive an exact and tractable objective for this temporal component, avoiding the substantial computational overhead associated with previous regularization schemes. Across peptide and fast-folding protein systems, STEC-trained EBDMs accurately reproduce equilibrium distributions with free-energy errors within chemical accuracy, while supporting stable long-time simulations that recover key metastable transition patterns. On held-out octapeptides, STEC reduces free-energy errors by more than 5-fold relative to the strongest competing baseline, while achieving a median production-cost reduction of approximately 1,700-fold relative to atomistic molecular dynamics under a defined structural-coverage benchmark. These results establish STEC as a scalable framework for learning thermodynamically reliable CG force fields for increasingly complex biomolecular systems.

articles.title: Symmetry and Redundancy in Cremer-Pople Phases for Ring Puckering
articles.abstract: Cremer-Pople (CP) coordinates provide an exact description of ring puckering, yet direct sampling of their phases generates many symmetry-equivalent representations of the same puckering pattern. We develop a general analytical framework that identifies these equivalences before Cartesian reconstruction and geometry optimization. For homogeneous rings of arbitrary size, explicit transformations of the CP phases and the signed special coordinate of even-membered rings generate the complete symmetry orbit of the ordered elevation pattern. We classify the redundancies into four types and derive a factorized orbit-size formula linking CP multiplicity to puckering symmetry. These results yield exact single-phase fundamental intervals and sequentially reduced multiphase covering domains, including the restriction to a positive special coordinate. The framework is extended to rings containing one heteroatom or two identical heteroatoms, with reductions determined by the operations that preserve their placement. We also introduce a semidiscrete conformational nomenclature that combines symbolic amplitude distributions with explicit active phases. In an application to cyclohexadecane, symmetry reduction alone decreases the number of sampled CP points by approximately a factor of thirty. Combined with selective phase-grid coarsening for three ordinary modes, the reduction approaches two orders of magnitude. These developments provide a systematic basis for generating, classifying, and efficiently sampling ring puckering patterns in CP space.

articles.title: Toward universal excited-state machine-learned potentials: a local excitation Hamiltonian for size consistency and transferability
articles.abstract: Universal machine-learned interatomic potentials could make excited-state simulations across chemical space routine, but excitation energies, unlike ground-state energies, are not sums of atomic contributions. The excited states of noninteracting molecules are the union of their states, which pooled multistate readouts reproduce at best for the lowest state. We introduce LEH-MACE, whose excitation energies are the eigenvalues of a local excitation Hamiltonian assembled from atom-centred blocks, so this union holds exactly. We generated TD-DFT energies and forces for about 300,000 equilibrium, thermal, and excited-state geometries of over 100,000 molecules. LEH-MACE's advantage over direct readouts grew with the distance from the training data and was largest above $S_1$, with about half their $S_2$ and $S_3$ errors for long conjugated oligomers. For molecule pairs, only LEH-MACE kept its single-molecule accuracy, while a softmin readout remained superior for $S_1$ dynamics of larger chromophores. Exact size consistency is thus one step toward such potentials.

articles.title: Universal Approximation by Equivariant Message-Passing Graph Neural Networks with a Bilinear Readout
articles.abstract: We prove universal approximation for the bilinear-readout equivariant message-passing network (BREMP), a reference architecture for equivariant graph neural network interatomic potentials. Its layers combine equivariant convolutions with affine maps, and its readout forms invariants from products of the equivariant features. We construct a one-layer feature that determines the local environment up to permutations of atoms of the same type. The construction uses spherical harmonic filters of degree no larger than the largest number of neighbors at a common distance from the center. Iterating the construction recovers the environment reachable in as many hops as there are layers, using the same bound on filter degrees at the layer cutoff. The readout approximates every continuous invariant function of the features uniformly on compact sets. Together these give universal approximation of atomic energies at a prescribed physical range using a shorter layer cutoff. We assume that, throughout the admissible class, message passing reaches all neighbors in each physical environment within a common number of layers. Finally, DPA4, an interatomic potential architecture in production use, inherits this result by approximating the BREMP layers constructed in the proof and realizing the bilinear readout.

articles.title: Asymmetric Dual-Atom Ruthenium–Tungsten on CeO2 Enabled Highly Active and Selective NH3 Oxidation
articles.abstract: Ru single-atom catalysts are promising for NH3 oxidation but still suffer from poor activity and N2 selectivity, mainly owing to the poisoning of the isolated Ru active sites by the over-strong NH3 adsorption. Herein, we fabricated an asymmetric Ru-W atomic pair anchored on CeO2 (Ru1–W1/Ce) exhibiting considerable low-temperature activity (∼90% at 200 °C), high N2 selectivity (∼85% at 350 °C), and notable stability (∼500 h at 200 °C), surpassing most of the previously reported catalysts for NH3 oxidation. Systematic experimental and theoretical investigations demonstrated that a strong d-f orbital interaction between Ru and W atoms was revealed, inducing the smooth electron transfer from W to Ru atoms. The electron-rich Ru single atom not only weakened NH3 adsorption strength to alleviate NH3 poisoning but also reduced the energy barrier of the rate-determining step of NH3 activation. Besides, isolated W atoms coordinated with active Ru species, leading to a decrease in Ru–O–Ce coordination number. This could suppress the activation of O2 and thereby the deep oxidation of NH3. Accordingly, the reaction mechanism over this asymmetric Ru–W catalyst changed from the initial i-SCR to an imide-like pathway, accounting for its considerable catalytic performance. This work provided a paradigm for advanced Ru-based catalysts enabling both high activity and high N2 selectivity in NH3 oxidation.

articles.title: From Promiscuity to Specificity: Machine Learning-Driven Multidimensional Evolution of Tropinone Reductase for Challenging Substrates
articles.abstract: A fundamental challenge in harnessing substrate promiscuity for industrial biocatalysis lies in reconciling broad substrate acceptance with high catalytic specificity. Although promiscuous enzymes provide attractive starting points for accessing non-natural transformations, their native active-site architectures and conformational dynamics often lack the precision required for efficient and selective conversion of desired unnatural substrates. Thus, systematically decoding and reprogramming the interplay between promiscuity and specificity remains a key obstacle toward versatile biocatalysts. Here, we address this challenge by integrating virtual screening, machine learning, and molecular dynamics simulations into a unified engineering framework. A tropinone reductase from Cochlearia officinalis (CoTR) was identified as a broadly promiscuous scaffold. By converting complex enzyme–substrate interaction dynamics into quantifiable and actionable design principles, we predict and validate key residues that govern substrate promiscuity. Guided by these insights, distinct CoTR variants were engineered for three representative substrates. The optimized variants—CoTR‑8M, CoTR‑5M‑1, and CoTR‑5M‑2—exhibited 7.0‑ to 16.3‑fold higher catalytic efficiencies than wild-type CoTR toward their respective target substrates and supported substrate loadings of up to 50 or 100 g L–1 while maintaining >99% ee. This work not only delivers scalable routes to three industrially valuable chiral alcohols but also provides mechanistic insights into the synergistic modulation of promiscuity and specificity. This study demonstrates a general strategy for translating intricate molecular-recognition features into rational design principles, thereby facilitating the development of tailored biocatalysts for non-native substrates.

articles.title: Enabling Outdoor Operation of Tin–Lead Perovskite Solar Cells via Lamination-Based Encapsulation
articles.abstract: Tin–lead (Sn–Pb) perovskites are essential narrow-bandgap absorbers for two-terminal perovskite–perovskite tandem solar cells, yet their extreme air sensitivity has confined stability studies indoors, leaving real-world durability unexplored. Here, we substantially lower this barrier using industrially relevant, lamination-based encapsulation that enables, to our knowledge, the first outdoor demonstration of Sn–Pb devices. Combining polyisobutylene edge sealing with polyolefin elastomer encapsulation, we demonstrate that the lamination process is highly compatible with Sn–Pb devices, causing negligible performance loss while preserving optoelectronic quality during short-term air exposure. Under package-oriented accelerated aging, epoxy-based encapsulation fails rapidly, whereas the lamination-based package remains intact. Outdoors under tandem-relevant filtered illumination, lamination-encapsulated devices retain ∼80% of initial efficiency after 12 days, while epoxy-encapsulated devices lose all output within 6 days. By adapting manufacturable module packaging to Sn–Pb devices, this work enables their realistic field evaluation, marks a critical step toward deployable all-perovskite tandems, and strengthens confidence in their commercial viability.

articles.title: An Organo–Inorganic Hybrid Nanomaterial to Disrupt Multicellular Communication within Tumor Microenvironment
articles.abstract: The lack of clear identification or understanding of the key perpetrators activating the tumor microenvironment (TME) impedes development of TME-modulating therapeutic strategies that could overcome the challenges associated with tumor growth, metastasis, and therapy resistance. Here, we report the development of a hybrid nanomaterial designed to genetically silence one key regulator, IGFBP2 (insulin-like growth factor binding protein 2), responsible for multicellular crosstalk within the TME. We demonstrated that silencing of IGFBP2 by this hybrid nanomaterial suppressed angiogenesis, stromal activation, and tumor cell phenotypes both in vitro and in vivo in preclinical models of ovarian cancer. Mechanistically, the hybrid nanomaterial utilizes the caveolae-mediated intracellular uptake pathway rather than a mixture of clathrin and caveolin as seen with a nonhybrid counterpart. Given the role of IGFBP2 as a prognostic factor for several cancers, and the absence of any small molecule inhibitor of IGFBP2, the current strategy may be exploited as a promising and generalized approach to target the TME and improve therapeutic outcomes in numerous cancers, including ovarian cancer

articles.title: Astrocyte Membrane-Engineered Extracellular Vesicles with Hypoxia-Remodeled Cargo Attenuate Reactive Astrocyte Programs and Promote Spinal Cord Repair
articles.abstract: Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) represent promising cell-free therapeutics for spinal cord injury (SCI). However, their therapeutic efficacy remains limited by variable cargo potency and insufficient cell-selective delivery. Here, we developed a modular biomimetic vesicle platform integrating hypoxic remodeling of mesenchymal stem cell-derived sEV (MSC-sEV) cargo with astrocyte membrane engineering. In a rat model of SCI, hypoxia-preconditioned MSC-sEVs (Hyp-sEVs) attenuated C3-positive astrocyte reactivity and improved functional outcomes. Proteomic profiling and functional analyses identified ERBIN as a key therapeutic cargo enriched in Hyp-sEVs that contributed to suppression of the NOD2/IRF3/GBP1 signaling axis. To enhance astrocyte-directed delivery, Hyp-sEVs were fused with astrocyte-derived membranes to generate astrocyte membrane-engineered vesicles (A-EVs). A-EVs were preferentially taken up by astrocytes, and blocking and knockdown experiments implicated MERTK and the ligands PROS1/GAS6 in this uptake. A-EVs outperformed Hyp-sEVs in preserving spinal cord tissue and promoting functional recovery. Together, these findings indicate that coupling hypoxia-remodeled sEV cargo with astrocyte membrane engineering promotes preferential vesicle uptake by astrocytes, attenuates C3-positive astrocyte reactivity, and improves functional recovery after SCI in rats.

articles.title: Bias-History-Driven Negative Differential Resistance in Heterojunction-Free WSe2 Multilayers
articles.abstract: As conventional complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology approaches its fundamental scaling limits in binary logic, alternative device concepts have attracted increasing attention. Negative differential resistance (NDR) devices offer a promising route toward multivalued logic. However, their practical implementation requires both a high peak-to-valley current ratio (PVCR) and high drive current density at room temperature, necessitating complex device architectures and fabrication processes. Here, we report a heterojunction-free WSe2 NDR device on a hexagonal boron nitride dielectric, exhibiting a PVCR of up to 42.9 and a width-normalized peak current density of approximately 280.8 μA/μm at room temperature. The NDR emerges evidently after gate-polarity reversal, thus suggesting the formation of a bias-history-dependent nonequilibrium carrier configuration. Systematic variations of the gate-bias magnitude, duration, hold time, and sweep rate indicate that the relaxation of this nonequilibrium carrier configuration governs the peak current, peak voltage, and PVCR of the NDR characteristics. Surface passivation using poly(methyl methacrylate) further enhances both the PVCR and peak current, highlighting the sensitivity of the NDR to the surface electrostatic environment. These findings establish a bias-history-driven electrostatic mechanism for NDR in homogeneous two-dimensional layered semiconductors and provide a simple and scalable strategy for realizing high-performance heterojunction-free NDR devices.

articles.title: Combating the Bloodstream Infection Cascade: Sequential Therapeutic Nanomaterials for Pathogen Elimination, Immunomodulation, and Organ Protection
articles.abstract: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) are life-threatening systemic syndromes with a high mortality rate, characterized by a highly sequential pathophysiological progression. Although early antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory treatments have improved short-term survival rates, single-stage interventions are insufficient to reverse the high risk of long-term mortality among survivors. To address the urgent clinical need for stage-specific interventions to improve patient outcomes, nanomaterials have emerged as a highly promising platform due to their design flexibility and intelligent microenvironmental responsiveness. This Review first outlines the pathophysiological characteristics of BSIs at each stage, from the initial pathogen invasion to the final multiple-organ dysfunction, which serves as the basis for the design of nanomaterials. Then, following the progression of BSIs, the representative nanotherapeutic strategies developed in recent years for different pathological stages are systematically categorized and discussed. Finally, the review discusses the challenges confronting nanomaterials in BSI management, such as the selection of optimal treatment timing and clinical translation, and provides future perspectives on design strategies and developmental directions for nanomaterials in BSI treatment.

articles.title: High-Reliability Ultrascaled IGZO FETs for Multibit 2T0C DRAM toward Monolithic 3D Integration of an AI Accelerator
articles.abstract: The continued scaling of silicon-based dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) slows down due to increased process complexity and reduced storage capacitance. Oxide semiconductors (OS), represented by InGaZnOx (IGZO), offer an attractive alternative owing to their ultralow leakage and low thermal budget, making them promising candidates for next-generation DRAM as well as monolithic three-dimensional (M3D) architectures. However, realizing IGZO devices with well-balanced overall performance, including high performance and high reliability under ultrascaled dimensions, remains challenging. Here, we report ultrascaled IGZO field-effect transistors (FETs) fabricated using an optimized O2 plasma-enhanced atomic-layer deposition (PE-ALD) process. The IGZO FETs deliver state-of-the-art performance, including an on-state current (Ion) of 785 μA/μm at a drain voltage of 0.5 V and a transconductance (gm) of 620 μS/μm at a drain voltage of 1.0 V alongside a contact resistance (Rc) of 164.5 Ω·μm with positive threshold voltage (Vth). Reliability degradation is effectively suppressed, with bias-temperature instability (BTI) down to 8 mV even at extremely scaled contact length (Lc) of 50 nm. Leveraging these optimized devices, we further demonstrated a scaled two-transistor-zero-capacitor (2T0C) DRAM capable of up to 6-bit per cell, long data retention over 4000 s, and write time down to 10 ns. We proposed an M3D-DRAM architecture with vertically stacked multilayer embedded memory for artificial intelligence (AI) accelerators, achieving 77× faster weight loading and 9.6× lower energy consumption compared with mature high-bandwidth memory (HBM) counterpart, while maintaining graphics processing units (GPU)-equivalent inference accuracy of 92.25%. This work demonstrates an effective approach for the co-optimization of performance and reliability in ultrascaled IGZO FETs, providing critical foundation for next-generation DRAM and M3D applications.

articles.title: Memory Window Improvement in Ferroelectric Thin-Film Transistors with HfZrO2/AlN Bilayers Grown by Atomic Layer Deposition
articles.abstract: This study demonstrates proximity-induced ferroelectric switching in a stacked ferroelectric film composed of fluorite-structured HfZrO2 (HZO) and wurtzite-structured AlN, which are grown by thermal atomic layer deposition (ALD) and plasma-enhanced ALD (PEALD), respectively. The stacked film shows remanent polarization close to that of HZO but with a much higher coercive field, desirable for enhancing the memory window of ferroelectric thin-film transistors (FeTFTs) for storage applications. The FeTFT with a 5 nm-thick amorphous In–Ga–Zn–O (a-IGZO) channel layer, also grown by ALD, shows a memory window of ∼6.1 V, and data retention over 10 years. It also shows stable endurance cycles of ∼104. These enhancements over the single-layer HZO or stacked HZO/Al2O3 films, which show a minimal memory window of ∼0.3 V and ∼−0.3 V, respectively, are ascribed to the proximity ferroelectric effects between the soft ferroelectric HZO and hard ferroelectric AlN. These results, together with the conformal deposition of the HZO/AlN stack in high-aspect-ratio structures, demonstrate the feasibility of extending the ALD/PEALD-based Prox-FE materials platform toward three-dimensional (3D) process integration.

articles.title: Dopant Dependent Grain Growth and Mechanical Property Heterogeneity in Al-, Cr- and Al/Cr-doped UO2 Nuclear Fuels

120‐Channel High‐Fidelity Optical Multiplexing Using a Minimal Meta‐Atom Set
articles.abstract: High‐capacity optical multiplexing is crucial for next‐generation intelligent information systems, spanning high‐speed communications, optical computing, and immersive displays. A fundamental challenge is to maximize the number of independent channels while maintaining high fidelity, compact footprint, and low structural complexity, constraints that severely limit existing diffractive optical elements. Here, we overcome these long‐standing trade‐offs by introducing a multi‐dimensional reconfigurable diffractive neural network (MRDNN) that enables high‐capacity, high‐fidelity optical multiplexing within an exceptionally compact and simple architecture through the co‐design of predictive neural optimization and multi‐physical‐dimension multiplexing. Experimentally, a dual‐layer MRDNN realizes 24 independent channels for distinct functionalities, including focusing, beam steering, and holographic image reconstruction. Owing to its excellent scalability, only four metasurface layers comprising a minimal library of 2002 meta‐atoms achieve 120 distinct optical channels with low crosstalk and high fidelity (measured mean structural similarity index measure of over 0.8), representing a record experimental multiplexing capacity with one of the smallest normalized footprints and simplest structural configurations in a metasurface‐enabled system. This work establishes a scalable and efficient paradigm for extreme optical multiplexing in multifunctional and reconfigurable photonics systems.

articles.title: A Cu2S/NiOOH Heterojunction Enables Highly Selective Ammonia‐to‐Nitrite Electrooxidation at Industrially Relevant Current Densities
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic ammonia oxidation reaction (AOR) offers a green route to nitrite (NO2 −) synthesis while coupling hydrogen evolution reaction. However, maintaining NO2 − selectivity at high current density remains challenging due to the narrow thermodynamic windows for NO2 − and nitrate (NO3 −) formation and competition of oxygen evolution reaction at high anodic potentials. Herein, we report a Cu2S/NiOOH heterojunction that sustains high NO2 − selectivity over a wide oxidative window at industrially relevant current densities. Operando Raman spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations reveal that the heterointerface induces interfacial electronic redistribution within the Ni–O framework, strengthens NH3 adsorption, and rebalances AOR energetics, favoring NO2 − release over oxidation. Consequently, in a membrane electrode assembly-based flow cell, Cu2S/NiOOH delivers a Faradaic efficiency for NO2 − (FE(NO2 −)) exceeding 90% at 800 mA cm− 2 with a high production rate of 383.2 mg cm−2 h−1. These results highlight the potential of Cu2S/NiOOH for NO2 − electrosynthesis at industrial production rate.

articles.title: A Memristor‐Based Saturation‐Constrained Information Capacity Framework for Temporal Information Processing
articles.abstract: Physical reservoir computing (PRC) has emerged as a highly energy‐efficient paradigm for processing high‐dimensional spatiotemporal data in edge‐intelligent systems. However, the deployment of PRC is often limited by the quantization mismatch between continuous input signals and the finite dynamic range of hardware substrates. Conventional binary time‐multiplexing ensures high noise immunity but necessitates protracted pulse sequences that induce high latency and premature physical saturation. Conversely, multi‐valued analog encoding enhances information density but frequently induces state overlap, operating devoid of physical quantization boundaries. To resolve this physical‐information trade‐off, we propose a saturation‐constrained information capacity (SCIC) framework. This framework considers task‐specific encoding variables and substrate‐intrinsic constraints, enabling device‐informed optimization of input mapping. We experimentally demonstrate this framework on a highly uniform, selector‐free 32 × 32 crossbar array, utilizing the volatile dynamics of memristors. Under the experimentally selected encoding conditions, the SCIC‐guided RC achieves exceptional performance in temporal prediction (NRMSE of 0.019), speech recognition (free‐spoken digit dataset (FSDD) subset accuracy of ∼94.5%), and real‐time obstacle avoidance. Our approach links encoding constraints to solid‐state device physics, providing a device‐informed method for PRC parameterization at the edge.

articles.title: A Micromesh‐At‐Grid Integrated Cotton (MAGIC) Gauze with Pressure‐Responsive Pore Gating Enables Sustainable Hemostasis via Spatiotemporally Coordinated Coagulation
articles.abstract: Achieving effective and economical hemostats requires a robust clot‐wound interface constructed by spatiotemporally coordinated coagulation. However, accumulated interfacial blood causes delayed clotting in adhesion‐reliant dense hemostats, and rapid but off‐site coagulation in absorptive porous materials. Here, we present MAGIC (Micromesh‐At‐Grid Integrated Cotton) gauze, which leverages a reversible transition between dense and porous states to precisely coordinate the spatial and temporal dynamics of coagulation. This transition is achieved by a pressure‐responsive micromesh composed of supramolecular procoagulant microparticles. Spatially, blood‐derived ions trigger the gelation of these procoagulant particles on the gauze surface, laterally repelling interfacial blood to ensure on‐site coagulation. Temporally, applied pressure induces micromesh dissociation to re‐expose the gauze macropores for wicking residual fluid, followed by the rapid co‐assembly of sol‐state procoagulant particles with blood components. This tightly synchronized process seals the cleared wound with a robust clot. Consequently, a single MAGIC pad arrested lethal porcine femoral artery hemorrhage within 30 s. Compared to standard gauze, it reduced blood loss by 98%, cotton consumption by 96%, treatment costs by 83%, and lifecycle CO2 emissions by 84%. Collectively, MAGIC gauze delivers exceptional preclinical first aid efficacy while pioneering a viable pathway for the decarbonization of surgical consumables.

articles.title: A Self‐Amplifying Ultrasound‐Activated Polymeric Prodrug Nanoplatform for Synergistic Sonodynamic Immunotherapy
articles.abstract: Ultrasound (US)‐triggered sonodynamic therapy (SDT) combined with immunotherapy shows considerable promise, yet its therapeutic efficacy remains constrained by insufficient intratumoral drug activation and limited immunogenicity. Herein, we report a self‐amplifying US‐responsive nanoplatform (PMB@R848) for synergistic sonodynamic immunotherapy. The nanotherapeutic was constructed by conjugating the sonosensitizer methylene blue (MB) to polylysine through US‐labile urea‐based linkages, providing a stable framework for efficient complexation of immunostimulant R848. Under physiological conditions, PMB@R848 exhibited excellent colloidal stability and biocompatibility. Upon US irradiation, the generated reactive oxygen species (ROS) initiated selective cleavage of urea bonds, exposing protonatable amino groups that enhanced intraparticle electrostatic repulsion under mildly acidic tumor microenvironment. This cascade process further accelerated nanoparticle destabilization and established a self‐amplified release behavior, enabling synchronized liberation of both MB and R848. The released MB markedly enhanced ROS generation, inducing robust immunogenic cell death and tumor antigen release, while R848 further amplified dendritic cell maturation and systemic antitumor immunity. Benefiting from the synergistic integration of self‐amplified SDT and immune activation, PMB@R848 achieved potent inhibition of primary tumors, effectively suppressed recurrence, and established durable immune memory in multiple murine tumor models. This work presents a self‐amplifying, US‐activatable nanoplatform for precision sonodynamic immunotherapy.

articles.title: A Single Quasi‐Vertical van der Waals Heterostructure Memristor as Opto‐Reconfigurable Artificial Intelligence Hardware
articles.abstract: The explosive advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has driven vast amounts of unstructured data that directly emerges at sensory interaction interfaces. Memristors with superior computing ability are among the most promising computing blocks. However, conventional vertical Metal/Resistive layer/Metal (V‐MRM) memristors tend to generate intense electric fields, suffer from limited sensory response, inflexible, and rigid functional modes, as well as long‐standing variability and overshoot issues. Here, we present an unconventional two‐terminal quasi‐vertical (QV) van der Waals heterostructure (vdWH) memristor as opto‐reconfigurable hardware. Unlike the V‐MRM memristor with a strong, rigid vertical electric field, this QV‐vdWH memristor realizes a significantly softened, tunable electric field, enabling parametric configurable and wavelength‐dependent reconfigurable modes across nonvolatile/volatile memory, neurons, synapses, and optical perception. Moreover, the light‐memristive switching‐vdWH coupling triggers a super‐additive synergistic enhancement of memristive performance (> 100‐fold) and photoresponse (> 3000‐fold). Meanwhile, the long‐standing variability and overshoot issues are overcome, yielding ultra‐uniform memristive behavior with even a single‐valued distribution. Leveraging the opto‐reconfigurability, high‐accuracy object tracking, and human motion recognition (∼96.8%) are successfully performed. Breaking through the inherent functional limitation of the conventional V‐MRM memristive structure, the QV‐vdWH memristor provides a flexible, opto‐reconfigurable hardware platform for emerging computing paradigms, and AI applications.

articles.title: A Sustainable Brand‐New Thermoelectric Cooling Material: High‐Mobility Diamondoid Cu3SbSe4 Crystal
articles.abstract: Diamondoid Cu3SbSe4 is an earth‐abundant thermoelectric material with strong potential for near‐room to mid‐temperature applications. However, its performance has been limited by intrinsically low carrier mobility. Here, we report the first successful growth of large‐sized Cu3SbSe4 crystals, achieving a fivefold enhancement in carrier mobility, and demonstrate the first Cu3SbSe4‐based thermoelectric cooling device. We show that Ag substitution reduces both the effective mass and deformation potential through strengthened bond covalency, yielding a high carrier mobility of ∼150 cm2 V−1 s−1. This leads to a remarkable power factor of ∼23 µW cm−1 K−2 at 300 K, a maximum ZT of ∼1.6 at 700 K and an average ZT of ∼0.85 over 300–700 K, representing state‐of‐the‐art performance among Cu‐based thermoelectric materials in this temperature range. A 7‐pair device based on Cu3SbSe4 crystal achieves a cooling temperature difference of ∼25 K at room temperature, and reaching a maximum of ∼34 K at 343 K. Additionally, the optimized sample demonstrates a single‐leg power‐generation efficiency of ∼7% at ΔT = 350 K. These results highlight crystal‐growth as a powerful strategy to unlock high‐performance refrigeration in previously limited materials, establishing diamondoid Cu3SbSe4 crystals as a viable, low‐cost and environmentally benign platform for practical thermoelectric applications.

articles.title: A Tightly Interlayer Bonded, Synchronously In Situ Co‐Injectable, Wet‐Adhesive, Hierarchically Biofunctionalized Bilayer Hydrogel for Functional Attachment and Orderly Periodontal Regeneration
articles.abstract: Periodontitis, the sixth most prevalent global disease, causes tooth loss and systemic disorders, imposing a significant global burden. Functional regeneration of the periodontium remains a major challenge due to the hierarchical soft‐hard tissue interface and complex spatiotemporal functional demands. In this study, a synchronously in situ co‐injectable, interlayer‐bonding, and wet‐adhesive bilayer hydrogel (Bio‐Fun bilayer) consisting of PCAC and PCMC layers is developed. An anti‐delamination interface is engineered via polymer chain topological entanglement and dynamic boronate ester and ionic networks, while precise complex viscosity matching enables synchronized microscale laminar co‐extrusion. Concurrently, the hydrogel maintains wet adhesion, especially to moist root and bone surfaces. Spatiotemporal biofunctionalization is achieved by loading microRNA‐26a liposomes in the PCAC layer to activate Wnt/β‐catenin signaling for osteogenesis, and covalently tethering a PDGF‐BB mimetic peptide within the PCMC layer to trigger PI3K/Akt‐LOX signaling for fibroblast recruitment and functional collagen formation. In vivo, the Bio‐Fun bilayer hydrogel achieves integrated regeneration of alveolar bone and aligned periodontal ligament fibers, forming Sharpey's fiber‐like structures with firm bone‐ligament attachment. Meanwhile, the modular and injectable design might provide broad reference for the reconstruction of periodontal, osteochondral, and other soft‐hard tissue interfaces.

articles.title: A Wireless Colorimetric Optoelectronic Microneedle Patch for On‐Demand Photodynamic Therapy of Wound Infections
articles.abstract: Wound infections represent a major clinical concern due to their high incidence and subtle early manifestations, often resulting in prolonged healing and increased risk of complications. While wearable bioelectronics facilitate real‐time diagnostics and therapeutic interventions, their widespread clinical translation remains constrained by the complexity, power demands, and high cost of current systems. Here, a wearable platform that integrates colorimetric sensors with a wireless optoelectronic microneedle patch was presented for in situ wound infection status detection and on‐demand photodynamic therapy (PDT). This wireless colorimetric optoelectronic microneedle (COMN) patch enables rapid (15 min) and reliable detection of typical wound infection biomarkers with minor interference. By integrating microneedles and wireless light‐emitting diodes (LEDs), this system supports concurrent delivery of photosensitizers and light into deeper wound tissues, achieving > 99.9% eradication of drug‐resistant bacteria through penetration‐enhanced PDT. In a murine full‐thickness wound infection model, this system promptly assessed the infection status of the wound and then triggered PDT, resulting in > 3 log reduction in bacterial burden and accelerated healing, with > 80% wound closure observed by day 14. This work demonstrates a flexible and adaptive bioelectronic platform based on colorimetric analysis and optoelectronic microneedle therapy, offering an accessible strategy for precision wound care.

articles.title: Atomic‐Scale Design, Performance Degradation Mechanisms, and System Integration of Multi‐Principal Element Hydrogen Storage Materials
articles.abstract: Solid‐state metal hydrides offer high volumetric hydrogen density and intrinsic safety for hydrogen storage, yet their practical application is severely hindered by poor room‐temperature thermodynamics, sluggish kinetics, impurity gas poisoning, difficult activation, and cycling degradation. Multi‐principal element alloys (MPEAs) have recently emerged as promising candidates to overcome these bottlenecks through their vast compositional space, severe lattice distortion, and synergistic cocktail effect. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in MPEAs for solid‐state hydrogen storage, bridging atomic‐scale design to system‐level performance. A unified composition‐process‐structure‐property framework is established that integrates engineering‐driven design rules, post‐processing techniques, multi‐scale computations, machine learning (ML), and high‐throughput experiments. Using advanced in situ and ex situ characterization, the atomic‐scale origins and cross‐scale evolution of surface poisoning, hydrogen‐induced amorphization (HIA), disproportionation, pulverization, and defect accumulation. A theoretical framework linking electronic structure to heat and mass transport is further developed, and hydrogen storage bed design, device integration, fuel‐cell coupling, manufacturing scalability, and cost analysis are discussed. Finally, key scientific and engineering challenges and future research directions are outlined. This review provides scientific guidance for designing MPEA‐based solid‐state hydrogen storage systems with high capacity, long cycle life, high poisoning tolerance, fast de‐/hydrogenation kinetics, and low cost.

articles.title: Beyond and Inside the Electrical Double Layer: Molecular‐Level Cation Effects in Aqueous Electrocatalysis
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic reactions occur at a dynamic, ion‐regulated electrochemical interface, rather than at a static electrode boundary. In electrocatalytic processes such as hydrogen evolution/oxidation and CO2 reduction, which operate at potentials below the electrode's potential of zero charge, electrolyte cations are not mere spectators but active participants that shape reaction behavior. Their size, charge density, solvation structure, and spatial organization within the electric double layer (EDL) govern interfacial energetics, transition states, and reaction activity and selectivity, giving rise to pronounced, system‐dependent cation effects. Furthermore, cation accumulation dynamically modifies the interfacial electric field, reorganizes water structure, and alters local pH, thereby coupling electrostatics, solvation, and mass transport in a highly nonlinear manner. These intertwined effects complicate mechanistic interpretation and have contributed to ongoing debates and seemingly contradictory conclusions across experimental and theoretical studies. Here, we synthesize the current understanding of cation effects at electrochemical interfaces, highlight emerging interfacial molecular structures revealed by in situ and operando studies that challenge classical EDL models, identify key unresolved debates, and outline pathways toward a quantitative, molecular‐level description of cation–interface–reactivity relationships.

articles.title: Bias‐Responsive S‐Scheme Heterojunctions Reconfigure Interfacial Water for Efficient Seawater Hydrogen Evolution
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic seawater hydrogen evolution is fundamentally limited by the rigidity of interfacial water structures and static electron distributions at catalyst surfaces. Here, we report a bias‐responsive S‐scheme heterojunction that dynamically couples nonequilibrium electron redistribution with interfacial water activation during operation. Using a MoN/NiCoN model system, in situ x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) reveals a cathodic‐bias‐induced reversal of interfacial electron transfer relative to the equilibrium state, leading to progressive electron enrichment at the catalytic interface. In situ infrared spectroscopy reveals potential‐dependent restructuring of the interfacial water environment associated with this electronic redistribution, transforming strongly and intermediately hydrogen‐bonded water into catalytically active free or weakly hydrogen‐bonded species. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations further reveal accelerated hydrogen‐bond exchange kinetics, shortened hydrogen‐bond lifetimes, and a more adaptive dipole orientation at the MoN/NiCoN interface, providing molecular‐level evidence for dynamic water‐network reorganization. Ionic‐liquid‐based experiments further demonstrate that this restructuring originates from electronically driven interfacial activation rather than bulk water availability. Consequently, water dissociation and hydrogen evolution kinetics are synergistically accelerated, enabling ultralow overpotentials in real seawater and high solar‐to‐hydrogen (STH) conversion efficiency. This work establishes dynamic S‐scheme heterojunctions as a general strategy for electronically programmable interfacial reaction environments in electrocatalysis.

articles.title: Binder Engineering for Phosphoric Acid Distribution and Retention in High‐Temperature Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell Cathodes
articles.abstract: High‐temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (HT‐PEMFCs) offer compelling advantages for energy conversion, including simplified water and thermal management and high tolerance to fuel impurities. In these systems, phosphoric acid (PA) serves as the primary proton conductor, enabling anhydrous proton transport. However, cathode performance and durability remain constrained by sluggish oxygen reduction kinetics and the challenge of controlling PA distribution and retention. Uneven acid distribution, manifesting as local flooding that blocks gas pathways and covers active sites or local depletion that disrupts proton‐conducting networks, causes severe mass‐transport losses and performance decay. Concurrently, gradual PA migration and loss during operation progressively degrade proton conduction pathways, accelerating voltage decay. Recent studies have established cathode binder engineering as an effective strategy to regulate both PA distribution and retention. This review systematically examines the design of cathode binder systems—encompassing polymer binder optimization and functional additive integration—and the characterization and diagnostic frameworks for evaluating their efficacy in PA management. We further integrate advanced PA characterization techniques with a comprehensive electrochemical performance evaluation framework. By establishing explicit connections among binder design, PA distribution and retention behavior, and device‐level performance assessment, this review provides an instructive guide for the rational development of high‐performance, durable HT‐PEMFC cathodes.

articles.title: Bioinspired Molecular Screening of Zwitterionic Dipeptides for Stable Ah‐Level Zinc–Iodine Batteries
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn─I2) batteries are attractive for large‐scale energy storage yet remain limited by two coupled failure mechanisms: unstable zinc interface at the anode and polyiodide shuttling at the cathode. To address both challenges with a single additive, we systematically screened 44 amino acids and dipeptides using molecular dipole moment and LUMO energy as key descriptors. L‐Carnosine (LC) emerged as a unique candidate exhibiting both the highest dipole moment and a moderate LUMO energy across the screened library. Experimentally, LC's zwitterionic, multicenter charge distribution drives persistent multidentate adsorption at the zinc interface, suppressing HER, directing (101)‐oriented crystallographic deposition through facet‐selective passivation, and enabling formation of a vertically graded organic‐inorganic hybrid solid electrolyte interphase. Concurrently, the electron‐rich imidazole group rapidly quenches polyiodide intermediates through a rapid redox reaction. This synergistic regulation enables Zn||Zn symmetric cells to operate stably for 4980 h, Zn||Cu cells to achieve 99.76% average Coulombic efficiency (CE) over 1400 cycles, and Zn||I2 full cells to sustain over 18 000 cycles with nearly 100% capacity retention. Furthermore, the practical viability is demonstrated in Ah‐level pouch cells with 85% capacity retention after 500 cycles. This work establishes a unique molecular transformation strategy for stabilizing high‐energy aqueous energy systems.

articles.title: Bioinspired Twisted Brick–Mortar Composites for Adaptive Thermo‐Mechanical Impact Protection
articles.abstract: Protective materials for harsh environments should dissipate transient impact energy while maintaining mechanical reliability under thermal fluctuations. Here, we report a bioinspired twisted brick–mortar composite that integrates a carbon‐nanotube‐reinforced photopolymer framework with a mechanically active shear‐stiffening gel mortar. The continuously twisted brick architecture redistributes stress waves and guides crack deflection, whereas reversible interfacial hydrogen bonding and dynamic boron–oxygen crosslinking enable rate‐dependent molecular dissipation. This structural–molecular coupling provides efficient impact protection, delivering a low energy transfer rate of 7.38% under high‐strain‐rate compression and reducing the residual impact force from 20°C to 100°C. The carbon‐nanotube‐containing framework further provides photothermal responsiveness, allowing reversible stifhefness modulation, adaptive force buffering, and shape recovery after localized high‐speed impacts. Together, these results establish a bioinspired twisted brick–mortar design strategy for adaptive thermo‐mechanical impact protection.

articles.title: How to Build an Ecosystem: Early Animals of the Ediacaran and the Emergence of the Tangled Bank
articles.journal: Annual Review of Ecology, Evolution, and Systematics
articles.abstract: The early animal communities of the Ediacaran (∼580–539 Mya) provide novel insights into how the modern biosphere operates by recording the initial ecological framework from which ecological interactions first built up. These Ediacaran communities do not have direct counterparts because they are soft-bodied, largely heterotrophic, and predator free. However, the exceptional preservation of immobile, benthic Ediacaran animals enables the resolution of their community dynamics to similar levels to those of extant benthic systems. While many of the key processes shaping the modern benthos were present in early benthic communities, the diversity of ecological interactions within communities, and the variability of these interactions through time and space, was notably simpler than that found today. In the Ediacaran, ecosystem dynamics and complexity started with reproduction and dispersal, with adaptations and responses to the environment a secondary effect, followed by direct biotic interactions. As these biotic interactions became dominant, coevolution established a tangled bank of complexity.

articles.title: Revisiting the Role of Biological Nitrogen Fixation in Forest Recovery Under Global Environmental Change
articles.journal: Annual Review of Ecology, Evolution, and Systematics
articles.abstract: Classical ecosystem theory depicts biological nitrogen fixation (BNF) as a mechanism that replenishes disturbance-driven nitrogen (N) losses, thereby alleviating N limitation and facilitating ecosystem recovery. These assumptions persist in present-day theories, models, and applications. However, disturbance regimes and environmental conditions have changed dramatically since the formation of the original BNF theories, motivating a new evaluation of the role of BNF. Focusing on forests, we find evidence that disturbance effects on BNF range from net positive to net negative and that current BNF fluxes have a limited capacity to replenish N losses if disturbances become more severe and frequent, or if they create conditions that suppress or constrain BNF. The subsequent effects of BNF on ecosystem recovery also vary. N-fixing trees and shrubs can have positive to negative effects on the recovery of carbon stocks, and under novel disturbance regimes they may alter, and even impede, forest succession. We present an updated view of BNF–recovery relationships in forest ecosystems undergoing global environmental change.

articles.title: The Pollen-Reward Strategy: The Paradoxical Realities of Trading Gametes for Sex
articles.journal: Annual Review of Ecology, Evolution, and Systematics
articles.abstract: Pollen-rewarding plants face a fundamental tension: Pollen serves simultaneously as the male gametophyte and pollinator reward. Despite this apparent paradox, pollen is the second most common floral reward and the sole reward for an estimated 20,000 angiosperm species. We review the ecology and evolution of the pollen-reward strategy, synthesizing literature encompassing pollen chemistry, floral morphology, and sex allocation. We find that this reward strategy is unevenly distributed among plant families, that the resource costs of pollen rewards remain poorly characterized, and that this reward strategy may influence plant sexual-system evolution. We offer hypotheses regarding the evolution and maintenance of the pollen-reward strategy and examine the ecological and evolutionary consequences associated with its expression. We suggest that floral rewards are not isolated traits, but key elements of plant reproductive strategies, and that this perspective allows comparison among strategies and can advance our understanding of the evolutionary ecology of plant reproduction.
