articles.title: Banana fruit with nutritionally significant concentrations of iron and zinc: results from the field evaluation of genetically modified bananas (Musa spp.) in Australia
articles.abstract: Iron and zinc distribution in wild‐type and transgenic Cavendish banana (Musa spp.) lines. Summary Iron deficiency remains a major public health problem in East Africa, where banana is a staple food for > 30 million people. This study investigated whether genetic modification could produce banana fruit containing nutritionally significant concentrations of iron while maintaining agronomic performance under field conditions. Six transgenes associated with iron homeostasis were expressed singly or in combination in Cavendish and Lady Finger bananas. In total, 450 genetically modified plants were field evaluated in Australia and fruit mineral concentrations assessed in the first planting crop. Elevated fruit iron and zinc concentrations, reaching 45.5 and 51.9 mg kg−1 dry weight, respectively, were associated with increased nicotianamine (NA) accumulation following expression of OsNAS. Iron concentrations sufficient to meet 50% of the estimated average requirement for children were achieved in 28 lines, with elevated NA suggesting improved iron bioavailability. Increased mineral accumulation negatively correlated with yield; however, this effect was partly mitigated by co‐expression of OsVIT1. Early indicators of yield penalty included low corm iron, high leaf zinc concentrations and reduced photosynthetic efficiency. These findings demonstrate the potential of using genetic modification for the mineral biofortification of bananas in East Africa while highlighting factors that may assist in the early identification of high‐performing biofortified lines.

articles.title: PhYAB4 directly activates PhAGL6‐2 to regulate lip‐related organ curvature morphology in Paphiopedilum henryanum
articles.abstract: PhYAB4–PhAGL6‐2 regulatory module controls lip‐related organ curvature in Paphiopedilum henryanum. Summary The orchid lip is a highly specialized floral organ that contributes to floral architecture and pollinator interaction. However, the developmental and molecular mechanisms underlying lip‐related organ curvature in Paphiopedilum remain poorly understood. Using Paphiopedilum henryanum and its Type A peloric mutant, we found that visible divergence between wild‐type petals and mutant lip‐like petals begins at Stage 4. Curvature was associated with adaxial–abaxial epidermal cell number imbalance in the distal region, whereas average epidermal cell area remained largely unchanged. Transcriptome and expression analyses identified PhAGL6‐2 as a lip‐associated AGL6 homolog enriched in lips and lip‐like petals during Stages 4–5. PhAGL6‐2 was preferentially expressed on the abaxial side, particularly in regions associated with curvature. Virus‐induced gene silencing‐mediated silencing of PhAGL6‐2 in Dendrobium Chao Praya Smile and P. henryanum affected perianth organ curvature, suggesting a broader role in floral organ morphogenesis. The YABBY transcription factor PhYAB4 directly bound the AGTGTG motif in the PhAGL6‐2 promoter and activated its transcription. Silencing PhYAB4 reduced PhAGL6‐2 expression and caused stronger floral curvature, lip outgrowths, and partial disruption of floral symmetry. These findings identify a PhYAB4–PhAGL6‐2 pathway associated with epidermal cell number imbalance and lip‐related organ curvature.

articles.title: The CitRWP–CsWUS regulatory axis governs citrus plant regeneration in association with chromatin remodeling
articles.abstract: Working model of the CitRWP–CsWUS regulatory axis in association with chromatin remodeling in citrus. Summary Plant regeneration underpins crop genetic improvement, yet its regulatory mechanism remains poorly characterized in woody fruit trees. The RWP‐RK domain‐containing (RKD) transcription factor CitRWP acts as a pleiotropic regulator of nucellar polyembryony and somatic embryogenesis (SE) in citrus, but its downstream molecular network remains elusive. We demonstrate that CsWUS, a core stem cell regulator, is a direct downstream target of CitRWP. CitRWP binds to the CsWUS promoter to activate its transcription. Additionally, CitRWP interacts with the SWItch/Sucrose Non‐Fermentable (SWI/SNF) chromatin‐remodeling ATPase SPLAYED (SYD), synergistically enhancing CsWUS activation, while chromatin accessibility at the CsWUS locus is enhanced upon CitRWP overexpression. We further uncover that CsWUS negatively regulates CitRWP expression via a feedback loop. CsWUS overexpression promotes SE in recalcitrant citrus callus, but causes abnormal meristem proliferation and impairs shoot organogenesis from epicotyl segments. CsWUS greatly enhanced in planta transformation efficiency in the model citrus. This study establishes the CitRWP–CsWUS regulatory axis as a central module that coordinates multiple developmental fate transitions in association with chromatin remodeling, providing novel insights into the mechanisms of cellular totipotency and plant regeneration.

articles.title: A Kampo medicine, kamishoyosan, ameliorates menstruation-associated symptoms in patients with premenstrual syndrome: An exploratory open-label, randomized controlled trial
articles.abstract: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is a psychological or physical symptom. We conducted an open-label, randomized, exploratory trial with the aim of evaluating the efficacy and safety of kamishoyosan (KSS) for PMS. KSS was administered orally during three menstrual cycles. The primary endpoint was the change in the premenstrual Menstrual Distress Questionnaire (MDQ) total score. The secondary endpoints included MDQ total and subscale scores, a daily symptom questionnaire, the Work Productivity and Activity Impairment (WPAI) Questionnaire, overall impressions, sleep status, and heart rate. A total of 50 patients were enrolled. The primary endpoint, the premenstrual MDQ total score, was significantly ameliorated after KSS treatment. Furthermore, KSS reduced MDQ scores during the menstrual cycle. Among the MDQ subscales, KSS decreased score of pain, concentration, behavioral change, and negative feelings during the premenstrual cycle. In addition, hyperthymia reduced during the menstrual cycle. The results of the daily symptom questionnaire indicated that KSS treatment alleviated irritability, easy anger, anxiety, emotional instability, abdominal distension, coldness, and stiff shoulders.The WPAI activity impairment score was lower in the KSS group, and overall impression favoured in KSS treatment.. The only adverse event related to KSS was headache in one case. These exploratory findings suggest that KSS may improve menstrual-related symptoms in PMS.

articles.title: A psychological perspective on peer tutoring in EFL collaborative writing in Chinese higher education contexts
articles.abstract: In Chinese higher learning institutions, students learning English as a foreign language (EFL) often demonstrate low writing self-efficacy (WSE) and poor writing competence. The present study examined the associations between the integration of peer tutoring with collaborative writing and students’ WSE and writing outcomes from a psychological perspective. A quasi-experiment was implemented for 11 weeks for 100 Chinese university students studying EFL. Changes in WSE were examined, and writing competence was assessed using tests. The results showed a notable rise in students’ WSE after the instructional intervention. The multiple linear regression analysis indicated that gains in WSE were positively associated with the writing outcome after controlling for pretest writing competence and group membership, explaining 20.2% of the total variance. These results suggest that peer-supported collaborative writing was associated with higher EFL writing competence alongside increased WSE. These findings align with theoretical justifications based on peer scaffolding and the Zone of Proximal Development, although these processes were not directly measured in the present study. These findings imply that incorporating peer tutoring into collaborative writing might be associated with the development of WSE and improved writing competence among EFL students at Chinese universities. Increased WSE appeared to be a significant, albeit partial, predictor of writing competence, highlighting the potential relevance of WSE development in peer-supported collaborative writing contexts.

articles.title: Adaptive–based cascaded PI–PID controller for load frequency regulation with real time verification
articles.abstract: by Abdullah M. Alharbi, Mohamed A. Awad, Mahmoud A. Attia, S.F. Mekhamer, Ahmed H. EL-Ebiary In order to address Load Frequency Control (LFC) problems in single-area and interconnected two-area power systems, this work proposes a cascaded control scheme that combines PI–PID control with the Set-Membership Affine Projection Algorithm (SMAPA). The proposed approach is evaluated under various practical operating conditions, including step load disturbances, random load variations, wind power fluctuations, and parameter uncertainty. In addition, frequency-domain stability analysis is performed to further assess the robustness of the proposed controller, while real-time validation is conducted for the two-area system to demonstrate its practical effectiveness. The proposed controller is compared with conventional PI controllers tuned using five optimization methods for the single-area system. For the two-area system, its performance is benchmarked against PID controllers designed using three optimization methods and the recently reported SPPI-based approach. The simulation results show that the proposed controller achieves lower overshoot and faster settling time in both configurations. These improvements are attributed to the integration of real-time adaptive parameter updating provided by SMAPA with the favorable dynamic characteristics of the PI–PID control structure. The results demonstrate that the proposed cascaded SMAPA-based PI–PID controller provides robust frequency regulation under different operating conditions and offers promising potential for practical interconnected power system applications.

articles.title: Aligning entity of knowledge graph based on graph convolutional network with maximum translated similarity
articles.abstract: Entity alignment is a pivotal technology for integrating heterogeneous knowledge graphs, yet most embedding-based alignment methods destroy the inherent structural embedding information of knowledge graphs when unifying cross-graph embedding spaces, resulting in limited alignment accuracy and stability. To tackle this issue, this paper proposes a novel model for entity alignment tasks, which named as Graph Convolutional Network with Maximum Translated Similarity (GCN-MTS). GCN-MTS innovatively leverages a maximum translated similarity mechanism to optimize the adjacency matrix, degree matrix and loss function. This core design effectively maintains the original relative embedding structure of cross-graph entities during embedding space unification, which is the key improvement over existing approaches. Comprehensive experiments on 3 pairs of real-world knowledge graph dataset demonstrate the superior performance of GCN-MTS against advanced baseline methods. It achieves average performance gains of 5%–15% in Hits@1 and 4%–16% in Hits@10. Ablation results confirm that the optimized module brings a nearly 22% improvement in alignment metrics compared with the vanilla GCN. Furthermore, GCN-MTS presents excellent robustness and stability across different seed alignment quantities and seed combinations.

articles.title: Antibiotic stewardship challenges in Madagascar’s poultry sector: informality, knowledge gaps, and market constraints
articles.abstract: Antibiotic resistance (ABR) is a major global public health threat, largely driven by the overuse and misuse of antibiotics. Tackling its animal health component is particularly difficult in low- and middle-income countries, where data and resources are limited. This qualitative study aims to explore antibiotic use (ABU) and its underlying drivers in poultry farms in Analamanga, Madagascar’s region with the highest poultry density. In April 2023, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 79 poultry farmers (13 backyard and 66 semi-intensive), 10 animal health professionals, and 10 agrovet shop sellers. Thematic analysis was used to examine farm characteristics, poultry health management, veterinary medicine supply and use, and interactions with poultry production stakeholders, in order to identify antibiotic stewardship challenges in Madagascar's poultry sector. Backyard and semi-intensive farmers shared several features: informality (absence of farm registration, rare cooperative membership, limited training), irregular profitability, easy access to antibiotics, recurrent antibiotic misuse (for example use in poultry viral infection treatment, first-line fluoroquinolone treatments), and limited veterinary inspection by competent authorities. However, the two farmer groups differed, as semi-intensive farmers had slightly greater knowledge of ABU and ABR than backyard farmers; they primarily consulted chick and feed suppliers for health advice and medicine purchase; and they widely perceived antibiotics as essential to maintaining poultry health and productivity. Practical roadblocks to invest in preventive measures or adopt effective antibiotic stewardship (ABS) were their narrow profit margins, limited access to credit, and weak bargaining power towards poultry product buyers. Tailored approaches such as supporting professionalization of poultry sector, building capacity of chick and feed suppliers to provide training in appropriate ABU and management of flocks, flock vaccination, deworming schedules, treatment record keeping and ABS principles may enhance antibiotic usage in the Madagascar poultry sector. Future research should build on this exploratory study, which used a convenience sample of stakeholders, by examining ABU trends and drivers in Analamanga with representative sampling and rigorous quantitative validation across Madagascar’s poultry sector.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and Chinese art teachers’ career exploration behavior: The roles of job substitution risks, job insecurity, and organizational AI readiness
articles.abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in art education raises questions about teachers’ professional security and career development. Drawing primarily on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and, in a complementary manner, on Career Construction Theory (CCT), this cross-sectional study examined associations among AI adoption, perceived job substitution risk, job insecurity, career exploration behavior, and organizational AI readiness. Survey data from 381 Chinese art teachers were analyzed using Mplus 7.4. AI adoption was positively associated with career exploration behavior. Statistically significant indirect associations were observed through job substitution risk, job insecurity, and their hypothesized sequential combination. Organizational AI readiness positively moderated the AI adoption–career exploration relationship: the association was stronger at higher readiness. COR theory offers a resource-threat interpretation of the indirect associations, while CCT highlights that career exploration may reflect threat-related coping, growth-oriented development, or both. The data did not separately measure these motivations or establish causal ordering. The findings provide context-specific insights into career exploration among art teachers during AI-related technological change.

articles.title: Clinical and epidemiological characteristics of invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella disease in Ghana
articles.abstract: Background Invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella (iNTS) disease remains a significant public health threat in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Although the disease is important, its clinical characteristics are not well described in literature. This study describes the clinico-epidemiological profile of iNTS disease in Ghana aiming to bridge important knowledge gaps and inform more effective management strategies. Methods The study spanned 8 years and utilized selected fever surveillance sites in Ghana. Patients with fever and/or history of fever for ≥ 3 consecutive days within the week prior to visit were approached and blood sample taken after consenting for investigations including blood culture. iNTS isolates were recovered using BACTEC blood culture, identified by Analytical Profile Index (API), sero-grouped using the Kauffmann–White scheme and confirmed by Illumina whole genome sequencing. Conditional logistic regression was used to assess associations between clinical and laboratory features and iNTS blood culture positivity in a 1:3 age-, sex-, and residence-matched case–control analysis. Results Of 271 blood-culture-derived bacterial pathogens, 15.5% (42/271) were identified as iNTS making it the second most common cause of bacteremia. iNTS disease exhibited seasonality with peak detections coinciding with the rainy seasons in Ghana. 23.7% (9/38) of iNTS isolates were multidrug-resistant (MDR), of which 5.3% (2/38) were extensively drug-resistant including resistance to ceftriaxone and ciprofloxacin. Several factors showed crude associations with iNTS disease; however, only anaemia retained its association after adjustment of other factors (aOR=2.41 p = 0.030). Conclusion iNTS is a major cause of bloodstream infections with the highest burden in children under 5 years of age with susceptibility to the infection amplified by anaemia. The Salmonella serovars involved are increasingly becoming multidrug-resistant, including resistance to critical antibiotics.

articles.title: Deep learning optimisation for cardiology: Neural Architecture Search-driven arrhythmia classification with electrocardiograms
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death worldwide. Sudden cardiac death (SCD) accounts for roughly 50% of all cardiac deaths. The electrocardiogram (ECG) is widely used for diagnosing cardiac disease. However, the complexity of interpretation limits the ECG’s efficacy. Modern deep learning methods can assist clinicians in diagnosis. We applied Neural Architecture Search (NAS) to identify optimal deep learning architectures for classifying cardiac arrhythmias with ECGs. We applied the Differentiable Architecture Search strategy to an AutoFormer search and trained, validated, and tested the resulting model on the PhysioNet Challenge 2021 (PC21) dataset (n = 88,253 from three continents). We optimised hyperparameters on the NAS output, exploring input patch size, class weighting, and loss function. The PC21 metric and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) are the performance metrics. The NAS converged towards minimal architectural configurations (embedding dimension: 384, depth: 4, self-attention heads: 4, MLP ratio: 1) with a validation and test PC21 metric of 0.66 (PC21 winner: 0.63). The NAS-created network achieved an AUROC of 0.97 and a PC21 metric of 0.72 during testing (PC21 winner: 0.69). We tested the PC21 winner architecture (1D-convolutional neural network with attention mechanism) without the attention mechanism and with the NAS-suggested architecture of 4 self-attention heads (instead of 8). The architecture without the attention mechanism performed similarly to the one with 8 self-attention heads (AUROC: 0.90, PC21 metric: 0.69). The architecture with 4 self-attention heads scored an AUROC of 0.91 and improved the PC21 metric to 0.71. The attention mechanism visualisation for two SCD-related arrhythmias (premature ventricular contractions and prolonged QT-interval) showed more clinically relevant attention for the 4-self-attention-head architectures. We interpret architectural simplicity as driving performance in arrhythmia classification. The self-attention mechanism can autonomously abstract clinical representations, simplifying clinical deployment by eliminating the need for an explicit feature-extraction pipeline.

articles.title: E-Service quality and customer satisfaction in online shopping: Implications for sustainable digital commerce
articles.abstract: by Mohammed AL Awadh The rapid growth of e-commerce has intensified competition among online retailers, making e-service quality increasingly important for building customer trust, satisfaction, and sustainable customer–platform relationships. This study examines the relationships among e-service quality, customer trust, customer satisfaction, and customer loyalty using a second-order Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) framework. The five SERVQUAL dimensions such as empathy, responsiveness, reliability, assurance, and tangibles were modeled as first-order constructs reflecting the higher-order construct of service quality. Data were collected through an online questionnaire from 402 respondents with prior online-shopping experience. Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) and SEM were employed to assess the measurement and structural models. The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability, convergent validity, discriminant validity, and overall model fit. The structural results showed that service quality significantly and positively influenced customer trust and customer satisfaction, while customer trust significantly enhanced satisfaction. Trust also partially mediated the relationship between service quality and satisfaction, indicating that e-service quality improves satisfaction both directly and through increased customer confidence. The SERVQUAL dimensions contributed positively to overall service quality, with responsiveness and assurance showing particularly strong contributions, while empathy exhibited a comparatively moderate contribution. In contrast, customer loyalty had no significant direct effect on trust or satisfaction, and its indirect effect on satisfaction through trust was also nonsignificant. These findings demonstrate that reliable, responsive, secure, and well-designed digital services are important for strengthening trust and satisfaction in competitive e-commerce environments. By identifying trust as a key mechanism linking multidimensional e-service quality with customer satisfaction, the study contributes to SERVQUAL and digital-commerce literature and provides implications for the economic and relational sustainability of e-commerce platforms through more resilient and durable customer relationships.

articles.title: Editorial Note: Early Growth Response Gene-2 (Egr-2) Regulates the Development of B and T Cells

Effectiveness of dose-matched immersive virtual reality-stationary cycling combined with neurological physiotherapy versus neurological physiotherapy alone in individuals with chronic stroke (CIVIS): A single-blind, randomized crossover trial protocol
articles.abstract: Background Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability worldwide and frequently results in persistent motor and functional impairments, particularly affecting gait and balance. Given the high prevalence and impact of these limitations on independence and quality of life, innovative rehabilitation strategies are needed. Immersive virtual reality combined with stationary cycling (IVR-SC) has emerged as an innovative rehabilitation approach with the potential to improve mobility and functional outcomes after stroke. Aim To analyze the comparative effectiveness of two dose-matched programs, one combining IVR-SC plus neurological physiotherapy (NP), versus the other consisting of NP alone, in individuals with chronic stroke. Methods A randomized, single-blind, crossover clinical trial will be conducted. After calculating the sample size, a minimum of 8 participants with chronic stroke (≥6 months), hemiparesis, and gait and balance impairments will be randomly assigned to one of two sequences of intervention. Each participant will receive both neurological physiotherapy and IVR-SC across two 4-week intervention periods separated by a washout period (4 weeks). Each intervention period consists of 8 sessions delivered over a 4-week period, with each session lasting 60 minutes. The primary outcome will be gait quality, assessed using Wisconsin Gait Scale (WGS), while secondary outcomes will include walking endurance, balance, motor function, and muscle tone. Clinical outcomes will be assessed at baseline and after each intervention period. Satisfaction with using the IVR-SC intervention will also be evaluated. Statistical analyses will follow an intention-to-treat approach using a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) with treatment, period, sequence, baseline, and center as fixed effects, and participant as a random effect. Statistical significance will be set at p < 0.05. An individual responder analysis will be performed to determine if participants exceeded the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) of 2.25 points on the WGS. Discussion This study will contribute to understanding the potential comparative effects of IVR-SC in stroke rehabilitation. Given the heterogeneity of individuals with stroke, which may limit the conclusiveness of findings in parallel-group studies, the crossover design allows each participant to serve as their own control, reducing inter-individual variability and strengthening the interpretation of the results. If effective, IVR-SC could represent a feasible and scalable option for partially replacing NP within standard neurorehabilitation, with potential for implementation in both clinical and home-based settings. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT07529665. Effectiveness of dose-matched rehabilitation with immersive virtual reality-stationary cycling combined with neurological physiotherapy versus neurological physiotherapy alone in individuals with chronic stroke (CIVIS): study protocol for a single-blind, randomized crossover trial. URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07529665. Date of registration: 2026-04-14. Version 1.

articles.title: Effects of vitamin D supplementation on vitamin D status and physical performance in football players: A systematic review and meta-analysis
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives Low vitamin D status is frequently reported among athletes, but whether vitamin D supplementation improves physical performance in football players remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of vitamin D supplementation on serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] concentration, jump performance, sprint performance, aerobic capacity, and muscular performance in association football and futsal players. Methods PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to 31 May 2026. Controlled intervention studies comparing vitamin D supplementation with control conditions were eligible. Standardized mean differences were calculated as Hedges’ g and pooled using random-effects meta-analyses. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using RoB 2 or ROBINS-I. The certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261430873). Results Eleven reports representing nine independent studies and 312 players were included. In RCT-only primary analyses, vitamin D supplementation was associated with higher circulating 25(OH)D concentrations (g = 1.41, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.92; I² = 58.0%). Pooled effects were not statistically significant for jump performance (g = 0.21, 95% CI −0.10 to 0.53), sprint performance (g = −0.03, 95% CI −0.40 to 0.34), aerobic capacity (g = 0.00, 95% CI −0.45 to 0.45), or muscular performance (g = 0.19, 95% CI −0.14 to 0.51). The certainty of evidence was low for circulating 25(OH)D, jump performance, and muscular performance, and very low for sprint performance and aerobic capacity. Conclusions Vitamin D supplementation was associated with increased circulating 25(OH)D concentrations, whereas current evidence is insufficient to support a consistent improvement in physical performance. Given the low to very low certainty of evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Larger, well-designed randomized controlled trials using standardized, football-relevant performance tests are warranted.

articles.title: Efficacy of diadynamic currents versus transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation for transcutaneous tibial nerve stimulation in subjects with overactive bladder syndrome: A double-blind randomized controlled trial
articles.abstract: Background In the traditional treatment of overactive bladder (OAB) with transcutaneous posterior tibial nerve stimulation (TTNS), physical therapists currently use only transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS). However, the literature has commonly replaced TENS with diadynamic currents for various musculoskeletal pain syndromes. Moreover, no literature describes the use of diadynamic currents in the TTNS procedure. Therefore, our study aimed to determine the efficacy of diadynamic currents (DDC) versus TENS for TTNS in OAB Treatment. Methodology A randomized controlled trial was conducted among female patients with OAB aged 18–80 years. Subjects were randomly allocated to control and experimental groups. Participants in the control group received TTNS with TENS, and those in the experimental group underwent TTNS using DDC. Both groups received 8 TTNS sessions, two per week for 4 weeks. We measured pre- and post-intervention improvements using the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire (ICIQ) for OAB and the ICIQ OAB Quality of Life (QOL). The study is registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India under registration number CTRI/2025/12/099269. Results The mean age of the included sample was 59.75 years. Pre- and post-intervention ICIQ-OAB and ICIQ-OAB QOL scores showed significant improvements in disease symptoms and quality of life among patients with OAB in both the control and experimental groups. Comparison of improvements between the two groups on the ICIQ questionnaires showed no significant difference (p-values of 0.87 and 0.95). Correlations between patient-related characteristics and improvements in outcome measures were also not significant. Conclusion Eight sessions of TENS and DDC, combined with conventional physical therapy, including Kegel and breathing exercises, can reduce OAB symptoms and improve QOL in subjects with OAB syndrome. Diadynamic current can be used as an adjunct to conventional TENS in TTNS for treating OAB syndrome.

articles.title: Epidemiological surveillance of bacterial pathogens in cultured European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax) along the Aegean coast of Türkiye
articles.abstract: Intensive aquaculture of European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax) along the Aegean coast of Türkiye faces continuous production challenges from infectious diseases, yet comprehensive multi-year baseline data remain limited. This study presents a multi-year retrospective surveillance program (2020–2025) monitoring bacterial pathogens associated with 748 distinct cage-level disease outbreaks in fish across 19 discrete offshore commercial sea farms. To maintain industry confidentiality, diagnostic data from these separate facilities were fully aggregated and evaluated across three broad macro-regional surveillance zones. A total of 5,235 fish displaying clinical signs underwent diagnostic necropsy. Presumptive bacterial identification was conducted using phenotypic profiling through the API 20E system, and organ touch-imprint cytology. Six distinct bacterial species were isolated from positive clinical individuals, recovering a total of 2,490 isolates. Across the recorded outbreak events, etiological agents were ranked as primary drivers as follows: Photobacterium damselae subsp. piscicida (48.80%; N = 365), Tenacibaculum maritimum (35.83%; N = 268), Vibrio (Listonella) anguillarum (9.49%; N = 71), V. harveyi (3.74%; N = 28), V. ordalii (1.20%; N = 9), and V. alginolyticus (0.94%; N = 7). This hierarchy directly mirrored the overall bacterial isolation frequency, where P. damselae subsp. piscicida showed the highest relative distribution rate (46.18%; n = 1,150), followed by T. maritimum (34.10%; n = 849). Significantly lower isolation rates were recorded for V. (Listonella) anguillarum (11.41%; n = 284), V. harveyi (5.26%; n = 131), V. ordalii (1.77%; n = 44), and V. alginolyticus (1.29%; n = 32). Descriptive tracking of the purified laboratory isolates revealed localized variations in diagnostic recovery frequencies among the three sectors, while establishing a highly stable baseline dominated by P. damselae subsp. piscicida and T. maritimum across the Eastern Aegean Turkish mariculture network.

articles.title: Estimation of aerobic and anaerobic performance using a novel intermittent reactive agility test – An exploratory correlation study
articles.abstract: Separate tests are usually used to assess an athlete's ability to meet the aerobic and anaerobic demands of ball sports. These tests often compromise ecological validity by relying on linear runs and sprints rather than multidirectional reactive agility. This study investigated the correlations between a novel motor-cognitive reactive agility (RA) test and aerobic and anaerobic performance indices. Twenty-two trained participants (V˙O2max: 56 ± 6.4 ml ∙ kg-1 ∙ min-1) performed a treadmill ramp test to determine maximum oxygen uptake (V˙O2max), a running-based anaerobic sprint test (RAST) to determine peak power output (PPO), average power putput (POAV), fatigue index (FI) and anaerobic capacity (AC) and a motor-cognitive RA test on the SKILLCOURT. The RA test required participants to perform four 150 m maximal multidirectional change of directions runs with a break of 30 s. Running time, heart rate and power output were determined for all runs and correlated to V˙O2max and anaerobic performance indicators. Running time of the 4th SKILLCOURT run was correlated to V˙O2max (r20 = −0.80, p 20 = 0.72, p < 0.001). The SKILLCOURT RA test provides a promising tool for sport coaches to monitor aerobic and anaerobic performance indices, considering reactive agility. This needs to be validated in future studies.

articles.title: Exploratory cluster analysis of noninvasive vascular measures reveals heterogeneous vascular profiles after stroke
articles.abstract: by Bria L. Bartsch, Amanda N. Engler, Sandra A. Billinger Vascular dysfunction is prevalent after stroke and contributes to elevated cardiovascular risk; however, the extent to which vascular heterogeneity exists in this population remains unclear. This study examined whether distinct multi-domain cluster-derived vascular profiles are present in individuals with chronic stroke and whether these profiles are associated with functional performance. Vascular structure and function were assessed using flow-mediated dilation, carotid intima-media thickness, pulse wave velocity, and augmentation index, with age included in vascular clustering to account for vascular aging. Unsupervised k-means clustering was applied to identify vascular profiles. Functional performance was assessed using gait speed and predicted peak oxygen consumption (VO2peak) derived from a submaximal exercise test. Between-cluster differences were characterized using analysis of variance. Forty-five individuals with chronic stroke (62 ± 12 years; 29 ± 30 months post-stroke) were included. Three vascular profiles were identified (cluster 1: n = 13; cluster 2: n = 11; cluster 3: n = 21), with significant differences across clusters for all vascular measures (p 2peak (p = 0.31) or gait speed (p = 0.65). Three exploratory cluster-derived vascular profiles emerged among participants with chronic stroke, and age did not fully account for the observed vascular heterogeneity. Multi-domain cluster-derived vascular profiling revealed heterogeneous vascular profiles in individuals with chronic stroke, providing a basis for future studies to evaluate their relevance to cardiovascular risk stratification and long-term health management. articles.title: Finite-time robust motion control of intelligent vehicles based on neural approximation and disturbance estimation
articles.abstract: by Lijuan Zhang This paper addresses the inherent trade off between rapid convergence and high‑precision disturbance rejection in intelligent vehicle motion control under severe nonlinearities, parametric uncertainties, and time varying external perturbations. A composite finite‑time robust control strategy is proposed by synergistically integrating a nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode (NFTSM) surface, radial basis function neural networks (RBFNN), and a finite time disturbance observer (FTDO). The NFTSM guarantees singularity free finite time convergence of the tracking errors. The RBFNN approximates the slowly varying unknown dynamics, while the FTDO compensates online for the neural approximation residual and fast varying disturbances in a cascaded “coarse to fine” manner. Lyapunov-based Extensive co‑simulations with MATLAB/Simulink, conducted under double lane change and sinusoidal path scenarios with simultaneous road friction drops and stochastic lateral wind gusts, demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms conventional nonsingular terminal sliding mode control and disturbance observer based sliding mode control in terms of tracking accuracy, convergence speed, and chattering suppression.

articles.title: HIF-1α/PPAR-γ/SIRT1 axis drives astrocyte senescence and regulates endothelial function via GDNF/NRTN in diabetic retinopathy
articles.abstract: Background Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of blindness in working-age populations. Astrocyte senescence is highly prevalent in DR, but the underlying regulatory mechanism remains unclear. This study aims to investigate the role of the HIF-1α/PPAR-γ/SIRT1 axis in regulating retinal astrocyte senescence and endothelial function in DR. Methods Mouse retinal astrocytes were exposed to high glucose (30 mM) to mimic diabetic conditions. Senescence was evaluated by β-galactosidase staining. Signaling pathways were manipulated using HIF-1α inhibitor (PX-478), PPAR-γ inhibitor (T0070907), SIRT1 agonist (SRT2104), and autophagy inhibitor (3-MA). Protein and mRNA levels of key factors were detected by Western blot and RT-qPCR. Astrocytes and retinal microvascular endothelial cells were co-cultured in Transwell systems to assess paracrine regulation on endothelial migration, proliferation, and apoptosis. Results High glucose induced astrocyte senescence, inflammatory activation, and downregulation of GDNF and NRTN, accompanied by elevated HIF-1α and PPAR-γ, and reduced SIRT1 expression and autophagy activity. Inhibiting HIF-1α or activating SIRT1 attenuated senescence, apoptosis, and inflammation, restored autophagy, and upregulated GDNF/NRTN secretion. HIF-1α negatively regulated SIRT1 expression via PPAR-γ. Senescent astrocytes impaired endothelial function through reduced GDNF/NRTN; overexpression of GDNF or NRTN in astrocytes preserved endothelial migration and proliferation, and inhibited apoptosis. Conclusion HIF-1α/PPAR-γ/SIRT1 axis mediates high glucose-induced astrocyte senescence via autophagy dysfunction. Senescent astrocytes disrupt retinal endothelial homeostasis by reducing GDNF/NRTN secretion. Targeting this axis may represent a novel neurovascular protective therapeutic strategy for DR.

articles.title: HIV/AIDS knowledge and stigmatizing attitudes among adult residents of the United Arab Emirates: A cross-sectional study
articles.abstract: Background HIV-related stigma remains a significant barrier to prevention and treatment efforts in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. This study assessed HIV knowledge and stigmatizing attitudes among United Arab Emirates (UAE) residents. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted across the UAE between January and March 2025. A total of 1,211 eligible adult residents were recruited through convenience sampling. Demographic analyses included all 1,211 participants, while HIV knowledge and stigma analyses included 1,171 participants with analyzable outcome data. The questionnaire assessed demographics, HIV transmission knowledge, and stigmatizing attitudes using the Stigmatizing Attitudes Towards People Living with HIV/AIDS Scale (SAT-PLWHA-S). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, bivariate analyses, and multiple linear regression. Results Among the 1,211 participants included in the study, 1,171 contributed analyzable data to the HIV knowledge and stigma analyses. While 96.4% had heard of HIV/AIDS and demonstrated moderately high transmission knowledge (mean score: 75.5%), significant misconceptions persisted, particularly regarding condom effectiveness (60.5% overestimated risk). Strong stigmatizing attitudes emerged, especially regarding criminalization of transmission (79.6% support) and moralistic views. Higher knowledge correlated with less stigma (r = 0.347, p < 0.001), though nationality, language preference, and knowing someone with HIV were stronger predictors. Only 6.2% knew someone with HIV. Conclusions Despite adequate basic knowledge, significant HIV-related stigma persists in the UAE, driven by cultural and moral perspectives. Comprehensive interventions combining education, contact-based strategies, and policy reform are needed to reduce stigma and improve HIV prevention outcomes.

articles.title: Harrowing experiences of vagina fistula victims in the Kpandai District of Ghana: A qualitative study
articles.abstract: Background Vaginal fistula (VF), particularly vesicovaginal fistula (VVF), remains a significant reproductive health challenge in many low-resource settings, including the Kpandai District of Ghana. Despite its profound physical and psychosocial impact, the lived experiences of affected women in rural districts remain under-documented. Aim This study explored the lived experiences of women diagnosed with vesicovaginal fistula in the Kpandai District of Ghana, focusing on their physical, emotional, and social challenges, as well as coping strategies. Methods A qualitative descriptive study was conducted using in-depth interviews with ten women with clinically confirmed VVF. Participants were initially identified through a district health facility and subsequently recruited using a combination of purposive and snowball sampling techniques. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed thematically. Results Prolonged and obstructed labour—often occurring at home—emerged as the primary reported cause of VVF. Cultural beliefs, gender-based decision-making dynamics, limited access to healthcare, and financial constraints were key barriers to timely medical intervention. Consequences included persistent urinary incontinence, social stigma, emotional trauma, marital dissolution (reported by eight participants), loss of livelihood, and social isolation. Coping strategies included frequent washing, use of absorbent materials, and reliance on perfumes or herbal remedies. Conclusions Vesicovaginal fistula remains a devastating yet largely preventable condition in rural Ghana. The findings highlight the need to strengthen maternal health services, improve timely referral systems, and integrate psychosocial support within community-based care frameworks.

For quasi-one-dimensional charge neutral fl…

articles.abstract: Theory and experiments suggest that the mysterious fractures that appear when a brittle material is compressed result from a hidden buildup of internal tension.

articles.abstract: An experiment enables the first systematic, absolute superfluid-density measurement across the full superconducting dome of an infinite-layer nickelate.

articles.title: Similarity of Fractional Chern Insulators to Fractional Quantum Hall States: Moiré-Enhanced Gaps and Excitation-Spectrum Correspondence
articles.abstract: The excitation spectrum of fractional Chern insulators is identical to their fractional quantum Hall counterparts except for an enhancement factor, making it possible to predict their excitation spectrum from the Landau-level problem.

articles.abstract: We solve Dicke superradiance with two or more competing collective decay channels of tunable rates using a symbolic quantum-trajectory construction. The method yields closed time-domain populations and observables as finite combinations of exponential terms for arbitrary numbers of emitters and arbi…

However, definitive signatures of ultrastrong coupling remain elusive. Focusing on the quantum photon statistics of light transmitted through a cavity-embedded superconduc…

articles.title: Order by Inertia in Spinning Active Matter: Holey Fluids and Spin-Textured Crystals
articles.abstract: Experiments with macroscopic spinning particles that stir the surrounding fluid at high Reynolds numbers reveal that inertia plays an organizing role in active systems, promoting the emergence of collective structured phases.

articles.title: Thomas Plumb-Reyes translates quantum concepts for public policy
3D printing across the crop growth cycle: Toward sustainable agricultural systems
A full-hardware edge detection system based on a highly robust dual random number generator
articles.abstract: Conventional edge computing hardware at autonomous driving terminals is limited by chip area and power efficiency for complex image data. Recently, researchers have used memristors to construct dedicated hardware systems, achieving advancements in multiple image processing fields such as pattern recognition and edge detection. However, a full-hardware image processing system with anti-interference, low power, and high real-time performance remains challenging. Here, we fabricated a volatile Ag/AlO x /n-Si memristor with exceptional stability and low power. High-resolution electron microscopy visualized Ag conductive filament formation. Integrating two memristors with a logic circuit, we designed a low-power edge detection unit using dual random number hardware computation. Its energy consumption is 92.3% lower than traditional logic circuits, with strong anti-interference. To validate practical use, we constructed a 32-channel parallel full-hardware system with 64 devices, achieving 31.25 frames per second and excellent edge detection. The system exhibits excellent scalability, stability, and anti-interference, offering great potential for edge vision hardware in autonomous driving, safety monitoring, and surgical assistance.

articles.title: A robust spin-coupled tetraradical via nonalternant design
articles.abstract: Polyradicals in open-shell polycyclic hydrocarbons (PHs) offer access to multiple spin states and hold great promise for spintronics and quantum technologies. Here we report a nonalternant, air-stable tetraradical featuring two fused 7-5-7 rings and a strongly correlated singlet ground state. This molecule displays an exceptional tetraradical character ( y 0 = 1.00, y 1 = 0.89) and exhibits long ambient stability ( t 1/2 = 33 days). Comprehensive electronic structure and magnetic response analyses reveal that the spin topology is governed by both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions, with robust electron correlation ( J 1 = +321 K, J 2 = −44 K, and J 3 = −29 K). The unique nonalternant design suppresses hyperfine and vibrational decoherence, giving rise to long spin relaxation and coherence time. These findings demonstrate that embedding nonalternant motifs into PH polyradicals provides a powerful strategy to simultaneously promote molecular stability, spin-exchange coupling, and spin robustness—key features for materials in the rising field of quantum information science.

articles.title: A single–amino acid difference between rodent and human Andes virus affects viral glycoprotein trafficking
articles.abstract: Andes virus (ANDV) causes hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), with rare outbreaks involving person-to-person transmission. A human ANDV isolate from one such outbreak and a rodent isolate from the same region differ in lethality in Syrian golden hamsters. Genomic analysis revealed 25 nonsynonymous substitutions, including one leading to a T641I change in the human ANDV glycoprotein precursor near its cleavage site. Although the isolates differed in growth kinetics, strand-specific RT-qPCR did not support major differences in viral RNA synthesis, whereas virion release was delayed in the case of the human isolate. In human cell expression systems, a single I641T substitution in the human ANDV glycoprotein resulted in decreased Golgi retention and faster release of virion-like particles relative to wild-type glycoprotein. Since ANDV egress takes place at the Golgi, the T641I change present in the human ANDV isolate may represent a human adaptive mutation influencing glycoprotein trafficking and virus particle release.

articles.title: A transcriptional and cellular exploration of obesity and type II diabetes in human adipose tissues
articles.abstract: Obesity is tightly linked to metabolic disorders such as type II diabetes mellitus (T2D), although a subpopulation of individuals with obesity do not present with these morbidities. The biological factors conferring T2D vulnerability remain incompletely understood. We recruited 58 individuals with obesity with or without a clinical diagnosis of T2D (Ob + T2D and Ob). We profiled paired samples of omental and subcutaneous adipose by single-cell RNA sequencing ( n = 10), flow cytometry under basal and stimulated conditions ( n = 42), and histology ( n = 17). Flow cytometry and chemokine quantification were also performed in paired whole blood. We identified reprogramming of the omental stromal compartment, centered on mesothelial and endothelial cells, alongside contrasting innate T cell and macrophage phenotypes across depots. Mesothelial and IGFBP2 + cells exhibited a fibrotic, epithelial-mesenchymal transition–like phenotype, while omental endothelial cells exhibited a lipid-overload, inflammatory, antigen presentation profile in T2D. Omental and subcutaneous adipose innate T cells exhibited divergent inflammatory profiles between tissues. These findings reveal previously unidentified insights into the pathophysiology of T2D in adipose tissue and identify compensatory networks within the tissues that could be exploited by targeted therapeutics.

articles.title: Adaptive dual-programming magnetic soft robot with lifelike behavior
articles.abstract: Magnetic soft robots with embodied intelligence of multimodal motions, environmental perception, and functional decoupling depend on ingenious material arrangement and programmable morphing information introduction. While some efforts have been made, achieving lifelike behaviors for soft robots in system-level strategy remains a notable challenge. Here, we present dual-programming hydrogel-based soft robots (DHSRs) that couple magnetic and anisotropic programming through the spatial arrangement of patterned magnetic skeletons into responsive and structural hydrogel bodies. These DHSRs exhibit programmable exquisite and multicurved structures in three-dimensional (3D) space, environment-adaptive deformation behaviors proved by switching from random jumping on land to regular swimming in water of a fish-like soft robot, and further locomotion-function decoupling capabilities of region-selective cargo delivery in an integrated “locomotion-perception-action” workflow. Our strategy in biomedical potential is exemplified by a ring-like pH-responsive DHSR for gastric ulcer therapy, which integrates multimodal locomotion (rolling, tumbling, and rotating), adaptive matching, and microneedle-mediated penetration. By collaborating with a capsule endoscopy system, we explore the possibility of a wireless and painless diagnostic-therapeutic platform in a pig model. This strategy endows the robot with perception and multitask execution capabilities, highlighting a promising route for the intelligent evolution of soft robots across diverse application domains.

articles.title: Age reshapes selection on melanoma driver mutations
articles.abstract: Aging is a major risk factor for melanoma. However, it is unclear whether aging fuels tumor evolution by altering mutation rates, changing the microenvironmentally induced selection on drivers, or both. We analyzed 5472 melanomas, estimating how selection on individual variants changes with patient age while accounting for differing neutral mutation rates. Neutral mutation rates increased only modestly with age; ultraviolet damage remained predominant, but endogenous processes increasingly contributed to older tumors. In contrast, selection on major drivers was strongly age dependent: The advantage of BRAF V600E declined precipitously with age, whereas NRAS Q61 mutations gained advantage. TERT promoter mutations became more frequent, yet less advantageous. Aging therefore reshapes melanoma evolution primarily by altering selection, motivating age-conscious evaluation of clinical biomarkers and therapies.

articles.title: Brainstem enkephalinergic neural circuit underlying cold-induced pain relief in mice
articles.abstract: Application of cold or cold-mimicking chemicals to injury has long been recognized as an effective means of pain relief. However, underlying neural mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we identified a cold-responsive neuronal subset within the lateral parabrachial nucleus (lPBN), the thermosensory relay region in the hindbrain, that mediates cold-induced analgesia in mice. Activation of these neurons and their projection to ventrolateral periaqueductal gray (vlPAG) increased the nociceptive threshold, while ablation of these neurons attenuated analgesia induced by cold-mimicking chemicals. We further identified that these neurons express precursor gene of enkephalin ( Penk ), which is necessary for TRPM8 (transient receptor potential melastatin 8)–mediated pain relief. Mechanistically, cold-responsive lPBN neurons frequency-dependently released enkephalin peptide into vlPAG to activate the descending pain modulation circuitry via disinhibition. Activation of cold-responsive neurons reduced spinal cord responses to noxious stimuli, suggesting the involvement of a top-down pain modulation pathway. These findings propose a central mechanism underlying cold-induced pain relief, which could be a novel therapeutic target.

articles.title: CD8+ T cells induce RIPK1-regulated brain endothelial cell death in cerebral malaria
articles.abstract: Cerebral malaria (CM) is a potentially lethal complication of Plasmodium falciparum infection characterized by blood-brain barrier disruption and brain hemorrhage. Although immune-mediated endothelial damage is central to CM pathology, the mechanisms linking cytotoxic immune responses to endothelial injury remain unclear. Here, we show that CD8 + T cells induce receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)–regulated cell death of brain endothelial cells in mouse CM, while RIPK1 phosphorylation is increased in brain endothelial cells in human CM. Using magnetic resonance imaging, three-dimensional tissue-cleared brain imaging, cross-species pathology, endothelial translatomics, immunocerebrovascular interactomics, and genetic association testing, we identify a CD8 + T cell–dependent, RIPK1-centered mouse endothelial cell death program. Combined RIPK1 and caspase inhibition protected cross-presenting endothelial cells from CD8 + T cell–mediated death in vitro. In vivo, brain endothelial-specific genetic inactivation or systemic pharmacological inhibition of RIPK1 kinase activity prolonged survival in mouse CM without altering parasitemia. These findings support RIPK1 inhibition as a promising therapeutic strategy to counter CD8 + T cell–induced endothelial death in CM.

articles.title: Combating drug-resistant Aeromonas veronii: Multiomics revealed the antibacterial mechanism of resveratrol
articles.abstract: Aeromonas , widely distributed in aquatic ecosystems, is a prevalent fish pathogen and can cause human infections via contaminated aquatic products, polluted water contact, or tainted food consumption. Escalating antibiotic resistance in Aeromonas strains highlights an urgent need for alternative natural antimicrobial agents. This study investigated resveratrol’s antibacterial mechanisms against Aeromonas veronii and evaluated its protective efficacy in hybrid sturgeon. Resveratrol exhibited strong activity [minimum inhibitory concentration: 128 microgram per milliliter (μg/ml), minimum bactericidal concentration: 256 μg/ml], disrupting cell wall/membrane integrity, inducing reactive oxygen species accumulation, inhibiting adenosine 5′-triphosphate synthesis, and down-regulating key metabolic pathways via transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses. In the sturgeon infection model, resveratrol-nanoemulsion notably improved survival, reduced tissue bacterial loads, mitigated oxidative stress and inflammation, and restored intestinal barrier function. These findings confirm resveratrol as a promising antibiotic alternative against A. veronii , with nanoemulsion formulation enhancing its therapeutic efficacy.

articles.abstract: Bystander T cells eradicate tumors in the absence of antigen recognition.

articles.title: Myeloid cells run amok in injured brains
articles.abstract: Aberrant, cranial bone marrow–derived myelopoiesis drives neuroinflammation in chronic traumatic brain injury.

articles.title: Programming immunity in situ: A new frontier of in vivo cell engineering
articles.abstract: In vivo cell engineering enables the direct programming of immune cells inside patients. Instead of isolating, modifying, and reinfusing cells, therapeutic instructions are delivered directly to selected immune cells through lipid nanoparticles or viral vectors. This approach could facilitate rapid and scalable deployment of varied immune cell therapies across disease contexts. Early clinical studies in oncology and autoimmunity demonstrate increasing technical and clinical feasibility. The next challenge lies in enhancing precision to ensure that vectors reach the target cell type and tissue, deliver the appropriate payload, and produce desired transient or durable activity. Progress in targeting ligands, vector design, biodistribution control, and genome editing is beginning to address these barriers. Ensuring safety against immunogenicity, inflammatory toxicity, off-target editing, and uncontrolled persistence remains a central priority. By mastering these constraints, in vivo engineering could turn endogenous immune cells into therapeutic agents generated directly in the body, expanding cell therapy to diseases refractory to current modalities.

articles.title: The structural basis of IL-36R proinflammatory signaling mediated by IL-36γ and IL-37
articles.abstract: The interleukin-36 receptor (IL-36R) drives proinflammatory signaling and is therapeutically targeted by spesolimab in acute skin inflammation. Beyond its three canonical agonists (IL-36α, IL-36β, and IL-36γ), IL-36R was recently proposed to be activated by IL-37. Together with antagonism by IL-36R antagonist (IL-36RA) and IL-38, this creates a complex structure-function landscape that remains poorly understood. Here, we report the cryo–electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structure of human IL-36γ bound to IL-36R and the shared co-receptor IL-1R accessory protein (IL-1RAcP). IL-36γ engages IL-36R with low affinity, enabling high-affinity IL-1RAcP recruitment. IL-37 exhibits the opposite binding signature, binding IL-36R with high affinity but IL-1RAcP weakly. Functional comparison of IL-36R engagement by IL-36γ and IL-37 confirmed their common proinflammatory signature, with IL-36γ exhibiting markedly higher potency, consistent with its more stable signaling complex. Structural comparison of cytokine-bound versus antibody-antagonized IL-36R revealed that spesolimab acts as an allosteric antagonist. This study therefore provides a structural and mechanistic blueprint for IL-36R activation by distinct cytokines.

articles.title: A simplified high-pressure freezing workflow in Autogrids
articles.abstract: Weber et al. introduce a modular planchette system that simplifies high-pressure freezing of biological samples for cryo-electron microscopy. By reducing sample handling and accommodating diverse specimen types, the Autogrid planchette approach makes it easier to study complex biological structures in their near-native state, expanding opportunities for cellular and biomedical research.

articles.title: Covalent remodeling of CRBN creates a non-canonical neosubstrate interface with NTAQ1
articles.abstract: De la Peña, Cruite et al. show that covalent modification of cereblon (CRBN) creates a new neosubstrate-binding interface that recruits NTAQ1 through a mechanism distinct from canonical G-loop degrons. This work reveals how site-specific chemical modification can reprogram E3 ligase specificity and expand the design space for molecular glue degraders.

articles.title: Dynamic ring rearrangements underlie transport by MCE proteins
articles.abstract: Ratkevičiūtė et al. identify inter-ring conformational plasticity as a shared property of structurally distinct MCE proteins. Coordinated ring and pore rearrangements dynamically reshape the central transport channel, providing a structural basis for substrate translocation and revealing how mutations triggering channel collapse can disrupt MCE protein function.

articles.title: Lab leak disease outbreaks: the long, murky history
articles.abstract: In the heart of Russia, fear of plague is spreading. Unbeknown to the outside world, authorities have quietly commandeered the building where the first case emerged. Rifle wielding guards stand at the entrances. Inside, people are locked in quarantine rooms. There have already been deaths—pneumonic plague. And it came from a laboratory.This was the scene at a Moscow hospital in 1939, according to a handful of recollections written by scientists who lived through it. The microbiologist Abram Lvovich Berlin had travelled in from the outskirts of the capital to discuss his experiments with Yersinia pestis, the bacterium that causes plague. But he had inadvertently infected himself, becoming highly contagious. He would soon be dead.Sources differ on the details—was it two or three people who succumbed after coming into contact with Berlin? Most accounts say that the doctor who first diagnosed plague in the stricken microbiologist and a hotel barber were...

articles.title: Managing risk and uncertainty includes ambiguity
articles.abstract: jason.hancock@nhs.netChris Whitty’s recent lecture on risk, uncertainty, and medical decision making resonated with my experience as a psychiatrist, director of medical education, and clinical education researcher with an interest in uncertainty.1 I welcome his suggestion that educators should support resident doctors to hold and manage progressively greater levels of risk throughout their training.But the lecture placed considerable emphasis on probability and complexity as sources of uncertainty, with less attention given to ambiguity.2 Whitty called for the medical profession to insist that large language models used by the public indicate the degree of uncertainty associated with a proposed diagnosis, for example. This assumes that the level of uncertainty can be quantified, as may be possible when uncertainty arises from probability. But many clinical decisions are made in the context of ambiguity—where information is missing, imprecise, or conflicting—and the degree of uncertainty may not be known or straightforward to communicate.The skills needed...

articles.title: [Clinical Rounds] Vertigo, multifocal brain lesions, and a diagnostic clue on the skin
articles.abstract: A woman aged 35 years was evaluated for a 1-year history of recurrent, brief (approximately 15 min) episodes of non-positional vertigo described as a spinning sensation. Episodes were not accompanied by headache, tinnitus, hearing loss, visual symptoms, or other neurological complaints. Blood pressure was normal, and there was no orthostatic hypotension or tachycardia upon standing. Neurological and vestibular examinations, including audiometry and the Dix–Hallpike manoeuvre, were normal between episodes.

articles.title: [Comment] Preparing for dialysis when dialysis might never begin?
articles.abstract: For older people (aged ≥80 years) with frailty or multimorbidity living with kidney failure, choosing a care pathway could involve deciding whether to prepare for dialysis long before it is needed. Preparation involves education, appointments, investigations, and, for some people, surgery to create dialysis access. The alternative care pathway is conservative kidney management, which involves active care aimed at slowing kidney disease progression, managing symptoms, and preserving quality of life without planning for dialysis.
