Catalytic domains encode product diversity in PUFA synthases
articles.abstract: Polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) synthases share similar architectures, yet produce distinct PUFAs. Recent mechanistic studies reveal how substrate recognition by dehydratase, ketoacyl-acyl carrier protein synthase, and acyltransferase domains controls double bond formation, chain elongation, and release, highlighting chemical principles underlying PUFA structural diversity and product distributions. These insights inform rational engineering.

articles.title: Inner-sphere iron photocatalysis unlocks direct decarboxylative borylation
articles.abstract: Carboxylic acids are attractive precursors to boronic esters, but redox requirements of decarboxylation are poorly matched to diboron reagents. Juliá-Hernández and coworkers report an iron ligand-to-metal charge transfer strategy activating coordinated carboxylates through photoinduced electron transfer. Free acids, from acetic acid to drug molecules, give boronic esters in one step.

articles.title: Strategic innovation in the total synthesis of Euphorbia diterpenoids
articles.abstract: Following Wender’s pioneering studies, the total synthesis of Euphorbia diterpenoids has undergone a remarkable renaissance over the past decade. This resurgence has been driven by the emergence of unified synthetic platforms, radical-based coupling strategies, and strategic cycloaddition reactions. These developments have not only enabled the concise and scalable synthesis of flagship molecules such as phorbol, prostratin, resiniferatoxin, and pedrolide, but also provided chemical probes for exploring their promising biological activities. This review summarizes the total syntheses of these four molecules, with a particular emphasis on the strategic innovations and emerging trends across the different synthetic routes developed for each, aiming to provide timely guidance for future synthetic efforts.

articles.title: A new view of collectivism
articles.abstract: Collectivism is the most widely studied cultural dimension. Yet recent evidence shows that the most-cited scales contain conflicting definitions of collectivism. I review evidence that conceptualizations conflate ‘warm fuzzy’ collectivism and responsibilism. I outline how clarifying the concept can resolve apparent contradictions in previous findings and advance measurement and theory.

articles.title: Consumer neuroscience: the emerging science of everyday choices
articles.abstract: Consumer neuroscience is a developing field at the intersection of neuroscience, psychology, economics, and marketing that seeks to uncover the neural and physiological mechanisms underlying consumer behavior. Building on early psychophysiological studies, the field has expanded substantially since the mid-2000s through an increasing range of methods and models. We highlight that its strength lies in spanning multiple levels of analysis to address marketing-relevant questions. We highlight four major trends driving the field: improving behavioral prediction, synthesizing evidence through multidataset analyses, developing formal models linking neural processes to consumer decision-making, and integrating brain and body measures. Together, these advances position consumer neuroscience as an integrative science with implications for marketing, policy, and consumer welfare.

articles.title: Trends at 50: a mission that matters
articles.abstract: What makes a great review article in your field? As more research is published every day, it has become increasingly difficult to keep up with the latest developments and to ensure that you are hearing from the leading scientists driving these innovations and advances. How do you know what is new and what is valuable?

articles.title: Embracing ignorance: tackling biodiversity knowledge shortfalls
articles.abstract: Global biodiversity information suffers from gaps, biases, and uncertainty over time and space, afflicting all taxonomic groups. Incomplete or biased data introduce uncertainty into models of biodiversity trends, potentially generating faulty inferences with knock-on effects for conservation. We revisit how the limitations of biodiversity knowledge are conceptualised, expanding the current classification to encompass eleven major shortfalls spanning taxonomic, ecological, evolutionary, and biocultural aspects, and examine the impediments that limit progress in reducing them. Information gaps have been moulded by our capacity and willingness to collect data, which are constrained by a series of financial, taxonomic, and technological impediments that vary across regions and taxa. Addressing these challenges is crucial for understanding biodiversity patterns and processes and developing effective conservation actions.

articles.title: Cavity-QED Molecular Dynamics: An eT-i-PI Interface for Ab Initio Cavity Born-Oppenheimer Dynamics and Joint Nuclear-Photon Path-Integral Sampling
articles.abstract: Simulating molecules in quantum electrodynamic (QED) cavities requires a consistent description of electronic response, nuclear motion, and electromagnetic-field fluctuations. Here, I present Cavity-QED Molecular Dynamics, an interface connecting eT and i-PI for atomistic simulations of finite molecular systems coupled to a single photon mode. The code evaluates a self-consistent cavity Born-Oppenheimer Hartree-Fock (CBO-HF) energy surface and supports classical-nuclei dynamics under canonical (NVT) and microcanonical (NVE) ensembles, as well as canonical joint nuclear-photon path-integral sampling including nuclear quantum effects (NQEs). A fixed-displacement gradient correction provides nuclear and photon forces consistent with the same energy surface as the photon coordinate evolves independently. OpenMP threading, concurrent bead evaluations, and analysis utilities support practical simulations. Water-monomer benchmarks assess both dynamical propagation and equilibrium sampling. Energy-derivative checks and NVE timestep tests demonstrate consistent force evaluation and integration, while path integral molecular dynamics (PIMD) simulations with PILE-L thermostatting reproduce analytic finite-bead photon second moments, including their centroid and internal contributions, within sampling uncertainties. At the tested parameters, cavity coupling produces a small but statistically resolved increase in photon fluctuations, while changes in mean molecular geometry remain within sampling uncertainty. The resulting Cavity-QED Molecular Dynamics framework enables controlled investigations of how coupled quantum fluctuations of matter and the electromagnetic field influence molecular equilibrium properties within the CBO-HF approximation, providing a foundation for future studies of cavity-modified hydrogen bonding, vibrational spectra, and molecular polaritonic phenomena.

articles.title: Classical control of quantum-state relaxation in confined molecular hydrogen
articles.abstract: Quantum-state conversion between the ortho and para nuclear-spin states of H$_2$ is forbidden in the isolated molecule but these states can become connected through interactions with a surrounding environment. How that same environment governs the dynamics of the newly connected states remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate this problem using H$_2$ confined in crystalline molecular solids, where the host environment selectively enables conversion between a pair of otherwise disconnected ortho-H$_2$ and para-H$_2$ states. Rotationally resolved infrared spectroscopy directly determines the state-specific conversion dynamics in crystalline CO$_2$ and N$_2$O at 10 K, revealing that increasing H$_2$ concentration suppresses nuclear-spin conversion by nearly an order of magnitude, reaching complete suppression by 20% H$_2$ loading. Molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations identify two complementary origins of this concentration dependence: changes in the thermally populated phonon modes available to mediate relaxation, and strain-driven H$_2$ clustering that progressively removes molecules from the host crystal field responsible for enabling conversion. The resulting picture connects a classical collective response of the host to microscopic quantum-state dynamics: H$_2$ loading generates strain that reorganizes the local molecular environment, thereby modifying both the phonon bath and the molecular coupling to that bath. These results establish a multiscale mechanism by which condensed-phase environments can govern the connectivity and dynamics of an effective two-level system.

articles.title: Density Matrix Renormalization Group Method for Core-excited Electronic States
articles.abstract: We present the formulation and implementation of the Core-Valence Separation (CVS) approximation within the Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) framework for the simulation of core-level X-ray spectra. Two symmetry implementations are developed and assessed, identifying a scheme that preserves spin symmetry and remains applicable to multiple core orbitals. Benchmark calculations for BeH$_2$ and [Fe(H$_2$O)$_6$]$^{2+}$ demonstrate excellent agreement with conventional multi-configurational methods for excitation energies and spectral intensities, while enabling substantially larger active spaces. Using quantum information theory measures, we show that the CVS constraint suppresses core-occupation fluctuations without significantly altering core--valence entanglement, providing a diagnostic for its applicability. Furthermore, we introduce a reference-free second-order perturbative correction that systematically reduces errors introduced by the CVS approximation. Finally, a generalized multi-core formulation enables the simultaneous treatment of excitations from different core shells. These developments establish CVS-DMRG as an accurate and computationally efficient approach to core-level spectroscopy of strongly correlated systems.

articles.title: Fortuitous Cancellation of Competing Effects in the Free Energy of Water Autoionization: Long-Range Electrostatics, System Size, and Nuclear Quantum Effects
articles.abstract: Few molecular processes are more fundamental to chemistry than the autoionization of water, whose equilibrium constant, $K_w \approx 10^{-14}$, underlies acid-base equilibria and the chemistry of life. Yet the molecular origins of the free energy cost of forming and separating ions remain incompletely understood. Efforts to explain it have been limited by the difficulty of modeling water reactivity in sufficient detail. Here we combine machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) with spectral adaptive biasing force enhanced sampling to connect proton transfer and water wire configurations to the underlying free energy landscape. We identify competing influences of long-range electrostatics, system size, temperature, and nuclear quantum motion on the predicted ionization thermodynamics. The free energy surface extends from neutral water to ions separated beyond the solvent-separated ion pair (SSIP). It reveals a transition state in which a proton is shared between the second and third molecules of a three-membered water wire. The contact ion pair is unstable and the SSIP only weakly metastable, so determining pK$_w$ requires sampling longer wires. Long-range electrostatics raise the free energy at ion separations beyond $3\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$. Models with comparable force errors give substantially different free energy profiles in this region. Increasing system size lowers the calculated pK$_w$, while nuclear quantum effects bring it closer to experiment and reproduce the higher pK$_w$ of D$_2$O relative to H$_2$O. These results establish a baseline for interpreting thermodynamic results from MLIP simulations in which charged and polar groups react and diffuse in finite cells. Our analysis also explains how cancellation among competing effects can yield ionization constants close to experiment even when simulations omit several physical contributions.

articles.title: Increased Crystal Nucleation in the Glassy State of a Polymer/Water Mixture
articles.abstract: Within classical nucleation theory, crystal nucleation requires sufficient supersaturation, but is suppressed at low temperatures due to reduced molecular mobility, leading to a maximum nucleation rate typically above the glass transition temperature $T_g$. Here, we experimentally show that this conventional picture breaks down in a biocompatible polymer poly(2-methoxyethyl acrylate)(PMEA)/water mixture. We find that the number of nuclei increases dramatically below $T_g$, with the effective nucleation rate exhibiting an unusual maximum at approximately $T_g-10$ K. Calorimetric experiments reveal a strong temperature-history dependence of cold crystallization of water in hydrated PMEA, which is explained by the observed nucleation behavior. We propose that the unusual enhancement of nucleation below $T_g$ provides a key mechanism linking high glass-forming ability and cold crystallization upon heating, thereby explaining the striking asymmetry in crystallization behavior between cooling and heating. Our findings suggest that a hidden nucleation-rate maximum below $T_g$ may also underlie cold crystallization in other glass-forming liquids.

articles.title: Propagating the Hierarchical Equations of Motion using the Multi-Layer Multi-Configurational Time-Dependent Hartree method
articles.abstract: The hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) are a powerful, numerically exact approach for simulating the time evolution of open quantum systems. Recently, several tensor-train- and tensor-network-based approaches have been suggested and realized to extend the range of applicability of the HEOM approach to larger and more realistic systems. In this paper, we build upon the existing twin-space formulation of the HEOM and present a novel approach to propagate the fermionic HEOM efficiently using the multi-configurational time-dependent Hartree method (MCTDH). We benchmark the resulting HEOM+MCTDH method with electron transport calculations for a Holstein-type nanojunction model. Furthermore, we demonstrate the capabilities of the HEOM+MCTDH method by applying it to a more complex vibronic coupling nanojunction model with strong molecule-electrode coupling for which fully quantum simulations have not been feasible previously.

articles.title: Time-gated optical-parametric-amplification and field-resolved detection of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals
articles.abstract: Infrared spectroscopy is a key tool to study complex structural dynamics in molecular systems. However, resolving weak or broad vibrational modes is challenging due to their rapid decay. Here, we demonstrate a technique to significantly extend the detectable lifetime - and thereby spectral resolution - of molecular signatures by employing synchronized time-gated optical parametric amplification of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals. Utilizing a Cr:ZnS laser system and a nonlinear ZnGeP2 crystal, we achieve a 10-fold increase in the electric field strength of the infrared molecular signal, yielding a two-orders of magnitude enhancement in dynamic range and a 2-fold increase in the signal-to-noise ratio. Using isopropyl alcohol as a model system, we demonstrate that OPA-enhanced detection extends the observable window of vibrational modes up to 72 %. This approach allows for the reconstruction of high-fidelity molecular fingerprints that resolve complex vibrational relaxation pathways and weak structural dynamics, previously hidden within the background and noise, providing a pathway for new high-sensitivity and time-resolved studies of complex chemical structures.

articles.title: Expectation-driven gain modulation of preparatory spatial attention
articles.abstract: The visual system can flexibly adjust attentional deployment to match task demands, but whether observers can proactively modulate the spatial scope of attention based on expectations about upcoming search difficulty remains unclear. According to the zoom lens model, attention can narrow or broaden its spatial extent, with narrower focus enhancing processing efficiency, a mechanism that would benefit target discrimination in crowded displays. We tested whether observers adjust attentional scope when expecting sparse versus dense search arrays by combining spatial cueing with block-wise manipulations of display density expectations. Participants performed a visual search task in which endogenous cues predicted target location, while blocks predominantly contained either sparse (1 target, 3 distractors) or dense (1 target, 7 distractors) displays. We applied inverted encoding models to broadband EEG data to reconstruct spatial channel tuning functions, enabling precise characterization of both the locus and breadth of attentional deployment. Behaviorally, expecting difficult searches selectively improved accuracy at cued locations without costs elsewhere. Consistent with this selective benefit, neural measurements revealed that expectancy enhanced the amplitude of spatially selective responses at the attended location but did not alter tuning width. These findings demonstrate that expectations about search difficulty modulate attention through gain-based signal enhancement rather than adjustments to spatial scope, revealing that preparatory attentional control operates via amplitude modulation within a stable spatial focus. This mechanism complements reactive attentional adjustments and provides an efficient means for the visual system to optimize processing under predictable task demands.

articles.title: Large inversions in Lake Malawi cichlids are associated with habitat, lineage, and sex determination
articles.abstract: Chromosomal inversions are an important class of genetic variation that link multiple alleles together into a single inherited block that can have important effects on fitness. To study the role of large inversions in the massive evolutionary radiation of Lake Malawi cichlids, we used long-read technologies to identify four single and two tandem inversions that span half of each respective chromosome, and which together encompass over 10% of the genome. Each inversion is fixed in one of the two states within the seven major ecogroups, suggesting they played a role in the separation of the major lake lineages into specific lake habitats. One exception is within the benthic sub-radiation, where both inverted and non-inverted alleles continue to segregate within the group. The evolutionary histories of three of the six inversions suggest they transferred from the pelagic Diplotaxodon group into benthic ancestors at the time the benthic sub-radiation was seeded. The remaining three inversions are found in a subset of benthic species living in deep waters. We show that some of these inversions are linked to XY sex-determination systems but are also likely limited to a subset of total lake species. Our work suggests that inversions have been under both sexual and natural selection in Lake Malawi cichlids and that they will be important to understanding how this adaptive radiation evolved.

articles.title: Simple methods to acutely measure multiple timing metrics among the sexual repertoire of male Drosophila
articles.abstract: Male Drosophila courtship behavior is a key model for studying temporal decision-making. While courtship index (CI) is widely used to quantify mating activity, other timing metrics like courtship latency, copulation latency (CL), and mating duration (MD) remain understudied. Traditional methods for quantifying these behaviors are often labor-intensive and prone to human error. In this study, we present a protocol combining a modular chamber system and automated software (DrosoMating) to quantify six key timing metrics during male courtship. Our image-based video analysis enables precise identification of courtship and copulation events, as well as quantification of their timing and duration under controlled conditions. Validation shows <0.05% error rates and 98–99% agreement with manual scoring for CL, CI, and MD. The protocol supports genetic and neural circuit manipulations, detecting subtle genetic, social, and environmental behavioral variations. By minimizing manual effort and standardizing data collection, this approach facilitates scalable, reproducible studies on adaptive trade-offs, learning, and neural mechanisms in mating behavior. This method streamlines timing analysis in male courtship, offering reproducible metrics for behavioral genetics.

articles.title: Spatial confinement induces oscillatory migration of epidermal keratinocytes and forms a three-compartment epithelial structure with epithelial–mesenchymal transition dynamics
articles.abstract: Epithelial cells undergo epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) during migration and regain their epithelial phenotype in the post-migration phase (mesenchymal–epithelial transition [MET]). We established an experimental system that reproduces a three-compartment epithelial structure comprising the original epithelium, its EMT state, and its MET state. Keratinocytes (KCs), skin epithelial cells, placed on a microporous membrane, migrated through 3.0 µm or larger micropores. The 3.0-µm-pored membrane induced an epithelial structure with three distinct states: stratified KCs above the membrane, KCs showing EMT within the micropores, and a new stratified epithelium under the membrane. The membrane with larger micropores failed to maintain the three-compartment epithelial structure. Live imaging revealed that KCs moved in an oscillatory manner, with actin-rich filopodia-like structures extending into and out of the 3.0 µm micropores, while the cells migrated unidirectionally into larger micropores. Piezo1 and keratin 6 were identified as negative modulators of KC entry into and exit from the 3.0 µm micropores. These results demonstrate that non-cancerous epithelial cells migrate through confined spaces in an oscillatory manner, which might contribute to the formation of a three-compartment epithelial structure that recapitulates key aspects of wound healing.

articles.title: The hypoxic response extends lifespan through a bioaminergic and peptidergic neural circuit
articles.abstract: A coordinated response to stress is crucial for promoting the short- and long-term health of an organism. The perception of stress, frequently through the nervous system, can lead to physiological changes that are fundamental to maintaining homeostasis. Activating the response to low oxygen, or hypoxia, extends healthspan and lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. However, despite some positive impacts, negative effects of the hypoxic response in specific tissues prevent translation of their benefits in mammals. Thus, it is imperative to identify which components of this response promote longevity. Here, we interrogate the cell-nonautonomous signaling pathway downstream of genetic activation of the hypoxic response. We find that HIF-1-mediated signaling in ADF serotonergic neurons is both necessary and sufficient for lifespan extension. Signaling through the serotonin receptor SER-7 in the GABAergic RIS interneurons is necessary in this process. Our findings also highlight the involvement of additional neural signaling molecules, including the neurotransmitters tyramine and GABA, and the neuropeptide NLP-17, in mediating longevity effects. Finally, we demonstrate that oxygen- and carbon-dioxide-sensing neurons act downstream of HIF-1 in this circuit. Together, these insights demonstrate a circuit for how genetic induction of the hypoxic response cell-nonautonomously modifies aging and suggests valuable targets for modulating aging in mammals.

articles.title: The resource elasticity of control
articles.abstract: The ability to determine how much the environment can be controlled through our actions has long been viewed as fundamental to adaptive behavior. While traditional accounts treat controllability as a fixed property of the environment, we argue that real-world controllability often depends on the effort, time, and money we are able and willing to invest. In such cases, controllability can be said to be elastic to invested resources. Here, we propose that inferring this elasticity is essential for efficient resource allocation, and thus, elasticity misestimations result in maladaptive behavior. To test this hypothesis, we developed a novel treasure hunt game where participants encountered environments with varying degrees of controllability and elasticity. Across two pre-registered studies (N=514), we first demonstrate that people infer elasticity and adapt their resource allocation accordingly. We then present a computational model that explains how people make this inference and identify individual elasticity biases that lead to suboptimal resource allocation. Finally, we show that overestimation of elasticity is associated with elevated psychopathology involving an impaired sense of control. These findings establish the elasticity of control as a distinct cognitive construct guiding adaptive behavior and a computational marker for control-related maladaptive behavior.

articles.title: Bioinformatic-Guided Discovery of O -Dealkylation Activity in Cytochrome P450 Monooxygenases
articles.abstract: The O-dealkylation of alkyl ethers—or the removal of small alkyl protecting groups (PGs)—remains a significant challenge in organic synthesis. While traditional chemical methods require harsh reaction conditions and lack sufficient selectivity, biocatalytic approaches represent valuable alternatives. However, enzymes facilitating the desired O-dealkylation reactions are scarce. In this work, we applied a sequence similarity network (SSN)-guided approach to identify cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (CYPs) with O-dealkylation activity within the growing sequence diversity found in public databases. We investigated six CYPs, three of which exhibited significant activity toward structurally diverse ethers bearing methyl, ethyl, propyl, or allyl groups. While P450ThcB and P450Terp enabled the deprotection of aromatic and aliphatic primary and secondary ethers, P450Sca2-mut complemented the substrate scope by effectively deprotecting sterically demanding tertiary ethers. In particular, P450ThcB and P450Terp exhibited high regioselectivity, preferentially cleaving phenolic over benzylic ethers. Furthermore, P450ThcB enabled the regioselective deprotection of veratryl alcohol. Preparative scale reactions of three substrates yielded up to 74% of the isolated and (regioselectively) cleaved alcohol product. Together, these findings substantially expand the enzymatic toolbox for the selective removal of alkyl PGs and highlight the suitability of SSN-guided database mining approaches for the identification of biocatalysts with the desired function.

articles.title: Durable Equilibrium-Level Dry Reforming of Methane over Strain Regulated Oligo-Ni/Y2O3
articles.abstract: Precise control of catalytic active centers and their interfacial strain is central to accelerating heterogeneous reactions, yet systematic regulation of strain at subnanometer metal–oxide interfaces remains challenging. Here, we report a class of 3d metal/heavy rare-earth metal oxide oligoatomic catalysts, in which finite metal ensembles are anchored on oxide surfaces to form nuclearity-dependent, strain-coupled metal–oxide interfaces. By varying the metal species, oxide support, and, most critically, the average number of metal atoms in each ensemble, we show that interfacial strain can be systematically tuned across diverse 3d metal/oxide combinations. In the Ni/Y2O3 system, an optimal nuclearity range of approximately 4–6 Ni atoms maximizes both compressive Ni–Ni strain and tensile Y–O distortion, creating a strained Ni–O–Y interface that balances CH4 oxidation and CO2 reduction during dry reforming of CH4. The resulting catalyst sustains near-equilibrium CH4 and CO2 conversion for over 1200 h without coke accumulation or detectable active-site collapse and remains stable under natural-gas reforming conditions. Theory and in situ spectroscopy reveal that nuclearity-regulated interfacial strain redirects carbon-containing intermediates away from deep dehydrogenation and toward continuous oxidation, thereby establishing a dynamic carbon balance. These findings position oligoatomic catalysts within the structural regime situated between single-/dual-atom and nanoparticle catalysts and highlight ensemble nuclearity as a tunable parameter for modulating interfacial strain in demanding catalytic reactions.

articles.title: Dynamic Zn-Based Ensembles Govern CO2 Hydrogenation to Methanol on Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 Catalyst
articles.abstract: The active site of the classical Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 (CZA) catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation remains elusive as its surface structures undergo dynamic change under reaction conditions. Here, we combine neural network interatomic potential molecular dynamics simulations and grand-canonical density functional theory calculations to investigate the evolution of the representative CuZn alloy and inverse ZnO/Cu surface phases, and we consistently observe drastic restructuring under hydrogenation conditions, forming fragmented Zn-based ensembles at Cu support. Among the pathways examined, CO2 hydrogenation on these ensembles preferentially proceeds through the HCOO pathway, with different ensemble compositions being thermodynamically favored for the intermediates formed at different reaction stages. Importantly, these Zn-based ensembles are highly dynamic on Cu, allowing the inert HCOO within the ensembles to access highly active Cu/Zn interfacial sites, thereby making its hydrogenation kinetically accessible. The formation of ensembles and their dynamic behavior may be related to a suitable Cu–Zn interaction, which stabilizes Zn on Cu while preserving its mobility. Overall, these findings identify dynamic Zn-based ensembles as potential operando active sites in the Cu–Zn component of CZA and show that catalyst restructuring not only changes surface morphology but also couples directly to the reaction mechanism.

articles.title: Unraveling Regio- and Stereoselectivity in Cyclopropane Fatty Acid Synthase (CFAS) Enzymes across Native and Non-native Lipid Substrates
articles.abstract: Cyclopropane fatty acid synthase (CFAS) enzymes catalyze the formation of cyclopropane rings within bacterial membrane lipids, a transformation implicated in membrane homeostasis, stress adaptation, and antimicrobial resistance. Despite decades of biochemical investigation, the molecular determinants governing CFAS regioselectivity, stereoselectivity, chain specificity, and substrate scope remain poorly understood. Here, we systematically investigate how enzyme orthology, lipid structure, and membrane environment shape CFAS selectivity. Comparative analysis of CFAS orthologues from Escherichia coli, Lactobacillus acidophilus, and Streptococcus thermophilus reveals that the extent of mono- versus di-cyclopropanation, regioselectivity, and stereochemical outcome are not conserved properties but diverge substantially across the enzyme family. A simple two-carbon variation in phospholipid acyl chain length (C16 versus C18) reverses the absolute configuration of the cyclopropane product, revealing an unrecognized structural determinant of stereochemical outcome. Furthermore, we demonstrate that CFAS catalysis extends beyond native phospholipids to synthetic pseudo-phospholipids bearing non-phosphate anionic headgroups and to fatty acids embedded within lipid vesicles, substantially expanding the substrate scope of this enzyme family. Together, these findings provide insight into the molecular basis of CFAS selectivity, advance the understanding of bacterial lipid cyclopropanation, and broaden the synthetic potential of these enzymes for the stereoselective preparation of non-natural cyclopropyl lipids.

articles.title: Chiral Two-Dimensional Perovskite Single Crystals Enable Flexible Piezoelectric Nanogenerators for High-Sensitivity Ultrasound Detection
articles.abstract: Hybrid perovskites are emerging as promising piezoelectric materials, yet the use of high-quality single crystals in flexible ultrasound sensing remains largely unexplored. Here, we report intrinsically noncentrosymmetric chiral two-dimensional perovskite single crystals, (S/R-NEA)2PbBr4, that exhibit strong piezoelectricity arising from chirality-induced symmetry breaking and enhanced lattice polarizability. By integrating these crystals into a polymer matrix, we realize flexible piezoelectric nanogenerators delivering high output (∼8 V) under ultrasonic excitation. The devices enable reliable detection and clear resolution of 50 kHz ultrasound signals, along with excellent mechanical durability and environmental stability. This work establishes a single-crystal strategy for flexible piezoelectric devices and highlights chiral 2D perovskites as a compelling platform for high-sensitivity ultrasound detection and energy harvesting.

articles.title: Gas Retention in Porous Cathodes Governs Bicarbonate Electrolysis Performance
articles.abstract: Bicarbonate electrolysis offers a direct route for converting captured CO2 into high-value chemicals without energy-intensive CO2 regeneration and compression. However, multiphase transport within liquid-fed porous cathodes remains poorly understood. We found carbon paper and carbon cloth yielded drastically different performance, and further analysis revealed gas retention, i.e., localized and temporary entrapment of internally generated gas within the pore network, as an important transport limitation. Flow pulse and recovery experiments under galvanostatic operations showed largely reversible performance losses, while operando X-ray imaging directly visualized gas retention. Gas retention intensifies with denser electrodes, lower catholyte flow rates, and higher current densities. Guided by these observations, an interdigitated flow field was employed to enhance through-plane convection and gas removal, increasing the maximum formate partial current density to 304 mA cm–2 and enabling 120 h of stable operation. These findings establish gas management as a critical design criterion for bicarbonate electrolyzers.

articles.title: Hierarchical toughening of Fe-Al bimetallic heterostructures through coupled intermetallic lattice chemistry, grain-boundary state and interfacial architecture
Engineering Energy‐Storage Interfaces With Atomic and Molecular Layer Deposition: From Surface Chemistry to Process Design
articles.abstract: The performance and lifetime of energy‐storage devices are determined at the interfaces between electrodes, electrolytes, and separators, where ion and charge transfer, parasitic reactions, and mechanical degradation originate within nanometers of the surface. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) and molecular layer deposition (MLD) enable precise engineering of these interfaces through self‐limiting surface reactions that produce conformal coatings with controlled thickness and composition, even on porous electrodes. Although ALD surface chemistry is well established on ideal oxide surfaces, energy‐storage materials present chemically and structurally complex surfaces, on which reaction mechanisms, growth per cycle, and coating function can differ. This Review develops a chemistry–process–structure–function framework that connects surface chemistry, precursor reaction pathways, and nucleation behavior with film structure, ionic transport, charge‐transfer kinetics, redox stability, and mechanical response. We examine growth on oxide, sulfide, metal, polymer, and carbon substrates and relate the films to their functions at cathodes, anodes, solid electrolytes, and separators in Li‐based and beyond‐Li batteries. We further assess process scalability in terms of precursor utilization, throughput, and energy consumption, and discuss in situ monitoring, post‐deposition characterization, and full‐cell test conditions needed to validate coating performance. These relationships are summarized as six design rules presented as a decision flow.

articles.title: Fast Dynamic Re‐Equilibration of Chloroaluminate Speciation Enables a Stable Electrode‐Electrolyte Interface in Aluminum Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: The sluggish dynamic equilibration of ions in ionic liquid electrolytes, particularly under high viscosity conditions, originates from strong interionic interactions and inefficient utilization of charge carrier species. Here, we present a strategic electrolyte design that reconfigures the interionic interaction network and accelerates the dynamic equilibration of charge carriers in AlCl3/EMIC ionic liquid electrolyte. By incorporating an optimized moderator with low polarity and small molecular size, the dynamic redistribution and re-equilibration of charge carriers during cycling are significantly accelerated, while the continuous depletion of effective charge carriers is suppressed. Guided by this principle, the dichloroethane-enabled electrolyte exhibits rapid chloroaluminate equilibration and improved electrode-electrolyte stability. In situ Raman spectroscopy confirms that the moderator promotes reversible AlCl4 − /Al2Cl7 − conversion. As a result, the reorganized AlCl3/EMIC electrolyte suppresses dendrite growth and achieves unprecedented Al anode stability in symmetric cells. Matched with flake graphite cathodes, the full battery capacity increased by 120.7% from 92 to 203 mAh g−1 at 200 mA g−1 after 7000 cycles. This work establishes a dynamic speciation regulation principle for designing ionic liquid electrolytes with fast ion equilibration and provides a pathway toward long-life aluminum-ion batteries.

articles.title: Ionomer‐Free Iridium Anodes With Low Loading for Zero‐Gap Electrolyzers via Direct Atomic Layer Deposition
articles.abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is among the most promising techniques to provide hydrogen as both energy carrier and feedstock for the chemical industry, due to its compatibility with intermittent renewable electricity sources. However, a major bottleneck in scaling up PEMWE is the limited supply of the anode catalyst Ir. This work shows a novel approach to tailoring ionomer‐free catalyst layers based on custom‐made microporous substrates and two different atomic layer deposition (ALD) processes, both using Ir(EtCp)(CHD) precursor. Thermal ALD using O3${\rm O}_3$ as counter‐reactant yields mostly metallic Ir/IrOx${\rm IrO}_x$ and an electrode Ir loading of 0.21 mg·cm−2${\rm mg}\cdot{\rm cm}^{-2}$. The PEMWE cell‐level performance is comparable to a commercial catalyst‐coated membrane anode despite 7×$7\times$ lower loading, and is maintained over an accelerated durability test equivalent to 600 h of intermittent operation. Moreover, using a low‐loading ALD‐made cathode, the total platinum group metal loading is only 0.24 mg·cm−2${\rm mg}\cdot{\rm cm}^{-2}$. Plasma‐enhanced ALD reduces the Ir loading to 0.04 mg·cm−2${\rm mg}\cdot{\rm cm}^{-2}$ by tailoring the catalyst distribution, however, yields lower‐activity IrO2${\rm IrO}_2$. Finally, direct ALD catalyst deposition needs no ionomer‐bearing ink. The anodes are therefore compatible with various membrane materials, as demonstrated in a CO2${\rm CO}_2$ electrolysis experiment with an anion exchange membrane.

articles.title: Non‐Stoichiometric Molybdenum Oxides Enable Phase‐Stable Proton Storage
articles.abstract: Aqueous proton batteries are promising alternatives to lithium‐ion batteries owing to their intrinsic safety, low cost, and fast proton transport. However, the small size, high charge density, and strong protonating ability of H+ often perturb host frameworks during repeated insertion/extraction, causing phase transformations, lattice strain, and rapid capacity decay. Herein, we synthesis we report a non‐stoichiometric tunnel‐structured molybdenum oxide, Mo5O14, as a highly reversible proton‐storage electrode. The interconnected tunnel framework enables direct and reversible H3O+ intercalation without phase transition, pronounced structural distortion, or significant volume variation, thereby ensuring excellent structural stability and rapid ion transport. As a result, Mo5O14 delivers a high capacity of 271 mAh g−1 at 1.5 A g−1 (∼5C) and retains 142.2 mAh g−1 even at 300 A g−1 (∼1000C) and sustains stable operation for over 310 000 cycles. When paired with a VHCF cathode, the full cell achieves 73.3 Wh kg−1 and maximum power density of 43.4 kW kg−1, and over 60 000 stable cycles. Furthermore, a flexible interdigital proton micro‐cell array demonstrates rapid‐charge capability, powering a red light‐emitting diode for over 5 min after only 10 s of high‐rate charging.

articles.title: Rethinking Battery Safety: Unveiling Aluminum Propellant‐Like Reactions During Thermal Runaway and Developing Protective Solutions
articles.abstract: Battery safety remains a critical challenge in the large‐scale deployment of lithium‐ion batteries. While thermal runaway is typically attributed to exothermic reactions involving electrode materials and electrolytes, the contribution of current collectors has been largely overlooked. Here, we demonstrate that the conventionally presumed inert aluminum (Al) current collector engages in intense exothermic reactions with various cathode materials at temperatures exceeding 600°C. This reactivity is catalyzed by fluorides, which disrupt the Al passivation layer, resembling combustion mechanisms observed in Al‐based rocket propellants. The specific heat release from Al oxidation (−22 to −33 kJ g−1) is nearly twice that of the electrolyte (−12 to −16 kJ g−1). Considering that the Al mass is approximately half that of the electrolyte, its theoretical thermal contribution during thermal runaway is comparable to that of the electrolyte. Employing fluorine‐free electrolytes can suppress the propellant‐like reaction. Together with flame‐retardant strategies, the total heat release during thermal runaway can be further reduced, with the measured peak temperatures around pouch cells being effectively suppressed below 400°C. This work uncovers a pervasive yet previously underappreciated high‐energy reaction in batteries and offers new design strategies for improving thermal safety.

articles.title: Spatial‐Decoupled Synergy between Asymmetric Ni‐N3 Sites and Ni Nanoparticles Extending the Air‐Tolerant Poisoning Limit of MgH2 Hydrogen Storage
articles.abstract: Solid‐state MgH2 holds immense promise for high‐capacity hydrogen storage, yet its practical deployment is severely hindered by extreme atmospheric susceptibility and an elusive activated dehydrogenation mechanism. Herein, we report a armor like architectural design featuring asymmetric Ni‐N3 sites and nanoparticles (NPs) co‐decorated within a flexible nitrogen‐doped graphene (NG). Driven by the electronic synergy between the Ni‐N3 sites and the highly active Ni NPs, the NG achieves robust encapsulation of MgH2, providing a rigid size‐exclusion barrier against ambient O2/H2O infiltration. Concurrently, strong electronic interactions between MgH2 and Ni species optimize the MgH2 electronic structure, which further reduces its reactivity toward O2/H2O, enabling the MgH2 to preserve its full capacity even after a 28‐day cumulative air exposure. Furthermore, the encapsulated Ni NPs undergo an in situ reaction to form Mg2Ni nanorivets, which serve as high‐flux interfacial hydrogen pumps, while creating a vital spatial buffer during dynamic cycling, thereby achieving 95% capacity retention over 360 cycles at 300°C. Density functional theory calculations confirm that the electronic hybridization induced by the asymmetric Ni‐N3 sites, Ni NPs, and Mg2Ni nanorivets destabilizes Mg‐H bonds. This multi‐scale engineering of environmental isolation, electronic modulation, and structural riveting presents a robust blueprint for air‐tolerant, fast‐kinetics solid‐state hydrogen storage.

articles.title: Stress‐Regulated Li Plating in Hybrid Ag–Carbon/Carbon Nanofiber Anodes for Durable All‐Solid‐State Batteries
articles.abstract: All‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) with Li‐metal or Li‐metal‐free anodes enable high energy density, yet high‐loading cathodes induce severe mechanical instability, leading to rapid cell failure. Herein, we identify stress accumulation caused by repetitive Li plating/stripping as a critical degradation origin in ASSBs and propose a mechanically adaptive Ag–carbon/carbon nanofiber (CNF) hybrid anode to address this challenge. Operando pressure analysis and mechanical modeling reveal that increasing cathode areal capacity substantially amplifies pressure fluctuations and dynamic mechanical instability, leading to interfacial disruption and short‐circuiting. To mitigate this behavior, the Ag–C interlayer and porous CNF framework were independently customized to provide complementary electrochemical regulation and mechanical buffering functions. The Ag–C layer promotes uniform Li nucleation through Ag–Li alloy‐assisted interfacial regulation, while the porous CNF host accommodates volumetric changes and dissipates stress. Phase‐field modeling and microstructural analyses reveal sequential Ag–Li alloying within the Ag–C interlayer, CNF lithiation and pore filling, and controlled interfacial Li deposition, thereby spatially redistributing volumetric expansion. Consequently, the Ag–C/CNF architecture significantly reduces pressure fluctuation and enables stable cycling over 250 cycles under high‐loading conditions (∼5 mAh cm−2). Furthermore, stable pouch‐cell operation is demonstrated under practical stack pressures of 1 and 2 MPa, highlighting a viable strategy for mechanically robust high‐energy‐density ASSBs.

articles.title: Super‐Toughness Self‐Healing Composite Solid Electrolyte With Structured Interfacial Reconstruction Enabling Fast Ion Transport and Stable Interface for High‐Performance Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Lithium–metal batteries are widely regarded as a key direction for next-generation energy storage systems due to high energy density. However, LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2||Li battery systems face severe challenges in practical application, including lithium dendrite growth, interfacial side reactions and structural degradation of high-nickel cathodes. Here, we proposed a versatile modification strategy combining in-situ interfacial transformation with polymer phase regulation to fabricate self-healing solid polymer electrolyte with fast ion transport and stable interface. This strategy not only constructs fast ion channels and suppresses hydrofluoric acid production by in-situ converting Li2CO3 on the Li6.4La3Zr1.4Ta0.6O12 surface into Li2PO3F interfacial layer, but also induces the transition of PVDF from α-phase to high polarity β-phase using ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid to promote lithium salt dissolution and reduce Li+ migration resistance. The as-prepared electrolyte exhibits extended electrochemical voltage windows (5.13 V), high room-temperature ionic conductivity (1.694 mS cm− 1), excellent thermal stability (200°C), high elongation at break (422.6%), and superior cycling stability (89.4% retention after 500 cycles at 1 C). A non-destructive monitoring method based on dp/|dQ| and dT/|dQ| differential signals has been developed to track electrochemical-mechanical-thermal responses during battery operation. This work provides an effective strategy for designing solid polymer electrolytes with high ionic conductivity and interfacial stability.

articles.title: Synergistic Anion Regulation Inducing Fluoride‐Rich SEI and Defect‐Rich MnO2 for Stable Dual Electrode‐Free Zn‐MnO2 Batteries
articles.abstract: Dual electrode‐free (DEF) Zn─MnO2 batteries based on dissolution‐deposition chemistry are promising candidates for large‐scale energy storage due to their lightweight architecture and high theoretical capacity (616 mAh g−1). However, poor interfacial reversibility and the accumulation of “dead manganese” significantly limit their lifespan. Here, we demonstrate a stable DEF battery enabled by an anion‐regulation strategy using a hybrid electrolyte (E‐OA) comprising trifluoromethanesulfonate (OTf−) and acetate (Ac−) ions. At the anode, OTf− facilitates the formation of a fluoride‐rich solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI), effectively suppressing dendrite growth and the hydrogen evolution reaction. At the cathode, the synergistic anionic environment elevates the MnO2 nucleation overpotential, shifting the electrocrystallization pathway to an instantaneous nucleation mode. The kinetically driven growth process traps abundant structural defects, identified as proton‐compensated manganese vacancies (Ruetschi defects). These vacancies lower the thermodynamic energy barrier for Mn─O bond cleavage, thereby ensuring highly reversible dissolution. Consequently, the E‐OA‐based DEF battery achieves exceptional stability for over 7500 cycles at 0.5 mAh cm−2 and sustains 600 cycles at 2 mAh cm−2 (10 mA cm−2), demonstrating superior rate capability and versatility in both flow and gel battery configurations. This work provides a transformative strategy for high‐energy aqueous batteries via tailored anion chemistry and kinetics‐driven defect engineering.

articles.title: Synergistic Fluoride and Polymer‑Regulated Interfacial Engineering of NiFe‑LDH Anodes for Ampere‑Scale Natural Seawater Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Alkaline seawater electrolysis is a promising route for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its practical implementation is severely constrained by chloride‐induced corrosion and limited anode durability during the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Here, we develop synergistic fluoride‐management, defect‐engineering, and polymer‐interfacial‐protection strategy for NiFe‐LDH anodes, enabling kilo‐hour‐scale operation at ampere‐level current densities in natural seawater. A custom‐designed microwave‐assisted method produces fluoride‐protected NiFe layered double hydroxide on nickel foam (F‑NiFe‑LDHMW/NF). The electrode is subsequently tailored through controlled Zn depletion to generate an evolving cation‐deficient environment, followed by electropolymerization of calmagite to construct a multifunctional poly(calmagite) (poly(CM)) interfacial layer. The optimized F‑NiFeZnvac‑LDHMW@CM/NF anode delivered exceptional stable operation for 1000 h in simulated seawater and 1650 h in natural seawater at a commercial‐scale current density of 1000 mA cm−2. Mechanistic analyses combining stage‐resolved characterization, electrolyte analysis, and DFT reveal complementary intrinsic and extrinsic stabilization mechanisms: F− regulation and the evolving cation‐defect environment modify the structural and electronic state of NiFe‐LDH, while poly(CM) suppresses Cl− access and adsorption and delays interfacial corrosion. During prolonged electrolysis, F− undergoes dynamic redistribution and gradual leaching, accompanied by controlled catalyst reconstruction rather than catastrophic structural degradation. This multilevel stabilization strategy can be a step forward toward practical seawater electrolysis.

articles.title: Synergistically Modulating Electronic Structure and Interfacial Wettability of MnF2/NF−CNF Toward Enhanced Oxygen Reduction in Zinc−Air Batteries
articles.abstract: Modulating the electronic structure and interfacial wettability of cathode catalysts is crucial for enhancing intrinsic activity and broadening triple‐phase interfaces for oxygen reduction reactions (ORR) in zinc−air batteries (ZABs), yet achieving their synergistic regulation faces a big challenge. Herein, an N/F source modulation strategy is proposed to synthesize porous carbon nanofibers anchored with MnF2 nanocrystals and N/F heteroatoms (MnF2/NF−CNF). The unique interconnected fibrous and hierarchical porous architecture, together with tailored MnF2 embedding and N/F doping, achieves an optimal balance between activity and wettability regulation. Excellent ORR performance with a high half‐wave potential of 0.87 V vs. RHE and limiting current density of 6.34 mA cm−2 is achieved, outperforming Pt/C and most previously reported Mn‐based/heteroatom‐doped systems. Theoretical and experimental analyses reveal surface N dopants as active sites, with MnF2 modulating p‐orbital configuration, refining ORR pathways. Meanwhile, surface F dopants, in synergy with the porous architecture, regulate wettability, equilibrate electrolyte/oxygen transport, and substantially extend triple‐phase reaction interfaces. The assembled ZAB delivers an exceptional peak power density of 181.5 mW cm−2 with high specific capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability. This work deciphers the regulatory mechanism balancing catalytic activity and interfacial wettability, proving a versatile strategy for developing advanced ORR electrocatalysts in ZABs.

articles.title: Unlocking Wide‐Temperature Battery States via Noninvasive Nonlinear Ultrasound
articles.abstract: Lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) are central to modern energy storage, yet evaluating their internal states under extreme thermal fluctuations remains a critical challenge. Here we present a non‐destructive evaluation framework that leverages the quasi‐static component (QSC) of nonlinear ultrasonic guided waves. By integrating an operando electro‐acoustic‐thermal platform, we isolate temperature‐induced artefacts from intrinsic acoustic signals. This statistical compensation enables the precise, simultaneous prediction of state of charge (SOC) and state of charge relative to nominal capacity (SOCN) across a wide temperature span (−10°C to 40°C). Furthermore, in situ multidimensional characterization maps these ultrasonic signatures to temperature‐dependent mechanics and irreversible capacity fade mechanisms. Ultimately, this unified framework provides a scalable, quantitative diagnostic tool for reliable energy systems operating under extreme environments.

articles.title: ZrO2 Clusters Enabling Room‐Temperature Hydrogen Absorption and Low‐Temperature Desorption of Commercial Mg Powder for Reversible Hydrogen Storage
articles.abstract: Magnesium‐based hydrogen storage materials exhibit great application potential, but high operating temperature and slow kinetics hinder their large‐scale utilization. Here, the amorphous‐carbon‐stabilized Mg particles decorated with sub‐2 nm ZrO2 nanoclusters are reported, which were in situ fabricated via ball milling of commercial Mg powder, acetone (ACE), and zirconium acetylacetonate (Zr(acac)4). The optimized Mg‐ACE‐1 wt.% Zr composite achieves rapid hydrogen absorption of 4.25 wt.% at 30°C within 60 min and exhibits high cycling stability with nearly no H2 capacity fading after 40 cycles at 300°C under 30 bar H2. Notably, the Mg‐ACE‐1 wt.% Zr sample enables reversible hydrogenation at room temperature and dehydrogenation at high temperature, achieving better energy efficiency than conventional thermally driven MgH2 and showing promise for coupling with renewable hydrogen production. Interfacial characterizations and DFT calculations confirm that the in situ formed ZrO2/Mg interface accelerates H2 adsorption, dissociation, and diffusion.

articles.title: Scope
articles.abstract: Scope taking is one of the most characteristic, distinctive, and ubiquitous phenomena in natural language. When an expression takes scope, it combines with surrounding material as its semantic argument. For instance, in Amy gave everyone a book , the semantic argument of everyone is an abstraction over the entire rest of the sentence, namely, λ x . Amy gave x a book , the property an individual has if Amy gave that individual a book. This ability to operate on surrounding context dramatically enriches (and complicates) the ways that meanings can be expressed. Although there are many formal theories of scope taking, Quantifier Raising—often thought of as a covert (silent) version of overt syntactic movement—is by far the dominant approach. There are many constraints on the availability of scope taking that depend on the identity of the scope taker as well as on its surrounding context.

articles.title: Voice Conversion, Voice Morphing, and Speech Style Modification
articles.abstract: A speech sample can be morphed from one voice to another by computing a sufficiently detailed time-frequency parameterization of the signal, optionally decomposing it into speaker-dependent and speaker-independent signal components, editing the parameterization or signal components, and then generating a speech signal based on the edited parameterization. Fine-grained control of time-frequency parameters has found applications in the scientific study of speech perception and in artistic applications such as voiceover and music. Coarse-grained control of speaker identity, emotion, and second-language accent have been applied to various tasks, including the training of speech recognizers and speaker anonymization.

articles.title: What Is Singular They and How Do We Use It? The Psycholinguistics of Singular They
articles.abstract: Singular they is valuable to psycholinguistic research because it has a long-standing usage in English that is currently undergoing changes, both in how often it is used and in what conditions. As a result, singular they is an informative testing ground for the cognitive mechanisms behind language change, which include both top-down intentional change and implicit learning and adaptation. Singular they is also an unusually socially salient function word that provides opportunities to examine how automatic psycholinguistic processes intersect with sociolinguistic issues like gender-fair language, linguistic prescriptivism, and the emerging use of they as a personal pronoun. Developments in the use of singular they are linked to broader shifts in concepts of gender. We suggest that there are two main varieties of singular they that currently differ in acceptability and processing characteristics. Psycholinguistic research shows that singular they is viewed as more acceptable and used more easily within a supportive context that helps to make the pronoun pragmatically appropriate.

articles.title: Viscosity and Phase State of Biomass-Burning Organic Aerosol
articles.abstract: Biomass-burning organic aerosol (BBOA) is a major component of atmospheric particulate matter and is expected to become increasingly important as wildfire activity increases. The viscosity and phase state of BBOA influence its climate and health impacts. This review summarizes current understanding of the viscosity and phase state of BBOA. Measurements show that the viscosity of unaged primary BBOA spans more than ten orders of magnitude, from liquid-like particles to glassy solids, depending on fuel type, combustion conditions, burn stage, and relative humidity. Aging by evaporation, OH oxidation, UV irradiation, and secondary aerosol formation can increase viscosity by several orders of magnitude. Field measurements indicate that atmospheric BBOA is often more viscous than unaged laboratory BBOA. Laboratory measurements further suggest that aged BBOA commonly exists in highly viscous or glassy states in the free troposphere and may exhibit mixing times exceeding one hour. We also highlight future research directions.

articles.title: Structure–performance relationships in CO 2 -assisted propane dehydrogenation over Mo–V-based catalysts
articles.abstract: CO 2 shifts the redox balance of Mo–V catalysts: mixed oxides undergo reduction and deactivate, whereas supported VO x /MoO 3 shows greater redox stability and less coke. Stability depends on the reduction-reoxidation balance.

articles.title: γ-Al 2 O 3 -stabilized molybdenum oxide as Lewis acid for epimerization of aldomonosaccharides
articles.abstract: As an efficient catalyst for the C-2 epimerization of aldoses, molybdenum oxide is hindered by surface instability, which adversely affect catalytic kinetics and product selectivity. In this work, a γ-Al2O3-supported...

articles.title: Leveraging human pangenome for improved somatic variant detection
articles.abstract: Fu et al. show that the human pangenome improves somatic-variant calling accuracy over GRCh38 and CHM13 and can infer donor-specific assemblies that reduce germline contamination and reveal functionally relevant somatic variants missed by GRCh38 in cancer, thereby offering a scalable alternative to costly de novo assemblies.

articles.title: Microbial metabolism of methotrexate produces a STAT3 signaling molecule that alleviates gut inflammation
articles.abstract: Cho et al. show that gut microbial metabolism of methotrexate generates DAMPA. DAMPA promotes mitochondrial function and protects against intestinal inflammation, revealing how microbial drug metabolism can generate beneficial signals that influence host physiology.

articles.title: A bivalent chromatin reader-WOX5 module maintains root stem cell niche in Arabidopsis
articles.abstract: Root stem cell niche maintenance requires precise control of quiescent center (QC) and columella stem cell (CSC) activity, yet how chromatin regulators interface with key transcription factors remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the bivalent chromatin reader EARLY BOLTING IN SHORT DAYS (EBS) as an essential regulator of root stem cell maintenance in Arabidopsis. A strong ebs-1 mutant shows CSC differentiation and QC activation, and EBS function requires its histone mark-recognizing BAH and PHD domains and a C-terminal SUMO-interacting motif. EBS physically interacts with the QC master regulator WUSCHEL-RELATED HOMEOBOX 5 (WOX5) and, together with WOX5, activates WOX5 transcription by promoting EBS enrichment at the WOX5 promoter. Consistently, wox5-1 is epistatic to ebs-1, and WOX5 overexpression rescues the ebs-1 stem cell defects. Together, this work uncovers a chromatin-based positive autoregulatory loop that integrates histone-state recognition and transcriptional feedback, providing a framework for epigenetic control of stem cell fate in plants.

articles.title: A shared multi-feature population code for sensory reliability across mouse visual cortex
articles.abstract: Successful behavior depends on evaluating both what is present in the environment and how reliable that information is. Yet how neural populations represent reliability, and whether this representation is shared across cortical areas, remains unknown. Using two-photon calcium imaging of over 150,000 neurons in mouse visual cortices during presentations of coherent motion stimuli, we find that sensory reliability is encoded through coordinated changes in response amplitude, selectivity, and signal-to-noise ratio. These coherence-dependent response patterns are not fully accounted for by stimulus-based normalization models; rather, they track the distribution of motion energy across directions, while remaining relatively invariant to total motion energy. This multi-feature code is expressed at the single-neuron and population levels and is consistent across visual areas, suggesting a shared encoding scheme rather than area-specific computations. Together, these findings support a common population code for stimulus reliability across visual cortices.

articles.title: ApoE-dependent lipid handling by median eminence microglia supports myelin remodeling and metabolic function
articles.abstract: Microglia regulate hypothalamic control of systemic metabolism, but the mechanisms underlying their contribution remain unclear. Here, we identify apolipoprotein E (ApoE)-associated microglial transcriptional states enriched in the median eminence (ME), a brain region involved in sensing peripheral cues and metabolic regulation. These transcriptional states are characterized by programs related to lipid handling, interferon-associated responses, and cellular stress. Consumption of a Western diet (WD) increased microglial lipid accumulation and altered myelin remodeling within the ME, while expression of the human APOE4 isoform exacerbated these changes. Deletion of Apoe altered microglial responses to nutritional stress, supporting a role for ApoE in microglial lipid handling. Finally, activation of liver X receptor using synthetic high-density lipoprotein (sHDL) nanoparticles enhanced microglial lipid-handling programs, improved hypothalamic leptin responsiveness, reduced food intake, and limited weight gain in WD-fed mice. Together, these findings identify ApoE-dependent lipid handling as a key component of adaptive microglial responses to metabolic stress.

articles.title: Exercise trains the liver to save the heart
articles.abstract: Wang and colleagues1 demonstrate that exercise triggers the liver to release clusterin into the bloodstream, improving cardiac remodeling and myocyte proliferation post-myocardial infarction. Their findings add another mechanistic facet to the complexity and controversial role of clusterin in cardiac injury.

articles.title: IDO1 methylation by EZH2 confers resistance to its targeted therapy in colorectal cancer through tryptophan-kynurenine metabolic rewiring
articles.abstract: Deciphering cancer metabolic reprogramming mechanisms can identify new targets to potentiate EZH2 inhibitor efficacy. Using an in vivo genome-wide CRISPR loss-of-function screen in a CRC mouse model, we pinpointed IDO1 as a key mediator of EZH2 inhibitor resistance. EZH2 blockade remodeled CRC cell metabolism by upregulating IDO1 protein and hyperactivating the tryptophan-kynurenine pathway. Both genetic and pharmacological inhibition of IDO1 suppressed tumor growth and rescued EZH2 inhibitor resistance in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, EZH2 directly binds and methylates IDO1. Methylation of IDO1 facilitates IDO1 ubiquitination and subsequent degradation. Accordingly, EZH2 inhibition stabilizes IDO1, augments tryptophan-kynurenine metabolic flux, and ultimately confers therapeutic resistance. In summary, our study identifies IDO1 as a non-histone substrate of EZH2 methyltransferase activity and validates that disrupting IDO1-mediated tryptophan metabolism is a viable strategy to overcome EZH2 targeted therapy resistance in cancers.

articles.title: Single-cell and spatial characterization of the human pancreas in cystic fibrosis
articles.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) causes severely damaged pancreatic morphology and cystic fibrosis-related diabetes (CFRD), but the cellular drivers of CFRD in the pancreas are not understood. Here, we perform single-cell and spatial profiling of 2.04 M cells from 23 non-disease or CF pancreas donors. A high-mucin ductal sub-type had relatively preserved abundance and genomic profiles but altered localization in CF. Changes in inflammatory and fibrotic pathways were driven by crosstalk between immune and pro-fibrotic cells in specific niches. Beta cells had extensive changes in CF, including increased stress responses and evidence for compensatory secretion, that were distinct from those in type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Islets localized near large adipose tissue and collagen in CF had reduced beta cells linked to signaling from adipocytes, macrophages, stellate cells, and high-mucin ductal cells. Overall, our results highlight pancreatic microenvironments of beta cell dysfunction in CF and offer in-roads to preserving beta cells in CFRD.

articles.title: Theta-based organization of information in the frontal cortex
articles.abstract: Theta (4-10 Hz) oscillations seem to coordinate activity across long-range distances. It is less clear how theta coordinates activity more locally within frontal subareas. We examined activity in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC), ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (vlPFC), and frontal eye fields (FEFs) as non-human primates categorized dot patterns. We characterized how theta coordinates activity within frontal cortex. First, theta phase selectively couples to behaviorally relevant information in spiking. Second, theta influences move in a posterior direction during choices (i.e., dlPFC/vlPFC to FEF) and after correct outcomes (i.e., dlPFC to FEF), but not after errors. Instead, anterior-direction (i.e., FEF to vlPFC) theta influences are stronger after errors. Third, theta participates in behaviorally associated nested cross-frequency interactions. Theta couples to beta (15-30 Hz) oscillations during choices and after errors, whereas beta couples to gamma (40-90 Hz) oscillations after correct outcomes. Our results position theta as a critical mechanism that flexibly and dynamically coordinates activity in frontal cortex.

articles.title: A peripheral blood mononuclear cell DNA methylation-based risk stratification tool for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
articles.abstract: There is an urgent need for minimally invasive and accurate tools to prioritize individuals for timely endoscopic evaluation of ESCC. Here, Li et al. developed ESCCseeker, integrating PBMC DNA methylation, demographics, and serum markers, which could reduce unnecessary endoscopies by 83% in 1,026 prospective participants.

articles.title: Antigen scaffolds drive preferential expansion of functional genetically engineered CAR and TCR T cells
articles.abstract: Manufacturing T cell therapies with CRISPR-Cas9 yields a low frequency of terminally differentiated knockin T cells. Johansen, Ramanathan et al. have developed artificial antigen scaffolds presenting cognate antigens, IL2, and IL21 that drive expansion of CRISPR- and lentivirally engineered CAR or TCR T cells with a proliferative and highly cytotoxic profile.

articles.title: Broad vaccine protection against globally diverse influenza A/H5Nx viruses
articles.abstract: Del Rosario et al. employ digitally immune-optimized synthetic vaccine technology to engineer a multi-antigen mRNA vaccine that confers broad immunogenicity and protection against globally distinct and evolving H5Nx influenza viruses. This demonstrates that computationally designed multivalent antigens can be harnessed as preparedness tools against contemporary and future H5Nx diversity.

articles.title: Clinical stewardship for medical AI translation: A systematic review of technological, human, and organizational barriers
articles.abstract: Wang et al. review contemporary medical AI studies to identify evidence gaps that can obstruct clinical translation. Their “clinical stewardship” framework assigns AI oversight across people, institutions, and technical systems, rather than shifting routine work back to clinicians.

articles.title: Immunogen-sponge hydrogel reverses TIM-3-mediated dendritic cell dysfunction in alveolar echinococcosis
articles.abstract: Shi et al. identify TIM-3-associated dendritic cell dysfunction as a barrier to protective immunity in alveolar echinococcosis. Their immunogen-sponge hydrogel shields dendritic cells from parasite-derived immunosuppressive signals while providing sustained antigen stimulation, restoring dendritic cell function, and promoting protective immunity in prophylactic and therapeutic settings.

articles.title: Lipid homeostasis and cellular metabolism in neurodegenerative diseases: A maturing framework to guide therapeutic development
articles.abstract: Isacson et al. describe a paradigm shift in understanding Alzheimer’s disease, Lewy body dementia, and Parkinson’s disease, moving beyond proteinopathy-centered observations toward primary lipid and metabolic disturbances. The perspective explores how deeper insights into cell biology and brain health may enable innovative therapeutic interventions against neurodegeneration.
