Durable and reversible epigenetic programming of human hematopoietic stem cells as a platform for modulation of platelet function
articles.abstract: Sankaran and colleagues establish DNA methylation-based epigenome editing in human hematopoietic stem cells and their progeny. Targeting ITGB3, they show that silencing persists through self-renewal and megakaryocytic differentiation to alter platelet function and can be reversed through targeted demethylation. Extension to additional platelet genes demonstrates broad applicability.

articles.title: Liquid metal biomimetics: a chemical perspective
articles.abstract: A chemistry-centered framework for Ga-based liquid metal biomimetics, linking multiscale material design and interfacial reactions to matter simulation, energy conversion, information processing and cross-habitat adaptation.

articles.title: Regulating glycerol electrooxidation pathways via catalytic environments
articles.abstract: A step-resolved framework explains how catalytic environments regulate adsorption, dehydrogenation, chemical conversion, C–C cleavage and desorption to shape glycerol electrooxidation selectivity, activity and stability.

articles.title: Cathode-Induced Stress Can Suppress Dendritic Failure in Thin Solid Electrolyte Separators
articles.abstract: Solid-state batteries pairing lithium metal anodes with inorganic solid electrolytes promise a step change in energy density, but during charging at practical rates lithium dendrites penetrate the solid electrolyte, short-circuiting the cell. Our current understanding of dendrite propagation derives largely from symmetric Li−Li cells with millimetre-thick electrolyte pellets, whereas practical cells will employ solid electrolyte separators less than 100 μm in thickness. In this work, we use in situ synchrotron X-ray computed tomography to show that dendrites in a thin Li6PS5Cl separator, which generally propagate from the lithium anode to the cathode, can be made to propagate laterally by the cathode. Volume contraction of the NMC cathode during charge places the thin separator under lateral compressive stress, deflecting dendritic cracks to propagate laterally (parallel to the electrodes) rather than transversely (across the separator). The result is that the cell resists short circuit even after passing 3 mA h cm−2 capacity at a rate of 3 mA cm−2. Replacing NMC with zero-volume-change pre-lithiated Li4Ti5O12 removes this compressive stress, and the cell rapidly fails by transverse cracking. Chemomechanical modelling rationalises both behaviours, with cathode volume change emerging as a design parameter that can suppress or accelerate failure, with direct implications for cathode selection and cathode/separator interface engineering in practical solid-state batteries.

articles.title: Discovery of One-Dimensional Rare-Earth Hybrid Nitrate Double Perovskites
articles.abstract: Rare-earth hybrid nitrate double perovskites (REHNDPs) have recently emerged as an intriguing subclass of functional materials, combining structural diversity with rich intrinsic optoelectronic, magnetic, piezoelectric, and ferroelectric properties. Although notable progress has been made in three-dimensional (3D) and 2D REHNDPs, 1D counterparts have yet to be discovered. Herein, by introducing the bulky organic cation 1-adamantyltrimethylammonium (TMAA+), we report a family of 1D REHNDPs with the general formula (TMAA)2LnCs(NO3)6 (Ln = La3+, Ce3+, Pr3+, Nd3+, Sm3+, and Eu3+). Distinct from the μ2-κ3(O,O′,O″) mode characteristic of 2D and 3D REHNDPs, the bridging NO3− ligands adopt a μ2-κ3(O,O′) coordination mode in 1D counterparts. Strikingly, (TMAA)2SmCs(NO3)6 possesses a step-like high-temperature dielectric switch at 431.7 K. (TMAA)2EuCs(NO3)6 shows brilliant photoluminescence with a quantum yield of 65.46% and a lifetime of 5.21 ms. The X-ray detector based on (TMAA)2EuCs(NO3)6 demonstrates high X-ray sensitivity of 560 μC Gyair−1 cm−2 and a low detection limit of 153 nGyair s−1 under a bias of 25 V. This work bridges a critical dimensional gap and significantly expands the structural and functional portfolio of the REHNDPs.

articles.title: Dopant-Dependent Surface Interaction Modulation by Pt with Hexagonal Perovskites for Robust Bifunctional Oxygen Electrocatalysts in Rechargeable Zn−Air Batteries
articles.abstract: Rechargeable Zn−air batteries (ZABs) have attracted considerable attention as promising energy storage systems owing to their high theoretical energy density and environmental compatibility. However, their practical application is hindered by the sluggish ORR/OER kinetics at the air cathode. This study investigates low Pt-modified Fe- and Ni-doped hexagonal perovskites (BaTi0.8M0.2O3−δ, M = Fe and Ni) as robust bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts, focusing on the modulation of their participating metal and electronic structures. Structural analysis confirms the formation of stable hexagonal phases, while Pt deposition induces distinct electronic reconstruction depending on the dopant species. With a higher ORR catalytic behavior than the Pt/BTO-Ni catalyst, the Pt/BTO-Fe catalyst demonstrates remarkable bifunctionality driven through dopant-dependent surface interaction modulation by Pt with optimized surface/lattice oxygen distribution. Notably, in full-cell ZAB tests, the optimized Pt/BTO-Fe catalyst achieved a comparable peak power density of 124.8 mW cm−2 with a remarkably low round-trip efficiency decay rate of 0.41%/h under stable operation for 60 h, compared to the commercial IrO2 + Pt/C benchmark (125.2 mW cm−2 and 1.39%/h) even at lower Pt content. These findings highlight the critical role of Pt2+-mediated interfacial interactions in governing catalytic durability, providing a rational strategy for designing highly durable bifunctional electrocatalysts for next-generation energy storage systems.

articles.title: Editorial: Celebrating the 80th Anniversary of Jilin University
Emergent Structural Prototypes of Stable Inorganic Materials
articles.abstract: The number of possible crystal structures vastly exceeds the number realized among thermodynamically stable inorganic materials, suggesting that experimentally accessible structure space is organized around a limited set of preferred structural frameworks. Analysis of 23,160 structures on the thermodynamic convex hull identifies 6820 distinct structural frameworks, of which 2382 recur across multiple chemically distinct materials and are therefore classified as structural prototypes. Within a filtered dataset, metallic systems exhibit particularly strong structural recurrence, with 6270 materials grouped into 535 frameworks and 327 prototypes, while 5557 ionic compounds occupy 1704 frameworks and 696 prototypes. These results demonstrate that stable inorganic materials naturally coalesce into recurrent structural prototypes and do not require any a priori definition through manual curation. The resulting recurrence-based catalog also provides an empirical measure of framework prevalence, enabling the relative likelihood of structural frameworks in future materials to be estimated from their recurrence among known compounds.

articles.title: Multicenter Bonding in Periodic Solids through the Lens of Atomic- and Molecular-Orbital Partitioning
articles.abstract: To understand the nature of multicenter interactions in periodic solids and their associated materials (transport) properties, we investigate and quantify multicenter bonding on the basis of the underlying wave function, namely by a combination of quantum-chemical tools for a diverse series of functional materials. First, we probe all compounds by projected force constants based on plane-wave phonon calculations, followed by a projection from plane waves onto a local-orbital framework and its thorough quantum-chemical analysis. While the three-center crystal orbital bond index is used to quantify multicenter bonding between atomic orbitals, the linear combination of fragment orbitals provides a molecular-orbital lens. Eventually, both approaches are fused into the molecular orbital contribution index that directly attributes the contributions of a single molecular orbital to a multicenter bond.

articles.title: Three-Dimensional Hollow Square Array SAPO-34 with Optimal Acidity Distribution Showing Excellent Methanol-to-Olefins Performance
articles.abstract: SAPO-34 is an excellent catalyst for methanol-to-olefins (MTO) reaction. Simultaneously alleviating the diffusion limitations and optimizing the acidity of SAPO-34 is extremely challenging. Herein, a three-dimensional hollow square array SAPO-34 (SAPO-34-HSA) with a sinusoidal-like distribution of silicon was synthesized in a simple way. The role of triethylamine (TEA) switches between the etchant and structure-directing agent according to the reaction temperature. In the heating stage, the seed with high silicon content was etched by TEA; during the crystallization process, TEA guides the epitaxial growth of raw materials on the seed crystal, forming a hollow core−shell structure; after crystallization, the shell was partly leached to form a hollow square array structure. The sinusoidal-like distribution of silicon is conducive to promoting olefin cycling in the hydrocarbon pool mechanism and significantly improving the selectivity of ethylene. So the SAPO-34-HSA catalyst exhibits 70%−400% longer catalytic lifetime in MTO reaction compared with the seed under different reaction conditions.

articles.title: Transition Metal Chalcogenides as Electrocatalysts for Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Amid escalating energy demand and severe environmental effects, green hydrogen production via water electrolysis has emerged as a cornerstone technology. Conventional alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) generally suffers from low hydrogen purity and current density, while proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) relies on high-cost noble-metal catalysts and harsh acidic conditions. To mitigate these limitations, researchers have turned to anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) as a promising alternative, offering an intermediate pathway that pairs the non-noble metal-based catalysts of AWE with the high purity and compact architecture of PEMWE. However, AEMWE technology remains comparatively underdeveloped. Herein, we have summarized transition metal chalcogenides (TMCs) as a low-cost catalyst platform for AEMWE devices. The current review focuses on a comparative analysis across the chalcogen family and discusses how variations in their physicochemical properties influence the overall catalytic performance of anion exchange membrane devices. In addition, the underlying mechanisms of AEMWE, the membrane-electrode assembly, and cell configurations have also been explored in detail. The review critically examines the intrinsic activity of the transition metal chalcogenide-based catalyst layer against device-level performance metrics and further highlights emerging future directions. The review aims to provide a clear roadmap toward the development of highly efficient and commercially competitive AEMWE systems for next-generation green hydrogen production.

articles.title: Ultralow Pt-Loaded Pt/Fe2O3 with Pt−Fe Pair Sites for Efficient Seawater Hydrogen Production
articles.abstract: Seawater electrolysis for green hydrogen production urgently demands high-performance electrocatalysts that simultaneously deliver fast reaction kinetics with robust chloride ion (Cl−) resistance. Herein, we report an ultralow Pt-loaded (<1 wt %) Pt/Fe2O3 catalyst rich in Pt−Fe atomic pairs synthesized via a photoreduction synthetic strategy. Photogenerated electrons drive the selective reduction of Pt precursors at low-coordinate Fe3+ sites on α-Fe2O3 (012) facets, constructing Pt−Fe pair interfaces that enable directional electron transfer from Fe-dz2 to Pt-dz2 orbitals. This electronic modulation optimizes the Gibbs free energy of hydrogen adsorption, weakens the intrinsic affinity of active sites toward Cl−, and accelerates water dissociation. The as-synthesized catalyst achieves ultralow overpotentials of 9 and 51 mV at 10 and 100 mA cm−2 respectively in alkaline simulated seawater, with a slight potential decay of only 0.08 mV h−1 over 1000 h of continuous operation, outperforming most state-of-the-art electrocatalysts. When integrated into an anion exchange membrane electrolyzer, it delivers a low cell voltage of 2.0 V at 500 mA cm−2 and maintains stable operation for 200 h at 100 mA cm−2.

articles.title: A Robust Assay for Molecular Sexing of Emperor Penguins Using Degraded DNA and the Potential Applicability to Other Spheniscids
articles.abstract: Molecular sexing is a widely used approach for identifying the sex of monomorphic birds, but existing primers often target relatively large products that are difficult to amplify from highly degraded DNA. In this study, we developed a new primer set (voEP_F/voEP_R/P2) based on allele‐specific polymerase chain reaction (ASPCR) to facilitate the sexing of emperor penguins (Aptenodytes forsteri) using non‐invasively collected guano. Our assay targets short sequences within a conserved exon of the chromodomain helicase DNA binding 1 (CHD1) gene and can therefore be used with a broad range of sample types. We compared the performance of our new primer set in both plucked feathers and guano to the commonly used intron‐based sexing primers (2550F/2718R and P8/P2) and evaluated its sensitivity through a cross‐factorial fragmentation and dilution experiment of synthetic CHD1 templates. We then independently validated the accuracy of our assay in a small subset of feather samples using whole‐genome sequencing (WGS) data. Although P8/P2 was highly effective compared to 2550F/2718R for sex determination in emperor penguins, it was less reliable when used with guano samples. In contrast, the voEP primers consistently yielded higher amplification success and showed greater analytical sensitivity across both feathers and guano. Sequence alignments of CHD1 from multiple penguin species revealed conservation of the primer‐binding sites, suggesting that the newly designed primers can potentially be used with other Spheniscids. Our results demonstrate that the voEP assay is a robust and reliable alternative method for sex identification in penguins and may provide a solution for sexing with lower‐quality genetic samples.

articles.title: Contrasting Spatial Genomic Structure in Two Widespread Grassland Species Across Norway Supports Species‐Specific Seed Sourcing
articles.abstract: Ecological restoration typically relies on locally sourced seed material, yet seed sourcing in many countries is based on broad administrative regions rather than empirical genetic data. Whether these generalized zones reflect biologically meaningful population genomic structure, particularly among co‐occurring species used together in restoration, remains poorly understood, thus limiting genetically informed restoration practices. Here, we use genome‐wide double‐digest RAD sequencing (ddRAD‐seq) to examine spatial population genomic structure in two widespread perennial grassland species commonly used in restoration in Norway: Silene dioica, an obligately outcrossing species with limited seed dispersal, and Achillea millefolium, a polyploid complex characterized by high gene flow and dispersal capacity. Analysis of 17 populations of S. dioica (355 individuals; 19,200 SNPs) and 23 populations of A. millefolium (428 individuals; 21,294 SNPs) across broad latitudinal and climatic gradients in Norway revealed strikingly contrasting patterns of genetic structure. Silene dioica showed moderate spatial structure, significant isolation‐by‐distance, and multiple geographically coherent genetic groups, indicating spatially restricted gene flow and supporting the delineation of multiple seed transfer zones. In contrast, A. millefolium showed weak population differentiation, extensive admixture, and little geographic structuring, but significant isolation‐by‐environment, with annual precipitation emerging as the strongest environmental predictor of genomic differentiation independently of geographic distance, justifying the delineation of three broad genomic zones. Because species‐specific life‐history traits likely contributed to these patterns, a single generalized seed‐sourcing framework can be inadequate even for sympatric species restored together. While the structured genomic patterns in S. dioica support localized seed sourcing, the high connectivity in A. millefolium supports broader transfer zones. Overall, our study highlights the importance of incorporating genomic data into restoration planning by aligning seed transfer distances with species‐specific connectivity to reduce genetic risks and maintain evolutionary potential under environmental change.

articles.title: Density‐Dependent Response of Alpine Meadows to Plateau Zokor Disturbance on the Tibetan Plateau: Nonlinear Relationship and Ecological Thresholds
articles.abstract: The plateau zokor (Eospalax baileyi) is a keystone subterranean rodent species in the alpine meadows of the Qinghai‐Tibet Plateau, and its burrowing and foraging activities exert complex dual effects on grassland ecosystems. Quantifying the relationship between zokor bioturbation and vegetation, ground‐surface and community characteristics, and identifying the ecological management threshold are crucial for sustainable land management. This study selected 21 typical alpine meadow sites along a disturbance gradient on the eastern Qinghai‐Tibet Plateau. We used unmanned aerial vehicle remote‐sensing to extract new mound density as a proxy for relative disturbance intensity and integrated multiple ground‐surveyed indicators into a grassland degradation index, so as to evaluate the association between overall grassland condition and disturbance intensity and to identify the key ecological management threshold. The results showed that vegetation cover and mean height declined linearly and the proportion of bare ground increased linearly with increasing disturbance intensity; community composition exhibited an inverted U‐shaped pattern in species richness and a U‐shaped pattern in the proportion of poisonous plants, whereas aboveground biomass and the proportion of edible forage showed no significant relationship with relative disturbance intensity. Furthermore, a nonlinear relationship was detected between zokor disturbance and the grassland degradation index, and we identified 166 new mounds·ha−1 as the ecological management threshold for plateau zokors; above this threshold, the tendency of grassland condition toward degradation became more pronounced, with surface denudation and deterioration of community composition emerging as the primary constraints on overall grassland condition. This study provides a quantitative basis for shifting alpine meadow management from conventional “pest control” toward threshold‐based adaptive management, and offers a reference for identifying and regulating bioturbation thresholds in other vulnerable ecosystems.

articles.title: Envenomation Leads to Venom Protein Reduction and a Recovery Period in Bumblebee Workers
articles.abstract: The evolution and deployment of venom systems in animals have been central to their ecological success, though not without costs. For social bees, venom plays a key role in nest defence; yet for species such as honeybees, the act of stinging generally leads to death. However, for other social bee species such as bumblebees, where stinging is not apparently fatal, it raises the question of what, if any, are the consequences associated with venom usage (envenomation). Here, we investigated proteomic changes to understand consequences that can occur at the molecular level in the venom sac, the primary reservoir for venom storage, of Bombus terrestris workers over a short time‐course post‐envenomation. Our analysis reveals three key findings: (1) envenomation leads to changes in the venom sac proteome, with affected proteins generally reduced in the bumblebee venom sac, suggestive of a molecular cost; (2) quantified reductions of traditional venom‐associated proteins post‐envenomation indicate changes in individual venom protein abundance post‐usage; and (3) recovery period for bumblebee post‐envenomation to return to a non‐envenomation state was required, further indicating a potential cost at the molecular level associated with venom usage. Overall, our findings provide new insights into the molecular consequences of venom usage in bumblebees.

articles.title: Formal Description of Cladocopium proximale sp. nov., a Coral Photosymbiont From the C1 Radiation
articles.abstract: Coral reefs are among the most biodiverse ecosystems on Earth and rely on endosymbiosis with Symbiodiniaceae, a diverse family of dinoflagellates essential for coral nutrition and which also play an important role in thermal tolerance. Despite their ecological importance, resolving species boundaries within Symbiodiniaceae remains challenging, partly due to limited phylogenetic signal in commonly used genetic markers and the absence of broadly accepted criteria for species delimitation. Refining taxonomic resolution is therefore critical for understanding symbiont diversity, distributions, and evolutionary relationships. In this study, we delimit two closely related Cladocopium species using a meta‐haplotype framework applied to two hypervariable loci—the ITS2 region and the psbA non‐coding region (psbAncr). Slowly evolving markers failed to differentiate Cladocopium proximale (SCF049; described here) from its sister species C. proliferum. In contrast, consistent genetic differences between the two taxa were detected across both hypervariable regions. Together with morphological differences, these results support the recognition of C. proximale and C. proliferum as distinct species. Our results highlight the value of combining multiple hypervariable markers to improve taxonomic accuracy in Symbiodiniaceae, providing a stronger basis for understanding how symbiont diversity and ecological differentiation may influence coral resilience and responses to environmental change. More broadly, closely related Symbiodiniaceae such as these provide important systems for examining speciation processes, including potential ecological differentiation and reproductive compatibility.

articles.title: Observations of Mammalian Predation on Pacific Sleeper Sharks in Southeast Alaska
articles.abstract: The predator–prey relationship between marine mammals and sharks may not be as well defined as originally believed. Both groups can be either predator or prey. In the case of the Pacific sleeper shark, previous studies have documented the sharks predating upon juvenile Steller sea lions and scavenging whale falls, while other studies have reported offshore killer whales predating upon Pacific sleeper shark. Here, we report two observations of likely marine mammal predation upon Pacific sleeper sharks in Southeast Alaska; one of Steller sea lions actively predating upon an approximately 2 m shark; and the other a stranded carcass of a 3 m shark likely predated by killer whales. The observations reported herein are unique in that Steller sea lions have not been documented to predate upon Pacific sleeper sharks, and previous reports of killer whale predation upon Pacific sleeper sharks have been near open ocean passages.

articles.title: Under Fire: High Survival Rates of a Critically Endangered Marsupial During a Low‐Severity Prescribed Burn
articles.abstract: Climate change is intensifying fire weather globally, increasing land managers' reliance on prescribed burning to reduce fuel loads and mitigate wildfire risk. Yet the direct effects of prescribed fire on threatened wildlife remain poorly understood, partly because individual‐level data on survival and behaviour during fire events are exceptionally rare. We used VHF telemetry and accelerometry to track the survival, space use and diel activity of nine western ringtail possums (Pseudocheirus occidentalis; ngwayir; eight collared, one uncollared joey)—a Critically Endangered arboreal marsupial widely regarded as highly sensitive to fire—through a low‐ to moderate‐severity prescribed burn at Yalgorup National Park, south‐west Western Australia. All nine animals survived direct fire exposure despite several refuge trees being scorched or structurally damaged. Post‐fire, possums relocated an average of 181 m, but movement distances were unrelated to burn severity and possums showed no selection for unburnt habitat, suggesting limited spatial disruption at the home‐range scale. This may partly reflect the predominantly low‐severity nature of the burn (95.7% of the burnt area). Accelerometry revealed suppressed nocturnal activity during smoke exposure and the fire period, with only partial recovery in the days following the burn, indicating measurable sublethal costs even where direct mortality did not occur. We interpret these behavioural responses as potentially consistent with adaptations shaped by long‐term exposure to frequent, low‐severity fire regimes historically associated with Noongar burning on the Swan Coastal Plain. Although based on a small number of individuals at a single site, and a carefully implemented low‐ to moderate‐severity prescribed burn, our findings provide rare empirical evidence that a critically endangered marsupial can survive prescribed fire. These results have implications for how prescribed burning programs are designed and implemented in the context of evolving fire regimes under climate change.

articles.abstract: Introducing homologous acceptors into PM6:L8-BO tailors aggregation kinetics during film formation, extending the crystal-growth window to ∼100 ms and reducing excited-state energetic disorder, enabling ternary devices to achieve efficiencies >20%.

The impacts of large wild grazers on soil carbon persistence are strongly modulated by the environmental context
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Wild animals, particularly large mammalian grazers, can influence ecosystem carbon dynamics and soil carbon sequestration. However, we lack a mechanistic understanding of how wild grazer communities influence soil carbon persistence, specifically in terms of the size of vulnerable free particulate versus more stable occluded particulate and mineral‐associated carbon pools. Resolving this is crucial for predicting how soil carbon is stored long‐term and how grazing management can contribute to soil carbon persistence. We investigated associations between a wild mammalian grazer community and soil carbon persistence in a fire‐prone savanna in South Africa's Hluhluwe‐iMfolozi Park. More specifically, we assessed how variation in grazing (areas grazed at high vs. low intensity) and woody cover (woody‐encroached vs. non‐encroached grassland areas) related to the amount of soil organic carbon (SOC) and pyrogenic organic matter (PyOM, as a proxy for pyrogenic organic carbon) in pools with varying residence times, and how environmental conditions mediated these patterns. In order of increasing residence time, we looked at the free particulate, occluded and mineral‐associated soil carbon pools. Grazing was associated with more SOC in the mineral‐associated pool in fine‐textured soils but less SOC in coarse‐textured soils. In contrast, grazing was associated with more PyOM in the mineral‐associated pool at lower rainfall and in coarser‐textured soils, but less at higher rainfall and in finer‐textured soils. Grazing was also associated with more PyOM in the free particulate pool in finer‐textured soils but less in coarser‐textured soils, and with more PyOM in the occluded pool at low fire frequency but less at high fire frequency. Woody encroachment was consistently associated with less SOC and PyOM in the mineral‐associated pool, with these associations intensifying with higher rainfall (and, for SOC, at higher fire frequency; for PyOM, in finer‐textured soils). In contrast, woody encroachment was associated with more PyOM in the free particulate and occluded pools, although the occluded PyOM associations weakened with higher rainfall and fire frequency. Woody encroachment was associated with less SOC in the free particulate and occluded pools at low rainfall and fire frequency but more SOC at high rainfall and fire frequency. Our study reveals that intense grazing by large wild grazers and woody encroachment are associated with divergent soil carbon persistence outcomes, where the direction and magnitude of these associations are strongly modulated by the environmental context. Therefore, future assessments of large wild grazer impacts on carbon cycling would benefit from considering soil carbon persistence, not just total stocks, together with the environmental context in which these animals occur. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Climate‐Driven Oceanographic Changes Shape Larval Dispersal Success in the Southern Ocean
articles.abstract: Although climate‐driven changes in ocean circulation are increasingly recognized as key drivers of marine ecosystem structure and dynamics, their consequences for the early life stages of deep‐sea fishes remain difficult to quantify. In the Southern Ocean, variability in frontal systems such as the Polar Front (PF) may influence larval dispersal and retention, with direct implications for recruitment. We investigated how interannual variability in ocean circulation and egg production shapes larval dispersal and retention in suitable recruitment areas of a large body size deep‐sea fish species, Patagonian toothfish (Dissostichus eleginoides), around the Kerguelen Plateau. We developed an integrated modeling framework which combined spatially explicit models of egg production with 24 years (2000–2023) of Lagrangian dispersal simulations driven by satellite‐derived geostrophic currents to quantify successful larval retention. Ontogenetic changes in distribution and fecundity were accounted for to model egg production, allowing retention metrics to reflect spatial heterogeneity in reproductive output. Larval retention rate in suitable recruitment areas varied from 9% to 28% over the study period. PF‐associated jet intensity was significantly associated with larval retention variability: years characterized by stronger PF‐associated circulation showed lower larval retention, with more larvae advected away from the shelf toward the eastern part of the plateau. The latter part of the time series, particularly after 2010, was characterized by stronger year‐to‐year fluctuations, a higher contribution of the North‐West recruitment area, and more frequent low‐retention years. Building on new findings on toothfish spawning dynamics and long‐term altimetry data, we showed for the first time that there is the potential for self‐recruitment in the northern part of the Kerguelen Plateau (French EEZ). We also discussed the implications for fishery management since PF‐associated indices may help interpret past recruitment trends and offer useful early‐warning for future recruitment anomalies.

articles.title: Compounding Human and Bioclimatic Factors Driving the Global Fire Crisis
articles.abstract: Over millennia, social and ecological systems have been shaped by fire and have in turn shaped fire regimes. However, recent decades have seen an escalating “fire crisis” characterized by an increasing incidence of large, intense wildfires, most notably in forests. Voices in the academic literature and media often attribute the fire crisis to a narrow range of mechanisms, for example, fuel management or climate change. This failure to acknowledge the complexity of causes leads to simplistic framings of risk, and ultimately, proposed solutions that are either not feasible or may lead to undesired outcomes. In this review we outline the human and bioclimatic factors that are driving this fire crisis. Factors reviewed include the impacts of colonial legacies, which disrupted Indigenous land stewardship and traditional burning practices over centuries; policies of fire suppression; population growth, urbanization and land management practices; biotic disturbances such as insect outbreaks and invasive plant species; and climate change, which is affecting both fire regimes and social‐ecological resilience to fire. Many of these factors co‐occur leading to complex interactions and, often, unexpected outcomes. Our review highlights that climate change is now having a compounding effect, building on a multitude of other factors to drive the fire crisis. Addressing this crisis requires first acknowledging its complexity and moving beyond simple framings of risk. We suggest solutions will vary across different places and through time, but may include supporting Indigenous land stewardship, adopting flexible fire responses, shifting societal expectations from aggressive fire suppression to “living with fire”, and fostering resilient social and ecological communities.

articles.title: Dual Constraints of Microbial Carbon Use Efficiency and Mineral Protection Govern Necromass Accrual
articles.abstract: Increasing soil organic carbon (SOC), central to food security and climate mitigation, is increasingly recognized as being mediated by microbial necromass C (MNC) accrual. However, how microbial production and mineral preservation jointly govern MNC accrual under contrasting resource conditions remains unclear. Here, we analyzed soils from 14 long‐term fertilization experiments (up to 47 years) to assess how edaphic and climatic conditions regulate the response of MNC accrual to manure (M) and non‐manure (NM) fertilization treatments. We found that the primary constraints on MNC accrual varied with resource availability, with microbial production under resource‐limited conditions and mineral preservation under resource‐abundant conditions. Under resource‐limited conditions, M treatments increased MNC by up to 122%, with changes tightly coupled to SOC gains. This accrual was associated with increases in dissolved organic C and microbial C use efficiency, indicating a production‐constrained pathway in which manure inputs alleviate substrate limitation and promote microbial C allocation toward biomass production and necromass formation. Conversely, under resource‐abundant conditions, MNC responses to fertilization were weaker (+56%) and uncoupled from SOC gains. Instead, MNC accrual was primarily associated with mineral protection capacity (e.g., Fe and Al oxides), consistent with a preservation‐constrained pathway. Overall, microbial processing and mineral preservation represent context‐dependent constraints on MNC accrual under contrasting resource conditions. These findings underscore the importance of resource context for site‐specific C management and for understanding soil C dynamics under global change.

articles.title: Fluxes Everywhere, All of the Time—A Tribute to Dennis Baldocchi
Revealing the Widespread Bias of Extinction Risk in the Antarctic and the Southern Ocean
articles.abstract: Accelerating environmental change in the Antarctic and Southern Ocean (ASO) necessitates robust extinction risk assessments to inform conservation priorities. Nevertheless, no systematic, region‐wide baseline of extinction risk currently exists for tracking ASO biodiversity responses to ongoing change, a significant barrier to global biodiversity monitoring. Here, we conducted the first ASO‐wide synthesis of current extinction risk knowledge for plants, animals and Fungi. This included examining biases in current assessments, the distribution of Threatened species and their associated threats. Using a data‐inclusive workflow, we compiled 8908 assessments representing 4970 species, more than doubling the number of ASO species assessed compared with any single source. As expected, assessments were heavily biased towards vertebrates (58% assessed), while invertebrates, despite their ecological prevalence, were markedly underrepresented (6% assessed). Among vertebrates, mammals had the highest proportion of Threatened species (26%). Birds within the ASO were disproportionately Threatened (25%) compared to the global average (11%), with the greatest threat for ASO species being ‘Biological Resource Use’. The sub‐Antarctic Islands had the highest density of both Threatened species and assessment effort, whereas many Antarctic species remain unassessed. Additionally, Threatened species have the lowest protected area coverage of any conservation status. These pronounced assessment biases highlight the need for more balanced, representative and data‐inclusive extinction risk assessments to be able to effectively detect conservation status change. This work represents an important step in ensuring ASO representation in global biodiversity monitoring frameworks, strengthening the capacity of these frameworks to detect, attribute and respond to future biodiversity changes.

articles.title: When Drought Is Not Drought: How Metrics Bias Estimates of Ecosystem Water Limitation
articles.abstract: Anthropogenic warming and shifts in global precipitation regimes are increasing rainfall variability and the frequency of intense precipitation events, raising uncertainty about how conventional meteorological drought indices capture ecosystem water limitation. This uncertainty arises from two key issues: temporal aggregation, as most meteorological drought indices are based on monthly integrated summaries, and drought definition, because atmospheric water deficits do not necessarily translate into vegetation water stress. Here, we quantified ecosystem gross primary productivity (GPP) responses to drought using three approaches: (1) monthly meteorological drought identified from monthly standardized precipitation evaporation index (SPEI), (2) daily meteorological drought defined by daily SPEI, and (3) ecological drought defined using an indicator of actual vegetation water limitation. Comparing monthly and daily SPEI‐based drought isolated the effects of temporal aggregation, while comparing daily meteorological and ecological droughts quantified the influence of drought definition. Across 130 eddy‐covariance sites spanning multiple biomes and climate zones, we analyzed 6691 drought months identified using monthly SPEI. Daily SPEI data revealed that within months classified as meteorological drought, nearly 50% of days did not coincide with atmospheric water deficits owing to daily rainfall variability. As a result, monthly SPEI overestimated GPP responses (20.60% ± 5.28% increase) relative to daily SPEI (4.61% ± 1.21% increase). In contrast, daily meteorological drought metrics underestimated drought‐induced suppression of GPP by ~46% compared with ecological drought, demonstrating that atmospheric drought metrics do not fully reflect water stress experienced by vegetation. Our results show that both temporal resolution and drought definition can bias estimates of ecosystem drought responses, underscoring the need for finer‐scale temporal and ecologically relevant measures of vegetation water limitation to improve understanding of biosphere–climate interactions in an increasingly drought‐prone world.

articles.title: Engineering a borate-rich interphase for highly stable all-solid-state sodium batteries
articles.abstract: All-solid-state sodium batteries (ASSBs) offer high energy density and safety, but conventional solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layers suffer from low efficiency and severe side reactions. This work proposes a novel strategy based on a borate-enriched SEI that effectively suppresses side reactions and enables dendrite-free Na plating/stripping, providing valuable mechanistic insights and a feasible pathway toward high-performance ASSBs.

articles.title: More stopovers facilitate migratory waterfowl tracking shifting vegetation green‐up
articles.abstract: By integrating tracking data from multiple migratory waterfowl species with remote sensing data, we showed that birds using more stopover sites are better able to synchronize their schedules with vegetation green‐up at their breeding grounds. Our findings highlight the importance of stopover sites in enhancing birds' resilience to climate change. Abstract Climate change is altering the phenology of food resources, and migratory birds may respond by adjusting migration timing to track shifting food availability (i.e. their phenological sensitivity). The ability to adjust migration timing can vary among species according to traits such as ecological guild, body size and migration distance. Stopover sites are critical components of migration, allowing birds to refuel and acquire updated environmental information. However, empirical evidence on how stopover use enhances phenological sensitivity to shifting spring green‐up remains lacking. In this study, we investigated how stopover frequency influences the phenological sensitivity of migratory waterfowl at breeding areas. We hypothesized that individuals using more stopover sites would better align their migration timing with shifts in vegetation green‐up. We reconstructed 220 spring migration paths from five East Asian migratory waterfowl species using high‐resolution tracking data collected from 2015 to 2023. Spring vegetation green‐up was derived from remote sensing data. We then fitted linear mixed models to test how stopover frequency influences the change of arrival timing at breeding sites. Individuals using a greater number of stopover sites showed closer alignment between their migration timing and local spring vegetation green‐up at breeding areas. More frequent stopover use was associated with stronger phenological sensitivity, suggesting greater behavioural plasticity in tracking shifting resources. Loss of stopover habitat may therefore limit their capacity to respond to changing resource phenology, underscoring the importance of stopover conservation for promoting resilience to climate change. 中文摘要 气候变化正在改变食物资源的物候，迁徙鸟类可能通过调整迁徙时间来追踪不断变化的食物可利用性，即表现出对资源物候变化的物候敏感性。不同物种调整迁徙时间的能力可能因生态类群、体型和迁徙距离等性状而异。停歇地是迁徙过程中的关键组成部分，不仅为鸟类提供补充能量的场所，也有助于其获取最新的环境信息。然而，关于停歇地利用如何影响迁徙鸟类对春季植被返青变化的物候敏感性，目前仍缺乏实证证据。 本研究探讨了停歇地利用频率如何影响迁徙水鸟在繁殖地的物候敏感性。我们假设，利用更多停歇地的个体能够更好地调整迁徙时间，从而使到达繁殖地的时间与春季植被返青变化保持更紧密的同步。 基于2015‐2023年高分辨率追踪数据，我们重建了5种东亚迁徙水鸟共220条春季迁徙路线，并利用遥感数据获取春季植被返青时间。随后，我们构建线性混合效应模型，检验停歇地利用频率对繁殖地到达时间变化的影响。 结果表明，利用更多中途停歇地的个体，其迁徙时间与繁殖地当地春季植被返青变化之间表现出更高程度的匹配。中途停歇地利用数量越多，个体表现出的物候敏感性越强，表明更频繁地利用中途停歇地可能有助于迁徙水鸟通过行为可塑性追踪不断变化的资源物候。因此，中途停歇地栖息地的丧失可能限制迁徙水鸟应对资源物候变化的能力。这一发现凸显了保护迁徙停歇地对于增强其应对气候变化能力的重要性。

Bacterial 2′,3′-cGAMP signaling induces membrane splitting in antiphage CBASS immunity
articles.abstract: Li et al. reveal how the bacterial CdnB-Cap14 CBASS pathway converts DNA sensing into membrane-disrupting antiphage defense. DNA activates autoinhibited CdnB to produce 2′,3′-cGAMP in vitro, which induces Cap14 filament assembly and partitions the membrane into two layers. Phage Acb2 counteracts this pathway by sequestering 2′,3′-cGAMP and blocking signal transmission.

articles.title: Biogeographic Barriers and Gut Microbiome Turnover Across the Peromyscus maniculatus Species Complex
articles.abstract: Biogeographic barriers are fundamental in shaping the distribution of animals and plants, yet the role of discrete landscape features in constraining microbial dispersal remains poorly understood. Identifying the barriers that partition gut microbial communities is essential for modelling the distribution of hosts and their symbionts across physical space and evolutionary time. The deer mouse (Peromyscus maniculatus species complex), which inhabits nearly all terrestrial environments in North America, provides an ideal model for testing these biogeographic drivers of the mammalian gut microbiome. Using NSF NEON biorepository samples, we characterized the gut microbiomes of 13 populations across the contiguous United States using full‐length 16S rRNA long‐read sequencing. The presence or absence of microbial taxa was best explained by eastern versus western regions compared to habitat or climate, suggesting a role of large fluvial systems as discrete barriers to microbial transmission, likely due to restricted host dispersal. Although we observed a consistent distance‐decay relationship across the continent, our results suggest that the Mississippi River is associated with increased microbial species turnover, with dissimilarity across the river exceeding levels predicted by geographic distance alone. Furthermore, we identified specific microbial lineages that exhibit varying patterns of isolation by distance across the continent, suggesting a gradient in microbial transmission patterns ranging from lineages that are freely shared across space to those that are dispersal limited. Together, these findings suggest that the gut microbiome may act as a bioindicator of landscape‐level ecological connectivity, revealing discontinuities in microbial transmission associated with large‐scale landscape barriers even among closely related host populations that lack reproductive barriers.

articles.title: Dietary Niches and Their Consequences for Five Insectivorous Passerines in a Seasonal Boreal Setting
articles.abstract: To understand the effects of climate change and other disturbances on ecosystems, methodologies capable of unravelling the complexity of biotic interactions are vital. Here, we present a dietary study on five passerines nesting in boreal forests: the crested tit Lophophanes cristatus, willow tit Poecile montanus, blue tit Cyanistes caeruleus, great tit Parus major, and pied flycatcher Ficedula hypoleuca. We used metabarcoding to describe their arthropod prey during the breeding season, and linked diets' properties with breeding success to understand birds' dependence on particular prey. The birds' diets contained hundreds of arthropod taxa, showing considerable richness and interannual variation. Most prey identities were resolved to species level. The most common prey were Lepidoptera, followed by Diptera, Coleoptera and Araneae. Dietary overlap was low to middling, conformed to temporal overlap, and fluctuated across the three studied years. Higher consumption of lepidopterans and their larvae was strongly associated with higher breeding success in blue tits and, to a lesser extent, great tits. In contrast, crested tits, willow tits and pied flycatchers had a more constant breeding success without relying on specific prey. The results suggest that the more recently settled blue tits and great tits are less capable of optimally utilizing the comparatively resource‐poor boreal environments. The apparent good adaptation to local foraging conditions contrasts to declining population trends in the Red‐Listed crested tits and willow tits. Our study highlights the complexity of arthropod communities and insectivore food webs, and showcase how molecular methods can be used to study ecological interactions.

articles.title: Genomic Divergence and Variation in Developmental Plasticity Across Inselberg Populations of a Tropical Frog
articles.abstract: Understanding how phenotypic plasticity and local specialization are shaped by gene flow and environmental heterogeneity requires natural systems that vary in both spatial isolation and environmental conditions across the landscape, yet such systems are uncommon. Naturally discontinuous inselbergs may provide this opportunity. Here, using populations of the inselberg‐specialist frog Leptodactylus lithonaetes, we evaluated whether habitat discontinuity translates into restricted gene flow and genetic structure and then tested how variation in connectivity and environmental heterogeneity shapes the balance between phenotypic plasticity and local specialization. We predicted that populations with higher environmental heterogeneity and higher gene flow would evolve plasticity in growth and development, whereas populations in more homogeneous environments and more genetically isolated would exhibit reduced plasticity and increased specialization. Using > 11,000 SNPs, we showed that the apparent habitat discontinuity among nine inselbergs spanning 300 km was reflected in a strong population structure and varying levels of gene flow among inselbergs, in an isolation‐by‐distance pattern. We then tested whether tadpoles alter their size or timing at metamorphosis to pond‐drying risk, and whether these plastic responses vary among populations with environmental heterogeneity (seasonality). Although tadpoles did not plastically accelerate metamorphosis under pond‐drying risk, the magnitude of body mass reduction under desiccation stress differed among populations, indicating developmental plasticity in body mass. Northern localities, exposed to greater environmental heterogeneity, showed greater survival and less body weight loss, resulting in higher tolerance to environmental stress than southern localities. Even in the absence of developmental acceleration, population‐level variation in responses to environmental stress is congruent with reduced plasticity, or increased specialization, in isolated populations exposed to less heterogeneous environments.

articles.title: The Influence of the Antarctic Circumpolar Deep Water on Deep‐Sea Eukaryotic Biodiversity and Distribution in the Western Pacific Ocean
articles.abstract: The Antarctic region, a centre of biodiversity origin, influences deep‐sea ecosystems by supplying species to distant regions. Understanding the influence of Antarctic Upper Circumpolar Deep Water (UCDW) on deep‐sea eukaryotic diversity is therefore essential for outlining global biodiversity patterns. Our results showed the UCDW community exhibited ~1.5‐fold higher taxonomic and phylogenetic diversity than the Caroline Basin control community and contained a substantial proportion of unique taxa across multiple eukaryotic lineages. Source tracking using the available Southern Ocean surface‐water reference detected a 4.42% Antarctic‐associated contribution to the UCDW community. Indicators and generalists of the UCDW community shared > 97% sequence identity with Southern Ocean samples. The community analyses suggested that the Yap‐Mariana Junction choke point did not constitute a strong barrier to connectivity between adjacent basins, consistent with UCDW‐mediated dispersal into the Philippine Basin. The UCDW microbial dispersal into the Philippine Basin occurs through two potential routes: directly through the YMJ at 2000–3000 m and via upwelling across seamounts at 500–750 m. Governed mainly by neutral, dispersal‐driven processes, the UCDW community showed strong genetic exchange and connectivity. These findings suggest a role for deep‐water circulation in shaping the diversity and distribution of eukaryotes detected in western Pacific deep‐water samples.
