articles.abstract: Ethylene oligomerization is pivotal in the petrochemical industry to produce olefins and polymers. In this work, we conduct density functional theory (DFT) calculations to investigate ethylene oligomerization catalyzed by a...

articles.title: Influence of particle size and metal–support interactions on nitroarene reductive amination over Pd/TiO 2 catalysts
articles.abstract: Pd/TiO 2 catalysts enable mild reductive amination of aromatic and bio-based aldehydes. Particle size control and SMSI enhance amine selectivity, boost turnover frequency nearly 200-fold, and support reuse.

articles.title: CRISPR mutagenesis of the MYC locus reveals a druggable ultraconserved RNA element
articles.abstract: CRISPR tiling mutagenesis of the 10-kb human MYC locus mapped the fitness landscape of an entire human gene at base-pair resolution. This unbiased interrogation revealed that 67% of functionally essential base pairs are noncoding. An ultraconserved RNA regulatory element was identified that controls MYC localization and can be therapeutically targeted to suppress cancer cell growth in patient-derived tumor organoids.

articles.title: 5-Azacytidine incorporation into mRNAs disrupts translation and induces ribosome collisions
articles.abstract: 5-Azacytidine (5-AzaC) is a cytidine analog chemotherapeutic widely used to treat myeloid malignancies. Although its activity is primarily attributed to DNA hypomethylation, the majority of 5-AzaC is incorporated into RNA, where its functional consequences are less understood. Here, we show that 5-AzaC treatment of cells leads to inhibition of protein synthesis. Ribo-seq, Disome-seq, and RNA-seq in treated cells exhibit a time-dependent C-to-G conversion in mRNAs. These conversion events are enriched within footprint positions corresponding to the A-site of monosomes or stalled leading ribosomes in a disome complex. Footprints are accumulated at sites with C-rich codons in the A-site, with particular emphasis on the second codon position. Consistent with disome-mediated signaling, 5-AzaC activates ZAK- and GCN2-dependent stress responses. Furthermore, loss of the ribosome-associated quality control factor, ZNF598, sensitizes cells to 5-AzaC. These findings suggest that translation disruption represents an additional layer of 5-AzaC's mechanism of action, alongside its known DNA-mediated effects.

articles.title: A hierarchical regulatory cascade programs chlamydospore formation in the nematode-trapping fungus Arthrobotrys flagrans
articles.abstract: Chlamydospores provide durable stress tolerance for fungal survival and enable shelf-stable biocontrol agents, yet their genetic regulation in fungi remains poorly understood. Here, using the nematode-trapping fungus Arthrobotrys flagrans as a model, we define a hierarchical regulatory cascade for chlamydospore formation. LaeA mediates H3K9 monomethylation to license this developmental program. Furthermore, we identify VeA and Ste12 as LaeA partners, and the importin KapA as a nuclear gatekeeper. This upstream module activates VosA/VelB, which induces AbaA/StuA to control the effectors ChsG, McdD, and McdD-modified glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchored proteins for chlamydospore cell wall biogenesis. The expression levels of regulators within this regulatory cascade (LaeA/VeA/Ste12-VosA/VelB-StuA/AbaA-ChsG and McdD) determine chlamydospore yield and convert environmental cues into differentiation. This framework guides strain engineering for high-yield chlamydospore production and suggests a regulatory paradigm potentially conserved across fungi.

articles.title: A single-cell atlas of pediatric undifferentiated recurrent fever reveals candidate immune regulators
articles.abstract: Children with periodic fever syndromes not attributable to infections, rheumatic disorders, malignancies, or known monogenic autoinflammatory conditions are classified as "syndrome of undifferentiated recurrent fever" (SURF). To date, treatment remains empirical, often resulting in only a partial response, underscoring the unmet clinical need for new therapeutic strategies. To advance the molecular understanding of SURF, we generated a large-scale single-cell RNA-seq immune atlas of 29 SURF patients with more than 200,000 cells. Comparison of patients with three healthy cohorts revealed large-scale metabolic shifts together with a distinct cytokine signature already observable during afebrile periods. This indicates that afebrile SURF cannot be considered a less inflammatory resting state but rather as a distinct homeostatic state. Furthermore, our analysis suggests an NAMPT-mediated autocrine feedback loop connecting the metabolic dysregulations with the pro-inflammatory phenotype in monocytes. This study offers insights into the SURF immunopathology and generates testable hypotheses to guide future therapies.

articles.title: Clearing perivascular light chain-derived amyloid to counteract aging-associated decline in liver regeneration
articles.abstract: Aging impairs organ regeneration, with insufficient angiogenesis as a key contributor. Here, we show that the endothelial immunoproteasome subunit PSMB8 is upregulated in aged mouse livers after partial hepatectomy. Endothelial PSMB8 deletion or PR-957 inhibition promotes angiogenesis and rescues liver regeneration. diGly proteomics identifies TAZ (transcriptional co-activator with PDZ-binding motif) as a ubiquitin-dependent immunoproteasome substrate, and TAZ activation restores aged liver regeneration. Aging triggers the infiltration of CD38+IGLC1+ IgM B cells and aberrant perivascular light chain-derived amyloid deposition in the liver. Recombinant light chain-derived amyloid fibrils directly induce PSMB8 expression in vitro. Anselamimab-mediated light chain-derived amyloid clearance mitigates immunoproteasome overactivation and restores regeneration. Single-cell RNA sequencing confirms that anselamimab reverses aging-induced endothelial marker loss and inflammatory gene upregulation. Our findings establish a pathway linking perivascular light chain-derived amyloid deposition to regenerative decline via endothelial immunoproteasome activation, suggesting amyloid clearance as a promising therapeutic strategy for aging-associated decline in liver regeneration.

articles.title: Exosome secretion is required for Sonic Hedgehog dispersal and signal gradient formation in the embryonic limb bud mesenchyme
articles.abstract: Carrier-assisted diffusion and cytoneme transport help disperse Hedgehog morphogens across diverse embryonic tissues, yet their relative contributions to patterning mesenchymal tissues remain poorly understood. Here, we combine signaling assays with quantitative microscopy to establish exosome secretion as a major mechanism for Sonic Hedgehog (Shh) dispersal. Using a synchronous release system to visualize Shh trafficking, we demonstrate that Shh traffics through the exosome biogenesis pathway in limb bud mesenchymal cells. Shh-bound exosomes diffuse through extracellular space and also bind and travel along cytonemes, providing two alternative modes of transport. We show that exosome secretion is essential to establish short-range Shh signaling gradients in vitro and contributes to shaping Shh protein gradients in the limb bud in vivo. We propose that exosome-based Shh secretion, combined with different modes of extracellular transport, provides a tunable mechanism to sculpt Shh gradients across different length and time scales.

articles.title: Hyperosmotic stress induces rewiring of 3D chromatin interactions
articles.abstract: Cells continually face environmental stressors that challenge homeostasis, yet how three-dimensional (3D) chromatin structure contributes to these stress responses remains unclear under hyperosmotic conditions. To investigate this, we map 3D chromatin structure, its molecular drivers, and transcriptional outcomes during sorbitol-induced hyperosmotic stress. Within 1 hour of sorbitol treatment, pre-existing loops and domains collapse, while several hundred de novo sorbitol-induced loops emerge. These loops are punctate, longer-range, and transient. 3D chromatin structure largely returns to baseline conditions by 24 hours. Loop reorganization is consistent across cell types and hyperosmotic stimuli. Sorbitol-induced loops require cohesin but not CTCF, and anchors are enriched at active promoters harboring GC-rich transcription factor motifs. Genes at these anchors show delayed activation following loop formation, consistent with loops acting upstream of transcription. Together, hyperosmotic stress triggers rapid, reversible, CTCF-independent chromatin reorganization that correlates with transcriptional adaptation.

articles.title: Intermittent fasting enhances muscle regeneration via an EDA2R-NIK-myomixer axis
articles.abstract: Skeletal muscle exhibits a remarkable regenerative capacity that relies on adult stem cells known as satellite cells (SCs), which differentiate into myogenic progenitors to drive muscle repair. How varying energy availability alters myogenesis, however, remains unknown. Here, we demonstrate that intermittent fasting (IF) in mice upregulates a myogenic gene program, including Myomixer, a muscle-specific fusogen that facilitates the merging of progenitor cells into myofibers. IF enhances the regeneration of injured muscles by expanding the SC population and promoting the proliferation and fusion of myogenic progenitors. These effects are absent in an SC-depletion model. We show that fasting-induced EDA2R-NIK signaling increases Myomixer expression and fusion in myoblasts. Notably, mice lacking EDA2R or NIK fail to respond to the myogenic effects of IF. Furthermore, our data suggest that mice with Duchenne muscular dystrophy also benefit from an IF regimen. Therefore, IF-induced regeneration holds potential for aiding recovery from muscle damage.

articles.title: Plagl2 reprograms adult mouse retinal Müller glia for proliferation and injury-enhanced neurogenic competence
articles.abstract: Müller glia (MG) in the adult mammalian retina have long been recognized as a potential endogenous source for the regeneration of lost retinal neurons. However, existing MG reprogramming strategies yield an incomplete regenerative response by favoring either proliferation or neurogenic differentiation. Here, we show that the zinc-finger transcription factor gene Plagl2, previously shown to reactivate quiescent neural stem cells, is sufficient to reprogram adult mouse MG into a progenitor-like state with coupled proliferative and neurogenic competence. Using histology, time-lapse imaging, and single-cell transcriptomics, we find that Plagl2 drives regulated rounds of MG cell cycle re-entry, while N-methyl-D-aspartate-induced retinal injury further promotes the acquisition of neurogenic competence biased toward inner nuclear layer neuronal identities. These findings indicate that Plagl2 regulates mammalian MG reprogramming, and supports a broader approach to tissue regeneration through the adaptation of reprogramming modules across distinct cell types.

articles.title: Programmed bacterial lysis in vivo alters host immune responses and microbial pathogenesis
articles.abstract: Vibrio cholerae injects toxic type VI secretion system (T6SS) effectors to lyse sensitive intestinal commensals, but how this bacterial antagonism enhances mucosal host immune responses and its pathogenicity remains unknown. To mimic T6SS-mediated killing, we engineered V. cholerae lysis strains by using CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) to knockdown essential genes in peptidoglycan biogenesis or lipopolysaccharide (LPS) transport. Our results indicate that controlled bacterial lysis in vivo leads to divergent mucosal immune responses that directly modulate colonization and pathogenicity of a bystander, non-lysing V. cholerae ΔT6SS strain. Mass spectrometric analysis of the lysis debris revealed proinflammatory muropeptides correlating with these changes. We confirmed that oral co-administration of a synthetic peptidoglycan-derived metabolite with a V. cholerae ΔT6SS mutant, but not the wild type, shows dramatic enhancement of disease symptoms. These findings show that intestinal exposure to discrete bacterial cell wall metabolites can differentially modulate host innate immune responses and consequently bacterial pathogenesis.

articles.title: Tau-driven hyperexcitability of locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons underlies sleep fragmentation and cognitive decline in mice
articles.abstract: Early sleep disruption is a hallmark of preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD), but its underlying mechanisms are unclear. The locus coeruleus (LC) dopamine-β-hydroxylase noradrenergic (LCDBH) neurons are vulnerable to early tau pathology in AD. Using P301S transgenic mice and cell-type-specific tau overexpression models, we show that pathological tau accumulation selectively increases the intrinsic excitability of LCDBH neurons. Tau-induced neuronal hyperactivity disrupts sleep homeostasis, reduces non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep and slow-wave activity, increases sleep fragmentation and microarousals, and delays both anesthetic induction and sleep onset. Furthermore, tau overexpression in LCDBH neurons leads to significant recognition memory deficits. Notably, optogenetic suppression of LCDBH-tau neuronal activity reverses sleep disturbances and rescues cognitive dysfunction. Our findings demonstrate that tau-driven hyperexcitability of LCDBH neurons is a core driver of early sleep and cognitive impairments in AD, providing a mechanistic insight and potential target for preclinical AD treatment.

articles.title: Temporal shifts in post-asthmatic immune responses define tumor outcomes via strain-specific monocyte reprogramming
articles.abstract: Epidemiological evidence linking asthma to lung cancer risk remains contradictory, presenting asthma as either a risk factor or a protective condition. We hypothesize that this heterogeneity stems from the temporal dynamics of inflammatory response and host genetic background. Using ovalbumin (OVA)-induced asthma models, we identify a temporal shift in immune effectors driving post-asthmatic tumorigenesis. During acute airway inflammation, eosinophil infiltration accelerates tumor growth across mouse strains. Following resolution, however, tumorigenic outcomes in recovery diverge along genetic lines. Prior asthma reshapes chromatin landscapes of bone marrow myeloid progenitors, establishing innate immune memory that differentially programs monocytes across strains. In C57BL/6 mice, trained monocytes adopt oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), acquiring a suppressive, tissue-remodeling phenotype that promotes tumor progression. Conversely, BALB/c-trained monocytes utilize glycolysis to maintain a pro-phagocytic state, enabling tumor clearance. These findings delineate a biphasic mechanism wherein temporal shifts in post-asthmatic immune responses define tumor outcomes via strain-specific monocyte metabolic reprogramming.

articles.title: The YAP/TAZ-Tgfbr2-stiffness feedback loop governs divergent cell fates of muscle-resident mesenchymal progenitors
articles.abstract: Mesenchymal progenitors are essential for muscle regeneration, but also contribute to fat accumulation and fibrosis. Several extrinsic and intrinsic factors regulating adipogenic or fibrogenic differentiation of mesenchymal progenitors have been identified. However, it remains unclear how different cues are integrated to determine cell fate. Here, we demonstrate that interstitial stiffness and the mechanosensitive hippo pathway regulate mesenchymal progenitor cell fate. Fat accumulation model reduced interstitial stiffness and nuclear YAP/TAZ-positive mesenchymal progenitors compared with a regeneration model, whereas YAP/TAZ deficiency in mesenchymal progenitors enhanced fat deposition. Mechanistically, YAP/TAZ induced expression of the anti-adipogenic genes Aldh1a2 and Wnt5a, and the pro-fibrogenic gene Tgfbr2, which mediates TGF-β binding. Loss of Tgfbr2 in mesenchymal progenitors reduced transient collagen deposition, decreased stiffness, and increased fat accumulation during regeneration. We propose a stiffness-YAP/TAZ-Tgfbr2-collagen regulatory loop governing mesenchymal progenitor cell fate and highlight its importance for optimal muscle regeneration.

articles.title: eHLAstic reveals an extended canonical and non-canonical HLA-E immunopeptidome in human cancers
articles.abstract: HLA-E is a non-classical MHC class I molecule with restricted polymorphism, offering a putative path to broadly applicable off-the-shelf therapies. Yet, the wider HLA-E peptide repertoire remains poorly defined and is largely assumed restricted to signal peptide-derived sequences. We developed eHLAstic, a dedicated HLA-E-binding predictor, that improved the precision of HLA-E ligand discovery almost 3-fold compared with existing approaches. Using eHLAstic and orthogonal biochemical validation, we report 30 previously unrecognized canonical and non-canonical HLA-E-associated peptides, including six cancer-restricted ligands detected in acute lymphoblastic and myeloid leukemia but not healthy blood or bone marrow cells. Most identified ligands were shared across individuals with diverse HLA backgrounds and were detected across hematological and solid cancers. All but one non-canonical ligands were detected exclusively in cancer-associated samples and not in healthy tissues. These findings redefine the HLA-E ligandome and uncover canonical and non-canonical HLA-E ligands with potential for immune recognition and therapeutic targeting.

Aromatic tripeptide predicted insoluble displays highest known solubility
Ynamide β-hydroselenization and β-hydrosulfuration enable sequential selenocysteine/cysteine editing in peptides and proteins
Perivascular macrophages restrict CXCR4-dependent accumulation of stem-like CD8+ T cells in tumors and limit chemotherapy efficacy
articles.abstract: Cheung et al. show that HO-1 expressed by PvTAMs restricts the post-chemotherapy accumulation of stem-like CD8+ T cells in the TME. These cells enter tumors through a CXCR4-dependent pathway associated with chemotherapy-expanded CXCL12+ PvCAFs. Once within the TME, they differentiate into anti-tumor effectors, contributing to durable anti-tumor immunity.

articles.title: Annulation reactions by intramolecular cross-electrophile coupling
articles.abstract: Intramolecular cross-electrophile coupling (iXEC) offers a unified strategy for building semisaturated rings directly from simple dielectrophiles. This work establishes conditions that generate persistent nickel intermediates capable of rapid radical capture through solvent-controlled activation of aryl and alkyl electrophiles. The approach enables efficient access to heteroaromatic, spirocyclic, and macrocyclic compounds under mild conditions, thus providing a broadly applicable platform for pharmaceuticals and natural products where arrays of diverse ring systems can be synthesized from a single core.

articles.title: Atom transfer radical polymerization for sustainable processes and materials
articles.abstract: Atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP) combines increasingly sustainable polymerization processes with precise macromolecular engineering to create materials with extended lifetimes, improved circularity, and advanced functions for energy technologies. This perspective discusses recent advances and future opportunities for greener, scalable ATRP processes and the design of high-performance polymeric materials that integrate functionality and sustainability.

articles.title: Cellular protein delivery through cell-penetrating peptide-mediated water pores driven by membrane potential
articles.abstract: Combining quantitative live-cell imaging, electrophysiology, and atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we establish a mechanism by which CPP additives drive the direct translocation of proteins across cellular membranes through membrane potential-dependent water pores. This framework provides a basis for intracellular delivery of protein therapeutics to expand access to intracellular, previously undruggable targets.

articles.title: Photocatalytic therapy via cross-coupling hydrogen evolution in cancer cells
articles.abstract: Zhou et al. develop an oxygen-independent photocatalytic strategy that converts glutathione to its oxidized form while generating hydrogen in cancer cells, thereby disrupting the intracellular redox balance. This catalytic redox remodeling induces ferroptosis and antitumor immune activation, establishing an oxygen-independent mode of photocatalytic cancer therapy.

articles.title: Predicting battery stability from electron-ion transport mismatch
articles.abstract: A battery stability prediction model covering LIBs, SIBs, and ZIBs has been proposed. The electron-ion transport mismatch is identified as a key determinant of battery stability. A linear correlation between the battery stability and the electron-ion transport mismatch has been revealed: the closer the transport rates of electrons and ions, the more stable the battery. The battery stability could be predicted rapidly from the electron-ion mismatch, with no need for time-consuming long-term cycling.

articles.title: Atomic-Scale Origin of Spatially Heterogeneous Insertion in Hollandite-Type MnO2
articles.abstract: Hollandite-type α-MnO2 is a prototypical tunnel-structured host for rechargeable batteries, yet the atomic-scale mechanisms governing multivalent-ion insertion remain poorly understood. Here, we reveal how guest-ion species dictate electrochemical reaction pathways through distinct occupation modes within the one-dimensional tunnels of α-MnO2. By combining electrochemical analyses, atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, and soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy, we directly correlate reaction kinetics with guest-ion configurations and the accompanying structural and electronic responses of the host framework. Electrochemical measurements reveal substantial diffusion-controlled contributions for both Na+ and Mg2+, whereas Ca2+ exhibits predominantly surface-controlled behavior. Atomic-resolution imaging demonstrates that, despite their comparable macroscopic kinetic contributions, Na+ and Mg2+ exhibit distinctly different microscopic insertion modes: Na+ homogeneously occupies the tunnel-center sites throughout the particles, whereas Mg2+ occupies both tunnel-center and off-center sites, with pronounced near-surface enrichment accompanied by local tunnel distortion. In contrast, the Ca2+ reaction is largely confined to the near-surface region, with no clearly detectable occupation of the internal tunnel sites. Soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy further reveals spatially heterogeneous Mn reduction, with more pronounced reduction near the structurally less constrained particle surface. These results establish a direct relationship between guest-ion occupation modes, electrochemical reaction pathways, and the resulting structural evolution, providing an atomic-scale design principle for engineering tunnel-type host materials for multivalent-ion insertion.

articles.title: Electronic Structure Perspective on Cation and Anion Redox in Li2FeS2
articles.abstract: Multielectron redox in Li2FeS2 involves both cation and anion contributions. While prior studies have investigated this process experimentally, questions remain about the Fe-to-S redox transition, persulfide formation, and incomplete delithiation. Here, we revisit the electrochemistry of Li2FeS2 using density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Initial Fe oxidation is shown to proceed via increased Fe−S covalency driven by ligand-to-metal rehybridization. This accounts for only ∼60% of the Fe capacity, after which phase separation into Li1.5FeS2 and Li0.5FeS2 induces a shift to S oxidation. We identify nonbonding S 3p orbitals as redox-active centers. To track their evolution during delithiation, we isolate the localized nonbonding states by subtracting the bonding and antibonding contributions from the total electronic densities of states. These orbitals undergo S-to-Fe rehybridization, progressive oxidation, and eventual reorganization into persulfide bonds. At high states of charge, Li vacancies enable FeS4 tilting and facilitate S−S bond formation. Further delithiation beyond Li0.5FeS2 would require unstable S hole formation or conversion to pyrite FeS2, explaining why it is challenging to fully delithiate this material. These findings offer insights into the interplay of cation and anion redox, guiding the design of high-capacity sulfide cathodes.

articles.title: Microenvironment-Responsive Polyaniline− Gelatin Conductive Hydrogel Promotes Infected Diabetic Wound Healing by Modulating Skin-Resident Cells Behavior
articles.abstract: Diabetic wound healing is severely impaired by persistent inflammation, bacterial infection, impaired angiogenesis, and especially disrupted bioelectrical signaling. Conductive hydrogels can help restore local bioelectrical signal transmission and provide an attractive strategy for intractable wound healing by modulating the behaviors of bioelectrically responsive skin-resident cells. Here, we developed a glucose/pH-responsive polyaniline− gelatin conductive hydrogel (HGP@D) based on double dynamic covalent crosslinking of the imine bond and boronic ester bond for promoting the Staphylococcus aureus-infected full-thickness diabetic wound healing. The HGP@D hydrogel had strong mechanical property, great tissue adhesive strength, glucose/pH dual-responsive drug release behavior, alongside robust broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, and potent intracellular antioxidation. The HGP@D hydrogel restored local bioelectrical signaling and created an anti-inflammatory wound microenvironment, thereby modulating the behaviors of skin-resident cells involved in diabetic wound repair, including fibroblast migration, macrophage M2-like polarization, and endothelial angiogenic activity. Mechanistic analyses suggested that the HGP@D hydrogel promoted infected diabetic wound healing through two Ca2+-associated regulatory axes: the Ca2+/CaMKKβ/AMPK/NF-κB axis for inflammatory regulation and the Ca2+/PI3K/Akt/mTOR/HIF-1α/VEGF axis for angiogenesis and tissue reconstruction. Overall, HGP@D provides a promising clinical therapeutic strategy for the advanced healing of diabetic wounds and other non-healing wounds by integrating glucose/pH-responsive microenvironment regulation with bioelectrical modulation.

articles.title: A Waterfowl Reproduction Model to Predict Carryover Effects of Oil Spills
articles.abstract: For wintering and migrating birds, contamination from oil and other substances may delay arrival on the breeding grounds and lead to lower body mass upon arrival. These delays and losses of body mass could lead to smaller clutch sizes and lower propensity to renest. To determine potential effects of these consequences on breeding, we used an augmented version of an existing mallard (Anas platyrhynchos) reproduction model. By combining that reproduction model with the outputs of a previously developed migration and energetics model, we assessed carryover effects of simulated wintering ground oil spills on duckling production and other breeding season‐related population parameters. For simulated oil spills that occurred in January, reduced adult population and sublethal effects of migration delays both contributed to decreases in duckling production. For a simulated oil spill that occurred in March, sublethal effects from reduced body mass were the primary driver of decreased duckling production. By combining migration and energetics modeling with a reproduction model, this framework could provide the basis for a tool to generate quantitative estimates of lost reproduction resulting from carryover effects. Furthermore, this modeling framework could also be adapted for other avian species, facilitating assessments of reproductive loss in the context of Natural Resource Damage Assessments following contamination events.

articles.title: Elephant Presence Shapes Butterfly Communities in an East African Coastal Forest
articles.abstract: Habitat disturbances shape the diversity and composition of plant and animal species. It is important to distinguish between natural disturbances caused by megaherbivores and anthropogenic disturbances caused by human activity, as different disturbance regimes differently affect biodiversity. In this study, we analyse butterfly diversity and community structure in three forest areas with different habitat disturbances in the Arabuko Sokoke dry coastal forest of south‐eastern Kenya. We assessed butterfly diversity with bait‐traps in primary forest with and without elephants, and in secondary forest characterised by previous human use and where elephants are currently present. In total, we activated 24 traps, eight traps per forest type. We found differences in the butterfly diversity and community structure depending on forest type and disturbance regime. The rather dense primary forest harboured a considerably higher proportion of dark‐coloured forest butterfly species than the secondary forest, particularly in areas with elephant disturbance. The secondary forest has higher butterfly species richness than the primary forest due to the occurrence of savannah species. Correspondence analyses clearly separated the three forest types with respect to community composition. Species occurring also in anthropogenic habitats were significantly more abundant in the secondary forest than in the two primary forest types. Our findings underline that forest type and disturbance regime shape butterfly diversity and community structure. Our study underlines that the effects of natural disturbances and human‐induced disturbances on butterfly diversity differ fundamentally. Natural disturbances such as by elephant activities seem to promote typical forest butterflies.

articles.title: Marine Heatwave and Extreme Hypoxia Coincide With Rapid Coral Bleaching and Mortality on a Central Red Sea Coral Reef
articles.abstract: Coral bleaching and mortality are commonly associated with heat stress during marine heatwaves (MHWs), yet attributing these responses solely to heat stress may overlook the complexity of contemporary MHWs. Here, we document a severe MHW affecting a central Red Sea reef in mid‐2024 that coincided with repeated nighttime low‐oxygen events. By integrating satellite and in situ records of temperature, dissolved oxygen and wind, alongside repeated surveys of in situ nursery‐reared coral fragments, we document the temporal coincidence of these conditions with rapid coral bleaching and mortality. As temperatures approached and exceeded 33°C during the MHW peak, nighttime oxygen minima were extreme (down to 15.2–57.8 μmol O2 kg−1) and diel temperature variability diminished (down to 0.31°C–0.67°C), indicating a loss of nighttime thermal reprieves. Coincident responses of nursery corals were atypical, with transitions from healthy or bleached states to mortality occurring within 7–8 days. Bleaching and mortality also occurred across diverse coral species in nearby habitats after the MHW peak, with < 1% live coral cover documented eight months later. Sustained high temperatures, reduced vertical mixing and increased nighttime respiratory demand likely constrained oxygen availability, resulting in low‐oxygen extremes. We posit that similar compound MHW extreme events may have gone undetected in the Red Sea and elsewhere, potentially obscuring the contribution of co‐occurring low‐oxygen extremes to coral responses attributed to heat stress.

articles.title: Plastome‐Based Phylogenomics Resolves Phylogenetic Complexity in Lysimachia and Reveals Unexpected Placement of L. thyrsiflora
articles.abstract: The genus Lysimachia is taxonomically complex, especially in East Asia. We analyzed the complete chloroplast (cp) genomes of four Lysimachia species (L. acroadenia, L. leucantha, L. thyrsiflora, and L. arvensis). The cp genomes (153–155 kb) showed the typical quadripartite structure. Comparative analysis identified two highly variable regions, which are promising molecular markers. Most protein‐coding genes showed Ka/Ks ratios below 1, but rps12 and psaI showed elevated Ka/Ks ratios that require further validation using codon‐based selection tests. The Maximum likelihood phylogenetic tree confirmed the monophyly of Lysimachia. Importantly, L. thyrsiflora clustered within subgenus Lysimachia section Lysimachia, contradicting its traditional classification and suggesting a complex biogeographic history, potentially involving historical connections across the Bering Land Bridge. Divergence time analysis estimated the genus origin at approximately 33 Mya. Our results clarify the phylogenetic status of key taxa and provide essential genomic resources for future evolutionary and taxonomic research on Lysimachia.

articles.title: Predator Becomes Prey: Records of Intraguild Predation Between Velvet Worms (Onychophora) and Arthropods (Arthropoda) With an Expanded Review of Predation on Velvet Worms
articles.abstract: From 3954 citizen‐science observations screened, we report novel cases of predation by omnivorous arthropods on velvet worms, including the first confirmed records for harvestmen and a cave wētā. Using photographic evidence derived from citizen‐science observations, we document multiple predation events involving harvestmen (Opiliones: Cranaidae and Triaenonychidae) and a cave wētā (Orthoptera: Rhaphidophoridae), encompassing both intraguild predation and higher‐order opportunistic predation within cryptic terrestrial habitats. These interactions represent previously undocumented trophic links between phylogenetically distant lineages and expand the known repertoire of omnivorous arthropods as predators of onychophorans. Our findings document a previously unrecorded vulnerability in Onychophora, a group traditionally regarded as specialized predators defended by an adhesive slime system, and underscore the trophic flexibility of arthropod predators operating within leaf‐litter and subterranean ecosystems. Collectively, these observations document previously unrecorded trophic links in cryptic environments and illustrate the value of natural history data and citizen‐science platforms for detecting rarely documented interactions.

articles.title: Songbirds as a Potential Vector for Snail Dispersal
articles.abstract: For species with limited mobility, leveraging highly mobile species through animal transport can provide a mechanism for dispersal and range expansion. As such, migratory birds may serve as vectors to disperse mobility‐limited species long distances to potentially novel geographies. To further document the potential use of migratory songbirds as vectors of animal transport for land snails, we provide two accounts of amber snails (Succinea sp.) attached to songbirds during post‐breeding migration. Both accounts took place in southwest Louisiana; the first instance occurred on a White‐throated Sparrow (Zonotrichia albicollis) and the second occurred on a Northern Waterthrush (Parkesia noveboracensis). Observations like these can improve our understanding of species interactions that may impact ecology, distributions, and life histories.

articles.title: Suppressing dynamic energetic disorder for efficient organic solar cells
articles.abstract: Molecular-level energetic fluctuations in organic semiconductors remain a critical challenge for achieving efficient organic solar cells (OSCs). However, how molecular organization regulates dynamic energetic disorder remains largely unexplored. Here, we...

articles.title: Boron-driven closed-pore formation and interphase stabilization in hard carbon anodes for sodium-ion batteries
Cross-modal topology decodes battery faults from sparse voltage snapshots
Co-producing ‘nature’: autonomous grazing in the Dutch Room for the River programme
articles.abstract: Conservation biology has traditionally sought to justify public investment made specifically for biodiversity. I explore an alternative proposition: whether biodiversity can be co-produced through investments that society already undertakes for other public purposes. Using the Dutch Room for the River programme as a case study, I examine how autonomous grazing contributes to the long-term management and functional improvement of restored river wetlands created primarily to improve flood safety. Rather than evaluating autonomous grazing as a restoration philosophy, I analyse it as a management technology operating within contractual hydraulic boundary conditions defined by the national river management authority. This study demonstrates that self-organising groups of large herbivores can maintain floodplain vegetation within prescribed hydraulic limits whilst contributing to wetland functions and reducing the need for repeated mechanical intervention. Nationally standardised Dutch cost estimates indicate that vegetation management based predominantly on autonomous grazing costs approximately one quarter as much as management relying largely on repeated mowing and biomass removal. Biodiversity therefore emerges not as the primary objective of public investment, but as a valuable co-produced public good arising from the management of an engineered landscape. This study also illustrates the practical application of the Ecosystem Approach adopted under the Convention on Biological Diversity. Indeed, a clearly defined societal choice (flood protection) can be achieved through management that allows self-organising ecological processes to contribute simultaneously to economic efficiency, wetland functioning and biodiversity. It demonstrates that biodiversity need not always justify public investment, but can instead emerge as a valuable co-produced public good.

articles.title: The price of adulthood: ontogenetic patterns of mandibular wear in a drywood termite
articles.abstract: IntroductionIn eusocial insects, the division of labor often entails significant mechanical costs for working individuals. In one-piece nesting termites, such as the Chilean endemic drywood termite, Neotermes chilensis, the colony's labor is performed by totipotent immatures that inhabit and consume structurally sound wood. This translates directly into severe mandibular wear. While the intense wood-processing activity of immatures has traditionally been viewed as an altruistic behavior that benefits the colony, recent evolutionary frameworks suggest it may represent a selfish developmental cost, the mechanical "price of adulthood", to fuel their own ontogeny into winged reproductives (alates). Conversely, alates, which can no longer molt to renew cuticular structures, must preserve their mandibles to excavate a nuptial chamber and found a new colony.MethodsTo investigate this, we quantified structural wear using a Mandibular Wear Index (MWI) and high-resolution scanning electron microscopy (SEM) across different developmental stages and sexes of N. chilensis (N = 147). To rule out size-related allometric artifacts, absolute mandibular dimensions were evaluated using an interactive Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) log -log model and estimated marginal means at a standardized common size (512.4 µm).ResultsOur results revealed no sexual dimorphism in wear but highly significant differences among castes that persisted independently of absolute mandibular size. Nymphs exhibited the most severe mandibular wear, consistent with their feeding activity to sustain energetic developmental demands. In stark contrast, swarmed alates possessed the sharpest, least worn mandibles. Primary reproductives and pseudergates displayed intermediate levels of wear.DiscussionThese findings reveal a caste-specific balance between mandibular wear in working immatures and preservation of mandibular structure in adult dispersers.

articles.title: Fitness and flexibility of metabolic phenotypes in a temperate resident bird
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Resident songbirds in seasonal environments are adapted to fluctuating conditions and show marked phenotypic flexibility of metabolic rates. However, the potential strength and direction of selection for metabolic phenotypes may depend on the context of the seasonal and environmental conditions, which standardized metabolic rate is measured, and which life-history traits (i.e., survival and reproduction) are considered. To investigate how metabolic rates co-vary and to characterize individuals by a metabolic phenotype, we measured three different metabolic rates that we expected to be important for fitness – the maintenance metabolic rate (BMR), maximum cold-induced metabolic rate (M sum) and maximum exercise-induced metabolic rate (MMR) – in a population of blue tits (Cyanistes caeruleus) in southern Sweden. We then monitored different predictors of fitness for those individuals; apparent survival and breeding success. All three metabolic rates were positively related, and the relationship between M sum and MMR was positive independent of body mass. MMR was repeatable between seasons, suggesting consistent individual differences consistent with metabolic phenotypes. From breeding data, individuals with higher metabolic rates in spring were marginally more likely to return to breed the following year. However, high metabolic rates were associated with somewhat lower reproductive success. This study contributes to our understanding of how individual phenotypic variation and flexibility manifests in a population of temperate resident birds. While clear associations between metabolic rates and fitness remain elusive, our results provide tentative support for context-dependent selection on metabolic rates. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Weapon regeneration can promote unreliable signalling when reduced strength goes undetected
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Animal weapons often signal fighting ability, and signalling theory predicts that weapon size should reliably reflect weapon performance. Weapon loss and regeneration can disrupt this relationship by decoupling signal magnitude from functional capacity, but the consequences of such mismatches should depend on whether opponents can detect regenerated structures and whether signal reliability is tested during contests. We tested these hypotheses in the crayfish Cherax destructor by experimentally removing one chela from 40 individuals and comparing weapon morphology, strength, growth, swimming performance and contest outcomes with 40 control individuals after 12 months of regeneration. Regenerated chelae were smaller, more slender and weaker for their size than original chelae, demonstrating a decoupling between weapon size and strength. Despite this reduction in performance, regeneration imposed few detectable costs on body growth or swimming performance. Contest experiments revealed that weapon size alone predicted success in interactions resolved by signalling, whereas both weapon size and strength predicted success when contests escalated to physical combat. Consequently, individuals bearing regenerated weapons gained the benefits of enlarged weapons during signalling interactions despite possessing inferior weapons during fights. Our findings are consistent with the expectation that unreliable signals can persist when opponents do not detect reduced performance and only occasionally test signal reliability through escalation. However, additional experiments are needed to isolate the sensory mechanisms underlying receiver assessment and to directly test detection of regenerated weapons. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Embracing the Heterogeneity Within Particulate and Mineral‐Associated Organic Matter for the Next Generation of Soil Carbon Questions
articles.abstract: Soil organic matter (SOM) is a complex and dynamic substrate central to the functioning of terrestrial ecosystems. Because of its heterogeneity, SOM is routinely parsed into physical fractions with more uniform composition and behavior. Over the last several years, particulate (POM) and mineral‐associated (MAOM) organic matter have become the most widely adopted of these fractions, which has given the field a shared, comparable framework for resolving the first‐order heterogeneity within SOM. As fractionation has become routine, however, it has become clear that POM and MAOM identity alone cannot resolve the finer, second‐order variation that additional mechanistic inference requires. This is in part because the fractions are operationally defined composites, whose properties vary across composition, formation pathway, and behavior. Conceptualizing them as the terminal state of analysis collapses each fraction to its central tendency, flattening the distribution and obscuring the structure on which more complex questions depend. Here we propose embracing this within‐fraction heterogeneity rather than averaging over it, treating POM and MAOM as composite distributions whose internal structure underlies the variation in how they form, persist, and function. We suggest that this view can be operationalized via two complementary approaches: tailoring fractionation methods to target subpopulations most relevant to a question, and pairing fractions with orthogonal measurements. Together, these resolve the within‐fraction distribution that bulk measurements integrate over, narrowing the analysis onto the most explanatory slice of the bulk SOM. Similar to the original framework, we do not aim to prescribe a certain methodology, but rather a way of thinking about heterogeneity within SOM, in which a separation is justified by the understanding it produces rather than the data it generates. This way of reasoning allows POM and MAOM to continue linking organic matter to its functions, and in doing so supports more informed stewardship of soil carbon.

articles.title: Resolving the Multiple Controls of Biomass Production Efficiency in Woody Plants
articles.abstract: Plants assimilate carbon through photosynthesis to support biomass production (BP), autotrophic respiration (R a) and the synthesis of non-structural compounds. Biomass production efficiency (BPE), the fraction of assimilated carbon allocated to BP, is one key factor influencing ecosystems' potential to store carbon. However, there is no consensus on the controls of BPE, and even the sign of its response to growth temperature is unclear. By means of statistical hypothesis testing using the largest observational dataset to date on annual BPE (n = 514 records) from evergreen and deciduous woody plants, we confirm earlier findings that BPE declines with stand age and is greater in deciduous plants. However, we also show that BPE declines toward more organic, sandy, or alkaline soils and increases with climatic aridity, while declining with warmer growing seasons and increasing with warmer winters. Such a dual temperature response is consistent with additional carbon costs due to the need for cold-hardening processes, and reconciles contradictory published reports of both positive and negative effects of temperature on BPE. Notably, our analysis provides novel evidence that BPE is significantly higher in species associated with arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi than in those associated with ectomycorrhizal (EcM) fungi and mixed EcM–AM associations. Our analysis explains the observed BPE patterns better than dynamic global vegetation models (DGVMs) from the TRENDY (Trends and Drivers of the Regional-Scale Terrestrial Sources and Sinks of Carbon Dioxide) project, which show a weaker correspondence with observations. In particular, our model captures reduced BPE in boreal regions, consistent with the predominance of ectomycorrhizal (EcM) species there. This study advances understanding of the global controls of BPE, and suggests a route toward the improved representation of plant growth in vegetation and land surface models.

articles.title: Rethinking the Role of Cattle in Wetlands: An Underexplored Dimension of Biodiversity Connectivity

An AI‐driven soil extractor for high‐throughput measurement of soil microarthropod taxon densities using live individuals
articles.abstract: Soil invertebrates play a key role in ecosystem functioning, yet their monitoring remains constrained by labour‐intensive extraction and taxonomic identification procedures. Consequently, large‐scale and high‐frequency assessments of soil biodiversity remain difficult despite increasing demand for standardized monitoring tools. Here, we present an AI‐driven soil extractor that combines classical dry extraction with real‐time computer vision and deep‐learning‐based classification of soil microarthropods. Organisms are detected and classified while moving through the device, allowing automated quantification of taxon densities while individuals remain alive and available for subsequent analyses. System performance was evaluated using a validation framework that separately assessed AI classification accuracy, the integrated detection and transport workflow, and extraction performance relative to conventional Berlese funnels. Automated image classification achieved an overall accuracy of 80.9% (95% CI: 79.9%–81.8%; Cohen's κ = 0.767) when compared with expert image identification. Automated detections and manual identification of the same extracts showed high agreement in community composition, with a median Bray–Curtis similarity of 0.80, indicating limited mechanical bias introduced by specimen transport. Abundance estimates obtained with the automated system closely matched those produced by conventional Berlese extraction, with only minor taxon‐specific differences. Controlled experiments further demonstrated high mechanical reliability, with detection success exceeding 97% and transport success exceeding 92%. The system provides a scalable approach for quantitative monitoring of soil microarthropod communities while preserving live specimens for downstream analyses. By integrating extraction, image acquisition, classification and specimen collection into a single workflow, the AI‐driven soil extractor offers a practical tool for high‐throughput soil mesofauna monitoring.

articles.title: Early Metabolic Reprogramming in the Placenta Shapes Resilience to Gestational Hypoxia in High‐Elevation Deer Mice
articles.abstract: Environmental hypoxia at high elevations is linked to increased rates of gestational complications. Evolutionary adaptation to high elevation environments mitigates these complications across mammals, in part through changes in placental function that shape foetal growth potential in late pregnancy. To investigate the developmental origins of placental adaptation to hypoxia, we acclimated pregnant deer mice (Peromyscus maniculatus) derived from low‐ and high‐elevation populations to normoxia or hypoxia (equivalent to 4300 m) and characterized the structure and transcriptome of foetal placentas. We show that gestational hypoxia induced remodelling of the placental transcriptome in susceptible, lowland‐derived mice, but not in highland‐derived mice. A subset of this transcriptional plasticity displayed genetic assimilation, in which highland placentas expressed the induced value observed in lowlanders. However, we also found evidence that highland‐derived mice reversed some of the ancestral lowland responses to hypoxia. Specifically, gestational hypoxia tended to suppress metabolic pathways in the placentas of lowland mice, whereas these responses were attenuated in highland mice. This divergence was centred on mitochondrial metabolic pathways. More broadly, we show that both constitutive population‐level differences and remodelling of ancestral plasticity in the placenta tune expression within a stable transcriptional network architecture. Our results point to the developing placenta's metabolic responses to hypoxia as an early and developmentally specific functional target that likely contributes to pathologies associated with gestational hypoxia in humans and other mammals.

(PEA)2(FA)Pb2I7/PVDF Composite Flexible Films Enable Self-Powered X-ray Detection with High Sensitivity and a Low Detection Limit
articles.abstract: Metal halide perovskites (MHPs) have attracted significant interest in the field of X-ray detection due to their unique semiconducting properties. However, the self-powered detection capabilities of almost all of these materials rely on their inherent ferroelectricity or heterojunction structures, yet the structure design and fabrication still pose significant challenges. By incorporating a polymer into a centrosymmetric MHP, we successfully prepared (PEA)2(FA)Pb2I7/PVDF composite flexible films (PEA = β-phenylethylamine, FA = formamidine, PVDF = poly(vinylidene fluoride)) and obtained self-powered X-ray responses in a nonpolar perovskite. Notably, the photodetector based on thin films exhibits excellent self-powered X-ray detection performance with a high sensitivity (559.11 μC Gyair–1 cm–2), a low detection limit (29.09 nGyair s–1), and excellent radiation stability. Our work offers a new strategy for self-driven devices without relying on ferroelectricity or heterojunctions, expanding halide perovskites in flexible film applications.

articles.title: Anisotropic Nanoscale Coherent Polariton Transport in CrSBr
articles.abstract: In a combined experimental and theoretical study, we demonstrate anisotropic polariton transport on the nanoscale in the van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr. While effective cavity-polariton formation emerges via the self-hybridization of ultrahigh oscillator strength excitons with a thin slab photonic mode, the absence of external mirrors facilitates spectroscopic investigation of these polaritons via cathodoluminescence (CL) on length scales inaccessible to optical excitation. This direct access allows us to precisely chart the polariton landscape with nanometric resolution, and probe polariton interference phenomena. Our finding highlights that coherent polariton transport follows the C2v symmetry of CrSBr, highly directional transport along the a-axis, while no coherent features are found along the b-axis. By extending CL spectroscopy to strongly anisotropic cavity polaritons, our work establishes this technique as a powerful tool to probe highly directional expansion and relaxation phenomena on the nanoscale, paving the way for investigating complex polaritonic landscapes in asymmetric systems.

articles.title: Decoupling the Intrinsic Li/Mn Disorder Mechanism in Li-Rich Layered Oxides
articles.abstract: Li-rich layered oxides (LLOs) are promising high-energy cathodes but suffer from irreversible oxygen redox and structural degradation associated with Li2MnO3 domains. Recently, disorder engineering has emerged as an effective strategy to regulate the local coordination environment and stabilize the oxygen redox of LLOs. Herein, we confirm the existence of intrinsic intralayer Li/Mn disorder within the Li2MnO3 domains, which can be classified into local Li-excess and TM-excess configurations derived from the initial Li-rich framework. Furthermore, DFT calculations suggest complementary local roles for the different disordered configurations: Li-excess domains promote oxygen redox activity, whereas TM-excess domains reinforce TM–O bonding and stabilize the framework against irreversible degradation. Consequently, M-LLO containing the coupled disordered configurations promotes more reversible anionic redox, suppresses irreversible oxygen release and transition-metal migration, and thereby delivers improved electrochemical stability. This work provides new insights into the role of intrinsic disorder regulation in Li-rich layered cathodes.

articles.title: Divalent Cations Induce Rigid and Compact Structures in Underwound DNA
articles.abstract: Negative supercoiling (underwinding) of DNA plays a vital role in regulating genome organization and gene expression. These processes often depend on the DNA structure, yet the influence of ionic strength on supercoiled DNA structure is still not well understood. Here, we develop an approach to extract detailed insight into the mechanical properties of underwound DNA from force–distance measurements. Using this approach, we demonstrate that low concentrations (2 mM) of divalent cations are sufficient to induce substantial increases in DNA persistence length at high superhelical densities. This is consistent with the formation of Z-DNA, a rigid, left-handed conformation, and suggests that Z-DNA-like structures can be more readily formed than is often assumed. We also show that divalent cations can induce extensive sawtooth-like behavior in force–extension curves of underwound DNA, revealing unexpectedly strong stabilization of secondary structures. Together, these findings demonstrate how divalent salt can sensitively modulate the stability of different underwound structures.

articles.title: Gigahertz-Clocked Generation of Highly Indistinguishable Photons at C-Band Wavelengths
articles.abstract: High-performance single-photon sources at telecom C-band wavelengths are key building blocks for applications in long-distance quantum communication. Here, we report the generation of highly indistinguishable single photons at a clock rate of 2.5 GHz. This is achieved by coherently driving the biexciton transition (T1XX=64(1) ps) of a semiconductor quantum dot embedded in a microcavity with strong asymmetric Purcell enhancement. Employing pulsed two-photon resonant excitation, strong multiphoton suppression with g(2)(0) < 4% and high two-photon-interference visibility of Vraw > 85% are observed. The observed photon indistinguishability is close to the theoretical limit expected for the photonically engineered radiative cascade and matches values obtained at lower repetition rates. Our results show a substantial advancement toward interference-based quantum information protocols at unprecedented data rates in the telecom C-band.

articles.title: In-Plane Heterostructures Enable Deterministic and Repeated Biomolecular Sensing by Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
articles.abstract: Applications of plasmonic nanopores for molecular sequencing remain limited by poorly controlled translocation dynamics and predominantly single-pass readout. Here, we propose an in-plane heterostructure architecture that integrates molecular transport, confinement, and surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) readout to enable deterministic and repeated interrogation of individual biomolecules. Using all-atom molecular dynamics coupled with nanoplasmonic simulations, we show that the heterostructure can actively guide molecules into and through a localized sensing region while constraining their conformational and translational dynamics. Simulated SERS signatures discriminate single-stranded DNA sequences with resolution approaching the single-nucleobase scale and further suggest the feasibility of distinguishing polyglutamine tracts of different lengths. Importantly, the in-plane geometry allows molecules to be controllably transported back and forth across the sensing region, providing a route to repeated measurements of the same molecule rather than relying on stochastic single-pass translocation. These results suggest a strategy for improving the accuracy and reproducibility of nanopore-based biomolecular sensing.

articles.abstract: BackgroundSevere hypertriglyceridemia is associated with an increased risk of acute pancreatitis. Plozasiran, a small interfering RNA targeting APOC3 messenger RNA, lowers triglyceride levels and potentially mitigates the risk of acute pancreatitis.MethodsIn two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, 757 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive plozasiran (25 mg) or placebo at baseline and at months 3, 6, and 9. These trials had identical designs, end points, and analytic plans. The primary end point was the percent change in the fasting plasma triglyceride level from baseline to month 12. Key secondary end points were the percent change in the fasting triglyceride level from baseline to month 10, a fasting triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.6 mmol per liter) and less than 150 mg per deciliter (1.7 mmol per liter), the percent change in the fasting serum triglyceride level at month 12 for patients with a baseline triglyceride level of 880 mg per deciliter or greater, and changes in remnant cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol. A pooled analysis addressed adjudicated acute pancreatitis, incidence, and first-event timing.ResultsAt month 12, patients in the plozasiran groups had a median triglyceride level that was lower than the baseline level by 79% and 81% in the two trials. These reductions corresponded to a median difference in the plozasiran groups as compared with the placebo groups (placebo-adjusted change) of -45 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -51 to -38) and -47 percentage points (95% CI, -54 to -39). A triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter at 12 months was reported in 91% and 93% of the patients in the plozasiran groups and in 51% and 50% of those in the placebo groups (PConclusionsAmong patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, the use of plozasiran resulted in lower triglyceride levels and a lower risk of acute pancreatitis than placebo at 12 months. Duality of root‐dominated net soil organic carbon gain and mycelium‐mediated carbon loss in hyper‐arid afforestation
articles.abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) pool dynamics during hyper‐arid afforestation by root pathway and mycelium pathway. Summary Afforestation regulates soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration via plant‐ and microbial‐derived carbon (C) inputs, but root‐ and mycelium‐derived C inputs differ in quantity, turnover, and stabilization mechanisms, and these differences may shift as stands develop. However, how root vs mycelium pathways drive SOC dynamics across a dryland afforestation chronosequence remains unclear. Using the ingrowth‐core method along a dryland afforestation chronosequence (young forests, middle‐aged forests, and mature forests), we quantified the contributions of root and mycelium pathways to SOC. The root pathway promoted SOC accumulation via particulate organic C and mineral‐associated organic C inputs, contributing to 77.19–85.05% of the SOC changes. By contrast, the mycelium pathway induced net SOC loss via particulate organic C depletion, contributing to 14.95–22.81% of the SOC changes. SOC concentrations peaked in middle‐aged forests, whereas relative SOC stability peaked in young forests. This study provides the first quantitative assessment of the distinct contributions of root and mycelium pathways to SOC accumulation and stabilization during dryland afforestation, advancing understanding of their roles in regulating SOC dynamics. As climate change intensifies land‐use pressure, management strategies should integrate stage‐specific root and mycelial traits to enhance SOC sequestration in arid forests.

A frugal automated contact angle analyser for low-cost surface wettability characterization
articles.abstract: Contact angle measurement is a fundamental technique for evaluating surface wettability in materials science, biomedical engineering and coating technologies. However, the high cost of commercial contact angle analysers limits access to surface characterization, particularly in resource-limited laboratories. This study presents a low-cost automated contact angle analyser developed using frugal engineering principles and open-source hardware. The system integrates Arduino-based control, NEMA 17 stepper-motor actuation, automated microdroplet dispensing, smartphone-based optical imaging and a 3D-printed polylactic acid (PLA) framework. A calibrated 330-step dispensing cycle generated reproducible 5 μl water droplets, with fixed optical alignment minimized operator variability. Wettability measurements were performed on polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and aluminium substrates and analysed using ImageJ. Mean contact angles were 108.5° for PTFE, 73.9° for PVC and 85.8° for aluminium, closely matching published literature values. One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) demonstrated significant differences between substrates (p < 0.001), with measurement variability of ±2.3° indicated good repeatability. The total fabrication cost was £114.26, representing approximately 99% cost reduction compared with commercial instruments. The proposed platform demonstrates that automated, reproducible surface wettability characterization can be achieved using low-cost, open-source instrumentation, providing an accessible solution for research, education and engineering laboratories while broadening access to advanced materials characterization.

articles.title: Beyond sperm competition: perspectives on sperm economy from external fertilizing fishes
articles.abstract: Research on sperm economy has traditionally focused on sperm competition as a major selective pressure shaping sperm production and allocation. In this review, we broaden this perspective by considering how other reproductive and ecological pressures influence the management of a costly and finite sperm supply. We synthesize evidence showing that in externally fertilizing fishes, high mating frequency, low female fecundity, prolonged spawning, rapid sperm dilution and costly male reproductive investment can favour sperm-economy strategies even when sperm competition is weak or absent. Across fish taxa, these constraints have led to convergent behavioural and physiological adaptations, including fractionated ejaculation, temporal matching of sperm release to egg deposition and manipulation of the fertilization microenvironment, which improve fertilization efficiency while minimizing sperm expenditure. We further highlight a recurring association between these strategies and semi-cystic spermatogenesis, consistent with the possibility that optimization of sperm use extends beyond ejaculate allocation to the regulation of sperm production during spermatogenesis. By integrating evidence from behaviour to reproductive physiology, this review reframes sperm economy as a general resource-allocation problem, with sperm competition representing one of several selective pressures. Externally fertilizing fishes emerge as an exceptional model for understanding the diverse evolutionary routes by which males optimize reproductive investment.

articles.title: Decoding the dead: new combined application of strontium and lead isotope analysis to Romano-British cremations from Colchester (UK)
articles.abstract: This paper presents an innovative application of two distinct isotope systems to paired otic capsule and outer petrous bone samples from cremated remains. This dual analysis approach, applied to 22 human cremation burials from Roman Colchester (UK), demonstrates evidence for origins outside Britain for several individuals, shedding fresh light on an emerging capital city within a new province of the Roman Empire. Results have implications for understanding the population dynamics of large Roman provincial urban centres following the conquest period in the north-western provinces, when cremation is the dominant burial practice. The method also allows a detailed reconstruction of individual mobility at different ages within an individual's life.

articles.title: Design principles for natural SGLT2 modulators from multi-scale computation
articles.abstract: Human sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (hSGLT2) is a membrane-embedded renal transporter and an established therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes. Hyperoside, myricetin, cyanidin-3-O-glucoside and isoliquiritigenin were investigated as a chemically diverse panel of natural scaffolds using a multi-scale computational workflow combining redocking-validated molecular docking, reconstruction of an unresolved transporter segment, molecular dynamics (MD) in an explicit POPC bilayer, molecular mechanics/Poisson–Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) calculations, principal component and free-energy landscape analyses and density functional theory (DFT). The membrane simulations preserved the global hSGLT2 fold while revealing distinct ligand-dependent binding behaviours. Myricetin and cyanidin-3-O-glucoside exhibited limited positional deviations; hyperoside achieved persistent accommodation following an initial adjustment, whereas isoliquiritigenin underwent a marked late rearrangement. Ensemble-based energetic analysis prioritized cyanidin-3-O-glucoside, while hyperoside and myricetin formed an energetically comparable intermediate group and isoliquiritigenin displayed the least favourable profile. Electronic-structure analysis further characterized cyanidin-3-O-glucoside as the most responsive ligand within the DFT subset. Collectively, these findings indicate that glycone-assisted polar anchoring, aromatic complementarity and restricted conformational flexibility promote persistent hSGLT2 recognition. Direct hSGLT2 inhibition and hSGLT1 counter-screening assays remain necessary to establish potency and selectivity.

articles.title: Discovery of potential ALK inhibitors from Glycosmis phytochemicals via integrated machine learning and umbrella sampling approaches
articles.abstract: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) is a key therapeutic target for various cancers because of its central role in tumor growth and survival signaling. This study employed an integrated computational workflow combining machine learning (ML), molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, umbrella sampling (US), and toxicity prediction to identify potential ALK inhibitors from 307 phytochemicals of the Glycosmis genus. A previously validated CatBoost regression model predicted binding free energies, leading to the selection of 26 compounds with ΔGML < −11 kcal mol−1. Molecular docking identified six top candidates with favorable binding affinities ranging from −5.856 to −9.667 kcal mol⁻¹, which subsequently underwent 200 ns MD simulations. Structural analyses confirmed the stability of all ALK–ligand complexes, while interaction studies revealed extensive hydrophobic contacts and conserved hydrogen bonds involving key ALK residues. US calculations estimated binding free energies from −8.354 to −13.272 kcal mol−1, with compound 54 exhibiting the strongest affinity (ΔGUS = −13.272 kcal mol−1). Several alkaloids, including acrifoline, heptazoline, and atalaphyllidine, also demonstrated promisingbinding properties and reported anticancer activities. Toxicity prediction indicated acceptable safety profiles, highlighting Glycosmis-derived phytochemicals as promising potential ALK inhibitor candidates and supporting the utility of ML-guided virtual screening combined with advanced molecular simulations for natural product-based anticancer drug discovery. Nevertheless, biochemical and cellular experiments are required to confirm their ALK inhibitory activity, selectivity, and therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Drivers of zoonotic spillover at human–domestic animal–wildlife interfaces: a multi-species model incorporating wildlife chronic stress
articles.abstract: Zoonotic disease emergence at the wildlife–domestic animal–human interface results from a complex interplay of ecological, physiological and anthropogenic factors. Here, we have developed a multi-environment, multi-host compartmental model to identify key drivers of spillover risk across urban, rural and natural environments. The framework incorporates heterogeneous host populations, inter-species contacts and host movement, and includes wildlife chronic stress as one factor influencing susceptibility, transmissibility and recovery. Sensitivity analyses show that domestic animal populations at agricultural interfaces strongly amplify spillover risk through their recovery dynamics and per-contact transmission probabilities, while within-wildlife transmission across environments also shapes system dynamics. Chronic stress effects can further increase spillover risk, and the model indicates that reducing wildlife stress alongside improving domestic animal health and management can markedly lower the likelihood of cross-species transmission. These findings highlight the importance of maintaining ecological conditions that reduce chronic physiological stress in wildlife populations and integrating physiological and ecological data into epidemiological modelling. Such models can inform both bottom-up interventions targeting domestic animals and top-down strategies that sustain resilient wildlife communities and, thereby, mitigate zoonotic spillover.

articles.title: First direct measurement of food transit time through the gastrointestinal tracts of plant-eating primates using isotopic tagging
articles.abstract: The time it takes for food to transit animal gastrointestinal tracts is essential information to fields from organismal evolution to ecosystem ecology. Nevertheless, current estimation methods do not measure food directly, are impractical for many species and often require unnatural conditions to administer. We overcome these limitations by adopting techniques from organic geochemistry. We trace isotopically tagged greens in lemurs, from ingestion to excretion, through isotopic analysis of higher plant biomarkers recovered in faeces. For frugivorous ruffed lemurs (Varecia rubra), omnivorous ring-tailed lemurs (Lemur catta) and frugo-folivorous sifakas (Propithecus coquereli), respectively, the biomarkers first appeared at 1.2, 4.3 and 23.4 h after ingestion and peaked at 2.9, 5.7 and 48.4 h after ingestion. These measurements generally match published estimates from pre-existing proxies. However, not all animals cleared the isotopic signal by the end of sample collection, yielding minimum gut retention times of 23.9–29.5 h for ruffed lemurs, 25.5–30.3 h for ring-tailed lemurs and 95.7 h for sifakas. We thus extend gut retention times approximately threefold from pre-existing proxies. Our interdisciplinary approach is applicable across diverse plant eaters, can help refine models of nutrient, seed and pathogen dispersal and be used to probe consequences of lifestyle and medical interventions on organismal nutrition and health.

articles.title: Generalized maximum entropy: when and why you need it
articles.abstract: The classical maximum entropy principle based on Shannon entropy is widely used to construct least-biased probability distributions from partial information. However, the Shore–Johnson axioms that single out the Shannon functional hinge on strong system independence—an assumption often violated in real-world, strongly correlated systems. When that assumption fails, enforcing the Shannon form imposes an independence the data do not support, and can systematically distort the inferred distribution. We provide a self-contained guide to when and why practitioners should abandon the Shannon form in favour of the one-parameter Uffink–Jizba–Korbel (UJK) family of generalized entropies. After reviewing the Shore–Johnson axioms from an applied perspective, we recall the most commonly used entropy functionals and locate them within the UJK family. The need for generalized entropies is illustrated with two applications, one in economics and the other in ecology. A simple mathematical model worked out in detail further shows the power of generalized maximum-entropy approaches in cases where strong system independence does not hold. We conclude with practical guidelines for choosing an entropy measure and reporting results so that analyses remain transparent and reproducible.

articles.title: Influence of soft coral density and depth on benthic communities on Fiji's Rainbow Reef
articles.abstract: Some soft corals have the potential to increase in prevalence on tropical coral reefs as the severity of anthropogenic climate change increases. While soft corals are therefore an increasingly important component of reef ecosystems, little is known about their ecological role on coral reefs and their influence on community dynamics and diversity. We used Bayesian network inference (BNI) to identify the associations among benthic taxa across sites with varying degrees of soft coral dominance on Fiji's Rainbow Reef, and then employed spatial point process analysis (SPPA) to reveal the ecological processes behind these associations. We found that depth was a dominant driver of community dynamics, and that white Nephtheidae soft corals were negatively associated with scleractinian corals and positively associated with algal proliferation—possibly owing to soft corals reducing grazing pressure. Our results show distinctions in reef benthos and ecological dynamics between scleractinian and soft coral-dominated components of the Rainbow Reef. We found that diversity levels were significantly lower on soft coral-dominated quadrats relative to scleractinian-dominated quadrats, potentially highlighting the reduction in benthic diversity when Nephtheidae soft corals dominate reef walls.

articles.title: Large language model developments
articles.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are generative artificial intelligence (AI) models trained with vast amounts of data and context, and excel at processing, understanding and generating human language, using transformer models to learn statistical relationships between tokens. LLMs are a subset of transformer models, and hence are closely related but not interchangeable. Given the ‘explosion’ of LLM research, the challenge is tracking emerging developments and matching LLMs to applications. This paper reviews LLM developments with the aim of understanding the underlying models’ computational strengths and weaknesses, building on previous work focusing on LLM optimization (Sharkey & Treleaven 2025 Optimising large language models: taxonomy and techniques. SSRN Scholarly Paper no. 5278456. Rochester, NY: SSRN). We find that despite their power, LLMs (transformers) face several key challenges. These include: (i) computational complexity and resource requirements—training and deploying large models is extremely costly and slow, and energy consumption is a concern; (ii) understanding long sequences and dependencies—even with enhancements, models can struggle with very long-range dependencies or context lengths beyond their window (e.g. maintaining coherence in a long document), which reflects the more fundamental absence of continual learning; (iii) interpretability and bias—it remains difficult to interpret why a model produces a given output, and models can inadvertently amplify biases present in training data; and (iv) optimization challenges, including fine-tuning for specific tasks without overfitting or losing generality and ensuring efficient inference (latency, the delay before a response is completed) for real-time applications. In summary, this review focuses on architectural, optimization and interpretability developments in LLMs. It does not aim to provide a systematic benchmark comparison, exhaustive implementation details or empirical performance evaluation, which are covered extensively elsewhere. The authors are committed to updating this review aligned to constant changes in the technology; please reach out with any additions.
