Elevated nitrogen deposition protects an invasive plant from herbivory through altering leaf volatile‐mediated tritrophic interactions
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Atmospheric nitrogen deposition disrupts plant–herbivore interactions, but its impact on leaf volatile organic compounds (VOCs)‐mediated multi‐trophic herbivore resistance remains unclear within the context of plant invasion. In this study, we initially investigated the differences in leaf feeding damage and number of eggs laid by herbivores between the invasive weed Alternanthera philoxeroides and its native congener, Alternanthera sessilis, in different terrestrial habitats that experienced various levels of atmospheric nitrogen deposition. Furthermore, we compared the quantity and composition of leaf constitutive plant volatiles (CPVs) and herbivore‐induced plant volatiles (HIPVs) between the two plant species under simulated nitrogen deposition and tested olfactory and oviposition responses of herbivores and natural enemies at multi‐trophic levels. Field surveys showed less consumed leaf area and fewer herbivore eggs laid on A. philoxeroides than on A. sessilis in terrestrial habitats experiencing high levels of atmospheric nitrogen deposition. Laboratory bioassays revealed that simulated nitrogen deposition increased the emission and altered the composition of both CPVs and HIPVs in A. philoxeroides compared with A. sessilis. These changes reduced its attractiveness to specialist and generalist herbivores while enhancing its appeal to predatory beetles. Methyl salicylate was identified as the key compound driving these changes in insect behaviours, highlighting its critical role in mediating plant–insect interactions in A. philoxeroides under elevated nitrogen deposition. Synthesis. These findings suggest that leaf VOC‐mediated multi‐trophic interactions may facilitate A. philoxeroides invasion success under elevated atmospheric nitrogen deposition in this specific study system, providing a mechanistic basis for understanding how nitrogen enrichment could influence plant–herbivore–predator interactions. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. 摘要 大气氮沉降会干扰植物–植食性昆虫的相互作用，但其在植物入侵背景下对叶片挥发性有机化合物介导的多营养级抗虫性的影响仍不清楚。 本研究首先调查了在不同大气氮沉降水平的陆生生境中，入侵杂草空心莲子草与其本土同属种莲子草在叶片取食损伤程度和植食性昆虫产卵数量上的差异。随后，我们比较了模拟氮沉降条件下两种植物的叶片组成型植物挥发物和虫害诱导型植物挥发物的数量与组成，并测试了多营养级水平上植食性昆虫和天敌的嗅觉与产卵反应。 野外调查表明，在大气氮沉降水平较高的陆生生境中，与莲子草相比，空心莲子草被取食的叶面积更小、植食性昆虫在其上产卵数量更少。室内生物测定显示，与莲子草相比，模拟氮沉降增加了空心莲子草叶片组成型和虫害诱导型挥发物的释放量并改变了其组成。这些变化降低了其对专食性和广食性植食性昆虫的吸引力，同时增强了其对捕食性甲虫的吸引力。水杨酸甲酯被鉴定为驱动这些昆虫行为变化的关键化合物，凸显了其在模拟氮沉降条件下空心莲子草–昆虫相互作用中的关键介导作用。 综合而言，这些发现表明，在该特定研究系统中，叶片挥发物介导的多营养级相互作用可能促进了高氮沉降条件下空心莲子草的入侵成功，为理解氮富集如何影响植物–植食性昆虫–捕食者相互作用提供了机制基础。

Seed‐derived microbiota in the Medicago holobiont: Associations with host phylogeny and breeding‐associated traits
articles.abstract: Seed‐derived bacterial communities tracked host phylogeny across wild Medicago, revealing a phylosymbiotic pattern, whereas fungal communities did not. In cultivated alfalfa, bacterial composition differed between cultivars with high‐yielding and stress‐resistant traits. Trait‐associated bacterial SynComs improved plant growth under non‐stress or combined drought–salinity conditions, respectively, demonstrating the functional relevance of breeding‐associated microbiota. Abstract Seed microbiota occupy unique ecological niches within plants and can form intimate associations with their hosts. However, how seed‐derived microbial communities are related to host phylogeny and breeding‐associated traits across natural and agricultural contexts, and whether trait‐associated microorganisms influence plant performance, remain poorly understood. Here, we characterized endophytic communities in sterile‐grown seedlings from surface‐sterilized seeds of 10 wild Medicago genotypes representing 8 species and 20 domesticated alfalfa cultivars spanning multiple breeding decades. We assessed phylosymbiosis in wild hosts, examined associations between microbial community composition and breeding‐related cultivar characteristics in domesticated alfalfa, and constructed trait‐associated bacterial synthetic communities (SynComs) for functional evaluation. In wild Medicago, bacterial, but not fungal, community composition exhibited significant congruence with host phylogeny, consistent with phylosymbiosis. In domesticated alfalfa, bacterial community composition was associated with cultivar trait category (high‐yielding vs. stress‐resistant), whereas fungal communities were not. Six cultivable candidate bacterial strains associated with the two trait categories were assembled into two SynComs, SynComY (high‐yielding associated) and SynComR (stress‐resistance‐associated). In vitro assays revealed multiple plant growth‐promoting and stress‐tolerance capacities among the constituent strains, while greenhouse experiments showed that SynComY promoted plant growth and SynComR enhanced plant performance under combined drought–salinity stress. Synthesis. Together, these findings show that seed‐derived bacterial community structure is associated with host phylogeny in wild Medicago and breeding‐related trait differentiation in cultivated alfalfa, and further establish that selected bacteria associated with the latter can influence plant performance. Viewed within a holobiont framework, this combined evidence broadens our understanding of seed‐derived microbiota across natural and agricultural contexts and highlights their potential value for microbiome‐informed crop improvement.

articles.title: How the TREX-2 complex associates with the nuclear pore
articles.abstract: Obarska-Kosinska et al. combine cryo-electron tomography, AI-assisted modeling, and crosslinking mass spectrometry to build an extended model of the human nuclear pore. They identify five additional nucleoporins and show how the nuclear basket and TREX-2 complex are attached to the nuclear ring, revealing the spatial organization of mRNP export.

articles.title: Genomic Signatures of Endemic Pathogen Exposure in a Declining Amphibian
articles.abstract: Endemic wildlife diseases can impose strong selection on threatened populations, yet whether persistence is associated with adaptive genomic responses remains poorly understood. We tested whether long‐term exposure to Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd) following population declines has left detectable selection signatures in the genome of the alpine tree frog, Litoria verreauxii alpina. Because prior work suggests limited immunity to Bd within the species, we did not expect persistence to be explained primarily by repeated shifts at canonical immune genes. Instead, we expected pathogen‐associated differentiation, if present, to be diffuse and weakly shared across contrasts, potentially involving regulatory, signalling or reproduction pathways consistent with tolerance, compensatory recruitment or demographic turnover. Using genome‐wide SNP data, we compared Bd‐naïve and Bd‐endemic populations and two 11‐year temporal resampling contrasts. Candidate SNPs were annotated to identify genomic context, nearby genes, putative functions and overlap with previously reported Bd‐associated transcriptomic responses. Using an empirical 99th‐percentile XtX threshold, scans identified high‐differentiation candidate SNPs in all contrasts. Most occurred in noncoding and putatively regulatory regions, with relatively few canonical immune genes. Candidate‐associated genes were more often linked to signalling, transcriptional regulation and cell‐cycle processes. A descriptive comparison with previous work in the species identified 64 candidate‐associated genes matching Bd‐associated transcriptomic annotations, supporting several immune‐adjacent, regulatory, cellular and reproduction candidates. Persistence under endemic Bd might reflect pathogen‐associated selection, compensatory recruitment and demographic change following recurrent adult mortality rather than uniform adaptive rescue through immune resistance.

articles.title: Divarasib as Compared with Sotorasib or Adagrasib in KRAS G12C–Mutated NSCLC
articles.abstract: BackgroundDivarasib, a next-generation, oral KRAS G12C inhibitor, is more potent and selective in vitro than the first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib.MethodsIn this phase 3, international, open-label trial, patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomly assigned to receive divarasib orally at a dose of 400 mg once daily or control treatment (sotorasib orally at a dose of 960 mg once daily or adagrasib orally at a dose of 600 mg twice daily) until the occurrence of disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, loss of clinical benefit, withdrawal of consent, death, or trial termination. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival, confirmed overall response, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, and safety.ResultsA total of 338 patients received divarasib (167 patients) or control treatment (171 patients; 156 received sotorasib and 15 received adagrasib). The median follow-up was 14.3 months. The median progression-free survival was 9.8 months with divarasib and 5.7 months with control treatment (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.44 to 0.76; PConclusionsAmong patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic NSCLC, divarasib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than control treatment. (Supported by F. Hoffmann-La Roche; Krascendo 1 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06497556.).

articles.title: Osimertinib–Savolitinib in Advanced NSCLC after Progression during EGFR-TKI Therapy
articles.abstract: BackgroundSavolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Combination therapy with savolitinib and osimertinib, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-TKI, has shown activity in patients with EGFR-mutated, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both, after progression during EGFR-TKI therapy.MethodsIn this international, phase 3, open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression (staining intensity of 3+ for MET in ≥90% of tumor cells on immunohistochemical analysis), MET amplification (≥10 gene copies on fluorescence in situ hybridization), or both whose disease had progressed during osimertinib therapy to receive osimertinib (at a dose of 80 mg once daily) plus savolitinib (300 mg twice daily) or intravenous platinum-pemetrexed. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival and safety.ResultsOf the 1746 patients screened, 338 were randomly assigned to receive osimertinib-savolitinib (171 patients) or platinum-pemetrexed (167 patients). Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free survival than platinum-pemetrexed (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.72; PConclusionsOsimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than platinum-pemetrexed among patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both that had progressed during osimertinib therapy (Funded by AstraZeneca; SAFFRON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05261399.).

articles.title: Neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and chemotherapy versus standard of care for locally advanced rectal cancer (UNION): a prespecified interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial
articles.abstract: BackgroundTo our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). Here, we present a prespecified interim analysis of event-free survival.MethodsThis open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial was conducted at nine hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years with untreated cT3-4 or N+ rectal adenocarcinoma (≤10 cm distance from the anal verge) and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; stratified by clinical T stage and N stage), using permuted blocks, to receive neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions) followed by two cycles of intravenous camrelizumab (200 mg on day 1) plus CAPOX (oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 and intravenous oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1; experimental group) or long-course chemoradiotherapy (50·4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent oral capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily) followed by two cycles of CAPOX (standard-of-care group). After surgery, both groups received six cycles of adjuvant CAPOX, and the experimental group additionally received adjuvant camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles. The primary endpoint was BIRC-assessed pathological complete response rate in the intention-to-treat population, which has been previously reported. Here, we performed a prespecified interim analysis of investigator-assessed event-free survival (one of the key secondary endpoints, defined as time from randomisation to radiographic progression precluding surgery, local recurrence or distant metastasis, or death) in the intention-to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients) with a boundary of a two-sided p values less than 0·0102. Safety was evaluated in all patients who received at least one dose of the study treatment according to the assigned regimen. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04928807, and is active, but no longer recruiting.FindingsBetween July 23, 2021, and March 1, 2023, 231 patients (153 [66%] males and 78 [34%] females; 227 [98%] were Han Chinese, and four [2%] were other ethnicity Chinese) were randomly assigned to the experimental group (n=113) and standard-of-care group (n=118). As of Oct 1, 2025, the median follow-up duration was 36·7 months (IQR 32·6-39·9) in the experimental group and 34·7 months (31·1-39·1) in the standard-of-care group. The 3-year investigator-assessed event-free survival rate was 91·3% (95% CI 83·9-95·4) in the experimental group versus 77·4% (67·9-84·4) in the standard-of-care group (stratified hazard ratio 0·33 [0·15-0·71]; two-sided log-rank p=0·0029). During the entire treatment period, the most common grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were decreased lymphocyte count (23 [20%] of 115 in the experimental group vs 31 [28%] of 112 in the standard-of-care group), decreased white blood cell count (13 [11%] vs 16 [14%]), decreased neutrophil count (13 [11%] vs 13 [12%]), and decreased platelet count (seven [6%] vs 15 [13%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 22 (19%) versus 15 (13%) patients, with the most common being decreased platelet count (one [1%] vs six [5%]), and radiation gastroenteritis (two [2%] vs four [4%]). Treatment-related deaths occurred in one patient in the experimental group (septic shock related to chemotherapy, but unrelated to camrelizumab) and none in the standard-of-care group.InterpretationIn this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX.…

articles.title: Robust Full-Spectrum-Responsive Multi-junction Tandem Solar Cells via Enhanced Near-Infrared Photon Harvesting
articles.abstract: Developing robust multi-junction tandem photovoltaics remains constrained by the instability of mixed-halide perovskite subcells, given their dominating contribution to overall power output. Integrating near-infrared (NIR) PbS quantum dots (QDs) with FAPbBr3 and crystalline silicon (c-Si) broadens spectrum utilization while improving overall operational stability by reducing the perovskite power contribution. However, enlarged (100) facets and the trade-off between film thickness and quality limit efficient NIR photon harvesting. Herein, a Lewis-basic dihydrazide molecule achieves universal passivation across diverse PbS QD facets via synergistic lead chelation and hydrogen-bonding interactions. Consequently, 0.8 eV PbS QD solar cells with a 685 nm-thick active layer achieve a short-circuit current density of 41.31 mA cm–2 and a 1100-nm-filtered efficiency of 1.80%. The resulting FAPbBr3/c-Si/PbS triple-junction tandems achieve a promising efficiency of 31.04%, with the perovskite subcell contributing 30.4% of the total power output, demonstrating a well-matched operational lifetime. This work offers a strategic framework for efficient multi-junction tandem photovoltaics.

HOST MATTER: Parasite infection drives chemical reconfiguration of decomposing host and shapes insect behavioural responses
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Host–parasite interactions shape ecosystems by driving species dynamics, yet their influence is typically considered in terms of host mortality rather than the chemical environments generated during infection and decomposition. Here, we show that parasitic infection actively reconfigures the chemical phenotype of decomposing hosts, reshaping ecological interactions through volatile‐mediated signalling. Using soil‐dwelling parasites‐entomopathogenic nematodes (EPNs) and their symbiotic bacteria‐as a model system, we integrate behavioural assays, comprehensive volatolomic characterization and CO2 quantification across three insect orders and two EPN species over four post‐mortem intervals. We demonstrate that EPN‐infection generates a distinct and conserved volatile signature dominated by carboxylic acids, sulphur‐containing compounds and unsaturated hydrocarbons, accompanied by elevated CO2 emissions. These infection‐derived blends elicit contrasting behavioural responses: they repel non‐natural hosts while consistently attracting natural hosts, indicating that infected cadavers function as chemically structured information hubs. In contrast, frozen‐killed insects exhibit fermentation‐type profiles, and bacteria‐only infection produce simplified alkane‐dominated blends, demonstrating that the full chemical phenotype emerges from the nematode–bacteria complex. Our findings reveal parasitic infection as a process that reorganizes decomposition chemistry with measurable behavioural consequences, uncovering a previously underappreciated mechanism by which parasites structure soil food webs and influence multitrophic interactions. articles.title: Local adaptation to host plants in herbivorous insects: A meta‐analysis
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Local adaptation, wherein populations are well‐adapted to local biotic and abiotic conditions, is a common outcome of natural selection and a driver of diversification. Previous theory identified two criteria to detect local adaptation: (a) the home‐away criterion compares the fitness of a population in its home environment to its fitness in a different environment and (b) the local‐foreign criterion examines differences in fitness between a local and a foreign population when experiencing the local environment. We conducted a meta‐analysis synthesizing empirical evidence of insect herbivores' local adaptation to their host plants using both criteria to assess how diet breadth, geographic distance among populations, herbivore taxonomic affiliation, herbivore clonality, the herbivore response variable measured, taxonomic distance among host plants and features of the study design impact the likelihood of detecting local adaptation. Overall, we found patterns consistent with herbivore local adaptation using both the home‐away and local‐foreign criteria. Herbivore diet breadth, taxonomic affiliation and geographic distance between herbivore populations did not affect the likelihood of finding local adaptation. In contrast, the detection of local adaptation varied with herbivore clonality, the specific response variables measured, taxonomic distance among host plants and elements of the experimental design. These findings clarify the conditions under which local adaptation emerges in the world's most diverse group of multicellular organisms. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Resumen La adaptación local consiste en el desarrollo de características que permiten un mejor desempeño de las poblaciones en las condiciones bióticas y abióticas de su entorno. Este fenómeno es una consecuencia común de la selección natural y uno de los mecanismos de diversificación biológica. Se han identificado dos criterios para detectar adaptación local: (a) el criterio ‘en casa‐fuera de casa’ que compara la adecuación de una población en su propio ambiente contra la adecuación de esa misma población en un ambiente foráneo; y (b) el criterio ‘local‐forastero’, que compara la adecuación de dos poblaciones, una local y otra foránea, cuando habitan el ambiente natal de cada una de ellas. Utilizamos un meta‐análisis para sintetizar evidencia empírica de la adaptación local de insectos herbívoros a sus plantas hospederas de acuerdo con cada uno de los criterios anteriores. Este análisis nos permitió evaluar el efecto de la amplitud de la dieta, distancia geográfica, afiliación taxonómica del herbívoro, clonalidad, variable de respuesta, distancia taxonómica entre la planta local y la foránea, y características del diseño experimental, en la probabilidad de detectar adaptación local. Encontramos patrones consistentes con la noción de que los insectos herbívoros exhiben adaptación local a sus plantas hospederas de acuerdo con ambos criterios. Adicionalmente, encontramos que la amplitud de la dieta, afiliación taxonómica y la distancia geográfica entre las poblaciones de herbívoros no afectaron la probabilidad de detectar adaptación local. Por el contrario, variables que sí afectaron la probabilidad de detectar adaptación local incluyen la clonalidad del herbívoro, la variable de respuesta que se utilizó para evaluar el desempeño del herbívoro, la distancia taxonómica entre las plantas local y foránea, y algunos elementos del diseño experimental. Nuestros resultados contribuyen al esclarecimiento de las condiciones que determinan la ocurrencia de adaptación local en el grupo más diverso de organismos multicelulares.

articles.title: Biodegradable and Non‐Biodegradable Microplastics Drive Divergent Microbial Carbon and Nitrogen Metabolism Regimes in Soil–Plant Systems
articles.abstract: The accumulation of microplastics (MPs) in soils worldwide has raised concerns about their potential impacts on microbially mediated carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) cycling. However, whether biodegradable and non‐biodegradable MPs differently affect microbial C and N metabolism and coupling, and whether these responses are modulated by co‐occurring plant identity remain uncertain. We combined a meta‐analysis with a controlled pot experiment comparing soil responses under two congeneric plant species exposed to two biodegradable and two non‐biodegradable MPs at doses ranging from 0% to 2% (w/w). In the meta‐analysis, MPs generally increased CO2 emission and microbial biomass N (MBN), but had no significant overall effect on microbial biomass C (MBC). In the pot experiment, MPs likewise increased CO2 emission, whereas overall effect sizes of MBC and MBN were nonsignificant. Nevertheless, these overall responses did not capture the distinct patterns of microbial C–N metabolic coordination between MP types. Under biodegradable MPs, tighter MBC–MBN coupling with a dose‐dependent shift toward greater respiratory C loss relative to MBC collectively indicated a maintenance‐associated metabolic pattern. In contrast, MBC–MBN decoupling and stronger MBC–CO2 coupling under non‐biodegradable MPs indicated a biomass‐linked metabolic pattern. In addition, plant identity modulated these microbial metabolisms in an MP‐type manner, particularly in N‐related processes. These metabolic responses were accompanied with changes in soil property conditions and substrate availability, weakened DOC–DON coupling, and shifts in microbial community structure and life history strategy. RDA‐based hierarchical and variation partitioning and SEM further indicated that modeled soil property pathways were more prominent under non‐biodegradable MPs, while substrate‐related pathways were prominent under biodegradable MPs. Together, the meta‐analysis reveals the general microbial metabolic patterns under MP type, and the pot experiment further reveals how MP type and plant identity jointly influence microbial C–N metabolism through contrasting associations with soil substrates and property conditions.

articles.title: Conservative Spruce Outperforms Acquisitive Larch Under Warming and CO2
articles.abstract: Predicting boreal forest growth is hindered by limited experimental tests on the compounding effects of climate change and atmospheric CO2. We integrated regional tree‐ring data with a peatland warming and CO2 manipulation experiment, including 45 trait measurements, to assess growth responses of two widespread boreal conifers, Larix laricina and Picea mariana, to temperature, vapor pressure deficit (VPD), soil moisture, and elevated CO2. L. laricina growth was consistently more climate‐sensitive than P. mariana, increasing strongly with soil moisture and declining slightly with VPD at the regional scale, but responding positively to VPD and temperature—not soil moisture or CO2—at the experimental peatland. L. laricina's acquisitive strategy enhanced water and nutrient uptake, sustaining growth but reducing hydraulic safety. By contrast, P. mariana's conservative strategy maintained water‐use efficiency and hydraulic resilience without compromising growth. Our results challenge projections of widespread CO2 fertilization in boreal forests and highlight conservative conifers as potential winners under warming and drying, sustaining growth while maintaining low mortality risk. This dynamic could reshape projections of the boreal carbon sink and its role in global climate feedback.

articles.title: Corrigendum to “Machine learning accelerated interfacial fluxionality in Ni-supported metal nitride ammonia synthesis catalysts” [J. Catal. 450 (2025) 116224]
Visible-light-driven piezo-photocatalytic water purification by an SPR-enhanced Bi0.5Na0.5TiO3/Bi-QDs/BiOBr heterojunction: dye mineralization, detoxification, and bacterial disinfection
Canopy spectral variability is a weak proxy for plant alpha diversity
articles.abstract: Canopy spectral variability is a context‐dependent and incomplete proxy for plant alpha diversity in herbaceous communities. Explicit consideration of community composition is therefore important when canopy spectral variability is used to infer plant alpha diversity across plant communities. Abstract Canopy spectral variability is widely used as a proxy for plant alpha diversity, yet this relationship often varies among plant communities and spatial scales. This instability may partly arise because canopy spectral variability responds not only to species richness and evenness but also to community composition, including differences in species identity and dominance structure. We examined the influence of community composition on canopy spectral variability using two herbaceous datasets: airborne hyperspectral imagery from 706 National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON) grassland plots across the United States and UAV multispectral imagery from 330 quadrats in the Northeast China marshes (NECM). For each dataset, we quantified canopy spectral variability using the coefficient of variation of reflectance (ReflCV), and calculated alpha diversity indices and Bray–Curtis‐based community‐composition gradients. We then assessed how canopy spectral variability varied along community‐composition gradients, compared the variance contributions of community‐composition gradients and alpha diversity, and evaluated how relationships between ReflCV and alpha diversity changed after accounting for community composition. Canopy spectral variability changed significantly along community‐composition gradients, and community composition accounted for more variance in ReflCV than alpha diversity in both datasets. Accounting for community composition also altered the estimated relationships between ReflCV and alpha diversity, but in contrasting directions: these relationships generally weakened in NECM but strengthened in NEON. These contrasting responses indicate that community composition can either enhance or obscure apparent associations between canopy spectral variability and alpha diversity, depending on the underlying compositional context. Synthesis. Canopy spectral variability is a context‐dependent and incomplete proxy for plant alpha diversity in herbaceous communities. Explicit consideration of community composition is therefore important when canopy spectral variability is used to infer plant alpha diversity across plant communities.

articles.title: Vendi information gain for active learning and its application to ecology
articles.abstract: While monitoring biodiversity through camera traps has become an important endeavour for ecological research, identifying species in the captured image data remains a major bottleneck due to limited labelling resources. Active learning—a machine learning paradigm that selects the most informative data to label and train a predictive model—offers a promising solution, but typically focuses on uncertainty in the individual predictions without considering uncertainty across the entire dataset. We study Vendi information gain (VIG) as an active learning policy that selects images based on their impact on dataset‐wide prediction uncertainty, capturing both informativeness and diversity. We applied VIG to two representative datasets in ecological image classification, the Kenya Camera Trap Dataset and the Missouri Camera Trap dataset, and compared VIG against common active learning methods. On both datasets, VIG achieves higher accuracy with fewer labelled examples. We further conducted extensive ablation studies to investigate the effects of the predictive model, batch sizes and other hyperparameters to find relatively robust performance from VIG. VIG has broad applicability beyond ecology, and our results highlight its value for biodiversity monitoring in data‐limited environments.

articles.title: Interspecific Gene Flow and Potential Hybrid Breakdown in South Atlantic Sea Turtles
articles.abstract: Interspecific hybridisation can play an important evolutionary role, generating new taxa or outbreeding depression, which can also lead to behavioural reproductive isolation through reinforcement. Still, there are few studies investigating how divergence time relates to hybridisation rates and its impact on introgression. Sea turtles are known to hybridise, despite their long divergence times and behavioural, ecological and morphological differences. Several genetic studies have attempted to determine the extent of hybridisation between four of the seven extant sea turtle species (Caretta caretta, Eretmochelys imbricata, Lepidochelys olivacea and Chelonia mydas) in the South Atlantic coast of Brazil, an area known to include nesting and feeding sites for all these species. In this work, we combined new and published genomic data of all four sea turtle species and their hybrids in a detailed population genomics study. Although hybridisation does occur in Brazilian nesting sites between three of the four species, it appears to be limited to first‐generation hybrids and few backcrosses, which points to some postzygotic barriers between species and hybrid breakdown. Moreover, our evidence suggests a moderately high level of relatedness among hybrids, indicating a reduced number of independent hybridisation events. Despite this fact, we found evidence of backcrosses involving different species, and an F2 progeny between Ca. caretta x E. imbricata F1 hybrids, which suggests hybrid male fertility. Limited interspecific gene flow appears to be part of the long history of divergence of sea turtles, as low levels of deep time introgression were inferred. In summary, this work contributes important evidence regarding the rate and success of hybridisation at large scales of divergence, and how this seemingly equates to low rates of introgression, pointing to temporal limits to gene flow.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant nivolumab with or without visugromab in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: the phase 2a GDFATHER-NEO trial
articles.abstract: As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026: In this exploratory, nonrandomized phase 2a trial, treatment of patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-naive muscle-invasive bladder cancer with the GDF-15-neutralizing antibody visugromab and nivolumab produced encouraging pathological complete response and radiographic response rates with no new safety signals, supporting further evaluation in larger randomized studies.

articles.title: Relatlimab plus nivolumab versus nivolumab for advanced melanoma: 5-year survival and biomarker analyses of the phase 3 RELATIVITY-047 trial
articles.abstract: As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026: In a 5 year follow-up of survival and correlative data from the pivotal phase 3 RELATIVITY-047 trial comparing relatlimab plus nivolumab versus nivolumab alone in patients with metastatic or unresectable melanoma, statistically significant differences in progression-free survival, overall survival and melanoma-specific survival were seen with high baseline levels of LAG3 high CD8+ T cells associated with improved response in the combination arm.

articles.title: [Articles] 14-day versus 28-day trifluridine–tipiracil plus bevacizumab for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer (PRABITAS): a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial in Japan
articles.abstract: A 14-day schedule of FTD–TPI plus bevacizumab was non-inferior to the conventional 28-day schedule for overall survival, while reducing haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity. These findings support this simplified schedule as the new standard for FTD–TPI plus bevacizumab in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer.

articles.title: [Comment] Optimising late-line treatment administration in metastatic colorectal cancer: an even brighter SUNLIGHT
articles.abstract: Offering late-line systemic therapy to patients with chemo-refractory metastatic colorectal cancer demands a careful estimation of the balance between the expected treatment benefit and its potential impact on quality of life, including adverse events, hospital visits, and psychosocial consequences.1 In such a comprehensive and individualised assessment of patients’ general conditions, usually summarised by Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status, the cumulative burden of disease-related symptoms and previous treatment-related adverse events, together with the potential decay of organ functional reserve, cannot be neglected.

articles.title: High-Performance LiNiO2 Cathodes through Microstructural Engineering
articles.abstract: LiNiO2 (LNO) is a promising high-capacity cathode, but its practical application is hindered by severe structural and microstructural instability. Herein, we develop a two-step calcination strategy that decouples lithiation from Ta introduction. This approach promotes the segregation of a Ta-rich phase at grain boundaries, producing nanosized, radially aligned primary particles that mitigate strain and suppress microcracking. It also preserves a layered–rocksalt nanostructured multiphase that reversibly transforms into a layered–spinel-like state during charging, which may contribute to structural stability and Li-ion transport. The optimized TS-Ta-LNO delivers 252.7 mAh g–1 and retains 88.4% of its capacity after 100 cycles. Furthermore, a TS-Ta-LNO/Li-metal pouch cell maintains stable voltage profiles under an electric vertical take-off and landing dynamic-load protocol, demonstrating its potential for high-energy, high-power batteries.

articles.title: Hot Carrier Cooling Dynamics in Tin Tri-Iodide Perovskites Thin Films
articles.abstract: Hot carriers (HC) offer a potential route to surpass conventional efficiency limits in solar cells. Generated after light absorption, these high-energy carriers can significantly boost device performance if extracted before dissipating energy as heat. Although HC cooling has been studied in tin-based perovskites, interpreting these dynamics is challenging because high-energy, high-fluence pump pulses required to generate HCs have shallow penetration depths, confining excitation near the surface. In tin-based perovskites, surface properties differ from the bulk, and surface defects may strongly contribute to the optical response. Here, by using pump-push-probe ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy, we photo-excite the semiconductor thin film with a low-energy pump, in a photon density range typical for solar cell operation, making relevant the bulk electronic properties, and selectively re-excite the photo-carriers only once they cool down, enabling direct tracking of HC relaxation in the relevant spectral region while minimizing surface contributions. We track the cooling process in FA0.85Cs0.15SnI3 (FA = Formamidinium) as a benchmark sample and extend the analysis to single-cation FA+, MA+ (MA = methylammonium), and Cs+ tin perovskites. Across all compositions, and at different doping densities, we find cooling timescales in the 150–600 fs time range. These results highlight the central role of phonon-mediated interactions and show that ultrafast cooling fundamentally limits hot carrier extraction in tin halide perovskites.

articles.title: Quantifying Sodium Metal SEI Dissolution and Relation to Corrosion Using Quartz Crystal Microbalance
articles.abstract: Sodium-metal batteries present a more abundant alternative to lithium-based batteries, with high theoretical capacity and comparable reduction potential. Ether electrolytes perform well in sodium-metal batteries under continuous cycling and are presumed to have a stable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI). However, the solubility of sodium SEI components is a cause for concern, and SEI evolution during calendar aging is not commonly studied for the ether sodium-metal system. In this work, SEI mass formation and dissolution are quantitatively measured for NaPF6 in diglyme. For varying potential hold levels, significant SEI dissolution is observed, from 55 to 76% of the originally formed SEI. Characterization shows that in addition to organic component dissolution, inorganic salts such as NaF and NaxPOyFz are unstable in SEI during open circuit rest. This instability results in continuous corrosion of sodium metal during calendar aging, highlighting an important understanding and concern of SEI stability in sodium-metal batteries.

articles.title: Weak-Solvating Carboxylate Ester Electrolyte Enables Hybrid Interphase via Cooperative Additives toward Wide-Temperature Sodium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Fast Na+ transport and durable interfacial stability remain challenging for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries. To address these issues, we developed a synergistic solvation-interphase regulation strategy by integrating methyl propanoate (MP) with a combined VC/NaDFOB additive pair. MP modifies the Na+ solvation sheath and facilitates Na+ desolvation, while VC and NaDFOB cooperatively generate a mechanically robust hybrid organicinorganic interphase. This coupled regulation enables enhanced ion transport and interfacial stability over a broad temperature range. The EC/EMC/MP + VC/NaDFOB electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 2.52 mS cm–1 at –40 ̊C and an increased Na+ transference number. Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cells retain 96.5% of their initial capacity after 1000 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.98% at room temperature. At –20 ̊C, the cells deliver 69.4 mAh g–1 for over 900 cycles, corresponding to 82% of their room-temperature capacity. This work establishes a practical solvation-interphase regulation approach for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries.

articles.title: Cell-state-specific metabolic networks govern ferroptosis versus apoptosis in small cell lung cancer
articles.abstract: SCLC cell states dictate how cancer cells respond to metabolic stress, revealing how metabolic plasticity determines whether the cells undergo ferroptosis or apoptosis.

articles.title: Perforin triggers iron-induced mitochondrial damage to drive ferroptosis and anti-tumor immunity
articles.abstract: Perforin is best known for delivering granzymes into tumor cells, but this study shows it has a second, independent killing function: it drives iron uptake and mitochondrial iron overload that trigger ferroptosis. This granzyme-independent pathway links cytotoxic immunity to iron metabolism, predicts patient response to checkpoint blockade, and points to iron supplementation as a possible lever for boosting anti-tumor immunity.

articles.title: Taurine lowers inflammaging by regulating the NLRP3 inflammasome in macrophages
articles.abstract: Taurine levels increase with age in mice and humans. Boosting taurine levels even further in aged mice increases health span and dampens inflammation through its regulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome.

articles.title: Secretory bile salt hydrolases regulate niche displacement and gut colonization of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus
articles.abstract: Hasegawa et al. show that a class of bile salt hydrolases (BSHs) harbored by Bacteroidales species promote elimination of vancomycin-resistant enterococcus (VRE) in the presence of Lachnospiraceae bai+ bacteria. In the gut, bacteria producing this subclass of BSH eliminate and displace VRE through deoxycholic acid (DCA) production.

Using NMR to predict molecular reactivity
articles.abstract: NMR chemical shifts are plainly transformed into machine learning features that have rational and intuitive chemical meaning. A small number of these features are used to predict molecular reactivity (via the HOMO-LUMO energy gap), resulting in a model that is not reliant on a priori knowledge of chemical structure or charge.

articles.title: Mechanochemical crystallization of covalent organic frameworks: from the linkage up
articles.abstract: This review discusses transferrable lessons and parameters from solution-based COF syntheses and small molecule mechanochemistry for the mechanochemical syntheses of imine and imine-derived COFs.

articles.title: Decoupling mass transport in wood-based separators enables ion selectivity for highly stable aqueous zinc-ion batteries
articles.abstract: By anchoring H 2 O molecules and reconstructing the hydrogen bond network through a hydrophilic delignified wood-based separator, the transport of Zn 2+ and H 2 O was decoupled to inhibit H 2 O-induced side reactions while ensuring Zn 2+ diffusion.

articles.title: Dynamic stress management in rigid wide-bandgap perovskites via molecular stereochemistry-engineered buffer springs
articles.abstract: Conformation-flexible molecule 1,4-CHD not only passivates defects in the perovskite film but also constructs a dynamic molecular spring at grain boundaries to dissipate stress, enabling 23.53% efficient wide-bandgap perovskite solar cells with superior thermal cycling and operational stability.

articles.title: Enhanced economic viability of direct seawater electrolysis: from cost reduction and resource efficiency to system-level techno-economics
articles.abstract: Direct seawater electrolysis (DSE) enables in-situ hydrogen production using natural seawater without pretreatment, emerging as a key technology to overcome resource bottlenecks and support offshore low-carbon hydrogen economies. Nevertheless, seawater's...

articles.title: pH-dependent charging and ion insertion promote bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysis on MnO 2
articles.abstract: The ORR and OER activity of α-K x MnO 2 simultaneously improve with increasing electrolyte pH. Electrochemistry, operando spectro-microscopy & grand-canonical DFT link this behavior to pH-dependent electrode charging and bulk cation (de)insertion.

Mechanistic asymmetry: Thermo-electrochemical interactions in silicon-graphite composite anodes
Coordinated development of the “water-energy-land-carbon” system in nine provinces and regions of the Yellow River Basin and analysis of obstacle factors
articles.abstract: Water resources, energy, land, and carbon emissions are the core resource and environmental factors that support the ecological protection and high-quality development of the Yellow River Basin. Using the panel data of nine provinces and regions in the Yellow River Basin from 2000 to 2024 as the research sample, by constructing the “water-energy-land-carbon” comprehensive coupling and coordination index (WELCNI), this study analyzes the coupling and coordinated development characteristics of the four subsystems and the composite system from both temporal evolution and spatial differentiation dimensions. The obstacle degree model is used to identify the core single obstacle factor restricting the system’s development, and the geographical detector model is used to reveal the interactive coupling driving mechanism of the obstacle factors. Combined with the upper, middle, and lower divisions of the basin for comparative analysis, this study systematically explores the evolution laws and constraint mechanisms of the basin system’s collaborative development. The research results show: (1) During the study period, the four subsystems of water resources, energy, land, and carbon emissions in the Yellow River Basin and the comprehensive coupling and coordination level of WELCNI have all continuously increased, and the quality of system collaborative development has significantly improved. (2) The coupling and coordinated development of the basin system presents a stable spatial gradient pattern of east being stronger a0nd west being weaker. The downstream areas of Shandong and Henan are the core areas of high-level coordination, while the upstream provinces such as Qinghai and Sichuan have weak development foundations and are the main bottleneck areas restricting the overall balanced development. (3) The constraint intensity of single obstacle factors shows a hierarchical characteristic of energy dimension > water resources dimension > carbon emissions dimension > land dimension. The energy consumption volume is the main obstacle factor, water resource endowment insufficiency is the secondary constraint key, and the land system has the weakest constraint effect. (4) Each obstacle factor has a significant collaborative enhancement interaction effect. The water, energy, and carbon systems form a complex linkage constraint network. Coal production, water resources volume, and total carbon emissions are the core factors with strong coupling effects. The cross-system superimposed constraint effect is prominent, and only unit GDP energy consumption is an independent constraint factor with weak linkage influence. This study systematically clarifies the evolution mechanism and obstacle mechanism of the “water-energy-land-carbon” system coupling and coordination in the Yellow River Basin, providing scientific references and theoretical support for differentiated zoning control, multi-factor collaborative governance, breaking through system development bottlenecks, and promoting the high-quality collaborative development of the basin.

articles.title: Enhancement of plant growth and soil stabilization by seaweed polysaccharides in the red soil region of Southern China
articles.abstract: Red soil is the second most extensively eroded soil type in China, predominantly distributed in the southern regions. Vegetative measures are widely recognized as an effective approach for controlling soil erosion in red soil areas, as they enhance slope stability and substantially reduce soil loss. However, during the early growth stages, the short and fine roots of plants are unable to extend beyond the shear failure surface, which constrains their capacity to stabilize the surface soil. To address this limitation, researchers have introduced seaweed polysaccharides as a soil ameliorant. Nevertheless, the specific mechanisms by which seaweed polysaccharides influence plant growth, root-soil complex mechanics, and the erosion resistance of red soil remain poorly understood. Accordingly, an experimental study was conducted to investigate the enhancement of plant growth and soil stabilization by seaweed polysaccharides in red soil. The results indicate that (1) seaweed polysaccharides exhibited an optimal concentration range for improving red soil. At concentrations below 2%, seed germination, plant height, and stem growth were promoted, whereas concentrations exceeding 2% exerted inhibitory effects. (2) In terms of mechanical properties, seaweed polysaccharides significantly enhanced the shear strength of the soil. Compared with the control group, application of seaweed polysaccharides increased the cohesion and internal friction angle by 103.68% ~ 180.52% and 13.92% ~ 31.76%, respectively. When seaweed polysaccharides acted in conjunction with plant roots, the improvement was further amplified, with increases of 143.33% ~ 220.65% in cohesion and 14.83% ~ 39.45% in the internal friction angle. (3) Under simulated rainfall conditions, the sediment yield from the slope significantly decreased with increasing seaweed polysaccharide addition. The synergistic effect of seaweed polysaccharides and plant roots arises from the formation of a “seaweed polysaccharide-red soil-root” three-phase unit structure, in which the polysaccharides encapsulate and connect roots with soil particles, thereby enhancing the integrity and flexibility of the root-soil complex. These findings not only broaden the selection of soil reinforcement materials but also provide theoretical guidance for vegetation restoration and soil and water conservation in red soil regions.

articles.title: Mean temperature determines whether winter variability accelerates or buffers energy loss
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Winter survival in dormant animals depends on conserving finite energy reserves, yet winter temperatures fluctuate around shifting means. In ectotherms, metabolic rate increases exponentially with temperature, so thermal variability is expected to accelerate energy loss, with consequences for overwinter survival under climate change. Whether dormant ectotherms can compensate physiologically, however, remains unclear. We overwintered Bombus impatiens queens under constant (2, 3, 4°C) or variable (2 ± 6°C or 4 ± 6°C) temperature regimes for 6 weeks, then measured metabolic rates across the temperature range. Thermal experience altered the temperature dependence of metabolism, but responses depended on mean temperature: variability centred on 2°C elevated metabolic rate at 11°C and increased thermal sensitivity of O2 consumption relative to constant 2°C, whereas variability centred on 4°C reduced baseline metabolism and thermal sensitivity estimated from CO2 production relative to constant 4°C. Using these responses, we simulated subsequent lipid depletion from a standardized energetic state. Variability around 2°C was predicted to shorten the time to lipid depletion, whereas variability around 4°C produced trajectories similar to those predicted for constant 4°C. Thus, identical thermal variance produced opposite physiological and predicted energetic outcomes depending on the mean temperature around which fluctuations occurred. Integrating both temperature means and variability is, therefore, essential for predicting overwintering energetics in a changing world. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Monospecific cover crops perpetuate soil biotic homogenization in croplands across diverse soils
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Croplands are known to support significant soil biotic homogenization. Cover crops are commonly used as a sustainable agriculture practice; however, many times these cover crops are composed of single‐species. Unfortunately, the influence of monospecific cover crops on soil biotic homogenization remains virtually unknown. Here, we performed a common garden experiment including soils from 27 agricultural fields across mainland China and two major cover crops grown separately in monoculture: a legume (Vicia villosa Roth) and a gramineae (Lolium multiflorum Lam.). We found that, on average, monocultures of both legume and gramineae cover crops significantly promoted soil biotic homogenization (i.e. lower β diversity) for bacteria, fungi and protists compared with control soils without cover cropping (p < 0.05). Moreover, gramineae cover crops also promoted multifunctionality homogenization (i.e. lower β multifunctionality), which was also connected with increasing biotic homogenization. Conversely, legume cover crops reduced the homogenization of bacterial generalists, thereby mitigating multifunctionality homogenization. Importantly, the homogenizing effects of monospecific cover crops on soil communities and multifunctionality were counteracted by the heterogeneity of initial soil properties, highlighting its key role in maintaining ecological heterogeneity. Our results suggest that monospecific cover crops contribute to soil biotic homogenization across diverse soils under controlled greenhouse conditions, with profound implications for managing soil biodiversity and ecosystem functioning in agroecosystems. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Nitrogen stimulation of soil carbon content differs between two types of mycorrhizal‐dominated ecosystems
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Increasing nitrogen (N) deposition has been suggested to favour arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) plants over ectomycorrhizal (ECM) plants, but how mycorrhizal association mediates N impacts on soil organic carbon (SOC) remains unclear. By synthesizing 315 N addition studies globally, we investigated the effects of N addition on SOC content in ecosystems dominated by ECM and AM plants (ECM and AM ecosystems). Our results showed that SOC increased by 4.1% in ECM ecosystems, likely due to reduced ligninase activity. In AM ecosystems, SOC did not change during the first 5 years of N addition, but increased by 7.3% over long‐term N addition (≥5 years), driven by increased litter inputs and progressive soil acidification. These findings highlight that N addition enhances SOC in both ECM and AM ecosystems via distinct mechanisms and temporal dynamics, implying that the potential of soil C sequestration may differ between the two ecosystems from short‐ to long‐term N addition. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: NF-κB phosphorylation controls enhancer selection to shape the inflammatory gene program
articles.abstract: Activation of the NF-κB pathway triggers diverse inflammatory outcomes despite similar upstream signaling. Leão et al. show that Ser276 phosphorylation of the p65 subunit of NF-κB p65 promotes CBP/p300 recruitment, enabling latent enhancer engagement and activation, and revealing an enhancer-selection mechanism that controls a distinct gene expression program shaping inflammatory and antimicrobial immune responses.

articles.title: The Battery Data Commons registry
articles.abstract: Public battery datasets are growing rapidly, but fragmented hosting and inconsistent descriptions make them difficult to find, compare, and reuse. Battery Data Commons presently indexes 349 datasets in a living, searchable metadata registry, using human- and machine-readable descriptions linked to the original sources. This exposes experimental context without relocating raw data to give datasets wider visibility and a second life to legacy ones. Together, these capabilities provide infrastructure for reproducible battery science, engineering, and AI-enabled innovation.

articles.title: Biologging and mechanistic niche modelling reveal thermal dependence of individual lizard movement patterns
articles.abstract: We combine animal‐borne biologging with mechanistic niche modelling to reveal how individual differences in thermal physiology shape lizard locomotor performance and movement patterns. Our framework links fine‐scale thermal variation with climate change responses, providing a new approach to understanding how ectotherm phenotypes may influence vulnerability to environmental change. Abstract Assessing how variation in thermal physiology and body size influences locomotor performance under ecologically relevant conditions is essential to predicting population vulnerability to climate change. We combined fine‐scale animal biologging and individual‐level mechanistic niche modelling to unravel animal–environment interactions in ocellated lizards (Timon lepidus) kept in semi‐natural mesocosms. We classified mobility states from accelerometer data to describe individual movement patterns. We produced continuous body temperature predictions through individual mechanistic models and used thermal performance curves (TPCs) to assess how body temperature influences locomotor performance. We further tested for evolutionary trade‐offs and simulated mobility windows under warming scenarios. Our results provided high‐resolution estimates of body temperature across mobility states, revealing how variation in thermal physiology is associated with movement. We found that individuals occupied different positions along a ‘specialist–generalist’ continuum of thermal strategies: some achieved higher locomotor performance but within narrower thermal ranges, while others displayed broader mobility windows but lower locomotor maxima. On the other hand, body size did not affect movement patterns under current climatic conditions, but warming simulations indicated that larger individuals may experience disproportionately greater increases in mobility under extreme warming. These findings demonstrate that even subtle variations in thermal physiology and body size can translate into differences in locomotor performance and mobility. By integrating physiological, behavioural and microclimatic data, our framework provides a powerful approach for predicting how climate change may reshape the spatial and temporal niches of ectotherms.

articles.title: Optimizing sampling and monitoring of species interactions within Biodiversity Observation Networks
articles.abstract: Using realistic simulations, this manuscript highlights that monitoring expectations for species interactions within Biodiversity Observation Networks should be much lower than for species richness. Yet, available information can optimize BON design to monitor interactions with higher efficiency, with a level of tolerance regarding the precision of the information needed for optimization. Abstract Optimal monitoring strategies should be designed to efficiently monitor all essential facets of biodiversity. Yet, species interactions are often overlooked in monitoring designs compared to spatial coverage and species richness, partly due to the inherent difficulty of sampling and monitoring interactions compared to species distributions. Here, we used simulations to test the efficiency of monitoring species interactions within Biodiversity Observations Networks (BONs). We tested several methods for designing and optimizing BONs to monitor species interactions and examined efficiency when increasing the number of monitored sites. We showed that the required sampling effort is considerably higher for interactions, especially when considering that interaction realization and detection realistically depend on species abundance. Thus, expectations to monitor a relevant proportion of interactions within a BON should be lower than expectations to monitor its species. However, from a single‐species perspective, optimizing monitoring designs based on a known species range proved an efficient strategy to retrieve its interactions, outperforming designs based on total species or interaction richness. Further efficiency gains required detailed knowledge of where realized interactions occurred, highlighting the need for better knowledge of where interactions are likely to take place and integration of factors influencing interaction realization, such as species abundances. Our results were consistent even when the total species range was over‐ or underestimated by 10%, which shows a tolerance in the precision of the information required for optimization. These findings highlight how attainable levels of information can lead to efficiency improvements when designing BONs. With the right target and optimization strategy, and readily available information, such as species ranges, we can therefore guide observation network designs to monitor species interactions as central biodiversity components.

articles.title: Parental death destabilizes wolf packs despite the benefits of larger pack size
articles.abstract: Larger wolf packs were associated with improved demographic performance overall, but these general benefits did not buffer the demographic consequences of parental death. Compared with packs in which both parents survived, packs experiencing parental death were substantially more likely to dissolve and fail reproductively and recruited fewer pups, demonstrating that parents perform demographic functions that cannot be fully replaced by additional group members. Abstract Cooperative breeding is a fundamental feature of many animal family groups. However, few studies have quantified whether variation in group size meaningfully buffers social and reproductive consequences following parental death. Using 17 years of data from a grey wolf (Canis lupus) population in Oregon, USA, we evaluated how parental death (the death of one or both parents) influenced pack dissolution, reproductive failure and pup recruitment and whether larger pack sizes mitigated these effects. Across 303 pack‐years, we recorded 69 parental deaths, 39 pack dissolutions and 112 reproductive failures. Packs that experienced parental death were nearly five times more likely to dissolve (95% CI: 2.12–11.12), nearly 16 times more likely to fail reproductively (95% CI: 5.34–47.26) and recruited 66% fewer pups (95% CI: 49%–78% fewer) than packs in which both parents survived. Larger packs were associated with improved demographic outcomes overall, but these group‐size benefits were insufficient to fully offset the elevated risks associated with parental death. Our results show that numerous individuals can provide generalized pack‐level demographic resilience but do not functionally replace parental roles, highlighting the importance of evaluating social structure in addition to population size. By clarifying the limits of social buffering in a cooperatively breeding carnivore, this study advances understanding of how social systems respond to parental death.
